### 3. Concerning Tin and Bismuth.
THESE two shall be calcined with a sulfur of vitriol and extracted with an *aqua fortis* <term>Aquafort: nitric acid, used to dissolve metals</term> / and applied to a calcined lead <note>original: ♄</note> / let that flow, two parts with two parts silver <note>original: ☽</note> / it yields its gold <note>original: ☉</note> tests.

### 4. Concerning Antimony and Arsenic.
OF these two, take / four loth <note>A loth is approximately 15–16 grams</note> of each, ground with copper <note>original: ♀</note> foil / make layer upon layer in a crucible / calcine this / and then grind it small / pour an *aqua fortis* upon it / let it extract day and night / thereafter put small granulated silver <note>original: ☽</note> into a glass / equal parts of four loth / pour the *aqua fortis* upon it / and precipitate / let this flow with an equal weight of the following flux / refine the regulus <term>König: literally "king," the metallic button that settles at the bottom of a crucible after smelting</term> / The mark of silver <note>A "mark" was a standard unit of weight for precious metals, roughly 233 grams</note> <note>original: ☽</note> holds four loth of gold <note>original: ☉</note>.

### The Flux.
IN one loth of silver-litharge <note>original: ☽ glett; lead oxide produced during silver refining, used here as a fluxing agent</note> take / four loth of common salt / two loth of raw tartar <term>Tartarum: potassium bitartrate, a byproduct of winemaking</term> / a half loth of iron filings / I tell you this flux is beyond price / it creates much profit in Antimonial matters.

### 5. A Work of Art with Silver <note>original: ☽</note>.
TAKE sulfurous gun-pyrite / and common shop-sulfur / mix it together, four loth of each / calcine with it your silver <note>original: ☽</note> which contains no gold <note>original: ☉</note> / let this become a "body" <note>A solid metallic mass</note> / let it flow in gun-pyrite by itself for an hour / the sulfur must be calcined. Thereafter, crush the silver <note>original: ☽</note> small and draw it off strongly with an *aqua fortis* / reduce that with the aforementioned flux / so you have iij. <note>three</note> loth of gold <note>original: ☉</note> in the mark of silver <note>original: ☽</note>.

### 6. A "Part with Part" <note>original: *pars cum parte*; an alchemical process where a small amount of a potent substance is added to a metal to improve or "multiply" its value</note>.
IN a loth of gold <note>original: ☉</note> that has fallen by quartation <term>Quartam: the process of separating gold from silver using nitric acid</term> take / wash this gold-ash sweet <note>Washing away acidic residues until the water is no longer sour/bitter</note> and dry it / grind into it half a loth of common sulfur / let it burn off / do this with fresh sulfur four times / so the gold <note>original: ☉</note> is prepared.
Now take *suginol* <note>Likely an alchemical oil or fatty substance</note> boiled with vitriol and iron <note>original: ♂</note> dross / half a loth / gun-pyrite three quintlin <note>A quintlin is about 4 grams</note> / Grind these two together small / put them in a glass / pour a saffron <note>original: Jafaron; likely "Saffron of Mars" or another metallic oxide reagent</note> upon it in which one loth of fine silver <note>original: ☽</note> has been dissolved / and draw it up and on / until the water remains upon it / do this with fresh saffron for the third time. Let this precipitate flow with the aforementioned flux / the silver-litharge <note>original: ☽ glette</note> / and refine until it brightens <term>blicken: the "brightening" or "lightning" of the silver, a flash that occurs during cupellation when the impurities are finally gone</term> / add to this silver <note>original: ☽</note> the aforementioned gold <note>original: ☉</note> / in equal weight / and cement it with the following cement.
Take red calcined vitriol / sal ammoniac and brick dust / four loth of each / so it is prepared / that will also be a high "part with part."

## 7. Another excellent *pars cum parte* <note>original: "p. c. p."; a "part with part" operation where a portion of a precious metal is used to "transmute" a larger portion of base metal</note> and it has been found correct 15 times.

Take Sulfur, pyrites <note>original: "Büchsenkiß"; likely iron or copper pyrites used in firearms</note>, and raw Antimony, all ground small, four lot of each; make layer upon layer <note>original: "stratum super stratum"</note> with copper <note>original: ♀</note> foil; let it calcine gently for five hours. Take these plates, grind them small, and [add] an equal weight of red calcined pyrites. Put this into a glass flask; pour a strong *Jasoron* <term>Jasoron: a specific alchemical solvent or acid mentioned in this manuscript, likely a variant of "water of sulfur" or a mineral acid</term> over it so that it covers it well by two fingers' breadth; let it stand in gentle heat for 26 hours, and thus the extract is ready.

Now take gold <note>original: ☉</note> calx <note>Calx: the powdery residue left after a metal is burned or "calcined"</note> which was precipitated by the *Jasoron* and prepared with sulfur as mentioned above, one lot; *Suginol* <note>likely a specialized alchemical name for a mercury preparation</note> mercury <note>original: ☿</note>, three quint <note>A quint or quintein is about 3.5 grams</note> rubbed into the gold calx; put it all together into a cucurbit flask; pour the extract over it, the sulfur one lot; and dissolve one lot of fine silver <note>original: ☽</note> in the *Jasoron*; pour that in too; and distill it off [until the liquid is reduced to] nine finger-breadths; pour the water back on and distill it off; do this until all the water remains upon it and the material becomes a precipitate. Grind this small, and [add] a large portion of the flux of equal weight to the scale, [made] with litharge <note>original: Glett; lead oxide</note>, common salt, and tartar; let it begin to melt gently for a quarter hour, and refine the regulus <term>König: literally "king," the metallic button that settles at the bottom of a crucible</term>; so the "part with part" is all gold <note>original: ☉</note>; a royal water <note>original: "Aqua regis"; a mixture of nitric and hydrochloric acid capable of dissolving gold</note> is better for the first extraction here.

## 8. The third *pars cum parte*.

Take this extract; pour it over a sublimated cinnabar <note>Cinnabar: the bright red ore of mercury</note>; precipitate it with this cementing *pars cum parte* of gold <note>original: ☉</note> and silver <note>original: ☽</note>; that which it takes into itself remains as gold; the rest is found in the powder; reduce that with the litharge flux.

## 9. Another dry piece, which goes as follows.

Take pyrites and red vitriol <note>Vitriol: a sulfate mineral, often used to create acids</note>, four lot of each; calcine copper <note>original: ♀</note> foil; grind these with the calcined pyrites, half as much by weight as the red [material]. Of this take three lot, and one lot of fine silver <note>original: ☽</note>; raw tartar, burned out with saltpeter, half a lot; and a quintle of iron filings. All this should be previously soaked with urine several times; let it flow strongly in the heat; the raw regulus thus poured through with fresh [material]; so it remains half gold <note>original: ☉</note> when it is done for the third time.

## 10. Another.

Take the copper <note>original: ♀</note> foil as it was calcined above, and add red calcined pyrites; also moisten such powder with urine three times; let one lot of fine silver <note>original: ☽</note> be refined on the cupel <note>original: "Treibscherben"; a shallow porous bowl used in assaying</note> with lead <note>original: ♄</note>; and when the lead is half driven off, add the powder once or twice upon it; do this until the silver takes no more; refine it to the "brightening" <term>blick: the sudden flash or gleam seen when a molten metal (like silver) reaches high purity during refining</term> and part it <note>to "part" is to separate gold from silver using acid</note>.

# Of 
# von Hagenthurn
## Solidification of Usifur with Oil of Saturn for fixation
### permanent / also to make a Chybur in this way.
#### Trismosini.

->Take heed of the Devil, so that he does not strike you with his fists; use all of this to the praise of the Most High, and for the poor.<-

Take eight lot <note>A "lot" is a pre-metric unit of weight, roughly 15-17 grams</note> of common <term>Usifur</term> <gloss>Usifur: an alchemical name for cinnabar or vermilion (mercury sulfide)</gloss>; put this upon a smooth grinding stone and moisten it with <term>Jasoron</term> <gloss>Jasoron: a specialized alchemical solvent or "sharp water" mentioned throughout this text</gloss> so that it becomes quite damp, and grind it for a good four hours. Afterward, put it into a glass vessel. Pour the following Oil over it; let it cook well therein until dry, then pour fresh Oil over it again, and cook it down for a third time. Afterward, solidify <note>original: "figiers"; the process of "fixing" a substance so it no longer evaporates when heated</note> it for several weeks until nothing more smokes away upon a glowing coal and it remains "fixed." Take one lot of this, and one and a half lot of <term>Feinfelch</term> <gloss>Feinfelch: an alchemical term for refined silver or a silver-rich alloy</gloss>; let them flow [melt] together for two hours. That is a "fixed moon" <note>original: "☽ a fixa"; fixed silver</note>. Let it flow "part with part" <note>original: "p. ☉ ☽ c. p."; gold and silver in a part-with-part operation</note> with an equal weight of the fixed Usifur for three hours; it passes all tests.

## The Oil.

Take eight lot or more of Lead Litharge <note>original: "♄ Glett"; lead monoxide</note>; grind it small and fine, put it into a glass vessel, and pour a strong wine vinegar over it. Let it extract for several hours; draw off this vinegar, so that a powder remains. Grind that again, put it into a glass, and pour a strong brandy <note>High-proof distilled alcohol</note> over it which contains no water. Let it extract well for several hours; draw this off until it reaches an oily consistency <note>original: "Deligkeit"</note>. Then it is ready for the Usifur, and also for a "fixed" Chybur, as follows:

Take a common <term>Chybur</term> <gloss>Chybur: an alchemical term for sulfur</gloss>, ground very small and rubbed with Jasoron; put it into a glass. Pour the oil over it twice and let it solidify for four weeks until it gives off no more smoke. Make an amalgam <note>A mixture of a metal with mercury</note> with one lot of gold <note>original: ☉</note> and four lot of mercury <note>original: ☿</note>; let that "smoke" <note>evaporate the mercury</note> in a crucible, and put one lot of this Chybur upon it. Let it remain in flux for two hours and afterward refine it in lead <note>cupellation</note>; that is "white gold," very heavy in weight and good. In the same way, make an amalgam with Feinfelch and let it flow with the Chybur; that is fixed Silver. 

Understand: take a Chybur sublimated with Verdigris <note>original: "Spongrün"; copper acetate</note> and Antimony, and drawn off with Jasoron until it turns yellow. This Chybur, solidified with the above-mentioned Oil of Lead, is a wonderful Chybur for "part with part" operations and Feinfelch.

<header>Trismosinian Treatise.</header>

### Part with part, with the great Fire of Salomon Trismosini.

This <term>pars cum parte</term> <gloss>part with part: an alchemical process of mixing substances in specific ratios to transform them</gloss> with the long fire is quite certain. Take 8 <term>lots</term> <note>A "lot" is an old German unit of weight, about 15-17 grams</note> of tin <note>Symbol: ♃</note> / 5 lots of <term>Realgar</term> <gloss>arsenic disulfide, a reddish-orange mineral</gloss> / and one and a half lots of common salt / both finely ground. Calcine the tin in a pot between two bricks with the realgar and salt. Grind that into iron filings, with an equal weight of <term>verdigris</term> <note>original: "Spongrün," literally "Spanish green"</note> mixed in. Now let it be applied to several lots of lead in a melting dish; add the powder into it and let it turn to slag <note>vitrified/glassy residue</note> in a glass. Take that glass and once more an equal weight of verdigris; grind it into the glass and put it back into the <term>driving lead</term> <gloss>lead undergoing cupellation/refining</gloss>. Let it slag into a glass again; do this a third time, and then it is ready.

Now take half a pound of steel filings, 5 lots of verdigris, 3 lots of raw <term>vitriol</term> <note>Sulfate minerals, usually iron or copper sulfate</note>. Grind these two finely beforehand; mix them into the steel filings. Let them macerate with intense heat in a crucible for two hours. Afterward, wash away the vitriol and verdigris that has not smoked away; dry the steel filings and grind twice as much raw <term>antimony</term> into it as there is iron <note>Symbol: ♂</note>, also 8 lots of <term>saltpeter</term>. Let it macerate in strong heat for two and a half hours. Then apply it to lead, and add this antimony with the saltpeter and iron into it; let it slag into a glass.

Take the upper glass with the verdigris and this glass; grind both together, so it becomes one glass, and it is thus ready.

If you wish to work with weights of lots, take 2 lots of the glass, 1 lot of fine silver <note>Symbol: ☽</note> which contains no gold <note>Symbol: ☉</note>, and 9 <term>quintlins</term> <note>A smaller unit of weight, 1/4 of a lot</note> of common salt. Let the silver flow <note>melt</note> physically with it for 30 hours. Afterward, take an equal weight of gold as there is silver; melt them together. Of the upper fresh glass, take two and a half times the weight of the gold and silver; put it in a crucible with the <term>part with part</term> sealed with <term>lute</term> <gloss>a clay sealant used to make vessels airtight</gloss> in the middle. Let it melt with a great fire for four days and nights. Afterward, refine the body until the <term>flash</term> <note>original: "blick," the moment a precious metal appears bright and clear at the end of cupellation</note>; that is all good gold, valid in all tests.

-> The great fire fixes <-
-> the duration. <-

### To the Reader.

Thus far in this first treatise, very old and ancient writings have been compiled into one volume, the original manuscripts of which were written by Salomon Trismosini’s own hand and script; nearly all of these are still at hand and preserved. Included also is the Universal Tincture of Crinotus, written in the old script with hidden letters, which, for the sake of the inconvenience of printing, is presented here only in German; likewise the Egyptian Tincture (although the original of that is lost). Whoever desires to see them will find them with me.

->is a dialogue about <term>Alchemy</term> <note>The medieval forerunner of chemistry, focused on the transformation of matter, particularly the turning of base metals into gold.</note> / wherein Theophrastus instructs <term>Chrisophilus</term> <note>From the Greek roots "chrysos" (gold) and "philos" (lover); literally, "Gold-lover."</note> (that is / the Gold-maker / or he who would gladly have much Gold) in all things.<-

### Chrisophilus speaks first with himself, saying:

I cannot sufficiently lament and bewail this everlasting and common misery of mankind / when I see that all those things / in which there is scarcely a shadow of good / are so difficult and complicated / that barely one in a thousand can obtain them / and even when they have been brought about / they escape us quite swiftly / on the other hand, however, evil and dangerous things / beset us with every misfortune / so persistently / that we can only judge them to be directed toward our destruction / for in a moment we go to ruin / misery / poverty / sickness / and pain fall upon us in heaps / but that we might be happy / that we might be rich / or that we might become healthy / for that we require many years / and that we should lack nothing / that barely happens to us once in a hundred years / for as far as my own affairs are concerned / I am entirely in that very state and condition / and because since my youth I have wished for nothing more (though I am ashamed to admit it openly) than that I might become exceedingly rich / so has that same thirst which I have for Gold / completely imprisoned and corrupted me / and yet, to attain it, I have until now received no perfect instruction.

# A Dialogue on Alchemy.

### Chrisophilus.

You will no doubt have heard how much great loss and damage I have suffered—not only in riches and money, but also in time (which is the most precious thing)—for the sake of this art which the learned call <term>Chymia</term> <note>original: "Chymiam"; at this time, the terms chemistry and alchemy were used interchangeably to describe the art of transmuting substances.</note>. I am ashamed to admit, yet I cannot deny, how miserably I have been deceived by that most perverse class of people—indeed, those rogues who boast of being alchemists and <gloss>disciples of the philosophers</gloss> <note>original Latin: "Jünger der Philosophorum." In this context, "Philosophers" refers to the ancient masters of alchemy who allegedly possessed the secret of the Stone.</note>. And what is most difficult of all is how severely I have damaged my health from the stinking soot and the horrific tastes which I endured and inhaled in those deep caverns and vaults, where I labored in hiding like the <term>Troglodytes</term> <note>A term from antiquity for cave-dwellers; used here to mock the alchemist's habit of working in dark, underground cellars.</note>. The total of all this loss and damage is so great that even those useful things that might be gathered from this art—even if everything were successfully accomplished—could not be weighed against the loss.

### Theophrastus.

Ha! Ha! Ha! I might laugh myself sick if I had not tasted that very thing myself, even if I was unaware of your specific affairs. For last month, when I passed by your little house in the garden, I noticed such a stinking and coal-black smoke coming out of a small vault you have under the earth that I might have supposed and believed it was the <gloss>hellish abyss</gloss> itself, in which the Devil's mother cooks porridge for her children. However, so that I would not form an unfair opinion of your <term>prudence</term> <note>original: "Fürsichtigkeit"; meaning wisdom, foresight, or careful management of one's affairs.</note>, several things stood in my way. First, your respectable authority; next, that you are born of the highest lineage here; then also your advanced age, which has experience in many things; and finally, so many obvious examples and precedents from which I would never have doubted you had become wise and cautious through the danger and damage of others. Therefore, I could not persuade myself that you would set your mind upon such things which are so clearly attended by harm and loss—much less listen to those most damaging deceivers and rogues, who are themselves the disgracers and mockers of the true art.

### Chrisophilus.

But I have been as prudent and cautious in this matter as I possibly could be; and yet, how could I have let that thing go untried which...

# A Dialogue on Alchemy.

...through common consideration and precise investigation of so many learned authors, it has been made and held as indubitable <note>That is, beyond doubt or certain.</note>. This is especially so because all things belonging to this business have been most diligently described by so many ancient and modern philosophers of great renown. Lastly, it is because I lacked neither a clever mind nor riches, neither the time nor the opportunity to properly carry out these matters. What should I say, however, of examples and patterns? You alone—of whom all people spread word and say that you have attained the end of this art, and for which reason all nations call you blessed—provide me with a satisfying example in place of many others. 

If you will now be helpful in my abandoned and wretched affairs, and guide my voyage—which currently tosses about in stormy waves—to the land and into the harbor, then I will ensure that you shall immediately notice for yourself how much honor, ornament, and dignity will be granted to you through my friendship and through my respectable authority, power, and might.

->Theophrastus.<-

Theophrastus turns around slightly and speaks to himself with secret words: "Oh, I know the crocodile's weeping <note>original: "Crocodils wainen." We now call these "crocodile tears"—an ancient metaphor for insincere or manipulative grief used to lure a victim.</note> well enough."

What are you saying?

->Theophrastus.<-

I said that I recognize your well-inclined will. For you to be granted your wish—namely, that you could obtain peace of life and mind from that which you have in your thoughts—is as fitting for decency, and indeed for reason itself, as if the spiritual virgins <note>Nuns.</note> desired to crave or hold a shameless harlot-feast <note>original: "unverschembte Hürenfest." Theophrastus is using a shocking contrast to tell Chrisophilus that his desire to find spiritual peace through the greed of making gold is a moral contradiction.</note>. And so that you may perceive these things clearer than the day, I will do what is proper regarding the alchemical art, its power, and its nature (as much as has come into my knowledge): I shall repeat certain things with somewhat more depth and thoroughness.

->Chrisophilus.<-

Yes, I have been waiting for that for a long time; speak on.

# A Dialogue on Alchemy.

->Theophrastus.<-

Firstly, you should consider and appreciate that the Alchemical art is, among all arts, the most ingenious of all. Likewise, it is of the greatest use to the human race—indeed, it is even necessary—so that it is (as you will hereafter understand) not unworthy for one to spend their entire life with it and in it. However, this art is much more extensive than you supposed. Therefore, we should hold and estimate that the entire art—both that which deals with metals as well as that which concerns other minerals—exists in a twofold difference or distinction. The first has sprouted from natural principles <note>original: "principijs"</note> or origins, and it arises from causes of shared communication or harmonious agreement, and from the opposition of two natures that are set against one another; this type of alchemy is to be highly praised and wondered at.

The other type, however, certainly wishes to be regarded as such—indeed, it would rather be held as the true art than be what it actually is—and for that reason, it is sophistical <note>Refers to "sophistry": the use of clever but false arguments. In alchemy, this meant using "tricks" to make things look like gold without changing their nature.</note> and deceptive. Since its result and end is deceitful, it has never been desired by any wise person; however, it is accepted as good by almost everyone among those who possess the same understanding as the common rabble. The other alchemy <note>Referring back to the first, "natural" type.</note> is accustomed to bring forth from the secrets of nature (as I mentioned) wonderful, very beautiful, and also healing—not to mention divine—effects. Some things have been conquered and discovered through this same art by ingenious people but have come into common use to such an extent that they are no longer worthy of being called "art." However, some effects of this art have not yet been discovered, though a great number are believed to exist. And thus, they are still rightly called <term>Arcana</term> <note>From the Latin "arcanum," meaning a "secret" or "mystery." In Paracelsian medicine, an arcanum is a powerful, hidden healing force within a substance.</note> and mysteries.

Thirdly, some things have indeed been well-discovered, but those same things have, through many thousands of years, been known and manifest to very few people and almost no one—except only to him to whom the highest Ruler of Nature <note>A reference to God or the divine guiding force of the natural world.</note> has shown it. From this alone comes that one principal thing, namely the Goal and the right End of the entire Alchemical art, which truly has always remained hidden with wonderful skill and high silence, so that it should still be counted among those <term>Arcana</term>. From this, it has happened that most people dare to stubbornly—rather than truthfully—assert that such a thing does not exist in nature, since so many ingenious minds have worked in vain to attain this end or goal and have spoken of it everywhere; and so that they, among the common...

<summary>Theophrastus distinguishes between "natural" alchemy, which works with the deep principles of nature to produce divine and healing effects, and "sophistical" alchemy, which is a deceptive practice embraced by the ignorant. He explains that the true goal of alchemy remains a hidden mystery (Arcanum) known only to those chosen by God.</summary>

# A Dialogue on Alchemy.

...they were considered wicked, as if they had achieved something; in this, they clung to human vanity and considered it best to take refuge in that other Alchemy, which I have called Sophistical, and thus—as I will explain later—they fished with golden hooks <note>original: "mit guldin Anglen gefischet"; a metaphor for spending a fortune in gold to chase alchemical secrets, or using gold to create a deceptive appearance of success.</note>.

->**Chrisophilus.**<-

Explain this better to me, for I do not know which inventions of this art you consider to have been discovered, and which are not yet discovered.

->**Theophrastus.**<-

Alchemical inventions (to point out only the most prominent ones) concern partly the metals themselves, or other mineral or metallic things. Among the metallic ones, some may be noted that involve mixing metals together so that they appear to be something else; examples of these are common enough and well-known. Others involve changing them to make them more malleable, and for the most part, to change their colors, to increase the weight or heaviness—or what is easier—to reduce and diminish it; to make some harder and others softer—and yet all this without any fraud <note>Theophrastus distinguishes between legitimate metallurgy (alloys and tempering) and "sophistical" fraud intended to deceive people into thinking a base metal is literally gold.</note>. Certain arts are understood regarding minerals, which can just as well be mixed with metallic things, such as gilding and silvering (I must use the common words here). Also, there are the separations, for which one uses the strongest prepared waters <term>strong waters: "aqua fortis" or acids, like nitric acid, used to separate gold from silver</term>, through which the wonderful powers of minerals have been investigated and recognized. From this, one has become aware of the friendship and enmity the minerals have with the metals, which we rightly call *Sympathy* <note>original: "Simpatiam"; the Renaissance idea that certain substances have a natural, almost magnetic attraction or "friendship" to one another.</note>; such as the relationship of antimony, mercury, sulfur, *Contorfet* <term>Contorfet: a zinc-based alloy used to imitate gold or silver</term>, mountain green <note>malachite or copper carbonate</note>, lead, tin, and other such things, with gold, silver, and brass. To these also belongs the discovery of gunpowder, which with its wonderful power imitates thunder and lightning, and has now reached the point where it maintains that same power in its cracking sound. To this also belongs the art by which glass is drawn out into the longest pieces. Likewise, the making of mirrors—specifically those made from *Electrum* <term>Electro: a natural or artificial alloy of gold and silver, or a specific copper-based alloy used for mirrors</term>, which are the most excellent—although some also come from the Philosophical art and were first discovered through arithmetic, such as those called "fire-mirrors" <note>parabolic or burning mirrors used to focus sunlight to start fires.</note>. I will omit mentioning the things which belong to various medicines, since almost no medicine is prepared without this art. They have all sprouted from what they call *Distillations* (the highest of which is the *quintessence* <note>original: "quinta essentia"; the "fifth essence," a purified spirit or extract believed to hold the medicinal soul of a substance.</note>, so named by the new Doctors), and are subject to Alchemy; they cannot be the most prominent...

->**Chrisophilus.**<-

Oh, dear Theophrastus! I have waited a long time for you to say this. To investigate this very thing, I have incurred great expense and suffered much loss. I have also read so many books brought to me from the various ends of the earth, and have given them to many learned men to translate. But I am (which is most miserable for me) robbed of all hope, and I drift—as I mentioned before—in the midst of turbulent waves. I feared that I might grow old among those same "Syrenic" cliffs <note>original: "Syrenischen Schroffen"; a metaphor referencing the Sirens of Greek myth, suggesting dangerous attractions that lead to ruin.</note>. They are almost all frauds or fools who wish to persuade themselves and others that they understand things which they do not know. Indeed, in almost all these books, nothing is contained but pure riddles or hidden speeches—nothing but circumlocution and darkness—which cannot be guessed, resolved, or explained even by an <term>Adept</term> <note>original: "Adepto"; a master of the alchemical arts who has achieved the Great Work.</note>.

->**Chrisophilus.**<-

Why then—if that is so—have those same tellers of tales or writers of fables devoted so much effort and labor to this pursuit? Why do they so boldly promise men such perfect wisdom and instruction?

Indeed, as you say, this has been done by nearly everyone. And so that I do not deny it, it seems to me that they were moved to do so for four reasons. First, so that they might exercise the understanding and minds of idle people. Secondly, to give clever people a reason to investigate and seek out the most magnificent and useful things that flow from it. Thirdly, so that they might govern the meddlesome people—as well as those who are so greedy for gold—miserably (as is only fair), and so that they [the greedy] might misuse their effort and labor (not without the particular amusement and laughter of those philosophers). Do you not see that they have done this quite often, by giving one thing many different names everywhere? Finally, so that they might leave a memory for posterity, and show that they themselves understood the secrets of nature and its natural workings.

->**Chrisophilus.**<-

Why then did they not rather remain silent, than choosing to describe things that no one understands with such babbling books? # A Dialogue on Alchemy.

->**Theophrastus.**<-

It is foolish that you want to hear things from me which I have never claimed to know, nor have I experienced them myself. For among those skilled in nature <note>original: "Naturkundigern"; referring to natural philosophers or early scientists.</note>, it is an undisputed and generally accepted maxim that from nothing, nothing can be born. Furthermore, the <term>principles<note>original: *principia*; the fundamental origins or starting points of a substance.</note></term> or origin of every use or generation—to speak without doubtful ambiguity—must not disagree with the thing they wish to produce. Rather, it must share a most similar property with it (as I will explain later). Thus, neither is a metal born from an egg, nor a *crocodile* from a metal, though the reverse can happen in each case <note>Theophrastus is likely referring to the "corruption" of things back into their base elements, whereas "generation" requires specific biological or mineral seeds.</note>; yet you have undertaken to perform many more foolish things. And to answer your question more clearly: metals—especially those that are unequal in weight and delicacy—cannot be transformed. Gold, however, is unlike other metals in its weight and strength; therefore, I will not speak of the others, in which not much is impossible regarding the aforementioned things; besides, that does not pertain to your question.

->**Chrisophilus.**<-

Yet even the oldest *Arabic* masters <note>Referring to medieval Islamic alchemists like Geber (Jabir ibn Hayyan) or Rhazes, who were the foundational authorities for European alchemy.</note> themselves do not deny what you are accustomed to calling false.

->**Theophrastus.**<-

Indeed, you have never understood them or their dialogues. This is a core alchemical concept: to transform a substance, one must first reduce it to its "first matter."</note>

Go now and bring forth your dreams and useless chatter, as if there were an artificial transformation or generation of all things, or something out of nothing through art—which is entirely absurd and unusual to the law of nature, in which there is not a single comparison or friendship <note>In this context, "friendship" or "affinity" refers to the natural sympathy between substances that allows them to combine or transform.</note>. # A Dialogue on Alchemy. 104

...it can be that a single half-measure, if it is poured into a whole measure of wine, converts the whole of it into its own nature and properties, together with the taste and smell of wormwood <note>original: *Wermuts*; a bitter herb used in medicine and to flavor wine, here serving as a metaphor for an alchemical "tincture" that can transform a larger body.</note>; why something similar could not happen with or among the metals, I do not know.

Furthermore, if I had attempted or wanted to experience such things, and were to confess it publicly, it would follow that either—if the work did not succeed—everyone would mock me and I would be regarded as no better than the vagabonds <note>original: *Landstreichern*; itinerant charlatans who claimed to know alchemy to swindle people.</note>. Now you see that such a thing cannot be done without obvious danger to myself. For this business is so fashioned that its effects have hardly ever passed by any extraordinary person without harm; and to kings, they have often reached the point of ruin. And for that reason, this art is not to be wished for even by a wise man, unless he be so perfect that he could also despise the overflow of all riches and endure the lack of all things. And now you understand (as it seems to me) why it happens that the <term>Secrets<note>original: *Arcana*; the hidden, powerful essences or mysteries of alchemical practice.</note></term> of this art have come to so very few people in so many years.

# Elixir and Tincture of Theophrastus.

## Cures Leprosy, <term>Gout</term> <note>original: *Podagram*, specifically gout of the foot.</note>, <term>Dropsy</term> <note>original: *Hydropisin*, an old term for edema or swelling caused by excess fluid.</note>, Stroke, and all sorts of incidental diseases.

### Now begins the work of the Elixir.

Take a good wine, put it into a <term>cucurbit</term> <note>A gourd-shaped glass vessel used in distillation.</note> so that it is not half full, and place upon it an <term>alembic</term> <note>The "head" or cap of the still that redirects vapors.</note>, well-sealed with wheat flour and egg white; let it dry. Then place it in a <term>water bath</term> <note>original: *Balneum*. Specifically a "Balneum Mariae," where the flask is heated by boiling water rather than direct flame.</note> with hair and lead weights so that it does not tip over. Thereafter, place a recipient vessel before it and seal the glass with wax. Then, place a small fire beneath it—not too hot, but such that you could endure your finger in it—so that the spirits of the wine are distilled through the alembic into the recipient slowly, so that barely one drop falls in the time it takes to say three <note>original: *Pater noster*</note> Lord's Prayers. Then it is right, for you will see long streaks going into the alembic—that is a true sign. 

Thus you shall distill until you see drops of water gathering on the alembic like drops of sweat; then take off the recipient vessel and seal it at the top with wax. Place another recipient vessel before it and catch therein still more spirits as long as they come out strong. You should test this in your hand; when it seems to you that they are no longer good and strong, take that recipient down as well and keep it separate. Do not add it to the first, for it is of no use to the work. 

Then place another recipient vessel before it; thus a poor water will come, but in large drops. Distill that off with a gentle fire until a material remains at the bottom like a thin, melted honey. Then let the fire go out and take the glass with the material out, and put it into another glass and guard it with care; that is the <term>Earth of Wine</term> <note>The solid residue or "feces" left after distillation, believed by alchemists to contain the "salt" of the substance.</note>. Do this until you have four measures of this Earth, and you should always put them together. And of the good [spirit] that comes thereafter, put that together as well; it is of no use for this work. And you shall distill until you have about eight measures of the good spirits of the Earth; these you shall distill until they have no more water within them and are entirely separated from it; then it is right.

# Elixir and Tincture of Theophrastus. 111

Likewise, if the earth is not yet as thick as melted honey once it has come together, put it into a wide glass and place it in a <term>water bath</term> <note>original: *Balneum Mariae*; a vessel of water in which a flask is placed for gentle, indirect heating.</note> until it becomes thick.

Likewise, to proceed now to the true art, you should take one measure of the <term>dead earth</term> <note>original: *Terra mortua*; the solid residue or "corpse" of the substance remaining after the initial distillation.</note> and pour over it the <term>rectified spirit</term> <note>original: *Spiritum rectificatum*; the purified essence distilled previously</note> into a flask, and seal it at the top with a <term>Hermetic seal</term> <note>original: *Sigillo Hermetis*; an airtight seal, traditionally made by melting the glass neck of the vessel closed.</note>. Place it to <term>putrefy</term> <note>In alchemy, "putrefaction" refers to a slow digestion or fermentation in gentle heat to break down the material.</note> in a water bath or in <term>horse manure</term> <note>original: *Equino*; horse dung was a standard laboratory heat source because it provides a steady, low temperature as it decomposes.</note> that is warm, for four days and nights, until the spirit is colored very thick. Then take it out of the manure and pour off the spirit very carefully so that no earth runs with it; but for safety's sake, distill it through a <term>filter</term> <note>original: *Filtrum*</note>. Put this into a <term>distilling vessel</term> <note>original: *Distillatorium*</note> and place it in a water bath, and distill off the spirit through the water bath so that the earth remains thick like honey. From this, one shall distill the "Air."

### To make the Air.

Take this aforementioned earth, put it into a <term>flagon</term> <note>original: *Schenckrug*; literally a serving jug, here used as a distillation vessel.</note>, and set it in <term>sand</term> <note>A sand bath allowed the alchemist to reach higher temperatures than a water bath without breaking the glass.</note>, and distill an <term>oil</term> <note>original: *Oleum*</note> that floats upon all waters. You should distill this until you see that your <term>Fixed Black Earth</term> <note>original: *Terra Nigra fix*</note> is ready; you should do this until your earth becomes quite dry, as follows. And from this oil, the "Air" is made through the <term>rectification</term> <note>Purification by repeated distillation.</note> of the oil.

### To make the Fire.

You should take the <term>Fixed Black Earth</term> <note>original: *Terram Nigram fixam*</note> and pour upon it its spirit that was distilled before, if you wish to have a <term>coagulated quintessence</term> <note>original: *coagulierte quintam essentiam*; the "fifth essence" or highest medicinal power, here in a solid or thickened form.</note>. But if you wish only to distill the "Fire" first, then put your distilled oil upon it and <term>putrefy</term> it for 14 days in horse manure, so that whatever of the "Fire" is in the earth may be drawn out of it. Then distill an oil again; this is quite fatty and also floats on top. Pour that back onto the earth and set it to putrefy in <term>manure</term> <note>original: *fimo*</note> for 14 days as before. Then distill the "Fire" out of the earth, dry it as before, and set it in the open air of the heavens. If you see that the earth wishes to <term>dissolve</term> <note>original: *soluieren*; to turn liquid or deliquesce by absorbing moisture from the air.</note> in the air, then pour the spirit that was previously distilled back upon it, or over it, and distill once more an oil that is "Fire," and keep the earth. Add this to the previous earth, and each time you should test your earth in the air to see if it becomes moist yet does not dissolve. Thus you must always pour the distilled "Fire" upon it and do this until you see that the earth remains entirely dry in the air; then it is right.

...to make it so that it performs this test. You should take a large glass flask / of six or eight measures / and distill into it half a measure of the subtle spirit / and seal the flask well with wax / and place the glass in the middle of your hand / and let it stand a short time in your hand / so that it feels the warmth / so that it then raises itself up within the glass / and moves through the glass in such a way / that it seems to you to be completely full / and it passes through itself like the **Spirit of Strong Water** <note>original: *Spiritus Aquæ fortis*; nitric acid, known for its volatile and reactive nature.</note> / and gives off a shimmer and a color / like the rainbow / then it is enough.

Then set it upon a soft cushion to rest / so it settles back to the bottom / preserve this with diligence / and you should know / if a single drop of it were to fall in a house / or in a church / the house or church would smell so wonderful throughout / that no person on earth / has ever smelled anything better / and it is called a **heavenly scent** / therefore preserve your work with diligence / so that it does not escape / for out of this is made the <term>quintessence</term> <note>The "fifth essence" or purest spiritual core of a substance.</note> in this manner / with which one makes <term>Potable Gold</term> <note>original: *Aurum potabile*; gold in a liquid, drinkable form, considered the ultimate medicine.</note> / for mankind.

Also, you should put the previously described <term>Spirit of Wine</term> <note>original: *Spiritum vini*; high-proof distilled alcohol.</note> into a distilling flask / and immediately set upon it an <term>alembic</term> <note>original: *Alembicum*; a distillation cap with a downward-slanting beak or tube.</note> with two tubes / as is designed hereafter / and attach a <term>receiver</term> <note>original: *Receptacul*; a vessel for collecting the distillate.</note> to each tube / and in the receiver of the uppermost tube there shall be the **Gold oil** / which you made previously with the rectified fire / and in the lowermost receiver there shall be nothing / and seal each receiver well / and then give it a small fire by means of a <term>water bath</term> <note>original: *Balneum*; a vessel of warm water used for gentle, indirect heating.</note> / so the quintessence rises upward / through the curve of the tube / into the Gold oil / and unites with one another / and becomes one thing / that can nevermore be separated / and it becomes a golden water / and gives off great, long golden streaks / or rays / and a great bright shimmer / as if it were in a dark chamber / so that the entire chamber is illuminated by it / and the Spirit goes into the lowermost receiver / and is no longer useful for this work / because it is spent of its quintessence.

Also, then take the golden water and put it into a simple glass <term>distillation vessel</term> <note>original: *Distilatorium*</note> / and distill it off once / then it is yellow-red / and gives an even greater shimmer / than before / and leaves a little blackness behind / which you should throw away / for it is worth nothing / and preserve your water with diligence / because it is the highest **Potable Gold** / with which one makes people healthy / from all diseases / none excepted / within one hour / to whomever you give it to drink / even a portion as large as a tiny drop / and thank God for it.

The Fire is either ( Warm / Cold / Wet / or Dry.

# The method of sowing the seed into the Earth.

The <term>fixed fire</term> <note>original: *bleibende Fewr*; fire that does not consume the substance but remains within it, often associated with the "Soul" of the material.</note> is the Soul; it <term>tinctures</term> <note>original: *thingiert*; colors or transforms the inner nature of a substance.</note> and makes the <term>Mercury</term> <note>quicksilver</note> fluid and able to penetrate into the metals; it also unites the Mercury with <term>Sol</term> <note>The alchemical symbol for Gold.</note> in such a way that they can no longer be separated, and these three things become one single thing.

{
The Body of <term>Sol</term> <note>Gold</note>.
The Spirit of <term>Mercury</term>.
*Animax Animaxini* <note>original: "Animax Animaxini x"; likely a specialized or corrupted term for a refined essence.</note> is the Soul of Wine.
}

The fixed fire increases the metals, and without this fire, the Art <note>The "Great Art" of alchemy.</note> is not performed.

### Preparation of the Water.

Take the best wine and distill it so many times that if a cloth is soaked in it and lit, it burns away completely <note>This describes the production of high-proof alcohol or "Spirit of Wine."</note>; and this wine is called the Water and the <term>Quintessence</term> <note>original: *fünffte Wesenheit*; the "fifth element" or purest essence of a substance.</note>. Give this water its spirit. The spirit of the burning water is the <term>Spirit of Strong Water</term> <note>original: *Spiritus Aquæfortis*; nitric acid.</note>.

## The Soul of Tartar.

Take two pounds of <term>Vitriol</term> <note>iron or copper sulfates</note> and one part <term>Saltpeter</term> <note>potassium nitrate</note>; from these make a <term>Strong Water</term> <note>original: *Aquafort*; nitric acid.</note>. Distill the spirits from the Strong Water into the previous Water [of wine] so that it becomes one, and let it sit for ten days in <term>digestion</term> <note>the process of applying gentle, consistent heat.</note>. Thus you have a burning fire in the Spirit of Vitriol. Now give this corporeal water its soul as follows: Take <term>Tartar</term> <note>original: *Tartarum*; potassium bitartrate deposits from wine barrels.</note> and make a Water of Tartar.

Mix them thus: Take half a pound of the burning water with the spirit and one pound of the Fire of Tartar. Place it in <term>ashes</term> <note>An ash-bath, used to provide a steady, indirect heat for a vessel.</note> for eight days until the soul and the spirit are united. Afterward, distill the <term>first virtue</term> <note>The first, most potent portion of the distillate.</note> of the wine and keep it separate; after that comes the water, which you should throw away; finally comes the Spirit, which you should add to the virtue of the wine. Then let it cool, and you will find at the bottom of the vessel an earth which is called the Soul. This <term>Earth</term> <note>original: *Terra*</note> is called the Earth of the Philosophers, into which you shall sow your seed.

## The Soul which is the Earth.

Dissolve this earth with the water you have made, and it will quickly dissolve itself. Seal it well and place it in the ashes for four days; thus the Medicine is ready.

### The Method of sowing the seed into the Earth.

Take the previous preparation or its <term>amalgam</term> <note>a mixture of a metal with mercury.</note>. Take 9 <term>Loth</term> <note>a historical weight; 9 Loth is roughly 4.5 ounces.</note> of Mercury and one Loth of Gold, well mixed, and add to it 5 Loth of purified Mercury. Put all of this into a <term>cucurbit</term> <note>a gourd-shaped glass distillation vessel.</note> and pour the previous water over it so that it covers it by one finger—

### Fixation by means of the Morning Star. <note>The "Morning Star" is a common alchemical code for Antimony or sometimes the planet Venus.</note>

Take the Morning Star, make small pieces out of it, and work *by descent* <note>original: *per descensum*; a distillation process where heat is applied to the top of a vessel so the substance melts or vaporizes and flows downward into a receiver.</note>, as you know. In this, dissolve Mercury [☿] as much as you wish, and strain off the water; do this three times, or until the Mercury becomes red.

Now take one part sulfur and one part <term>Mercury precipitate</term> <note>a solid powder formed when mercury is dissolved in acid and then made to "fall out" of the solution.</note>, grind it as finely as possible on a grinding stone, and pour over it the previously distilled water of Mercury and sulfur; let it evaporate away; thus you have the sulfur and Mercury prepared as one part.

Grind this matter finely, put it back into a glass vessel, let it stand well-<term>luted</term> <note>sealed with an airtight paste or clay.</note> for four days with gentle fire; afterward, strengthen the heat on the fourth day. Then break the glass or vessel and grind the matter; put it into a new vessel as before and seal it, and give it three days of gentle fire, and another three days according to the <term>four degrees</term> <note>a traditional system of increasing heat intensity in alchemy.</note>; then it is fixed, perfect, and ready.

Now dissolve the <term>vermilion of the Moon</term> <note>original: *fermileonem Lunæ*; likely a red preparation of Silver [Luna].</note> in the prescribed strong water, and add two Loth—or however much you have—of the ground matter to the dissolved Silver, and place it in hot sand. Then Gold [☉] will settle at the bottom of the glass; melt this into a "body" <note>a solid metallic form.</note>. The remaining Silver in the water you shall again treat with the ground medicine until it is all converted into Gold [☉], and <term>reduce</term> <note>returning a chemical compound to its metallic state.</note> it with <term>Borax</term> <note>original: *Borras*; a flux used to aid the melting of metals.</note> just as with other Gold [☉].

### Of the Green Lion.
<note>The "Green Lion" is a famous alchemical symbol, often representing antimony, copper ores, or a powerful acidic solvent capable of "devouring" metals.</note>

Make a distilled vinegar / therein dissolve the green lion / set in <term>putrefaction</term> <note>the process of digestion or fermentation, often achieved by keeping the vessel in a warm place like a dung heap.</note> / then take it out and filter it / thereafter set it to distill in a <term>bain-marie</term> <note>original: *B.*, abbreviation for *Balneum Mariae*; a water bath used for gentle heating.</note> and draw the water from it / until it reaches an oily consistency / then put the residue or oil into a retort / set in a sand-capel <note>a sand bath</note> / give it gentle fire until the moisture vanishes / then fortify the fire / so the green lion gives off its <term>gluten</term> <note>literally "glue"; refers to a sticky or volatile substance extracted by heat.</note> through this heat of the fire / this is called the <term>Air</term> / over the <term>dead head</term> <note>original: *caput mortuum*; the solid, useless residue left in the bottom of a flask after distillation.</note> pour its <term>phlegm</term> <note>the watery, initial distillate.</note> / set in <term>dung</term> <note>original: *in fimo*; using the natural heat of decomposing animal waste to maintain a steady temperature.</note> to putrefy / then distill it as before / so even more spirits pass / drive it stronger / so a lemon-colored thick oil passes over the remaining dead head / pour again its first distilled water / set to putrefy / then filter again / and distill as at the first / lastly with the strongest heat in open fire / so a blood-red oil passes / and this is called the <term>Fire</term> / Set the remaining earth in a <term>reverberatory furnace</term> <note>original: *Reuerber*; a furnace that reflects heat back onto the substance.</note> / <term>calcine</term> <note>to heat to a high temperature to reduce to powder or purify.</note> it until it becomes entirely white / then it is prepared.

Now take one part of the earth / one part of the white <term>Sulfur</term> / and two parts of its first water / set in a vial in the <term>athanor</term> <note>a "pigeon-house" furnace designed to maintain constant heat for long periods.</note> / so that it incorporates / and coagulates / then again pour on one part of its sulfur / and two parts of water as before / until you have brought and fixed all the white sulfur / or the Air into the white earth or into its own ferment / so you find a white stone transparent like a crystal / it <term>tinges</term> <note>transforms the color and nature.</note> every metal into the best <term>silver</term> <note>original symbol: ☽</note>, stable in the <term>cupellation</term> <note>original: *in cineritio*; a test where metal is heated to see if it remains pure.</note>.

But if you wish, my son, to bring it to the highest perfection / namely to the highest redness / then take the second oil, highly <term>rectified</term> <note>purified by repeated distillation.</note> / and pour it over the whitened, shiny earth / which should be well-ground on a smooth marble / set in a vial / pour the third part of the oil over it / coagulate it in the athanor / as first learned from the white stone / perform the work until you have brought all the oil into it / as you have now handled the Air / so handle the Fire / with the blood-red oil / highly rectified / so you will make the reddest stone / transparent like a ruby / penetrating / flowing / and its nature comparing itself to a true <term>carbuncle</term> <note>a mythical deep-red gemstone or garnet.</note> and ruby; it tinges every metal into the best <term>gold</term> <note>original symbol: ☉</note> and [brings] the human body to its highest health. <note>original: *Deo gratias*; Thanks be to God.</note>

# AUGMENTATION
<note>original: *AVGMENTVM*; in alchemy, this refers to the process of increasing the quantity or quality of a substance, usually gold or silver.</note>

->With the<-

## Mercury of Lead /
<note>original: *Mercurio Saturni*; Lead was traditionally associated with the planet Saturn in alchemical symbolism.</note>
## Johannes Trithemius /
### Abbot in Sponheim /

which came to <term>Doctor Paracelsus</term> <note>The famous 16th-century Swiss-German physician and alchemist who laid the foundations for modern toxicology and chemical medicine.</note> / and was copied from his own handwriting.

This following "augmentation" and making of the <term>Mercury of Lead</term> / the Lord Abbot of Sponheim / <term>Johannes Trithemius</term> gave to a blood relative / to provide him with a livelihood / which work the wife of Trithemius’s friend / sold for a great sum of money after her husband’s death / and thus it became public. It is an augmentation after the Colophonian manner <note>likely referring to a style of alchemical practice or a specific geographic tradition.</note> / called <term>Borras-water</term> <note>original: *Borraswasser*; likely a specific name for a chemical flux or solvent used in the process.</note> / and such <term>Mercury of Lead</term> / is prepared with Hungarian Gold <note>at the time, gold from Hungarian mines was considered exceptionally pure.</note> for the "augmentation of fixation" <note>the process of making a volatile substance stable and solid under high heat.</note>.

# PROCESS
<note>original: *P R O C E S S V S*</note>

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'N' featuring intricate floral scrollwork.</image-desc>
Take six <term>Loth</term> <note>A traditional Germanic unit of weight; one Loth is approximately 15 grams or half an ounce.</note> of <term>Red Lead</term> <note>original: *Saturni Menig*; also known as minium, a bright red-orange lead oxide.</note> / and four Loth of common salt / grind the two finely together / put it into a large crucible / place it in a charcoal fire / until it becomes glowing hot / stirring it constantly with a piece of wood / so that it <term>calcines</term> <note>the process of heating a substance to a high temperature to drive off volatile matter or to oxidize it into a powder.</note> well / do this two or three times / afterwards <term>wash</term> <note>original: *abluier*; to rinse or wash away soluble components.</note> the salt away with hot water / so you find the fine red lead at the bottom / the finer / the better / Take at least four Loth of this same red lead / three Loth of <term>sublimated mercury</term> <note>original: *Mercurium sublimatum*; a purified form of mercury, often corrosive sublimate.</note> / two Loth of extracted <term>Sal Ammoniac</term> <note>original: *Salarmoniac*; ammonium chloride, used as a flux in refining metals.</note> / which must have been <term>sublimated</term> <note>a purification process where a solid is heated into vapor and then condensed back into solid form.</note> again with salt and iron filings. Grind these pieces finely together / put them into a flask <note>original: *Kolben*; a round-bottomed or long-necked glass vessel used for boiling or distilling.</note>

<header>An Augmentation with Mercury and Saturn [Lead].</header>

In a retort flask, pour a strong <term>parting water</term> <note>original: *Scheydwasser*; nitric acid, used to separate metals</note> so that it covers it considerably; draw it off through a helm by way of a <term>Bain-Marie</term> <note>original: *Bal. Mariæ*; a gentle water bath for heating</note> until it reaches an <term>oily consistency</term>. Pour the parting water back onto it and draw it off again to an oily state; do this a third time. Afterward, pour a good <term>spirit of wine</term> <note>original: *Spiritum vini*; high-proof alcohol or ethanol</note> onto it, in which one lot of <term>sal ammoniac</term> <note>original: *Salarmoniac*; ammonium chloride, a common alchemical flux</note> has been dissolved and stood overnight. Draw off the spirit of wine by way of the <term>Bain-Marie</term> until nothing more comes over; pour it back on and draw it off again, doing this a third time with the great heat of the <term>Bain-Marie</term>, so that the entire substance rises over into the <term>receiver</term> <note>original: *Fürlag*; the flask that collects the distilled liquid</note>. This may also be <term>putrefied</term> <note>allowed to sit and decompose or break down</note> for eight or fourteen days before the distillation, and then distilled over. Once it has come over, pour the distilled material back and distil it once more so that everything rises; in this way, the entire material has entered into the four elements, and it is called the "hellish <term>Borras-water</term>," which turns <term>Saturn</term> <note>alchemical symbol for lead (♄)</note> into a <term>viscous substance</term>.

Now take thinly beaten <term>lead</term> [♄]; put this into a retort flask and pour the previously mentioned <term>Borras-water</term> over it so that it is well covered. Place it in a warm ash bath, well-sealed at the top, and let it stand for four hours; thus the <term>Borras-water</term> converts the <term>lead</term> [♄] into a very volatile <term>viscous calx</term> <note>a "calx" is a powdery metallic oxide produced by heating</note>. Afterward, pour the parting water off gently, wash the calx until it is "sweet" <note>rinsed of all acidic or salty traces</note>, and if you wish, you can make a living <term>mercury</term> [☿] out of it. Rub this with a proper <term>oil of tartar</term> <note>original: *Weinsteinöl*; a concentrated solution of potassium carbonate</note> on a stone, and it will run; it has no "feet" <note>an alchemical metaphor meaning it becomes fluid and mobile</note>.

### Augmentation.

Take common <term>red lead</term> <note>original: *Menig*; minium</note> and beat <term>Hungarian gold</term> <note>original: *Ungerisch ☉*; gold from Hungarian mines was prized for its purity</note> thin; place them <term>layer upon layer</term> <note>original: *stratum super stratum*</note> with the <term>red lead</term> in a <term>crucible</term>. Place it in a <term>coal fire</term> so that the smoke of the <term>red lead</term> <term>calcinates</term> the gold.

Take one part of this gold and three parts (or even more) of the <term>viscous lead</term>; grind everything fine together and put it all at once into a retort flask. Seal it with the <term>Seal of Hermes</term> <note>original: *Sigillo Hermetis*; an airtight, hermetic seal, often made by melting the glass neck of the flask</note> or otherwise, and place it in a sand bath. Regulate the fire according to philosophical practice for four weeks, so that the colors pass; finally, it will become grayish, yellowish, and brown. Then take it and add half a part more of the <term>viscous lead</term>; work it as before, and several colors will show themselves. Do this for 24 days, and it will become <term>fixed</term> <note>stable under heat, no longer volatile</note>. If you add more of the <term>viscosity</term>, proceed as before.

Take half of this and reduce it with a quick <term>flux</term>; then you will have a gold as high as has ever been seen. Add more <term>viscous lead</term> than you took away and proceed always for 16 days and nights, and it will already be fixed. Thus you have a <term>fixation which shall always endure and remain</term> <note>original: *figierung quæ semper durabit & manebit*</note>. If you understand the <term>Borras-water</term>, you have the <term>Tincture</term> <note>the legendary substance capable of transmuting metals</note> at hand.

## To Fix Mercury into a Precipitate.

Take an <term>oil of vitriol</term> <note>original: *Vitriolöll*; concentrated sulfuric acid</note>; <term>calcine</term> <note>heat a substance until it oxidizes or becomes a powder</note> mercury within it; leave it in <term>digestion</term> <note>gentle, steady heating</note> for 24 hours; then pour the <term>fixing water</term> <note>original: *aquam fixatiuum*</note> into it, and let it stand in digestion for nine days and nights; draw the water off from it <note>by distillation</note>, and you will have it.

### How the Fixing Water is Prepared.

Take three pounds of rectified <term>spirit of wine</term> <note>original: *Spiritus vini*; high-proof alcohol</note>, one pound of <term>vitriol</term> <note>original: *Vitrioli*; iron or copper sulfate</note>, and one pound of <term>saltpeter</term> <note>potassium nitrate</note>. Drive the spirits from the <term>aqua fortis</term> <note>original: *aquafort*; nitric acid</note> into the aforementioned <term>aqua vitae</term> <note>original: *aqua vitæ*; "water of life," a concentrated alcohol</note>, and let it stand for eight days and nights. Then add half a pound of <term>oil of tartar</term> <note>original: *Weinsteinöll*; a solution of potassium carbonate</note> and leave it again for eight days and nights in digestion. Afterward, draw the <term>aqua vitae</term> off from it; you will find a white earth at the bottom. This is the "fire of the <term>philosophers</term>" <note>original: *Feuer der philosophorum*</note>, for the fire generates spirit and soul. Put this earth into the drawn-off <term>aqua vitae</term>, and it will immediately <term>dissolve</term> <note>original: *soluieren*</note>; it is then called a "fixing water."

### Another Correct and True Fixation of Saturnine Mercury.

Take eight <term>loth</term> <note>a unit of weight, roughly 14.6 grams or half an ounce</note> of <term>mercury of Saturn</term> <note>original: *Mercurij Saturni*; mercury combined with lead</note>; let it become well-warmed in a <term>crucible</term> <note>original: *Digel*</note>; add two loth of thin, beaten gold; make an <term>amalgam</term>. Take four loth of sulfur; let it melt. When it flows, pour it over the aforementioned amalgam and stir it constantly with a piece of wood, and it will become a black stone. Grind this small, put it into a <term>vial glass</term> <note>original: *Violglaß*</note>, and seal it with the <term>Seal of Hermes</term> <note>original: *Sigillo Hermetis*; an airtight glass seal made by melting the neck of a flask</note>. Coat the glass well with <term>lute</term> <note>original: *Leym*; a protective clay-based paste</note> and place it in a <term>sand bath</term> <note>original: *Sandtcapell*; a container of sand heated to provide even temperature</note> upside down. After four weeks, take it out, and you will find a brownish-red powder. Afterward, <term>fix</term> it in the water described below.

Take <term>orpiment</term> <note>original: *Auripigmentum*; arsenic trisulfide, used for its yellow color</note> and <term>sal ammoniac</term> <note>ammonium chloride</note>, eight loth of each; <term>saltpeter</term> and <term>alum</term>, 12 loth of each; and four loth of <term>cinnabar</term> <note>original: *Zinober*; mercury sulfide</note>. Mix all of these well together and make a <term>parting water</term> <note>original: *Scheydwasser*; nitric acid used for separating metals</note> as is the custom. Afterward, take the fixed mercury with the gold—or the stone ground small—put it into a luted <term>flask</term> <note>original: *Kolbenglaß*</note>, and pour the aforementioned water upon it. Set it on gentle heat for a day and a night. Then draw the water off; do this three times, pouring it on and off. Finally, with a strong fire, drive off the spirits. Let it cool, grind it to powder, and let it melt into <term>Luna</term> <note>the alchemical name for silver</note>. While it is in flux, carry it quickly into the following flux, and quickly into a yellow <term>Saturnine glass</term> <note>original: *Saturnumglaß*; lead glass</note>. Leave it there in flux for eight hours; then separate it, and you have the Truth.

### How the Yellow Lead Glass is Made.

Take two loth of <term>minium</term> <note>original: *Menig*; red lead</note> and half a loth of white <term>pebble stone</term> <note>original: *Kißlingstein*; quartz or flint</note>; grind them well together. Let it melt well in a <term>wind furnace</term> <note>original: *Windtofen*; a furnace designed to create a strong draft for high heat</note> and pour it out; then you have the glass to be used for the work.

# Testament of Theophrastus Paracelsus.

In this, distill that which you know well, and through the manual skill of an experienced artist.

->P R A C T I C E.<-

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Take 1 part of the Liquor <note>original: "Liquoris"</note> | |
| 1 part of the Living Sun <note>original: "Solis viui", likely referring to a purified solar essence or mercury of gold</note> | **Parts.** |
| 1/2 part of the Red Lion <note>a traditional alchemical term for the red mineral form of mercury or antimony</note> | |

Coagulate them together over four alchemical days, and you will find the mass to be like a hyacinth <note>original: "Jacinth", a reddish-orange gemstone</note>. One part of this added to 100 parts becomes a powder; then cast one part of that onto 300. It tints it into good, lasting Gold and Silver <note>original: "Luna", literally Moon</note>, according to the fermentation of Solar Mercury <note>original: "Mercurij Solis"</note>. The coagulation should take place in a glass vessel marked with Number 2, and let it have its air.

Make your Lion <note>original: "Leonem"</note> out of Mars <note>the metal iron</note> along with his sister Venus <note>the metal copper</note>.

Let your projection <note>the act of casting the alchemical powder onto molten base metal to transform it</note> happen when it is in a strong flow, in an infernal flow, in the earth.

->Regarding the first Water of Venus.<-

Purify your water to the highest degree with its own body of Venus <note>copper</note>, and dissolve Venus out of Mars. Putrefy <note>a process of controlled decay or fermentation in a sealed vessel</note> it for 40 days, then separate the elements. Keep the fire for one part. Prepare the black <term>dead head<note>original: "capitis mortui", the solid residue left over after distillation</note></term> in the reverberatory furnace <note>original: "Reuerber", a furnace that reflects heat onto the substance</note>: at the first degree it becomes white, at the second yellow, at the third red or brown-colored. Dissolve it in its prescribed water and putrefy it for its allotted time until you see the sign. Separate its tinctures <note>the concentrated essences or colors</note> from one another. This redness is that which artists have never even thought of, nor understood—it comes from the earth of the unquenchable fire.

->Practice.<-

Take two parts of the first elemental fire, and one part of the Red Lime of the Sun <note>original: "Kalch Solis rot", a powdered oxide of gold</note>. Alkalize them together through putrefaction for forty days. The fermentation of gold is as follows:

Dissolve gold in its water; let it evaporate until it reaches an oily consistency <note>original: "Olitet"</note>. Then pour fresh water on and off five times. Set it to putrefy for its time until you see the start of its tincture <note>coloring essence</note>; the bottom part is white. Reduce it into a body. You shall grade this Tincture of the Sun <note>original: "Tincturam Solis"</note> beyond 24 or 28, up to 34 degrees.

Take half a part of this Red Lion and three times as much of its sister Sulfur <note>original: "Sulphuris"</note>—that is, the unquenchable fire of Mercury—and coagulate it in its Lion, in its glass vessel marked with Number 3.

->N O T E.<-

When these Tinctures of Venus and Mars are prepared, take one part to one hundred parts of the <term>first matter<note>original: "primæ materiæ", the original, undifferentiated substance from which all things are made</note></term>. Let it strongly produce its open body on the earth in an instant, according to the Kabbalistic <note>original: "Cabalischen"</note> custom. Thus it coagulates itself into a brown-colored powder. One part of this powder added to 300 parts of the body of Venus <note>copper</note> tints it into good gold.

# Testament of Theophrastus Paracelsus.

Take the body of Jupiter <note>original: "corpus Iouis", referring to the metal tin</note>; distill its own water, dissolved and resolved into the fire, until its tincture is brought forth. When it is fermented with the Sulfur of the Sun <note>original: "Sulphur Solis", the essential essence of gold</note>, apply this prepared tincture back onto its own body while it stands in a strong and most powerful hellish fire <note>original: "hellischen Feuer", referring to the highest heat of a furnace</note> upon the earth. Observe its weight as follows—understand its own first matter <note>original: "primam materiam"</note>—so that it flows without fire. This is Jupiter made alive again in the resurrection or the new birth, unto eternal life; this is truly the Sun and the Moon <note>gold and silver</note>, which withstands all examinations in the cupellation <note>the process of refining gold or silver</note>.

### The Practice.

Take the body of Jupiter, calcine it <note>reduce it to powder through heat</note>, and reverberate it until it becomes a subtle alkali <note>original: "Alculi", a salt-like residue</note>. Dissolve it in its own water, putrefy it for a philosophical month <note>traditionally 40 days of controlled decay in a sealed vessel</note>, and separate the elements. The element of fire is gold-colored; rectify it through its similar retorts. Take one part of this fire of Jupiter, half a part of the Sulfur of the Sun, and its own living water of Mercury <note>original: "aquam viuam Mercurij"</note>, three times as much by weight as the others. Coagulate all of this by weight together into a stone in a glass vessel marked Number 3. One part of the prepared Tincture of Jupiter added to 100 parts of <term>Mercury ☿</term> and <term>Jupiter ♃</term> will become a yellow precipitate. One part of this precipitate added to 300 parts of the body of Jupiter tints it into good <term>Gold ☉</term>; however, if it is light in weight, restore it with its own Gold.

### Upon the Saturn of Venus.

Command and bid Saturn <note>the metal lead</note> that he becomes a Venus <note>the metal copper</note>. Make this Venus into a vitriol <note>a sulfate or acidic essence</note>; dissolve this vitriol into an oil.

Take Saturn, calcine him, then dissolve him in a water of alum. Bring it to an oily state <note>original: "Olitet"</note> and keep one part of it. Take a good yellow sulfur made from copper ore <note>original: "Venus Ertz"</note>; sublime it several times with calcined vitriol so that it purifies itself well and gives—or becomes—beautiful white flowers <note>original: "Flores", the powdery substance produced by sublimation</note>.

Reverberate these to a red-brown color, dissolve them with vinegar, then resolve them into oil. Separate the vinegar from it and keep the oil.

### Composition.

After the separation of the elements and the fire itself, take the dissolved oil of <term>Saturn ♄</term> and rectify it to the highest degree. In one part of this oil of the Fire of Saturn, add half a part of the oil of vitriol (previously also made from the vitriol of Saturn), a third part of the sulfur of gold <note>original: "Sulphur auri"</note>, and a third part (or three times as much) of its own mercurial water. Coagulate these into a stone. One part of this added to 100 parts of the Venus of <term>Saturn ♄</term> becomes a red precipitate; one part of that added to 300 parts of the body of <term>Saturn ♄</term> becomes good <term>Gold ☉</term>.

Coagulate this in a glass marked with Number 3 or 4. This coagulation is completed in 40 alchemical days, and then the stone is ruby-colored <note>original: "Robinfarb"</note>.

->E N D.<-

->Thus far the Paracelsian writings.<-

# The Spiritual Sun
->from<-
# the Book of Carneson by Bartholomeus Korndorffer.
<note>Bartholomeus Korndorffer was a 16th-century alchemist and physician whose works were often circulated in manuscript alongside Paracelsian texts.</note>

### Tincture with Venus, Mars, and Mercury.
<note>In the symbolic language of alchemy, Venus represents copper, Mars represents iron or steel, and Mercury represents the metal or the "spirit" of quicksilver.</note>

<image-desc>A large ornamental initial 'N' decorated with intricate scrolling foliage and floral patterns within a square border.</image-desc>

Take eight *Loth* <note>A *Loth* is a historical unit of weight, approximately 15 to 16 grams or half an ounce.</note> of the best Hüttenberg steel <note>Steel from Hüttenberg in Carinthia, Austria, was highly prized for its quality and manganese content.</note> and dissolve it in oil of vitriol <note>original: "Vitriolöl," which is sulfuric acid.</note>. When it will no longer dissolve, pour in some common water. When everything has dissolved, filter it through paper and let it evaporate until it reaches an oily consistency. Place it in a cold spot so that beautiful crystals form; these are quite sweet; save them. Let the remaining liquid evaporate further until it is oily, and repeat the process until no more crystals form. Collect them all together, eight *Loth* in total, and keep them.

Secondly, take half a pound of <term>Antimony</term> <note>Specifically stibnite or antimony sulfide.</note> and half a pound of <term>mercury sublimate</term> <note>original: "Mercuri sublimatum," known today as mercuric chloride.</note>. Grind these two substances together as finely as possible and distill the oil from them using a retort. Finally, apply a strong fire, and it will sublimate in the retort into a cinnabar <note>original: "Zinober." In this specific process, this refers to the formation of "cinnabar of antimony."</note>; keep this separately. A powder will remain at the bottom; grind this small again and add as much mercury sublimate as before, repeating until you have distilled and sublimated the entire substance of the antimony. During the distillation, a "living" <term>Mercury</term> <note>Liquid metallic quicksilver.</note> will also pass over; separate it from the oil. Put the oil back into a retort together with the living Mercury and distill it on its own. Note: when it almost stops flowing, then cease the distillation; otherwise the Mercury will rise back over into the oil, which should not happen. Do this until it is all united.
