# The Spiritual Sun / by Bartholomeus Korndorffer.

Take four *Loth* <note>A historical unit of weight, roughly equivalent to half an ounce or 15 grams.</note> of mercury sublimate <note>original: "Mercurij sublimatum," or mercuric chloride, a highly toxic white crystalline powder.</note> and pour a strong nitric acid <term>Aquafort <note>original: "Aquafort" (aqua fortis), literally "strong water," the historical name for nitric acid.</note></term> over it so that it rises a hand’s breadth above it. Always distill off half of the water over gentle heat in an ash bath <note>A container filled with ashes used to distribute heat evenly around a glass vessel.</note>. Pour it back on, and distill it off again. Do this four times, pouring on and drawing off; the final time, use strong heat so that all the "volatile gold" <note>The alchemist likely refers to the yellow-colored distillate resulting from the reaction of mercury and acid.</note> rises over along with the water.

When it has all risen over, distill it very gently in a water bath <term>Balneo Mariæ <note>literally "Mary's Bath," a double boiler used for consistent, gentle heating.</note></term> for a short while until the watery parts <term>Phlegma <note>In alchemy, the "phlegm" is the tasteless, watery, or inactive part of a distilled liquid.</note></term> are removed; thus is the oil of the Spiritual Sun prepared.

Take four *Loth* of Armenian clay <term>Bolus Armeni <note>A red, iron-rich earth traditionally used in alchemical seals and as a flux.</note></term> and six *Loth* of common salt; grind them together finely. Take eight *Loth* of fine silver and place the powder in a crucible <note>A heat-resistant container for melting metals.</note> with the silver in the middle. Seal the crucible with lute <note>original: "perlutier," meaning to seal the vessel with a clay paste to make it airtight.</note>. The silver must lie entirely within the substance. Let it flow strongly for two hours in a wind furnace <term>Windofen <note>A furnace designed to create a natural draft through a chimney to reach higher temperatures.</note></term>. Afterward, take it out and let it melt by itself in a crucible; add a little borax <term>Borras <note>A flux used to help metals melt and to remove impurities.</note></term>. Pour it out and beat it into thin rolls. Place these in a glass vial so they do not lie upon one another. Pour the Spiritual Sun over them and seal the glass. Set it in gentle warmth, just as the sun shines, for sixteen days. Then the silver will become entirely black-brown and will be graded <term>gradieren <note>The process of increasing the purity, color, or "grade" of a metal.</note></term> through and through into gold of the best and highest degree. Afterward, pour off the "hellish water" <note>original: "hellisch Wasser," likely referring to the potent, corrosive acidic oil.</note> so that you spill nothing. Wash the silver that has become gold several times with clean water. Melt it together with an equal weight of common gold; thus you have the best and most excellent gold, highly graded in weight <term>pondus <note>Latin for weight or heaviness.</note></term>; in its coloration <term>Coloriz <note>Refers to the depth and quality of the gold's color.</note></term>, it will withstand all tests.

When you notice that the nitric acid from the Spiritual Sun has evaporated and it appears somewhat dry, always moisten it with six *Loth* of strong nitric acid and add five *Loth* of purified silver. Let it stand for sixteen days. You can do this again and again, for it does not lose its strength. Bartholomeus Korndorffer.

### A true and just process / or, the bringing of four ounces <term>Loth <note>A German unit of weight, roughly 14–16 grams.</note></term> of **Gold** <term>☉</term> into the **Mark** <note>A unit of weight for precious metals, approximately 8 ounces.</note> of **Silver** <term>☾</term> / as I myself (says Korndorffer) have seen.

Now take one ounce <term>Loth</term> of the first prepared Redness of Antimony, two ounces of the prepared Blade Dross, and one ounce of **red arsenic**. ## Following is the Process with Gold.

This is the true Philosophical fixation upon leaden <term>Viscosa <note>a "viscous" or sticky intermediate substance</note></term> which common laboratory workers call Mercury of Lead <note>original: ☿ ♄</note>; and it is to be known that Gold <note>original: ☉</note> does not allow itself to be mastered into a *Viscosa* as easily as Silver <note>original: Luna</note>.

Afterward, draw off the *Aqua regis* until dry. This Gold <term>☉ <note>Gold</note></term>, whether it has remained in a physical body <note>original: "corporaliter"</note> or has become a powder, amalgamate it with the six <term>Loths <note>A historical unit of weight, roughly 15 grams or half an ounce.</note></term> of the two viscous substances <note>original: "Viscosis"</note>. ## Note this.

When you have six Loths of the fire-resistant viscous substance made at the beginning, you can add six Loths of raw viscous substance or leaden Mercury <term>☿ ♄</term> for every one Loth [of the fixed matter]. # Another fixation upon Moon <term>☾ <note>Silver</note></term> with the Viscous Substance
## derived from Saturn <term>♄ <note>Lead</note></term> or Mercury <term>☿ <note>Quicksilver</note></term>.

Take two <term>Loths <note>A historical unit of weight, approximately 15 grams.</note></term> of fine silver <term>☾</term>; beat it very thin, and sulfurize it with sulfur <term>stratum super stratum <note>Latin: "layer upon layer." A technique where alternating layers of metal and sulfur are placed in a crucible.</note></term>, judged by eye in a crucible. Do this three times, so that the sulfur penetrates it well; then grind it small, and add one Loth of <term>Salmiax <note>Sal ammoniac (ammonium chloride), used as a flux to help metals volatilize or "rise."</note></term> beneath it. Put it in a flask, and pour upon it four Loths of unique <term>Jafaron <note>Likely "Saffron," referring to a metallic oxide or a specific chemical oil used as a solvent.</note></term> until it sizzles a little. Distill it <term>per latus <note>Latin: "through the side," using a retort or a side-neck flask.</note></term> out of the sand bath into another flask until it reaches an oily consistency. Pour the water back upon it and draw it off as before; do this three times, so that the Silver <term>☾</term> rises over through the side. Afterward, draw the water gently from the material in the receiver until it is dry. Then coat the glass with <term>lute <note>A protective clay-based sealant.</note></term> and drive it strongly with coal fire; thus the body of the silver <term>☾</term> rises up with the sal ammoniac. Scrape it off into a glass dish and pour warm water over it so that the sal ammoniac dissolves away; then the <term>viscosa <note>The "viscous substance"—a thickened, metallic oil or resin-like state of the metal.</note></term> falls to the bottom; dry this.

->An alchemical symbol consisting of three horizontal bars crossed by two vertical bars, resembling a grid or grate.<-

Recipe: Take 8 Loths of the viscous substance made from Lead <term>♄</term>, which the vagabonds <note>A derogatory term for traveling, self-taught, or fraudulent alchemists.</note> call Mercury of Saturn <term>☿ ♄</term>, which is merely quickened and yet spiritual; it must not be fluid. Place it in an earthenware <term>sublimatorium <note>A vessel designed for sublimation, where solids are heated to become vapor and then re-solidify at the top.</note></term> upon a pound [containing] 5 Loths of <term>Spongrün <note>Verdigris or "Spanish Green," a copper acetate.</note></term> at the bottom <note>original: "in fundo"</note>, and on top of that, a finger's breadth of <term>Eysensinther <note>Iron dross or forge scales, likely used for its iron oxide content.</note></term> that has been washed clean. It will rise up as a white powder; scrape this off. Take 7 Loths of this and 1 Loth of the Silver <term>☾</term> viscous substance; grind them both together until they have become one thing.

->An alchemical symbol consisting of three horizontal bars crossed by two vertical bars.<-

Now take 4 Loths of fresh viscous Lead <term>♄</term> or Mercury <term>☿</term> that has been previously quickened, cleanly washed <note>original: "abluiert"</note>, or boiled in fresh vinegar. Make an <term>amalgama <note>A mixture of mercury with another metal.</note></term> with three <term>quintle <note>A small weight, about 3.7 grams.</note></term> of fine silver <term>☾</term>. Grind into it one Loth of the two previously ground viscous substances of the Moon [Silver]. Put it all together in a flat glass, sealed with lute at the top. Place it in the sand bath with a low fire for eight days and nights so that nothing rises from it. Afterward, for eight days and nights with a strong fire, and for a third eight days even stronger; thus it will all become fixed and fire-resistant. Of this, take 4 Loths; add to it again as before 4 Loths of fresh Mercury of Saturn <term>☿ ♄</term>. Let it fix slowly for eight days, and then strengthen it with fire for 12 days; thus the 4 Loths are fixed once more. In this way, every 20 days and nights, add four Loths of fresh Mercury of Saturn <term>☿ ♄</term>. When you have taken out the four Loths you previously fixed, you will have an eternal fixation. Do not attempt more than four Loths at once; Nature will not endure it.

## A short way to make the two Viscous Substances <term>Viscosa <note>Refers to thick, oily, or "sticky" alchemical extracts believed to hold the essential soul of a metal.</note></term> out of Moon <term>☾ <note>Silver</note></term> and Saturn <term>♄ <note>Lead</note></term>, which one otherwise must make from each individually.

Take two <term>Loths <note>A historical unit of weight, about 15 grams.</note></term> of fine silver <term>☾</term> and 4 Loths of common lead <term>♄</term>; melt these two metals together and sublimate them four times, for four hours each; layer them <term>stratificiers <note>The process of "stratification," placing materials in alternating layers.</note></term> in a crucible with pure, common sulfur. Afterward, grind the metals small and put them into a flask <term>Kolbenglaß</term>; add one and a half Loths of sal ammoniac <term>Salmiar</term> to it. Pour four Loths of <term>Jassoron <note>Likely "Saffron" (Crocus), referring to a metallic oxide or an alchemical oil used as a solvent.</note></term> upon it. Distill it "through the side" <term>per latus <note>Using a retort or side-neck flask to draw off vapors laterally.</note></term> out of the sand bath; four times take this material into the receiver <term>Fürlegglaß</term> and draw the water off gently. Afterward, coat the glass with <term>lute <note>A protective clay sealant.</note></term> and drive it strongly with a coal fire. Thus, the viscous substances <term>Viscosma</term> rise upward. Scrape them off again, as described above, and wash them <term>abluiers <note>From the Latin "abluere," to wash or rinse.</note></term> with warm water, then dry them again; thus they are ready. Amen.

# How One Should Clarify the Seven Metals.

If you intended to take up metals with all kinds of filth <note>original: "Sudelwerck," referring to impurities or base, poorly-prepared materials</note> and try to make them into a perfect metal (as you call it), such as Gold <term>☉ <note>The Sun/Gold</note></term> and Silver <term>☾ <note>The Moon/Silver</note></term>—which are actually imperfect in themselves—yet make them good and stable in all tests: you will not achieve this with all your art in this case. You have not investigated the possibilities of nature within the metals. You and your crowd always work with the impossible, whereby one deceives the other, often costing life, honor, and property, and the true secret art is suppressed and brought to shame. In short, our alchemists want to make Gold <term>☉</term> and Silver <term>☾</term> out of unclarified metals, and afterwards they find nothing but filth and dung. Since this my hidden art is so important to you, as you report—nearly losing your mind with many thoughts over it—and since you would gladly have the foundation of this truth, and are also destined for it by the influence of the Almighty's grace: So I send you not only the right foundation from which you proceeded, the Mercury of Saturn <term>☿ ℏ <note>Mercury of Lead</note></term>, but all seven metals by a short way, to precipitate and to <term>tinge <note>From "tingirn," meaning to transform or "dye" a substance into another state, usually into gold or silver.</note></term> one into the other, with which everything is to be established. If you now know the right foundation to dissolve and clarify all metallic bodies and bring them into a **running dry water**, <note>An alchemical term for a liquid that does not wet the hands, often a metaphor for a purified solvent or a specific state of mercury.</note> you will bring this to an end, which I have explained to you according to my practice.

Although some vagabonds <note>original: "Landstreicher," a disparaging term for fraudulent traveling alchemists</note> forcibly bring some metals into their running water, and with many absurd corrosive substances (which are more harmful to the metals, whereby they lose their best power), yet this is not the way which belongs to my *precipitated practice* <note>original Latin: "Practicam præcipitatem"</note> of the metals. Rather, you, as a faithful follower of this art, will undoubtedly also encounter my short way for the *restoration of metals* <note>original Latin: "restaurationem metallorum"</note> in the meantime. This foundation, of which our ancient Egyptians wrote, I did not wish to hide from you, in a secret and trusted opinion (which you should keep hidden from all the godless). I commend myself to your prayers. Given in the 37th year. <note>Likely 1537, a period during which Paracelsus was active.</note>

# How One Should Clarify the Seven Metals.

->centered text<- ☉ <note>The Sun / Gold</note>

The second metal, Gold <term>☉</term>, precipitated with its corresponding clarified body; one part of this precipitate cast upon eight parts of Mercury <term>☿</term>, Saturn <term>♄ <note>Lead</note></term>, or Luna <term>☽ <note>Silver</note></term>, tinges <note>original: "thingiert," meaning to transmute or color a base substance into a noble one</note> into the best Gold <term>☉</term>.

->centered text<- ☽ <note>The Moon / Silver</note>

Luna <term>☽</term>, the third metal; this clarified body precipitated with a clarified metal, tinges one part of purged Venus <term>♀ <note>Copper</note></term> in the flow into the best Luna <term>☽</term>, as well as Mercury <term>☿</term> and Saturn <term>♄</term>.

->centered text<- ♂ <note>Mars / Iron</note>

Mars <term>♂</term>, the fourth metal, precipitated with its corresponding clarified metal; when this precipitate is finely prepared, it gives three <term>Loth <note>A traditional German unit of weight, approximately 15-16 grams or half an ounce.</note></term> of Gold <term>☉</term> into one <term>mark <note>A weight unit, usually equal to 8 ounces or 16 Loth.</note></term> of Luna <term>☽</term>.

->centered text<- ♀ <note>Venus / Copper</note>

Venus <term>♀</term>, the fifth metal; this clarified body, precipitated with another clarified metal, tinges three parts in one mark of fine Luna <term>☽</term> into Gold <term>☉</term>.

->centered text<- ♃ <note>Jupiter / Tin</note>

Jupiter <term>♃</term>, the sixth metal; this clarified corpus <note>body</note> precipitated with its corresponding sublimated metal. This precipitate tinges one part to four parts; it purges Jupiter <term>♃</term> into Luna <term>☽</term> and precipitates Mercury <term>☿</term> again <term>per se <note>by itself</note></term>.

->centered text<- ☿ <note>Mercury / Quicksilver</note>

The seventh metal, Mercury <term>☿</term>, with its four bodies and essences—elements drawn from the bodies of the metals—fixed and precipitated. One part of this precipitate cast upon two parts of molten Luna <term>☽</term> remains as Gold <term>☉</term>.

## Explanations of the Aforementioned Precipitates.

Take three Loth of Mercury of Saturn <term>☿ ♄ <note>Mercury derived from Lead</note></term> and one Loth of Mercury of Gold <term>☿ ☉</term>; to this add an <term>Orth <note>A small weight unit, typically a quarter of a Loth.</note></term> of a Guilder's worth of pure gold calx <note>original: "Goldkalch," gold reduced to a fine powder through heating or chemical action</note> for a ferment or seed. For whatever seed you see in the ashes <note>Referring to the ash-bath used to provide gentle, even heat to the vessel</note>, that you shall have. Precipitate this according to custom in a vial until it turns into a fixed precipitate; then add again as much Mercury of Saturn <term>☿ ♄</term> as the precipitate weighs. However, always take a little gold calx first and precipitate it again into a fixed precipitate. You may augment <note>Increase the quantity or potency</note> this as often as you wish. But it tinges no more than the sixth part into Gold; if, however, this precipitate is again pressed into the Mercury of Gold <term>☿ ☉</term> and precipitated, it tinges 30 parts into Gold <term>☉</term>.

### in which fine silver is graduated into good gold in four hours.
### A True Process.

How one should distill and prepare a truly excellent and strong Graduating Water <term>Gradierwasser <note>In alchemy, a "graduating water" was a solution used to "improve" or "graduate" a metal—specifically to turn silver into gold or to increase the purity and color of gold.</note></term> according to chemical usage, which graduates silver into the best gold without loss <note>original: "ohn raub," literally "without robbery," meaning no mass is lost in the process</note>, and creates great, unspeakable profit through which many thousands of <term>marks <note>A traditional weight unit, usually equal to 8 ounces.</note></term> of gold can be obtained. Furthermore, such gold does not lose its grade in the manner of gold during the cupellation of <term>Saturn <note>Lead. Do not forget the poor; let this be dear to you, for this was the piece that brought me joy; no such truth is to be found in all other graduating waters. This graduating water is also to be used without ceasing, as follows hereafter.

Take four <term>Loth <note>A German unit of weight, approximately 15-16 grams.</note></term> of Hungarian gold, which has no additives; beat it thin, and take two Loth of <term>Cinnabar <note>Mercury sulfide, a bright red mineral used often in alchemy as a source for both mercury and sulfur.</note></term>; grind it into a fine powder and arrange it layer upon layer <note>Latin: "stratum super stratum"</note> in a cementing crucible. Afterward, take it and put it into a glass flask and pour a strong <term>Aqua Regia <note>Latin for "Royal Water," a mixture of acids (typically nitric and hydrochloric) capable of dissolving gold.</note></term> over it, about eight Loth. The distillation should happen very slowly, as the gold then putrefies <note>decomposes or breaks down into its primary components</note> all the better. Afterward, take the dry residue that remains behind, which will be like a paste; pour a very sharp distilled wine vinegar over it, so that it stands quite high above it. Let it remain covered—

# Process of a Secret Graduating Water.

...although it is a short way to dissolve the Sun <note>original: "☉" refers to Gold</note> into a viscous state <note>original: "ad viscosam"</note>, it should not be revealed to loose or haughty people.

And there follows a "Parasolon" <note>likely referring to a "shield" or a protective supplementary instruction</note>, which is a technique by which the Gold is brought into a viscous state. Take three <term>Loth <note>A historical unit of weight, roughly 14.5 grams.</note></term> of gold and laminate it thinly. Combine it with three <term>Quintlin <note>A small weight, roughly 4 grams.</note></term> of Red Albacheton <note>original: "Albacheton Rubei," which the text identifies as cinnabar or vermilion</note> in a cementing box. Afterward, rub in three Loth of "volatile phantoms" <note>original: "volucum fantaslon," which the text identifies as <term>sublimated mercury <note>represented by the symbol ☿; mercury that has been purified through heating</note></term></note> to act as a "key." Then the bath will become viscous; take this along with the risen sublimated mercury and grind it all together. Place it in a flask and pour a strong "Jasoren" <note>likely a strong mineral acid, such as Aqua Fortis</note> over it until it is a finger's breadth deep. Heat it in the sand until it reaches a state of oiliness <note>original: "Olitet"</note>, and for a third time heat it strongly until a precipitate remains. Take this precipitate and grind it fine. Place it in a glass. Take three well-weighed Loth of the following flux and dissolve it in half a <term>Maß <note>A historical liquid measure, approximately 1 to 1.5 liters.</note></term> of vinegar. Pour all of this onto the precipitate and let it boil down gently until it is completely dry, stirring it constantly. Then take the precipitate and three Loth of fine silver that has been purified with <term>white sulfur <note>original: "Sulphur album"</note></term> and finely granulated. Thus you will find the fine silver has been transformed into gold of Rhenish standard. Praise be to God alone, Amen.

->The Flux.<-

Take four Loth of Poloton <note>A specific alchemical substance, often a refined salt</note> <image-desc>alchemical symbol consisting of an X-shape with small circles at each terminal point and a horizontal bar crossing the center</image-desc>, six Loth of <term>Calamine <note>original: "Galmey," a zinc ore</note></term>, and Rock Salt <note>original: "Salgeme"</note>. Mix these well together and grind them finely, along with Tartar <note>original: "Weinstein"</note>.

->The White Sulfur is made thus.<-

Take four Loth of Calamine and six Loth of Rock Salt; mix them well together. In summary, I tell you: wherever the Gold is viscosified and brought back to a physical body, there you will see a wonder. I say no more; my other processes and Graduating Waters will bear witness for me.

# Of Luna <note>original: "Luna" is the alchemical name for Silver</note>.

Take one <term>Mark <note>A historical unit of weight for precious metals, approximately 233 grams.</note></term> of fine silver; dissolve half of it in a <term>Jasoren <note>A strong mineral acid, likely Aqua Fortis (nitric acid), used to dissolve metals.</note></term>. Draw this off in a short glass flask until it reaches an oily consistency. Add one and a half <term>Loth <note>A unit of weight, roughly 14.5 grams.</note></term> of clean <term>Salmiac <note>Sal ammoniac or ammonium chloride, used as a flux or to make acids more potent.</note></term> to the Silver. It must all be gently distilled in hot ashes. Pour fresh Jasoren over it and draw the liquid off again to an oily state. Do this with fresh liquid a fourth time. The final time, apply strong heat so that the silver rises along with the spirit <note>The volatile part of the chemical mixture</note> over the helm <note>The cap or "head" of the distilling apparatus</note> and becomes "spiritual" <note>refined into a gaseous or volatile state</note>.

Now take four Loth of raw Silver; file it into very small pieces and place it in a <term>Simbelts flask <note>A specific type of alchemical glass vessel, often used for slow digestion or evaporation.</note></term>. Pour the "Silver Water" <note>the liquid prepared above</note> over it until it is slightly covered. Seal the glass at the top and set it in very gentle ashes. Thus it will gradually dry out over a day and a half. Then pour the same amount [of liquid] over it again; let it stand until it is completely dried out once more. Do this through evaporation until twenty-four days and nights have passed and everything finally remains dry. Then it is "fixed" <note>chemically stable and resistant to heat</note> and correct. Divide this into two parts and rub into it one part of freshly filed silver. Put it into the glass again and moisten it once more with the same Silver Water as before, spending twelve days and nights on this. Then it is fixed once more. Then add the third part to purified <term>Mercury <note>original: "Mercurij," represented by the symbol ☿</note></term> that has been purified through subtle iron scale <note>original: "Eysensinter," the flaky oxidation produced when iron is forged</note>. Moisten it once more with Silver Water, spending nine days and nights on this. Thus you have an everlasting "Augment" <note>A process or substance used to increase the quantity of a precious metal.</note>.

Whenever you take the three parts out to be reduced <note>melted back into solid metal</note>, always replace them with three parts of <term>mercury <note>☿</note></term> and moisten it with Silver Water as before, and it will always be completed in nine days.

# Tinctural Graduating Oil of the Black Eagle.

It matters little how one prepares the substance; for who would not believe that when a thing is <term>subtilized <note>Refined or broken down into its most potent, non-material essence.</note></term>, it shall penetrate better than when it remains in its earthy body? Although there is otherwise little to be hoped for in common <term>Particulars <note>Alchemical operations that work on specific metals rather than the "Universal" transformation of all matter.</note></term>, because the <term>Stemo <note>A variant of 'Stibium,' the Latin term for Antimony.</note></term> is subtilized, the work should not be neglected; for common Sulfur of Mercury and the <term>Bitruat <note>A variant spelling of Vitriol (metal sulfates).</note></term> have a great
->**sympathy with one another; mark this.**<-

### Thus make a Lye.

Take two pounds of willow-ash, beech, or other good wood-ash, and one pound of <term>quicklime <note>Calcium oxide, a caustic chemical used to make lye more reactive.</note></term>; pour over it half purified urine and half water; let it stand until it becomes sharp. Take three pounds of finely crushed <term>Stemo <note>Antimony.</note></term>; put it into a glazed vessel, pour the lye over it, and boil it for one hour until the lye becomes yellow. Then pour it off into a separate vessel and pour fresh lye onto the Antimony again; boil it in the same way and pour it off with the other. Continue boiling and pouring off until the lye no longer extracts anything. Then take the collected lye in a brass basin and take a clean brush, dip it into sharp vinegar, and sprinkle it onto the lye. Let it stand thus overnight, and the most beautiful redness will settle to the bottom. Carefully pour off the lye and dry the redness; keep this.

### Now make a Vitriol Oil from this extract.

Take five pounds of Vitriol and as much of the extracted redness as there is; crush them together. Put it into an earthen jar and burn off the <term>Phlegma <note>The watery, tasteless distillate that comes over first during heating.</note></term> through the <term>Helm <note>The top part of a still; an alembic.</note></term>. Then grind the <term>Caput Mortuum <note>original: "Todtenkopff" (dead head); the solid residue remaining after distillation.</note></term> fine, and <term>coagulate <note>The process of thickening a liquid or returning a distillate to its solid base through evaporation.</note></term> all the phlegma back into it until everything becomes dry. Into this, rub 24 <term>Loth <note>A historical unit of weight, approximately 14.5 grams.</note></term> of saltpeter; put it into a good jar that is not tall, set a helm upon it, well-sealed with <term>lute <note>original: "perlutiert"; sealed with an airtight clay or paste.</note></term>, and place a receiver in front. Burn it over a charcoal fire; first gently until the phlegma comes over, then take another receiver, seal it, and gradually strengthen the fire until the red drops fall. Then drive it very strongly until the spirits vanish; thus you have an oil of Vitriol; keep this for your needs.

### Now make an Aqua Regia for the dissolution of common Mercury [☿].

Take three Loth of raw Vitriol, 24 Loth of <term>Crocus Martis <note>Latin for "Saffron of Mars," a term for iron oxide or rust.</note></term> which has previously been eaten into rust with urine, and one pound of the <term>Black Eagle <note>A symbolic name for Antimony.</note></term> from which the redness was previously extracted. Crush everything together, put it into a jar, set a helm on top, and burn the phlegma into a recipient over a charcoal fire. Grind the <term>Caput Mortuum</term> fine and pour the phlegma onto it; coagulate it into a dry powder. After that, take saltpeter weighing as much as the residue, and well-dried salt weighing half as much as the residue. Put it back into a fresh jar, all well-sealed, with a receiver in front, and distill a strong <term>Aqua Regia <note>original: "Aquam Regis"; a powerful acid (literally "Royal Water") capable of dissolving noble metals.</note></term> from it.

# Tinctural Graduating Oil of the Black Eagle.

Take one pound of the water mentioned above in a glass vessel and dissolve 24 <term>loth <note>A German unit of weight, roughly half an ounce or 15–16 grams.</note></term> of common Mercury in it. Also dissolve 4 loth of Hungarian gold in eight loth of the water, and pour this into the 24 loth of Mercury. Distill this at first gently until it reaches an <term>oleosity <note>original: "Olitet"; refers to a thick, oily consistency.</note></term>, then precipitate it with a strong fire into a <term>precipitate <note>A solid substance that settles out of a liquid solution.</note></term>; grind this precipitate into a fine powder.

Take this precipitate in a glass flask that is flat on the bottom. Pour the previously made <term>vitriol oil <note>original: "Vitruatöls"; likely sulfuric acid or a related metallic sulfate solution.</note></term> over it so that it is well covered. Stir it well and <term>seal it <note>original: "perluttiert"; sealed with "lute," a clay or paste used to make vessels airtight.</note></term> at the top. Place it in sifted ashes and let it <term>coagulate <note>The process of a liquid thickening or becoming solid.</note></term> with gentle heat into a stone. Afterward, place it in a sand bath for three days and nights. On the first day, fire it so that you cannot bear to keep your hand in the sand; on the second day, make the fire twice as strong; on the last day, fire it until everything is glowing hot. Then let it cool, and you will find a red-brown stone. Grind this stone small and take as much of the **flux** (described below) as the precipitate weighs. Grind them together and put them into a crucible. Let it melt—at first gently, then strongly—in a <term>blast furnace <note>original: "Windtoffen"; a furnace that uses a bellows or natural draft to reach high temperatures.</note></term>. A <term>regulus <note>original: "König" (king); the metallic mass that settles at the bottom of a crucible during smelting.</note></term> will settle at the bottom. Refine this on a testing dish and a <term>cupel <note>original: "Capellen"; a shallow, porous bowl used in assaying to separate precious metals from lead.</note></term>. In this way, 18 loth of good Gold will remain for you from the Mercury at that very hour, which will remain stable through all tests. I say, however, that a short <term>fixation <note>The process of making a volatile substance stable under heat.</note></term> achieves nothing here.

->The Flux.<-

Take a half-quarter of raw <term>tartar <note>original: "Weinstein"; the sediment from wine casks used as a flux.</note></term>, a quarter of common salt, three-quarters of <term>litharge <note>original: "silberglett"; lead oxide, used to separate silver from other metals.</note></term>, and one loth of iron filings. Grind everything together into a fine powder. Boil it gently four times in urine, drying it each time; thus is the flux prepared.

->Process with Silver, which yields 10 loth of good Silver from the Mercury, of which the fourth part is Silver.<-

Take half a pound of running Mercury and put it into an iron pan. Take two <term>measures <note>original: "Maß"; a liquid volume roughly equal to a quart or liter.</note></term> from a flowing stream and dissolve in it four loth of <term>calcined verdigris <note>original: "Grünšpon Aešuštum"; copper acetate that has been roasted or "burnt."</note></term>, one and a half loth of yellow sulfur, and six loth of common salt—all crushed small. Pour enough of this water over the Mercury to cover it well and boil it. Keep pouring and boiling it for five hours. Afterward, take the Mercury and let it become hard in the open air.

### Tinctural Cementing Powder, as worked by a Count of Görlitz.

->[An alchemical symbol consisting of a grid formed by three vertical lines crossed by three horizontal lines.]<-

Take the coagulate mentioned above, the extracted vitriol, or <term>antimony <note>original: "Stibio"; stibium is the Latin name for antimony, often called the "Black Eagle" in this context.</note></term>, and cinnabar. ### A Specific Work for a Poor Fellow to Undertake.
In the beginning, when I started to work, I sustained myself for a long time with the following small piece. The eternal justice of God also wishes for us to pray for our sustenance.

->Particular work that a poor journeyman shall perform.<-

### Process.

Take three <term>loth <note>A German unit of weight, approximately 15 grams or half an ounce.</note></term> of good <term>Stemo <note>original: "Stemo"; an old term for antimony or stibnite ore, often used to purify gold and silver.</note></term>, two loth of finely filed good steel, and one loth of finely filed <term>Venus <note>The alchemical name for Copper.</note></term>. Crush these pieces and rub them well together. Put it all on a <term>cupel <note>original: "Tribscherben"; a shallow clay dish used in assaying to separate precious metals from base ones.</note></term>. Let the Stemo smoke very strongly from it until no more Stemo can be perceived. Then take fresh antimony; rub another three loth into these two metals. Let the Stemo smoke off once again. Do this for a third time with fresh Stemo, and you will find the two metals prepared. Rub these very small and add an equal weight of <term>amalgamated mercury <note>original: "impastierten Mercurium"; quicksilver that has been softened or combined into a paste-like state.</note></term>. Add common <term>native sulfur <note>original: "Berckschwefel."</note></term>—which at this time is called <term>cinnabar <note>original: "Zinober"; mercury sulfide.</note></term>—to the mixture. Put it together into a <term>luted crucible <note>original: "Digel perlutiert"; a melting pot sealed airtight with "lute," a paste of clay and other binders.</note></term>. Place it in hot sand for three hours until the mercury <term>evaporates <note>original: "hinweg zimentiert"; literally "cements away," referring here to the mercury leaving the mixture through heat.</note></term>. In this way, the two metals gain <term>entry into Silver <note>original: "Ingreß ins Lunæ"; meaning the prepared base metals can now be successfully incorporated into silver to increase its mass without degrading its quality.</note></term>.

<image-desc>A symbol consisting of three horizontal lines intersected by three vertical lines, forming a 3x3 grid or a large hash symbol.</image-desc>

Take one loth of fine silver, <term>mountain-feather <note>original: "Berckfeder"; likely asbestos or a fibrous variety of the mineral lithomarge, used here for purification.</note></term> white, and common salt, half a loth of each well-weighed. Let the silver flow [melt] completely within this for one strong hour. Then let it flow again <term>by itself <note>original: "per se."</note></term> so that it <term>purifies <note>original: "mundier."</note></term>; then it is ready.

Now take one <term>quintlein <note>original: "Quintle"; a small weight, 1/4 of a loth or about 3.75 grams.</note></term> of the prepared metal [the steel/copper mixture] rubbed small in a paper, with a small grain of <term>borax <note>original: "Porras"; a flux used to help metals melt and flow.</note></term>. Let the loth of silver that was prepared flow strongly by itself and throw [the paper] upon it. Let them go [melt] together for a quarter of an hour. Afterward, <term>refine it with lead <note>original: "treibs per Saturnum ab"; refers to cupellation, where lead is used to carry away impurities, leaving behind pure precious metal.</note></term>. Thus you have <term>fixed Silver <note>original: "Lunam fixam"; silver that has been stabilized so it does not lose weight or quality during chemical testing.</note></term>. Up to this point, I have taught this to my brother. I tell you: if the <term>purified silver <note>original: "Silber purgatum."</note></term> shows itself halfway with the "yellow needle" [test], then take one loth of gold, add it to that same silver, let it flow, and add one quintlein of the prepared metals upon it. Let it go for a quarter hour, then add another quintlein upon it, and everything remains at its best. Only see to it that the Stemo on the cupel flows strongly with the metal, so that the cinnabar can later take hold of the metal.

### Following is another piece; I have truly found it to be correct.

Take eight loth of well-calcined [burned to ash] lead with common yellow sulfur, five loth each of <term>verdigris <note>original: "Spongrün."</note></term> <term>burnt copper <note>original: "Aesustum"; refers to copper that has been oxidized by heat.</note></term> and cinnabar, and one loth of <term>common salt <note>original: "Sal commune."</note></term>. Rub these pieces together very small. Put them into an earthenware vessel. Pour <term>purified urine <note>original: "geleutterten Urin."</note></term> over it, moistened, and let this become dry. Rub it again and do this six times; then the powder is ready.

Take one loth of this powder and put it into a <term>round-bottomed flask <note>original: "Kolbenglaß."</note></term>. Pour upon it two loth of <term>Joforon <note>An alchemical solvent or "strong water," possibly a type of acid or specialized mineral water.</note></term> in which eight loth of silver have been <term>dissolved <note>original: "soluiert."</note></term>, and a sixteenth part of the first prepared <term>Mars <note>The alchemical name for Iron or Steel.</note></term> with the <term>Venus <note>Copper.</note></term>. <term>Precipitate <note>original: "precipitiers."</note></term> it in the sand into a stone. Let it stand for four days and nights in hot sand, so that whatever is volatile <term>sublimes <note>original: "sublimiert"; turns from a solid to a vapor and collects at the top.</note></term> upward. Then take the material in the glass, put it into a crucible, and let it flow very strongly by itself in a <term>wind furnace <note>A furnace designed to create a natural draft for high temperatures.</note></term>

# An ancient process, described by a Carthusian monk, left behind and found 100 years ago.

Then place it while warm in a damp cellar, so that it lies spread very thinly upon it. Place a glass [vessel] underneath; thus it dissolves all the mercury sublimate into a water, and the amalgam remains lying on the plate. Take this mercury water into a <term>retort <note>A glass vessel with a long, downward-pointing neck used for distillation.</note></term> which has a somewhat wide neck, and distill it low over into its receiver so that there is no residue. # Two eternal unextinguishable burning temporal Lights / by the Lord Trithemius, Abbot of Sponheim / which were transcribed from the manuscript of Bartholomew Korndorffer.

<note>Johannes Trithemius (1462–1516) was a celebrated German Benedictine abbot, polymath, and occultist. Bartholomew Korndorffer was a legendary alchemist of the late 16th century whose writings often claimed to reveal the secrets of famous masters.</note>

Two incombustible eternal lights are found herein / which I, Bartholomew Korndorffer / transcribed from a disciple of the Lord <term>Trithemius <note>original: "Trittemio"</note></term>, Abbot of Sponheim / who assured me upon his oath / that they had never yet come to the light of day / except for what his master the Abbot presented as a gift to a great <term>potentate <note>A monarch or ruler; in this case, likely Emperor Maximilian I.</note></term>. This highly renowned <term>Mage <note>original: "Magus"</note></term> Trithemius, Abbot of Sponheim / who lived at the time of the great Emperor Maximilian the First / and had no equal in Germany in his time / achieved and established much good with his arts / nothing of which was mixed with devilish work / as some evil people falsely accused and blamed him / but rather from the <term>starry secrets <note>original: "Gestirn der heymlichkeit"; likely referring to natural magic or astrology.</note></term> through which he learned everything that happened in the world / as he wished / and many times indicated things to come. 

Once, when I was on my travels / I came to St. Moritz / and unexpectedly found an acquaintance / from the electoral court / whom I addressed / he was glad to see me / he asked me to eat with him / he wanted to invite one more to join me / named Servatius Hochel / he had been with the Abbot of Sponheim / and had served him for twelve years / I was pleased by this / this acquaintance of mine indicated to me / that he [Hochel] was reserved / quiet / and only occasionally let slip a hint of the arts. As we then came together / and finished the meal / he asked me / Master Hochel, to go with him to his lodgings / which I did / and we both spoke much of the arts and because I saw / that he was an elderly man / I desired to leave him / but he would not let me go / he ordered a meal from his landlady / which we both consumed in his lodgings / At that time, Servatius Hochel presented me with the Lord Trithemius's manuscript / the following two incombustible lights / and several small magical pieces / which I afterwards especially tried and tested / and found them to be true / Hochel also told me / his master Trithemius had presented this great potentate, the Emperor / with this incombustible light / and placed it in a glass in his chamber / which the same potentate had well secured / so that one could see the glow from it. 

Afterwards, a <term>time of plague <note>original: "ein Sterbendt"; literally "a dying," referring to an epidemic.</note></term> occurred / so that the Emperor departed / and did not visit this place for 20 years / but when he once came back there / and the Abbot of Sponheim had long since died / he thought of this light / and went immediately to see it / and found it with all the signs just as it had been placed in the chamber by the Lord Trithemius / still unextinguished / just as the people of the castle told this great Lord / that they had always seen a glow in this place / like a lamp in a church. Thus this Lord let this light continue to burn / and it shall burn in this place without ceasing / that is a great <term>Arcanum <note>A deep secret or mystery of nature.</note></term> in this world. The Emperor Maximilian gave the Abbot of Sponheim 6000 crowns as a gift for these temporal eternal lights.

->Here follows the Process and the Practice.<-

Take eight <term>loth <note>A historical unit of weight, approximately 15-16 grams or half an ounce.</note></term> of sulfur / and as much calcined <term>alum <note>original: "Alaun"; a chemical compound used in alchemy, often as a mordant or astringent. ### The Vinegar.

Take one pound of well-dried salt / pour a very strong wine vinegar over it / draw it off / pour it back on / draw it off again / always to the state of oiliness / do this four times / then it is prepared.

# Preface.

Alphidius <note>Likely referring to an Arabic alchemist known in Latin as Alphidius, whose works were influential in the Middle Ages.</note>, one of the ancient wise men, says that for one who cannot visualize or conceive for himself anything in the <term>Art of the Philosopher’s Stone</term> <note>The "Art" refers to alchemy; the "Stone" is the legendary substance used to transform base metals and achieve spiritual perfection.</note>, it is more beneficial that he does not involve himself in it at all than to attempt something blindly. Rasis <note>The Latinized name for Al-Razi, a famous Persian physician and alchemist.</note> speaks similarly in the book *The Light of Lights* <note>original Latin: "Lumen Luminum."</note>. It is to be avoided with great diligence; I also most highly admonish you here that no one should presume to undertake the unknown mixing of the elements. Rosinus <note>A name often used in alchemical texts to refer to Zosimos of Panopolis, a 3rd-century mystic and alchemist.</note> also supports this, saying: all those who involve themselves in this Art and lack the understanding and knowledge of the things which the Philosophers have written in their books are without understanding. For the Philosophers have established the foundation of this Art upon a natural beginning but a hidden operation. Although it is obvious that all physical things take their origin from the Earth, as well as their essence, according to the order of time; just as the influence of the stars or planets—such as the Sun and Moon and the others—together with the four qualities of the elements, which they move without ceasing, all and every...

<summary>This preface warns the reader against practicing alchemy without a proper theoretical foundation, citing ancient authorities like Rasis and Rosinus. ### SECOND TREATISE.

**Morienus** <note>original: "Moriens"; a legendary 7th-century hermit and alchemist often cited in Hermetic texts</note> says: you should know that the entire work of this **Art** <term>Art: the practice of alchemy, often called "the Great Work"</term> is completed through two aptitudes, which are so connected that when one is accomplished, the other begins and brings the same to completion; for then the entire mastery is perfect. However, these do not occur except within their own matter. To understand this properly, it is first necessary to know what **Nature**, acting as the giver, <margin>for</margin> says in his *Mercury* <note>original: "Mercurij"</note> regarding the creation of metals. She works the metals <margin>Procreation of metals</margin> out of **Mercury** <note>represented by the symbol ☿</note> and **Sulfur** <note>original: "Sulphur"</note>. And **Serrarius** <note>likely a reference to a commentator or alchemical authority</note> confirms this in the "Question of Alchemy" in the 25th Chapter: that Nature, from the beginning of natural metals, takes a slimy, heavy water in the fire, mixed with a very white, nimble, and heavy earth; she dissolves this into a vapor or mist and raises it into the veins or crevices of the earth, cooking or steaming them together, strengthening the moisture and drying them, united as one, until a substance is formed from it which is called **Quicksilver** <note>Mercury</note>. And this is now the beginning and the very first matter of the metals, as was also mentioned above. Therefore, he speaks again in the 26th Chapter, where he says: those who wish to follow Nature should not take Quicksilver alone, but Quicksilver and Sulfur joined together—not common quicksilver and sulfur, but that which Nature has joined together, well-prepared and cooked in constant fluidity. In such a Quicksilver, Nature began with the first effect and ended in a metallic nature; and therewith she ceased, for she had accomplished her part and left everything to the **Art** to complete into a perfect **Philosophers' Stone**. From these words, it is evident to anyone who wishes to proceed correctly in this Art—as all the **Philosophers** <note>a term alchemists used to refer to themselves and their predecessors</note> say—that he should begin where Nature has left off, and should take the Sulfur and the Quicksilver which Nature has joined together in the <margin>all</margin> very purest form. For in that, a very rapid union has occurred, which no one else can prepare in such a way through Art. Nature has done all this for the sake of the procreation of the metallic form. But the same matter, which is thus informed by Nature, benefits the Art for the sake of receiving the power, which then quickly places itself into such matter. Afterward, some alchemists **calcinate** <term>Calcinate: to heat a substance to high temperatures to reduce it to a powder or change its properties</term> the **Gold** <note>represented by the symbol ☉</note> so that they may bring it to dissolution and the separation of the **Elements**, until they bring it into a spiritual, subtle nature and the purity of the natures of Quicksilver and Sulfur, and

<margin>p. 15.</margin>
Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure regarded as the father of alchemy.</note>, a Father of Philosophy, says: There is yet an end of this world, where heaven and earth come together. No one can [fully grasp] through the heaven and the earth the two aforementioned dispositions <note>The "two dispositions" likely refer to the dual nature of the alchemical substance (sulfur and mercury or the fixed and the volatile).</note>, but many accidents arise in the work before it is brought to an end, and they are understood through the comparison of figures, as follows hereafter. And this is the First Parable: God first created the Earth, plain, rich, and very fertile, without spirit, and without sand, stone, mountain, or valley. Through the influence of the planets and the operation of nature, the earth has now been transformed into many forms: outwardly with hard stones, high mountains, and deep valleys; inwardly with strange things and colors, namely the ores and their origins. And with such things, the earth has completely departed from its first form. This occurred because, although the earth was heaped up thick, large, deep, long, wide, and broad, yet through the constant operation of the Sun's heat <note>In alchemy, the "Sun's heat" often refers to both the celestial sun and the internal "central fire" of the earth.</note>, there arose within it a sweltering, hot, vaporous, and steamy warmth. This warmth permeated the entire earth down to the abyss and created, within the coldness and moisture of the earth, a strong vapor, both misty and airy, all of which were enclosed within the earth. Over time, these vapors increased and finally became so strong that the earth could no longer contain them within itself, as they naturally desired to rise upward. Finally, in those places of the earth where many of them gathered, they threw up one part of the soil into a heap here, and another there, and thus made many hills and mountains, and deep valleys; and at those places where such hills and mountains...

## The Second Parable.

Hermes, the first master of this Art, speaks thus: the water of the air, which is between heaven and earth, is the life of every thing. For through its moisture and warmth, this water is the mediator between the two contraries, fire and water. This same water has rained down upon the earth; the heavens have opened and dewed upon the earth, whereby it became sweet like honey and was moistened. This same blood <note>The "blood" refers to the life-giving moisture or "Sap of the Sages."</note> brings forth many kinds of colors and fruits. In their midst has grown a great tree with a silver trunk, which spreads out to the corners of the world. Upon its branches sat many kinds of birds, which all flew away toward the day, and the raven’s head <note>original: "Rappen Haupt." In alchemy, the raven's head or *caput corvi* symbolizes the "nigredo" or black stage of decay before purification.</note> has become white.

This same tree brings many kinds of fruit: the first are the finest pearls; the second is called by the philosophers *Terra foliata* <note>Latin: "foliated earth" or "earth of leaves," a purified state of the alchemical matter</note>; the third is the finest gold. This tree also gives fruits of health; it makes warm what is cold, and makes cold what is warm. It makes dry what is moist, and moist what is dry. It makes hard what is soft, and soft what is hard. This is the end of the whole Art, of which the Author of the Three Words <note>Referring to the *Tractatus trium verborum*, an alchemical treatise</note> speaks: the three moist stones, three precious words of the whole mastery.

This is also what Salienus means when he speaks of the herb *Lunatica* <note>Moonwort</note> or *Bera*: its root is a metallic earth, it has a red stem covered or spotted with blackness by its nature, and it also diminishes easily. It gains or receives flowers in time; after three days, if one puts it into <term>mercury</term> <note>mercury: In this context, it refers to "Philosophical Mercury," a transformative solvent, rather than common quicksilver.</note>, it changes into perfect silver; and if one seethes <note>boils or cooks</note> it further, it turns into gold. That same gold converts one hundred parts into the finest gold. Virgil reports of this tree in the 6th book of the *Aeneid* <note>original: "Eney"</note>, where he tells in his fable how Aeneas and Silvius went to a tree, and as one branch was broken off, another grew in the same
->place.<-

->❧ ( o ) ❧<-

# The Third Parable.

Avicenna says, in the chapter concerning moisture: when heat works within a moist body, it first gives birth to blackness <note>This refers to *Nigredo*, the first stage of the alchemical process, characterized by putrefaction and darkness.</note>. For this reason, the ancients saw from afar a mist arising that covered and moistened the entire earth; and they also saw the turbulence of the sea and the flowing waters over the face of the earth, and these became foul and stinking in the darkness. Also, they saw the King of the Earth sinking, and heard him cry out with a longing voice: "He who redeems me shall live with me eternally, and shall reign in my clarity upon my royal throne." And night surrounded all things.

On the next day, they saw a bright morning star rise above the King, and the light of day illuminating the darkness. The clear Sun pierced through the clouds in many forms of colors, with its stars and radiance, and a fragrant scent, surpassing all musk <note>Original: *Bisem*, a historical term for musk or ambergris, often used to describe the "odor of sanctity" or successful alchemical transmutation.</note>, rose from the earth. And the beautiful clarity shone forth, and in that moment all was perfected, so that the King of all honor was delighted and renewed, and was well-adorned and entirely handsome, at whose beauty the Sun and Moon marveled.

He was crowned with three precious crowns: one of iron, the second of silver, the third of gold. They saw in his right hand a scepter <note>Original: *Corper*, literally "body" or object, but contextually a rod or scepter.</note> containing seven stars, which all gave off a glowing radiance; and in his left hand a golden apple, upon which sat a white dove of a fiery nature, silvered over, with wings of a golden color. Concerning which Aristotle <note>Original: *Arles*, a common medieval/early modern contraction for Aristoteles.</note> said: the destruction of one thing is the birth of another. This is to say: through the

->Masterful Art <note>The "Great Work" of alchemy.</note> and the preparation of the destructive moistures,<-
->he is renewed with his essential<-
->moisture, which shall be his perfection and<-
->life.<-

# Hereafter follows the properties of Nature, through which she has her operation.

## FOURTH TREATISE <note>original: "TRACTATVS QVARTVS"</note>.

Everything in the Book of Birth <note>original: "Buch vonn der Geburt"; likely a reference to the Book of Genesis or a specific philosophical text on generation and procreation</note> speaks thus: the seed and the man give birth to a human, for the power and spirit of the seed bring life; and this occurs in seven ways and through the operation of the Sun's heat. But because the Philosophers <term>Philosophi: the alchemists, who referred to themselves as "natural philosophers" seeking the wisdom of nature</term> must assist Nature with Art <term>Kunst: the "Art" of alchemy—the human application of knowledge to accelerate or perfect natural processes</term> in their work, they must govern a heat by Art, commensurate with the Sun, so that they may give birth to the aforementioned Stone <note>the Philosopher's Stone, the ultimate goal of the work</note>; and this also occurs in seven ways.

->First, such a heat is required that softens and melts the thickness of the Earth, which has been baked thick and hard together; of this Socrates <note>Socrates was often cited in medieval alchemical texts, such as the *Turba Philosophorum*, as a symbolic authority on the elements</note> speaks thus: "The holes and cracks of the parts of the earth are opened, so that it may take unto itself the power of Fire and Water."<-

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration of a woven basket or ornamental pot filled to the brim with a variety of fruits, flowers, and leaves, including clusters that resemble grapes and round fruits like apples.</image-desc>

<meta>catchword: To the</meta>

<summary>This page introduces the Fourth Treatise, explaining that just as humans are born through the sun's natural heat, the alchemist must use "Art" to create a specific heat that softens the "Earth" of the matter to begin its transformation. It cites Socrates regarding the opening of the earth to receive the powers of fire and water.</summary>
<keywords>Nature, Alchemy, Philosophers, Philosopher's Stone, Socrates, Fire, Water, Art vs Nature, Generation</keywords>

This page moves to the "Second" property, focusing on the transition from darkness to light and the shift from the white stage to the red stage of the Great Work.</meta>

<image-desc>An alchemical illustration enclosed in a rectangular border. At the center is a large, pear-shaped glass vessel (a cucurbit) topped with an ornate golden crown. Secondly, it is fitting for the heat that through its power all darkness is driven from the earth, and it illuminates everything according to the proverb of Senior <term>Senior: referring to Senior Zadith (Ibn Umayl), a 10th-century Arabic alchemist whose writings were translated into Latin and became foundational to European alchemy</term>; heat makes every thing white, and every white thing red. For just as the water makes things white, so also the fire illuminates, so that then the color shines through the subtilized earth <term>Subtilierte Erden: earth or matter that has been purified, refined, and broken down into its most potent, "subtle" form through chemical processing</term>, like a ruby, through the tincturing spirit <term>Tingierenden Geist: the transformative essence or "tincture" capable of deeply penetrating and changing the color and nature of a substance</term> of the fire. Concerning this, Socrates <note>As noted on the previous page, Socrates appears here as a symbolic authority of ancient wisdom within the alchemical tradition, particularly the "Turba Philosophorum"</note> says: "You shall see a wondrous light [emerging] from the darkness."

<summary>This page describes the second property of alchemical heat, which purifies the matter by driving away darkness and facilitating the transition from the white stage (albedo) to the red stage (rubedo).</summary>
<keywords>alchemical heat, Senior Zadith, Socrates, albedo, rubedo, subtilized earth, tincturing spirit, light from darkness</keywords>

# Now Follows the manifold effects of the entire work /
### in four
# Short Articles
### understood properly.

## THE FIFTH TREATISE. <note>original: "TRACTATVS QVINTVS"</note>
### The first Article.

The first step that is fitting in the **art of Alchemy** <note>original: "Alchimiæ"</note> is **dissolution** <note>Also known as *solutio*; the process of turning a solid "body" into a liquid state so it can be purified</note>; for the order of Nature requires that the **body** be cooked in a **water**, that is, in a **mercury** <note>original: "Quecksilber"</note>. To put it another way: the **living silver** <note>Quicksilver or mercury, representing the fluid principle</note> dissolves the **sulfur** <note>The active, combustible principle</note> which is added and present to it. And this dissolution is nothing other than an ordering of the **moist** with the **dry**, and is actually **putrefaction** <note>original: "Putrifaction" — The stage of decay where the substance "dies" and turns black (nigredo), a necessary precursor to rebirth and purification</note>; and this same process will turn the **matter** <note>original: "Materiam"</note> **black**.

# Splendor Solis.

## The Second Article.

<margin>Coagulation</margin>
<margin>Colors</margin>
<margin>Coagulation:</margin>
The second stage is <term>Coagulation</term> <note>In alchemy, coagulation is the process where a liquid substance is "fixed" or solidified into a stable "body."</note>, which turns the water back into a body. This means that the <term>sulfur</term> <note>original: "schwebel"; in alchemical theory, sulfur represents the active, masculine, and combustible principle.</note>, which was previously dissolved by the <term>quicksilver</term> <note>original: "lebendigen Silber" or "living silver"; mercury, representing the fluid, passive, and feminine principle.</note>, now fetches the quicksilver back and draws it to itself out of the water of the earth and the body. It is necessary that different and many kinds of colors appear; for when the property of the active thing changes, it must be transformed by the agility of the living thing. Therefore, in the dissolution, the quicksilver is like the active agent, but in the coagulation, it is the passive subject in which the work is performed. For this reason,

->this art is compared to the play of children,<-
->which they played, so that what lay on top,<-
->now lies underneath.<-

<note>This "play of children" (Latin: *ludus puerorum*) is a common alchemical metaphor. it suggests that once the natural process is understood, the Great Work is as easy as a child's game, and it also refers to the constant inversion or "flipping" of the elements during the process.</note>

Splendor Solis.

### The Third Article.

<margin>
<unclear>Calx</unclear> <note>Likely "Kalk" (Calx), referring to the powdery oxide or residue remaining after a metal or mineral has been heated.</note>
</margin>

The third is <term>Sublimation<note>In alchemy, sublimation refers to the process where a solid is heated into a vapor and then collected again as a purified solid; here it represents a stage of spiritual and physical refinement.</note></term>, through which the aforementioned "earths" are distilled from their moisture. For when the water is reduced into the earth, it yields to the fluidity of the air, and the earth rises up like a lukewarm cloud, similar to an egg. This is the spirit of the <term>fifth essence<note>Also known as the Quintessence, the purest and most concentrated substance, thought to be the "soul" of the matter.</note></term>, which is called Tincture, <term>Ferment<note>original: "Fermentum"</note></term>, <term>Soul<note>original: "Anima"</note></term>, or the Oil. It is the very closest material to the Philosopher’s Stone. Through this sublimation, the ashes are produced, which—by their own desire given by God—find their own moderation of the fire. Thus, the fiery nature and property remain. This is the true philosophical sublimation, through which the perfect <term>whiteness<note>Known as the Albedo stage, this signifies the purification and washing away of impurities.</note></term> is accomplished. For this reason, one compares this art to <term>women’s work<note>A standard alchemical metaphor; just as laundry is washed until white or food is cooked until ready, the alchemist must patiently "clean" and "cook" their materials.</note></term>: that is, washing until it becomes white, cooking, and roasting until it is enough.

# The Splendor of the Sun.

## The Fourth Article.

The last, or fourth point, which is fitting, is that this water be separated from the earth, and again from the earth—or with the earth—be reunited, so that one occurs after the other if the Stone <note>The Philosopher's Stone, the ultimate goal of the alchemical work, representing perfection and transformation.</note> is otherwise to be completed. For this reason, everything that is gathered together in a natural thing, or joined into a body <term>Latin: *corpus*; referring to the physical matter of the substance</term>, is done so that the single thing might be the composite <term>Latin: *compositum*; a unified substance made of different parts</term>. In these four articles just mentioned, everything is contained about which the Philosophers <note>The "Philosophers" are the ancient alchemical authorities and sages whose writings form the basis of this tradition.</note> have filled the entire world with countless books.

Splendor Solis.

# Of the Governance of the Fire.

<margin>A</margin>
The following concerns the governance of the fire; once a thing is prepared by heat, no instability remains, for its order is transformed into the nature of the Sun. This is to say that the spiritual is made bodily—or beautiful—and brought together. Of these two planets, Senior <note>Referring to Senior Zadith, an influential 10th-century Arabic alchemist often cited in European texts.</note> speaks thus: "I am a hot and dry Sun, and you, Moon, are cold and moist; and as we ascend into the most noble state, a burning light will be poured into us." That is to say, through the teaching and mastery of the ancients, the renewal of moisture is received, and the Sun and Moon become transparent. In the <term>Ladder of the Natural Philosophers <note>original: "scala phisicorum"</note></term>, it is written thus regarding the fire: the heat or the fire of the entire work is of a single form. However, some say that the heat of the first stage <note>original: "Regiments"</note> should be like the warmth of a brooding hen. Others say it should be like the natural heat in the <term>digestion <note>original: "Deuwung"</note></term> of food and nourishment for the body. Some say it is like the heat of the Sun when it is in the sign of Aries <note>The Ram, marking the beginning of Spring.</note>. Although the Stone may be completed without such effects, the required temperament nevertheless changes; it must be a gentle and moderate heat. This should provide warmth until the matter blackens and turns into whiteness, and this is compared to the heat of the Sun when it is in Aries and begins to enter Taurus <note>The Bull.</note>. When the whiteness appears, the heat shall be increased until the complete drying or <term>reduction to ash <note>original: "Eschierung"</note></term> of the Stone; and this heat is equal to the heat of the Sun when it is in Taurus and also entering Gemini <note>The Twins.</note>. And when the Stone is dried and reduced to ash, the fire is strengthened once more until the Stone is perfectly red and is delivered from the fire in royal garments. This heat is compared to the heat of the Sun when it is in Leo <note>The Lion, the height of summer.</note>, which is the highest dignity of its house. Let this now be enough said regarding the governance of the fire.

## Of the Colors Produced in the Preparation of the Stone.

<margin>Of the Sun</margin>
Miraldus <note>Likely a reference to a philosopher in the "Turba Philosophorum," a famous early alchemical assembly text.</note> the philosopher says in the <term>Assembly <note>original: "Turba"</note></term>: "It turns black twice, it turns yellow twice, and it turns red twice," and it acquires many different colors. The heat is changed according to these colors. Although many colors appear, there are only three that are the foremost and primary colors, namely: Black, White, and Red. Between these, many other colors appear. Regarding the white and the first redness, Mizraldus notes—not because it is not a perfect color—as Ciliator <note>Likely referring to Pietro d'Abano, known as "Conciliator," a 13th-century physician and philosopher.</note> says, and they consist...

<summary>This page details the 'Governance of the Fire,' comparing the intensity of the alchemical furnace to the zodiac signs of the Sun, and introduces the three primary stages of the Great Work: Black, White, and Red.</summary>
<keywords>Governance of Fire, Senior Zadith, Zodiac Heat, Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Leo, Alchemical Colors, Nigredo, Albedo, Rubedo, Turba Philosophorum</keywords>

--- Page 229 ---
<meta>This page continues the technical instructions regarding the alchemical "work," specifically detailing the transition of colors and the management of heat. It builds upon the previous page's discussion of the "governance of fire" and the initial transformation from blackness to whiteness.</meta>

Splendor Solis.

...exist in the *Matter* <note>original: "Materia"</note> hardly long enough for one to see them; but the other yellowish color, which appears after the complete white and before the final Redness, shows itself for a time in the Matter. Therefore, some *Philosophers* have also considered it a primary color. *Miraldus* speaks as reported above; however, they do not appear for as long as the Blackness, Whiteness, and Redness, which remain in the Matter for more than four days. The Blackness and Redness occur twice; the perfect color is always Blackness, which manifests in the gentlest heat. Concerning this, *Senior* and *Ciliator* <note>Pietro d'Abano, a 13th-century physician and philosopher known as "The Conciliator."</note> speak thus: "When the cooking has occurred in the gentle warmth until the Blackness vanishes from it." And for this reason, *Lucas* the *Philosopher* says in the *Turba* <note>The *Turba Philosophorum*, or "Assembly of the Philosophers," an ancient alchemical text.</note>: "Beware of strong fire, for if you use excessive fire in the beginning, it will turn Red before its time, and that is of no use; for in the beginning of its governance you should have Blackness, thereafter Whiteness, and at the last Redness."

*Baldus* the *Philosopher* says in the *Turba* thus: "Cook your *Composition* until you see it white, and quench it in the vinegar, and separate the black from the white; for the white is a sign and approaches <term>Fixation <note>The process of making a volatile substance stable and resistant to heat.</note></term>. It also requires that it be drawn away from the blackness through the fire of <margin>Calcination</margin> *Calcination* <note>Reducing a substance to a fine powder or ash through intense heat.</note>." For thus, through the increase of heat, the superfluous parts are separated, and there remains a coarse Earth or 'father of the Matter,' which is like a black, raw Earth that no longer mixes with the pure and subtle Matter of the Stone. And that is the word of the *Philosophers* when they say that the Redness should be drawn from the Whiteness, for <margin>Red.</margin> there is nothing superfluous in it; nothing separates from it, but rather everything becomes perfectly Red. And therefore they command that sign with a strong fire, and *Pythagoras* <note>original: "Pitagros"</note> testifies to this when he says: "The more the colors change, the more you should strengthen the <margin>△</margin> <note>The symbol for Fire.</note> fire; for there is no more to fear from the fire, because the *Matter* is *Fixed* from the white color onward, and the <term>Spirits <note>Volatile elements that usually evaporate when heated.</note></term> do not flee from it." According to the proverb of *Lucas* the *Philosopher*: "When our <margin>Magnesia</margin> *Magnesia* <note>In alchemy, this refers not to the modern element, but to the primal 'living' matter or the 'lead of the wise.'</note> is made white, it does not let the *Spirits* escape from it." Thus much is said regarding the colors of the heavenly *Philosophers*, and the *Philosopher* follows thereafter.

*Hermes*, the Father of the Philosophers, says that one cannot <margin>White Magnesia</margin> finish the white *Magnesia* until it has completed all its colors, which are divided into four other waters: namely one to two, and three to one, of which one-third part belongs to the heat, but two-thirds to the moisture; these waters are the "weights of the wise." <margin>Weight.</margin>

# Concerning the Nature of the Entire Work of Preparing the Stone.

## SIXTH TREATISE.

<margin>Calcination</margin>
Calcination is placed at the beginning of the work, as the father in a lineage; and it is threefold: two belong to the *Body* <note>original: "Corpus"</note>, and the third to the Spirit. <margin>wood</margin> The first is a preparation of the cold moisture, which protects the wood so that it does not burn, and is a beginning of our work. The second is a fatty moisture that causes the wood to burn. And the third is a reduction to ashes, or incineration, of the dry earth, and it gives a true fixed and subtle moisture; its <margin>glass</margin> amount is also small, and it yields no flame, but gives a clear *Body* <note>original: "Corpus"</note>, like glass. In such a manner, the Philosophers command their calcination to be made, and that is accomplished with the <term>Permanent Water <note>original: "Aqua permanente"; a symbolic term for a solvent, often associated with mercury, that dissolves metals without getting them "wet" in the traditional sense.</note></term> or <term>Sharpest Vinegar <note>original: "Acceto acerrimia"; a metaphorical name for a powerful acidic agent used to break down substances.</note></term>. A similar moisture is in the metals, for it is a beginning of all soft things; therefore, the <margin>Calcination</margin> Calcination of the Philosophers is an indication of the destruction of moisture and a bringing forth of another Fiery moisture, from which the essence or <term>Quintessence <note>original: "Quinta Essentia"; the fifth element or the purest, most concentrated essence of a substance.</note></term> and life arise. For this reason, it is called a "melting"; it is accomplished with the water of the Philosophers, which is properly the <term>Sublimation <note>The process of heating a substance until it turns to vapor and then collecting it again as a solid to purify it.</note></term>, or the Philosophers' <term>Resolution <note>The process of dissolving or breaking a substance down into its fundamental parts.</note></term>, for through it the hard dryness is changed, and a softening occurs wherein the dryness is drawn out—the <term>Quintessence <note>original: "Quinta Essentia"</note></term>, or separation of the elements. And this occurs so that the parts, which were killed and compressed by the fire, become subtle through the Spirit, which is a Resolving Water and a moisture of the destroyed bodies, and with

Then they mix the water that has been drawn off from the Virgin’s Milk and bring it into a red, golden gum and into a transparent, thick water. This one should coagulate; thereafter they call it the *Tincture of Wisdom* <note>original: "Tincturam Sapientiæ."</note>, and a fire of colors, and a soul and spirit that, having wandered far, now returns home.

Therefore, Senior <note>Zadith ben Hamuel, a significant 10th-century alchemist</note> says: it is a wondrous thing, when you throw it over the other three mixtures, it helps the white; over the citrine and the red it makes it white like the color of silver; thereafter it helps the red over the citrine and makes the same white in color. And Morienus <note>A legendary 7th-century hermit and alchemist</note> speaks thus: look upon the perfect citrine <note>A golden-yellow color stage</note>, and it changes in its yellowness; and the perfect red, and it forms in its redness; and it demands the perfect black in its blackness.

<margin>Philosopher's Gold <note>indicated by the symbol ☉</note></margin>
From this it is clearly to be understood that the <term>Gold of the Philosophers</term> <note>A refined spiritual substance, distinct from the common metal used for currency</note> is something other than common gold or silver, although the comparisons of the philosophers have some connection to common gold or silver, and therefore to all metals. Senior says: I am a hard and dry iron, and there is nothing that resembles me, for I am a coagulation of the Quicksilver of the Philosophers. The *Turba* says: Copper and lead become a precious stone of the philosophers, which the philosophers call "that which is red."

<margin>Saturn <note>Lead</note> white lead <note>original: "bleiwissen"</note></margin>
Lead is a beginning of the whole work; without it, nothing is made, and it is spoken of thus: from red lead make an iron, or Saffron of Mars <note>original: "Crocum Martis"; a name for iron oxide (rust) used in alchemical processes</note>. From white lead make a white tincture, and so you have begun the wisdom. Though the Philosopher says: nothing is closer to gold than lead, for in it is the life, and it draws all secrets to itself; but this is not spoken of common lead. 

<margin>Saturn <note>Lead</note> marcasite</margin>
Likewise the Marcasite <note>A common iron sulfide mineral</note>, because the "stinking earth" gains glowing sparks, as Morienes says, it is also compared to arsenic, orpiment <note>A yellow arsenic sulfide mineral</note>, and tutty <note>Crude zinc oxide</note>. Likewise many things that are not mineral at all, being from the four complexions <note>The bodily humors: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile</note>, from the blood of the Basilisk, and many such superfluous things; and among mineral things: Salt, Alum, A. <note>likely Alkali or Azoth</note> and others, for the sake of many different properties.

But before all things, Alphidius <note>An Arab alchemist frequently cited in medieval texts</note> warns us and says: dear son, guard yourself against the spirits, bodies, and stones that are dead, as told above, for in them is no way, nor will you find your purpose or design, because their power does not increase, but comes to nothing; but the Philosophers'

However, the spirit, which is of a watery nature, tinges into an Elixir; and therefore, that which is drawn out of it is a white or red, true Fixation <note>a state where a substance is no longer volatile in fire</note> of perfect colors, a penetrating Tincture that mixes into all metals.
