When they are in the fire, they are always like a molten thing; and therefore, a small part hardens a large mass of common Quicksilver into true Gold. For the moisture or water that one extracts from the metallic bodies is called the Soul—the Soul of the Stone.

<margin>soul, spirit, body of the Sulfur <note>symbol: 🜍</note>, Salt <note>symbol: 🜔</note>. The 3-fold discovery.</margin>
The Mercury, however, or its power, is called the Spirit when it takes on a sulfurous nature; and the thick Earth is the Body, and the physical substance <note>original: "Corpus"</note> of the Quintessence <note>the "fifth essence" or purest part of a substance</note>, and the final Tincture. And these three are one single thing, from a single root, differing only in their effects. And the names of these things are countably many, yet all refer to one thing, and are like a chain, compared and linked to one another, so that when one ends, another begins.

# Splendor Solis.

First, it preserves humans from all kinds of diseases;
Second, it perfects metallic bodies;
Third, it transforms all stones;
Fourth, it makes every glass malleable <note>flexible or workable without breaking</note>.

<margin>R.</margin>
<margin>//</margin> Concerning the First, the wise Philosophers say that if one takes it in a warm drink—wine or water—it makes him healthy in that very hour, namely against paralysis <note>original: *Paraliticum*</note>, dropsy, leprosy, jaundice, heart palpitations, intestinal colic <note>original: *Darmgicht*</note>, fever, epilepsy <note>original: *Fallendesucht*, the "falling sickness"</note>, abdominal cramps, and many other afflictions within the body. It also heals the outside of the body if one anoints themselves with it. It takes away harmful humors from an unhealthy stomach, and all melancholy and despondency. It also wards off all diseases of the eyes, strengthens the heart, restores hearing, makes teeth good again, restores paralyzed limbs, and also heals all abscesses <note>original: *Apostemata*</note>, as well as all external injuries—fistulas, cancers, "the wolf" <note>original: *Wolff*; likely refers to lupus or similar corrosive skin ulcers</note>. In summary: take it internally, or apply it as a powder or an ointment. Senior <note>Zadith ben Hamuel, a 10th-century alchemist</note> says it makes a person joyful and young, and keeps his body fresh and healthy against internal and external defects. Therefore, it is a medicine above all other medicines of Hippocrates, Galen, Constantine, Alexander, Avicenna <note>List of the most famous Greek, Roman, and Arabic medical authorities</note>, and other learned men, all of whom it surpasses.

One should also mix this medicine with other medicines or waters that are appropriate for and combat the specific illness.

<margin>//</margin> Regarding the second virtue, it is written that it transforms all imperfect metals. This is evident, for it makes any silver entirely like gold in color, substance, and in its weight, and makes it stable.

<margin>//</margin> Regarding the third, it is written that this Medicine also makes other stones such as jasper, hyacinth <note>a yellow or orange gemstone, often zircon</note>, white and red corals, emeralds, chrysolite, and sapphire; likewise, from crystals, it makes carbuncles <note>deep red garnets</note>, rubies, and topaz <note>original: *Theopasius*</note>, which are much better and more powerful than the natural ones. This medicine also melts all precious stones.

<margin>//</margin> Regarding the fourth, if one adds the aforementioned Medicine into molten, crushed glass, it allows the glass to be cut and transformed into all colors. The rest may any clever artist experience and investigate through his own experimentation.

## Preface.

In many and various ways the <term>Philosophi: the ancient masters of alchemy</term> spoke with one another in times past through their writings, just as if in a darkness, and with a voice like a heavy mist they have left us obscured concerning an art above all other arts—the most noble—leaving it as if under a cloud of doubt. This they did not do without cause, for they did not wish that their writings should be shared with or benefit any but their own "children" <note>In alchemical tradition, "children" or "Sons of Art" refers to initiated students rather than biological descendants</note> and those strangers who were not ignorant of the truth. For they had previously discussed such matters orally with one another, and had also covered and hidden such things among themselves in the secrecy of faith. And in all things where they further encountered one another in their parables, they understood each other through those same parables; thus they had no need for open speech toward one another, nor toward their other dear friends, nor did they require any surer certainty.

Secondly, they did not wish for the gift of God and the secrets of the Art to be made public and revealed; and so they ensured that the wicked should never attain them. Only those to whom God specifically reveals the Art, and to whom He gives it according to their merit, shall possess it. For the Art would be given in vain or uselessly to the unwise and the ignorant. Therefore, to those who desire and are worthy to work in this Art, we wish to give and write the entire, perfect Art in its true form, naked and uncovered, without the intrusion or interference of obscure speech. We shall lead them through a short path and bring them to an unending joy.

And for that reason, I will write this and divide it into seven chapters—neither too few nor too many, but only what is necessary and useful to know. I will write seven clear chapters for you, in which you will ultimately find the mastery of our intent and purpose. Within them, your understanding will always grow in subtlety. A clear and subtle enlightenment is always found among the <term>Philosophi: the ancient masters of alchemy</term>, whereas among the peasants <note>meaning the unlearned or those lacking spiritual refinement</note> one finds only coarseness and ignorance. If you look upon these seven chapters diligently and review them with constant, studious application, you will find therein the sense and meaning of the Philosophers and the entire understanding of the Art upon which you may found and ground yourself—moving upon it most powerfully and steadily until, through constant practice, you have drawn out the meaning and the work according to your whole will.

I have promised the Art without any omission and also without any excess, which I will write here perfectly and openly without any doubt for those who have previously worked a little in <term>sublimation: purifying a solid by turning it into vapor and back to solid</term>, <term>descension: distilling a substance by heating it from above so the liquid flows downward</term>, <term>distillation: the purification of a liquid by heating and cooling</term>, <term>fixation: making a volatile substance resistant to heat</term>, <term>calcination: heating a substance to a high temperature to reduce it to powder</term>, <term>solution: dissolving a solid into a liquid</term>, <term>coagulation: turning a liquid back into a solid</term>, and <term>incorporation: combining different substances into one unified body</term>, and in other detours and endless deceptions. Although these terms are mentioned and written throughout all the books of the Philosophers and also in other deceptive books, I say finally to those who work in the backward and deceptive arts—such as in the four <term>Spirits: volatile substances, traditionally mercury, sulfur, arsenic, and sal ammoniac</term> <note>original: "Spiritibus"</note> of <term>Alchemy</term>, and in the seven <term>Metals</term>, and also in <term>salts</term>, <term>alums</term> <note>original: "Aluminibus"</note>, <term>borax</term>, and <term>atraments: vitriols or metallic sulfates</term> <note>original: "Atramenten"</note>, as well as in all kinds of <term>marcasites: iron pyrites or similar sulfide minerals</term>, <term>tutty: zinc oxide collected from furnace flues</term>, <term>magnets</term> or <term>magnesias</term>, and in many other <term>mineral</term> things, and also in many <term>vegetables: plant-based materials</term> <note>original: "Vegetabilibus"</note>—from these things they cannot come to a successful end; and in this they are

## The First Chapter.
### The description of the Art and interpretation of Alchemy: what it actually is.

<image-desc>A decorative woodcut initial 'I' featuring floral and vine motifs.</image-desc>In many and more ancient books and writings of the Philosophers, the description and interpretation of this very Art is found quite openly; therefore, we must also take note of that same opinion and interpretation in this first chapter. ## The Second Chapter.

### Concerning the Origin of Metals.

In the words just written, I have fulfilled and completed the first chapter. Now, in the second, I will fully explain the origin of minerals or ores from the mines—how and from what they naturally first arose and were created. Regarding this, it is first to be noted that the origin of minerals, ores, or mine-works is nothing other than <term>Mercury: representing the liquid, metallic principle</term> and <term>Sulfur: representing the combustible, active principle</term>. From these two things, all <margin>Mercury ☿ Jupiter (Tin) ♃</margin> metals are created and born.

Therefore, there are many and various forms, and they are also altered, one different from another. But Nature always intended and set the goal for itself to make Gold. However, the various contrary defects that occur produce many different and inferior metals through corruption, as is clearly written and found in many books of the philosophers. According to whether the two aforementioned Sulfur and Mercury are pure or impure, the metals are created or born: namely Gold, Silver, Copper, Lead, Tin, and Iron.

<margin>Gold ☉</margin> Now, to write of Gold: it is a perfect and pure metal, created and born from a pure and <term>Fixed: stable and resistant to the fire</term> Sulfur that is clear and red; it has no defects. <margin>Silver ☽</margin> Silver is a pure metal and nearly perfect, yet not entirely so. It is created from a pure and nearly fixed Mercury, and from a clear, white, and nearly fixed Sulfur. It lacks a little <term>Coction: the alchemical "cooking" or ripening of a metal in the earth's heat</term> and <term>Fixation: the process of becoming solid and unchangeable</term>; it also lacks in color and weight. <margin>Tin ♃</margin> Tin is an impure metal and is created from a pure Mercury and a Sulfur that is partly fixed and clear...

## Chapter Five.

With plain and uncovered words, I have surely described the Matter <note>original: *Materiam*; the physical substance used in the work</note>, as well as the meaning and way to work. Now, to speak of the vessel and furnace, and how and from what they should be made: it must be noted that just as Nature cooks metals in the mountains with her natural fire, that same cooking cannot happen without a vessel or an instrument suited for it. If we intend and desire to follow Nature in her cooking, why should we not also use a vessel or dish for it? Therefore, let us first look and notice the place where the metals are born.

<margin>§</margin>
Now we may quite clearly understand and notice that in those same places in the mountains, at the very bottom, there is a steady heat that is always equally warm. It is the nature and property of heat to always rise upward. In this rising, it dries and hardens all the water it finds in the belly of the mountain and hidden in the interior of the earth. From this thickening of the water, Mercury <note>original: ☿; the fluid principle of matter</note> is made; and from that warm earth everywhere flows a fatness, and from that fatness, Sulfur <note>original: *Schwebel*; the active, combustible principle</note> is formed.

<margin>
♁ <note>Symbol for Earth or Antimony</note>
☿ <note>Symbol for Mercury</note>
4.
</margin>
And where the vapor of the Mercury (which is born from the water through heat as mentioned above) is created through that same steady warmth and cooking (which always warms and cooks equally), then various metals are born in a longer or shorter time, depending on whether the place where they are born is well or poorly suited. Above all, it should be noted that the mountain in which the metals are born is surrounded by stones and is strongly and firmly closed off everywhere. If the heat could escape or smoke out anywhere, then no metal would be born or created within it in any way.

That same vessel should be round / or spherical / and should have a small and narrow neck / and it should be of glass / or made of such an earth / that may be like glass in its nature / so that it is transparent / and the neck or small hole at the top should also be closed with such a clay or paste <note>historically called "lute," a sealant used to make vessels airtight</note> / and sealed / so that the heat may not immediately touch or affect the Matter of the <term>Mercury <note>original symbol: ☿</note></term> and Sulfur / just as the heat cannot immediately touch the minerals within a mountain. (For the earth of the mountain absorbs the heat and the glow from all sides / and thus receives the warmth everywhere.)

<margin>gloss: in a 3-fold vessel.</margin>
Likewise, in our work, the fire / or the warmth should not immediately touch / or affect / the vessel in which our proven Matter is contained / but rather one should place it in another enclosed vessel / so that the heat / below and above / and all around / may reach it in an equally tempered way. Concerning this, it is written in the book called *Lumen Luminum* <note>original Latin title meaning "The Light of Lights," a famous medieval alchemical text</note> / that is, "A Candlelight" / that the <term>Mercury <note>original symbol: ☿</note></term> should be cooked / in a threefold vessel / or glass / and also the Philosopher should, in his preparation of that same <term>Mercury</term>, remove all superfluous things / or purify it / and whatever he requires / or is necessary / that shall be fulfilled in it / through such things / shall the Art be aided and completed.

### The Sixth Chapter. Regarding the various colors / that appear in the Work.

Concerning all the colors of our Stone / as you have now heard and noted of the Matter of our Stone / and have also certainly recognized the meaning and sense / and the way of the work / through which cooking / and governance our Stone should be cooked / and also how it often and frequently shifts and transforms itself in the work into many kinds of colors / and therefore, as many colors as it has / so many names it also possesses. For according to the various colors / that appear in the work / the Philosophers have given it just as many names.

### The Fifth Chapter.

With plain / and unconcealed words / I have surely shared the <term>Matter <note>original: *Materiam*; the raw substance used to create the Philosopher's Stone</note></term>, and also the meaning and the way to work. Now, to speak of the vessel and the furnace / how and from what they should be made / it is to be noted / that just as Nature cooks the metals in the mountains with her natural fire / that same cooking cannot and may not happen without a vessel / or an instrument suitable for it. And since we intend / and have the will / to follow Nature in her cooking / why then should we not also use a vessel or container for it? Therefore, let us first look and take note of the place where metals are born.

Now we may quite clearly understand / and observe / that in those places / in the mountains / at the very bottom of the mountain's floor, there is a steady heat / which is equally warm at all times. It is the nature and property of heat that it always rises / seeking to go upward / and in that same rising / it dries and hardens everywhere the water that it finds in the belly of the mountain / and hidden in the other parts of the earth / and from that thickening of the water / <term>Mercury <note>original symbol: ☿</note></term> is made / and from that same warm earth everywhere / a "fatness" flows / and from that fatness <term>Sulfur <note>original: *Schwebel*</note></term> is made.

# Mirror of Alchemy.

...[the nature of the medicine] is that it unites and mixes with the metals in the flux <note>The "flux" refers to the molten or liquid state of the metals in the crucible.</note> when it is thrown upon them.

Now you should also know that our **Elixir** becomes so potent that it tinctures well over a thousand times a thousand parts; however, it is difficult to accomplish this by throwing it upon so many metals all at once—so that it should transform and **tincture** <note>In alchemy, to "tincture" means to fundamentally change the color and nature of a base metal into gold or silver.</note> so much metal, and penetrate it so quickly and suddenly. Therefore, I reveal to you a great and hidden secret: if you wish to tincture, do it thus: Take one part of the **Tincture** and mix it among a thousand parts of the metals that are closest to **Perfection**, and put all of this together into a vessel that is suitable for it, and seal it very well. Place it in a melting furnace according to the **philosophical manner** <note>This implies following the specific timing and heat levels established by alchemical tradition rather than common blacksmithing.</note>, and first give it a gentle fire, then strengthen the fire more and more for three consecutive days, until they have distinctly united with one another; and this is a work of three days.

After that, one should take one part of that same mixture and throw it upon another thousand parts [of metal]. This should be cast upon the metal that is closer to or possesses more **Perfection** than another; for there is always a greater and more neighborly unity and friendship between the **Elixir** and **Tincture** and the nearest perfect metal than with the metals that are further from perfection. Therefore, the nearest are always to be chosen. This is called a work or a deed of one day, or one hour, or even one moment, which is then divine. Therefore, may the Almighty God be praised forever and ever, Amen.

->A Concluding Speech and the End of this Art.<-

I have now given you in my aforementioned writings and teachings a clear and perfect treatise. It is named or called a **Mirror of Alchemy**, wherein—just as in a mirror—the meaning and secret of the entire art of alchemy appears. In this, all philosophers <note>original: "Philosophi"</note> agree <note>original: "concordieren"</note> with one another. And so this treatise of the **Mirror of Alchemy** concludes, explains, and interprets itself. Therefore, I was not mistaken to call it a "treatise," for it reveals itself as a **Mirror**. Although it is intended to teach the art, it yet hides its face from the ignorant <note>The "unbekandten" or uninitiated, whom alchemists believed would misuse the power of the Stone.</note>, while to the wise it shows the true art very beautifully and subtly. It is just as when anyone looks into a mirror: they see and recognize their own figure, which then looks back at them.

# Royal Water of the Philosophers.
<note>original: "Aqua regis Philofophorum." While standard *Aqua regia* is a mixture of nitric and hydrochloric acids known for dissolving gold, the "Philosophers'" version here uses a specific distillation process involving vitriol and salmiak.</note>

Take **vitriol** <note>Iron or copper sulfate, a key mineral in alchemy.</note> which has been calcined <note>heated to a powder</note> to a yellow color, and **saltpeter**, 2 pounds of each; **calcined alum**, 1 pound. From these, distill an **Aqua fort** <note>original: "Aquafort" (Aqua Fortis). Literally "strong water," referring to nitric acid.</note> according to the usual custom, and drive the spirits out thoroughly. Weigh this **Aqua fort**, and for every 6 ounces <note>original: "loth." A historical German unit of weight, roughly half an ounce.</note> of **Aqua fort**, add 1 ounce of **salmiak** <note>Ammonium chloride.</note>. Let it dissolve therein, and thus you have the **Royal Water of the Philosophers**.

# Essence-ified Mercury.
<note>original: "Mercurius essenfuicatus." This likely refers to mercury that has been processed into its "essential" or spiritual form through repeated purification.</note>

Take **vitriol** and **saltpeter**, equal parts of each; mix them together and let them flow gently in an earthenware vessel until the moisture has evaporated. Rub the mass into a fine powder and place it in a bowl or vessel. Inside at the bottom, place 1 pound of **quicksilver** <note>original: "Mercurium viuum."</note> in a leather cloth, and press a portion of the powder upon it; then place another layer of the powder upon that, and proceed thus **layer upon layer** <note>original: "stratum super stratum."</note> until it is all put together. Then put this mixture into a coated **flask** <note>original: "beschlagenen Kolben." A glass flask reinforced with a layer of clay or lute to withstand high heat.</note> that is equally wide throughout, with a **helm** <note>The top part of a still used for cooling vapors.</note> sealed on, and **sublimate** <note>The process of heating a substance until it becomes a vapor and then collects as a solid again in the cooler part of the apparatus.</note> the mercury out as is the custom. 

Then discard the **residue** <note>original: "feces." The solid waste material left at the bottom after distillation or sublimation.</note> and sublimate the mercury by itself, without additions, two more times, or as often as needed until it rises alone and leaves no more residue behind it.

Then take the **Royal Water of the Philosophers** and place 1 pound of this **sublimated mercury** <term>Mercury Sublimate: A highly toxic but chemically significant white crystalline powder (mercuric chloride) used in many alchemical stages.</term> into a glass flask; let it dissolve and distill it off. Once the **Aqua fort** is gone from it, drive the mercury upward; it will then dissolve into a beautiful white color, like snow. Discard the residues which remain at the bottom and are black, and pour the **Royal Water** back over the residues, and distill and sublimate again as before. Do this until no more residues remain at the bottom and the mercury is sublimated into a beautiful crystalline form. Then you have **Essence-ified Mercury**.

### USAGE.

Its use for the medicine of the human body is as follows: Take a clean quill and dip it into the Mercury of Life, and when a single drop hangs from it, let that drop fall into the following wine, so that there is always one drop per dose. # Process and Fixation of the Philosophers’ Stone <note>original: "Processus & Fixatio lapidis Philosophorum." Fixation is the process of making a volatile substance stable under heat.</note>.

Take the other half of the composition of the **Mercury of the Sun** <note>original: "Mercurij solis"; philosophical mercury joined with gold.</note> and **Mercury of Life** <note>original: "Mercurij vitæ."</note> which you previously combined and set aside; from this, draw off its **phlegm** <term>Phlegma; the watery, inactive distillate</term> with very gentle heat until one-third remains. Place it into a beautiful, clean glass flask that holds four pounds, sealed tightly with the **Hermetic Seal** <term>Sigillo hermetis; an airtight glass seal made by melting the neck of the flask shut</term>. Place it in the **vapor fire** <note>original: "Ignem vaporis"; a steam bath or moist heat</note> of the philosophical furnace, so that at first it stands within like a moor <note>A dark, muddy sediment or "sludge."</note>. Through the subtle action of the fire, it will begin to form an "island" in the middle, and thus it will decrease daily and become as black as a shoemaker’s blacking, which the **Philosophers** call the **Raven’s Head** <note>original: "Rappen Kopff" or Nigredo; the first stage of the Great Work signifying decomposition.</note>. Afterward, this becomes a **Peacock’s Tail** <note>original: "Pfawen Schwantz" or Cauda Pavonis; a stage where many iridescent colors appear.</note>, taking on all the colors that exist in the world. Subsequently, it will gain **Swan’s Feathers** <note>original: "Schwannen Federn" or Albedo; the white stage signifying purification.</note> and finally take on the **highest redness** of the whole world—an indication of its fiery nature. Through this fire, it consumes and expels all defects of the human body, and revives, restores, and renovates cold, deadened limbs to their highest degree; it also clarifies imperfect metals into the highest **degree of Gold** <note>original: "gradum Solis."</note>.

According to the opinion and meaning of all **Philosophers**, such a **preparation** occurs in one vessel, in one furnace, and in one fire, without the cessation of the vaporous heat. Then, such a medicine is most heavenly and perfect, brought forth through its own "flesh and blood" and through its innermost fire, as just recounted: to wash away all the **filth** <note>original: "Sordes."</note> of the metals and to **manifest** all the **secrets of the metals** <note>original: "occulta Metallorum."</note>.

Instead, one should divide the aforementioned fixed Stone into two parts: one part shall be used as medicine for the human body and to transform metals (as will follow in its proper place), and the other half of this Stone you shall augment thus:

One should then allow the patient to sweat, and continue this until health is restored. With this medicine, you may safely proceed in many illnesses that cannot be treated with common medicines...

# Various Particular Procedures /

## The Solution of <term>Copper</term> <note>original symbol: ♀; Venus</note> and <term>Iron</term> <note>original symbol: ♂; Mars</note>

Take 8 <term>lots</term> <note>a historical unit of weight, approximately 15–18 grams</note> of copper, or as much as you wish, and 24 lots of your water taught here; let it dissolve gradually. Note well: pour a little good wine upon it, and then a little more, so that the water does not fume away too much; do the same afterward with the iron, as you well know that it reacts violently <note>original: "reissen"; literally 'tears' or 'attacks'</note> therein. When the 24 lots of water have been poured so gradually over the copper, set it upon the ashes; let it dissolve there day and night in constant warmth. Afterward, pour the dissolved part off into a separate flask and keep it. If the copper is not all dissolved, pour more water over it again, but not as much as the first time, and let it dissolve again day and night. Pour the dissolved part to the other and keep it until you have dissolved all the copper. Afterward, take all the solutions together in a flask and place it in the <term>water bath</term> <note>original: "B. M."; Balneum Mariae, a double boiler used for gentle, even heating</note> and distill it down as strongly as possible, and pour it back onto it again. Do this three times; thus the Venus [copper] is <term>calcined</term> <note>reduced to a powder or oxide through heat</note> and prepared for the solution, to proceed further as you will hear hereafter.

You must note here that no water dissolves or extracts more than it can bear <note>a reference to the limit of chemical saturation</note>; therefore, during the dissolving, you should keep what is dissolved and pour on fresh water until the metal is entirely dissolved. Otherwise, it will fall <note>precipitate back out of the solution as a solid</note> again. You should pay attention to this in future dissolving and extracting: you should always dissolve or extract with fresh water.

### Now you are taught how to strengthen again the waters which you have used, and make them good to use again.

In this way, take 2 pounds of <term>vitriol</term> <note>original: "Vitriol"; a sulfate mineral, likely iron or copper sulfate</note> and 2 pounds of <term>alum</term> <note>original: "alaun"; a chemical compound used as a fixative and astringent</note>; crush them together, put them into a glazed pot, and place it on the fire. # Here is the second and correct solution of Copper and Iron.

To prepare the <term>Copper</term> <note>original symbol: ♀</note> or <term>Iron</term> <note>original symbol: ♂</note>, grind it nicely to a powder on a grinding stone—each one separately. Place each into a <term>flask</term> <note>original: "Kolben"; a round-bottomed glass vessel</note> and pour your prepared spirit of urine over it, four times as much as there is copper or iron. Place it on a warm <term>cupel</term> <note>original: "Capel"; here referring to a sand bath or heating dish</note> in the ashes with its receiver and <term>alembic head</term> <note>original: "Helm"; the top part of a still</note> attached. Let it dissolve day and night with a very gentle fire, so that you can almost bear the heat with your hand. Pour off what has dissolved and add fresh spirit until both are dissolved in the spirit of urine.

You must note, as mentioned before, that nothing takes in more than it can bear. The solution of copper will become so blue that it delights the eyes, and the iron as yellow as gold oil. Once they are dissolved, place each <term>crocus</term> <note>original: "Crocum"; a fine metallic powder or oxide, named for its saffron-like color</note> separately into a vial, well sealed. Let it digest in a <term>water bath</term> <term>B. M.</term> <note>original: "B. M." for *Balneum Mariae*; a vessel of warm water used to provide steady, gentle heat</note> for 14 days and nights. Then take them out to <term>fix</term> <note>original: "figieren"; to make a substance stable and non-volatile under high heat</note> each separately in the ashes, ensuring that the external fire does not exceed the internal fire, as I have often advised you. The copper will show white, yellow, and red during fixation, but the iron will become deeper in color the longer it stays. Keep them until they no longer <term>flare up</term> <note>original: "liechten"; to emit light or sparks</note> on a copper plate, which happens at most in 8 or 14 days. Thus, you have the correct crocus of copper and iron to proceed with <term>Silver</term> <note>original: "Luna" (the Moon)</note>, as you will hear hereafter.

->7.<-

# What may go wrong here.

Nothing else goes wrong here, except that they do not dissolve the iron until it is transparent, nor do they allow it to digest and fix. And what they already digest in the silver, they burn away again during refining because they only <term>cement</term> <note>original: "Zimmentieren"; a process of heating metal with powders to change its properties or purity</note> the silver once with <term>Gold</term> <note>original symbol: ☉</note>, and the <term>tincture</term> <note>the coloring agent or alchemical essence</note> in the silver is not yet properly fixed; rather, it should happen four times. They only do this: they take the thin iron plates or iron filings with vinegar and urine, without letting the scent escape, and leave them behind the stove or in the sun until eaten away into rust; this is also not bad.

Place the gold <note>original symbol: ☉</note> into this same oil until it is thoroughly <term>tinged</term> <note>original: "Tingiert"; permeated or stained with the alchemical color</note>, which you can always test on a small silver plate. When you cut one from the other, then <term>cupel</term> <note>original: "treibs ab"; to refine the metal using a cupel</note> it. ### II.

## Now I want to teach you how to fix both the Flowers of Antimony and of Sulfur.

**T**ake 8 <term>lot</term> <note>a historical German unit of weight, approximately 16 grams or half an ounce</note> of saltpeter, or as much as you wish. Put it into a flask and pour over it twice as much <term>spirit of urine</term> <note>original: "Spiritus Urine"; an ammonia-rich solution derived from fermented urine</note> as you used for the copper <note>original: "Venus"</note>. Distill it off with a gentle fire, but at the end increase the fire so that the saltpeter in the flask melts. When you see this, stop the distillation and let it cool. If the flask with the saltpeter has not broken, pour the spirit of urine back over it slowly until it is dry; for you do not need to let it melt more than once. Let it cool and pour the spirit of urine over it again. Let this happen four times, and then the saltpeter is <term>fixed</term> <note>original: "fix"; made stable under heat so it does not evaporate</note>, and it will flow onto a copper plate like wax without smoke.

Take one part of this fixed saltpeter and one part of the <term>Flowers of Antimony</term> <note>original: "Florum Antimonij"; the volatile sublimate of antimony</note> or sulfur—for it is the same process that you used with the saltpeter, or a fresh one—for you can always refresh the used spirit of urine in a <term>water bath</term> <note>original: "B. M.," abbreviation for Balneum Mariae</note> with new material, and it will be good again. Distill the spirit of urine with the Flowers of Antimony and saltpeter slowly to dryness. Pour it on again so that it dissolves. Distill it off and on like this four times, and it will flow on copper just like wax without smoke, which is no small thing.

Afterwards, take 1 lot of the fixed antimony or sulfur to 3 lot of <term>amalgam</term> <note>original: "Amalgama"; a mixture of mercury and another metal</note> made with mercury and gold <note>original: ☉</note>. Place it in a small glass to be fixed. You will accomplish more with this sulfur than you put in here, for it will <term>coagulate</term> <note>original: "Coagulieren"; to thicken or solidify</note> into a hard stone for you. As soon as you have the stone—which will happen shortly—take it out, shake everything well together, and set it back in for eight days. After that, <term>imbibe</term> <note>original: "drencks ein"; to soak or saturate a solid with a liquid</note> it and cupel it. You may also melt the fixed Flowers of Antimony and copper <note>original: "Veneris"</note> in equal weight with silver <note>original: "Luna"</note> alone several times and see what gold <note>original: ☉</note> it will give you. Note that the saltpeter and spirit of urine will fix the gold <note>original: ☉ ☉ ☉</note> for you, and the <term>sublimated mercury</term> <note>original: "Mercurij Sublimatum"</note> as well, which you should add to the saltpeter in equal weight and proceed with the spirit of urine as described; for I have experienced this with my own hands.

### Here I will teach you another Dissolution and Calcination of Gold, which you shall use instead of the first one taught for the Stone, for it is much more noble.

Take the <term>Royal Water</term> <note>original: "Aqua Regis"; a highly corrosive mixture of nitric and hydrochloric acids capable of dissolving gold</note> described previously; dissolve the gold <note>original symbol: ☉</note> in it, as much as you wish. This extraction is performed with the vinegar described hereafter, which shall be used here instead of <term>sal ammoniac</term> <note>original: "Salmiar"; ammonium chloride</note>, as taught before; by this means, all corrosive nature may be removed from the gold.

### 18.

## Now I will teach you a dry calcination of the Sun.
<note>original: "Calcination Solis"; the process of heating a metal to reduce it to a fine, friable powder.</note>

The best work of **gold** <note>original symbol: $\odot$</note> is thus: Take 1 **lot** <note>a historical unit of weight, approximately 15 grams</note> of **gold** or as much as you wish; dissolve it in an **aqua regia** <note>original: "aqua regis"; a powerful mixture of nitric and hydrochloric acids known as "royal water" because it can dissolve gold</note>. Afterward, take 6 lots of the whitest calcined **tartar** <note>original: "Weinstein"; potassium bitartrate</note>, with its salt separated from its **dregs** <note>original: "fecibus"</note>. Pour the gold solution onto the 6 lots of salt gently, so that it [remains] therein; distill the water quite strongly from it in a sand bath. Then, from the gold and salt, a yellow stone will remain for you; take it out and grind it in a mortar. Add 2 lots of well-ground **cinnabar** <note>mercury sulfide</note>—the longer it is ground, the better. Place it in a **calcining dish** <note>original: "treibscherben"; a shallow ceramic dish used for high-heat processes</note>, spread out very well, and place another dish on top of it, carefully **sealed with lute** <note>original: "verlutiert"; an airtight sealant made of clay or paste to prevent vapors from escaping</note>. You do not need to make a small hole on top; set it in a **reverberatory furnace** <note>original: "referber ofen"; a furnace that reflects heat from the roof onto the material</note>. Begin to fire it gradually with coals, ever stronger, until you see a **blue smoke** begin to rise. Then keep the fire steady, always driving it as long as you see the blue fire. And when the blue fire has passed, begin to fire with wood for 12 hours. Afterward, let it cool and take it out; weigh it then. You must note here how much salt you should add; grind it again and add 2 lots of cinnabar into it, and once more it is set and driven as at first; afterward do it once more, so that it happens for a third time.

Afterward, take the gold along with the tartar and put it in a flask, and pour fresh water upon it; then the salt dissolves from the gold, and the [gold] falls to the bottom in the most subtle powder. Gently pour off the dissolved [liquid]. And if the salt of tartar should appear yellow during the dissolving, then distill the water strongly away from it again into a stone in the sand; and afterward take a common, good **spirit of wine** <note>original: "Spiritum Vini"; concentrated alcohol</note> without **phlegm** <note>original: "phlegma"; watery, inactive residue</note>, and extract the gold with the salt using the spirit of wine. Pour it off from the other **calx of gold** <note>original: "$\odot$ kalch"; the fine powder resulting from calcination</note>, so that the gold is all diligently carried up from the salt with the water; thus you have the true, high calcined gold which I have experienced. Then take your previously taught high spirit of wine and pour it onto the gold calx; and if the spirit of wine does not draw out the gold into a **magistery** <note>original: "magisterium"; a potent medicinal essence</note> and the **quintessence** <note>original: "quintam essentiam"; the purest, most concentrated essence of a substance</note>, even if an angel came from heaven, I would not believe that the gold could be broken down without **corrosives** <note>original: "corrosiuis"</note>, etc. Every quintessence of the sun tinges [transmutes] gold and **mercury** <note>original symbol: $\mercury$</note> into Sun [gold], which you should note, etc.

## Concerning Red.

Likewise, if you wish to truly turn the white earth, or white tincture, or white elixir, into a red elixir—that is the red tincture—with which you may tincture <note>original: "Tingieren"; to dye or transform the color and nature of a substance</note> silver and all other metals, and also red mercury, and transform them into true fine gold; and this tincture shall also be cast upon silver in a wax <note>a "wax-like" state achieved so the medicine melts into the metal without evaporating</note> with all management of the fire, just as with the white tincture, and after the tincturing, it should also be refined in lead upon the cupel <term>cupel; a shallow, porous bowl used in assaying to separate precious metals from base metals like lead</term>, at the flash, etc.

The Natural Masters say this tincture is black in the beginning, white in the middle, and after the white, it becomes red or gold-colored with strong fire.

Another philosopher says thus: heat acting within moisture creates a blackness at first, and the blackness works into dryness, thus creating a whiteness; thereafter, with great fire, it becomes yellow; then, if the fire is strengthened even further, it is brought to a beautiful redness, and is fixed <term>fixed; resistant to the fire and no longer volatile</term> and gold-colored. It is called red coral <note>original: "Corallium"</note>, and the surplus is called red sulfur <note>original: "Rubeum sulphuris"</note>, red orpiment <note>original: "Rubeum aucipigmentum"; orpiment is a gold-colored arsenic mineral</note>, and if it remains white, it is called lead of the ore <note>original: "Plumbum æris"</note>, and the virgin of the metals <note>original: "virgo metallorum"</note>, the ingot, or the thin plate <note>original: "lamina"</note>. These are the names the philosophers have given to this tincture or elixir.

Furthermore, it is to be noted regarding this praiseworthy medicine or remedy for the human body, with which all bodily sickness may be driven out by this most powerful tincture.

Furthermore, there are some fools who say they can make potable gold <term>Aurum potabile; literally "drinkable gold," an alchemical life-elixir believed to cure all ills</term> from common gold alone, and that it should be the best medicine to heal all diseases. There are also some physicians so deceitful as to say it is the best for healing all diseases. This is all against nature, and it is not truly potable gold. They also say it is quite good for the sick person to buy [gold], and then one should show the gold to the sick person, for looking at gold serves the sick person well; but that it creates health is not true. However, the true potable gold exists perfectly in the power of the Elixir; it is a medicine that drives out all excess diseases in the human body.

This is the noblest medicine for all people, and it was also the opinion of all philosophers and natural masters, and still is for those who understand it, from

## Arnold speaks.

Likewise, it also possesses a powerful virtue to heal illnesses beyond all other medicines, for it cheers the spirit <note>original: "gemieht"; referring to the mind, soul, or emotional state</note> of the person who takes it and drives away old age. It also drives out all "evil moisture" <note>harmful or "corrupt" bodily fluids</note> from the human body. And whoever carries it upon them shall overcome all strife; for Plato says, whoever has these gifts of God has the secrets, for he has come to the end of wealth and has broken this bond of poverty—that is, he has the power to transform all perfect metals into pure, fine gold and silver, and also that he may maintain a person in the health of their life.

## What the Elixir demonstrates.

When one gives it to a person, a dose as heavy as a mustard seed, it wards off fever; and if a leper takes it during the four seasons of the year, he will become healthy from the leprosy; and if a leper takes the Red Elixir within a year, such as in March, he will become healthy. And when a person takes of the elixir, whether the White or the Red, it heals the stroke <note>original: "den Schlag"; refers to apoplexy or sudden paralysis</note>. And if the elixir is held before the nose of women at the time of birth, she will not fail in the birth and will be delivered; so says Hermes, the wise master.

He who uses the elixir lives without illness until his appointed term, as has been set for him by God. The Natural Masters say: he who takes the Red Elixir, it drives all illnesses from him, from the crown of his head to the soles of his feet. For just as this elixir takes metals that are not perfect and makes them perfect into true gold or silver, so it also does for the human being. Therefore, this elixir, both the White and the Red, is called our blessed and consecrated stone; for God Himself has spoken well of it. <note>original: "curius auff"; it rises up remarkably or clearly.</note> and becomes white as snow. Let the glass cool down on its own. (Beware of the dust, for it has become poison!) Scrape off the Mercury <note>original: symbol $\text{\char"263F}$</note> and grind it into a fine powder.

### AUGMENTATION <note>original: "A V G M E N T A T I O"; the process of increasing the quantity or potency of the alchemical medicine</note>.

Take the sublimated Mercury <note>original: symbol $\text{\char"263F}$</note>, as described above, and make it "living" again using vinegar. Always add a third part of this to the Tincture; do this for all eternity. If you wish to work the substance to its highest degree: once the Tincture has become white, use only the fire, making it so weak that you can endure the heat on your hand for an hour. Do this for ten or twelve days. Then the entire Work will become "alive" and will allow itself to be coagulated—that is, to become hard—once more. Take care to use good quality glass, for the substance becomes so noble and so subtle <term>subtle; in alchemy, having the power to penetrate or flow through solid matter</term> that it flows through everything.

When you wish to perform the Tingeing <term>tingeing; the act of transmuting a base metal into silver or gold using the tincture</term>, take sixty parts of well-washed Mercury in a crucible <term>crucible; a ceramic or metal container used for melting materials at high temperatures</term>. Let it get hot. When it chatters <note>original: "plodert"; likely bubbling or making a crackling sound</note> in the crucible and smokes, cast one part [of the Tincture] upon it. Heap many coals around it and drive the heat with a bellows. It will then flow like a metal that is steadfast in every assay <note>original: "Probieren"; the testing of ore or metal for purity</note>.

The colors appear in this way: when the work stands for 12 or 14 weeks, it becomes completely black, looking like soot on top. Let it stand like that, and the Mercury <term>represented by the symbol ☿</term> will absorb the powder back into itself; it becomes smooth on top and begins to turn grey. Afterward, "taps" <note>likely crystalline growths or protrusions</note> emerge from the mass which are white. Let it stand, and these "taps" will settle again, and it becomes completely white—whiter than any silver. If you wish then to perform a white tincture <note>the process of transmuting base metals into silver</note>, you must begin the tincture there and proceed as described above. If you want to reach the red <note>the stage for transmuting into gold</note>, let it stand; it will change from a white color to a yellow color. It will "skin over" and look like feathers. Afterward, it throws up a brown powder, more and more from day to day; these powders are the "sulfur of gold" <term>Sulfur of Gold; in alchemical theory, this is the active, combustible principle or 'soul' extracted from the metal</term>. The higher the gold has risen, the more powder there will be, and the longer it stands. Let that stand, and the brown powder will quickly disappear and remain entirely brown, looking like nothing but a powder. However, open the air-holes in the furnace wider, fill the furnace with coals, and let the tincture melt and become a "body" <note>a solid mass</note>. Perform the tincture as described above; you will recognize when it has melted because the material will become completely level. At that point, it is "ripe" <note>ready for use</note>.

## POTABLE GOLD <note>original: "AVRVM POTABILE"</note>

Have a good wine distilled eight or nine times, always ensuring the wine boils during the draw-off. Thus the wine becomes very strong and as noble as if it were spiced. Take the red tincture, grind it very finely, and put the tincture into the wine. Place the small glass in warm ashes so that heat is applied; then the tincture dissolves and becomes just like the wine in substance, but it colors the wine gold. This is the true "Potable Gold" <term>Aurum potabile; a legendary alchemical medicine consisting of gold dissolved in alcohol, believed to be a panacea for all diseases</term> for all illnesses.

I found this piece years ago at the castle in Weißensteck in a chest full of medicines. I do not know what to make of it, but the "conjunction" <note>the joining or chemical union</note> of the two Mercuries—Gold <note>represented by the symbol ☉</note> and Silver <note>represented by the symbol ☽</note>—pleases me well enough.

# In the name of the Almighty / begin happily to bring your work to completion.

First / make an **aqua regia** <term>King's Water; a powerful mixture of acids capable of dissolving gold</term> / from 1 part yellow calcined **Vitriol** <note>sulfuric acid precursors</note> / and one part **Saltpeter** / prepare it as you know how / and drive it through an **alembic** <term>a distilling apparatus consisting of two vessels connected by a tube</term> for 24 hours / so that the **caput mortuum** <term>literally "dead head"; the useless solid residue left over after distillation</term> is burnt quite dry / into this water add a 4th part of **sal ammoniac** / set it on warm sand / and let it dissolve. Afterward, take these crystals of **Gold** <note>represented by the symbol ☉</note> or **Silver** <note>represented by the symbol ☽</note> and put them in a vial with a long neck / and then take an equal weight of **sal ammoniac**, water, and **oil of tartar** <term>a concentrated solution of potassium carbonate</term> / you must first pour them together into a glass / and you must **putrefy** <term>a process of slow digestion or rotting through gentle heat</term> it in a water bath for 8 days / and afterward filter it quite clean / for it deposits many **feces** <note>original: "fæces"; the dregs or impurities</note> during the putrefaction / and when this has been done / pour the three aforementioned parts together / and set it in a water bath to putrefy / but it is better / putrefied in its proper fire / namely in **philosophers' dung** <term>a bed of fermenting horse manure, which provided a steady, gentle heat for alchemical digestion</term> / keep it in such putrefaction for 40 days / and for as long as it takes until it begins to turn black / the blacker it is / the more it is corrupted / small crystals also tend to sprout in the vial / but do not take it out before 40 days have passed / then turn it into a **Mercury** / in which Mercury the entire mastery of this art is accomplished / for in it we have everything that we desire / etc.

> For it is certain that every thing is made from that into which it is dissolved; but all metals can be reduced back into mercury, or quicksilver. Therefore, they were originally quicksilver. <note>original: "Certum enim est, quod omnis res est ex eo, in quod resoluitur sed omnia metalla reducuntur in mercurium, seu argentum viuum. For this Mercury is the beginning / the **root**, Mother, and origin of all metals, both the perfect and the imperfect / and know that in it alone the very greatest secrets are hidden / and in no other / **for in mercury is whatever the wise men seek.** <note>original: "est enim in mercurio, quicquid quærunt sapientes."</note>

Then Geber speaks: it is highly necessary for every lover of this Art to have a whole, steady will in our Work, and not to take up many different things—now this, now trying another—for our Art cannot be completed in many things. For there is but one Stone, one Medicine, and it is composed of no external things; rather, we cast away its superfluity during its preparation.

Therefore, every person must be steadfast in this Art and attend to their work with gentleness <note>or "patience"</note> without any anger, and not leave off from the work once begun until they reach the perfect end.

Therefore, every seeker of this Art should know the beginning and root of the nature and way of our Art or Work; for whoever does not know the beginning cannot come to the end. And I will reveal the beginning to you with a very clear speech, so that you know how to conduct yourself in all your undertakings. **Make the fixed volatile, and the volatile fixed, and unless bodies are made bodiless, and vice-versa, you shall achieve nothing.** <note>original Latin: "Fac fixum volatile, & volatile fixum, & nisi fiant corpora incorporea, & econuerso, nihil efficies." This is a core alchemical principle: solid matter must be spiritualized (vaporized) and spirits must be solidified.</note>

Once it has putrefied <note>the process of "rotting" or breaking down the substance through gentle heat</note> for 40 days, take it out and open the vial <note>original: "Viol"</note> again. Pour it all together into a clean glass bowl and pour warm distilled rainwater over it. Wash the salts <term>salia; chemical salts or impurities produced during the chemical reaction</term> very well from it in the most subtle way. Mark well that you wash the salts from it cleanly, otherwise it will ruin everything during the sublimation; therefore, you must perform the washing <note>original: "absüssen," literally "sweetening," a term for washing out acid or salt</note> with all diligence.

Once the salts are washed quite clean, place the bowl with the material on warm sand and make it very fine and dry, even to the utmost dryness. When that is done, put the material into a coated, long sublimation flask <note>a "sublimir Kolben" is a vessel used to heat a solid until it turns into vapor and collects again at the top</note>—the longer the better. Place a helm <note>the "alembic" or cap of the still</note> on top, but do not seal it with lute <term>verlutiert; an airtight seal made of clay or paste</term>. Place it in a sand-bath <note>original: "Capell mit Sandt"</note> and give it a very little fire, so that the sand only begins to get warm for six hours. After that, strengthen the fire a little for another six hours; then again for six hours more; and for the last six hours, maintain it so that the sand at the bottom of the bath glows.

When you have thus sublimated the material for 24 hours, let the glass cool well. Then remove the sublimated material; take it out finely and subtly into a fine glass bowl and pour a little good distilled wine-vinegar over it—yet not too much, but so that it becomes like a dough. Begin to rub it with a finger, and it will begin to vivify <term>vifuicieren; to "bring to life," specifically returning a metallic substance to its liquid form</term> into a mercury <term>☿; quicksilver</term>. Thereafter, every month, add as much crude Mercury as the material weighs, and each time fix it again in the same manner as before. Or, take half the material or as much as you wish each month and add as much crude Mercury as the material weighs. Let the other portion flow in a crucible with Borax <term>Borras; a flux used to help metals melt</term> into a Body <term>Corpus; a solid piece of metal</term>.

# Process for the tincture,

And note: the first time you begin with crude Mercury <note>original: "☿ crudo"; quicksilver in its raw, liquid state</note> and perform the augmentation, you should add only half the amount of the medicine. But thereafter, every month—as mentioned above—you will have a thorough report of the two augmentations for Red and White <note>the two stages of the Philosopher's Stone: the White Stone for silver and the Red Stone for gold</note>, which proceed upon the right and true ground and foundation. Those, however, who go outside this foundation—whether they be "Particulars" <note>alchemists who seek only to transmute specific metals rather than achieve the Universal Medicine</note> or whatever they call themselves—are all liars, as all the Philosophers <note>the ancient alchemical authorities</note> say.

If you wish to use the aforementioned Mercury for your Universal <note>the "Universal Medicine" or the Philosopher's Stone</note>, mark this secret: you must sublimate the Mercury seven more times with white calcined tartar <term>Tartaro; the potassium bitartrate crust from wine barrels, burned (calcined) to a white powder</term>. Each time, take the same weight of fresh, white calcined tartar as the Mercury weighs. You must perform this sublimation with the tartar six times, and the seventh time you must sublimate the Mercury by itself. Note that such a sublimation serves to make it much more readily turn into a Water and Oil during the work, which otherwise does not happen except through this purgation <note>cleansing or purification</note>. It requires only this and no other for the Universal work; however, for the aforementioned augmentation, it does not require such purgation.

Now I will teach you how you shall bring your divine secret to a fruitful end, without any falsehood or deception, and it is quite easy and simple.

Now take this purged Mercury and dry it on warm sand in a fine glass bowl, so that no moisture remains. Afterward, press it through a leather one or three times back into a clean glass bowl, in the finest and most subtle way, ensuring nothing foreign is added. Then take it, thus purified, and put it into such a round glass as illustrated here:

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration of a round-bottomed glass flask with a vertical neck, shaded with fine horizontal lines to represent volume.</image-desc>

which should be strong and perfectly circular. Seal it well with the Seal of Hermes <term>Sigillo Hermetis; a method of hermetically sealing a glass vessel by melting the glass neck shut with a torch</term>, and take great care that no impure particle falls inside. Also note that three parts of the glass must remain empty, as was taught in the fixation of the augmentation. *Marvelous above all else, that in one fire and one vessel there occurs distillation, sublimation, mortification, calcination, reddening, and fusion, in solutions and coagulations and elsewhere.* <note>original: "super omne mirum, quod vno igne & vno vaſe fit deſtilatio, ſublimatio, mortificatio, calcinatio, rubificatio, fuſio, in ſolutionibus & coagulationibus & alibi."</note>

*It is sufficient to place the stone in our vessel once and close it until the whole mastery is completed, and elsewhere. Likewise, our stone, as the philosophers say, is made from one thing and in one vessel, and they speak the truth.* <note>original: "Sufficit lapidem in noſtro vaſe ſemel ponere et claudere, quouſque totum compleatur magiſterium, & alibi. Item lapis noſter vt dicunt philoſophi fit ex vna re, & in vno vaſe, & verum dicunt."</note>

<meta>This page continues the specific instructions for preparing the "Universal Medicine." # Process for the tincture,

For the round glass in which you place your Material <note>original: "Materiam"</note>, have a round wooden sphere made of good oak wood. This sphere should be large enough that the glass has plenty of room to stand. Note that the glass should sit upon a tripod <note>original: "Tryfuß"</note> wrapped in cotton. Furthermore, the space between the glass and the wooden sphere must be three fingers' breadth <note>original: "drey zwerch Finger"</note> all around, so that the vapors and the heat can circulate and move one another.

Also, note this secret regarding the wooden sphere: the bottom half, upon which it stands, must be full of holes up to about two fingers' breadth from the bottom center. These holes should be approximately the size of a large cherry pit <note>original: "Kirse kern"</note>. The other half (the top) must be solid and have no holes, so that this vaporous heat can operate correctly according to nature. Now, take this sphere along with the glass containing the material and place it in your fire—specifically in dung <note>original: "Fimum"; horse manure was frequently used in alchemy as a source of gentle, consistent heat</note>, as you will be taught later.

Inside, the Mercury <term>☿; the metallic principle or quicksilver</term> will gently begin to rise over eight or more days because of the vaporous mists and steady heat. From day to day, it gradually ascends, driven by the constant, moving warmth. Through this means, the Mercury dissolves <note>original: "soluirt"</note> into its own Water. That which is dissolved becomes "joyful" <note>or "volatile/light"</note> and rises gradually into its sphere, lifting itself and settling at the top of the glass in a circle, like dew. However, this does not happen all at once, but so slowly that one can hardly notice it.

As Arnold <note>Arnold of Villanova (c. 1240–1311), a celebrated physician and alchemist</note> says in his *Rosary* <note>The "Rosarium Philosophorum," a famous alchemical treatise</note>: "In our work, putrefaction <note>the breakdown or 'rotting' of a substance to release its essence</note> is necessary, because nothing ever grows—neither plant nor animal—except after putrefaction. If there is no putrefaction, it cannot be dissolved, and if it is not dissolved, it is reduced to nothing. Our putrefaction is not filthy or unclean, but is the mixing of water with earth."

For it rises only into the heights like a dew; it does not flow down the glass like alum or water. First, the Water dissolves the body, which happens because of the Oil; therefore it is called an "unctuous vapor" <term>Vapor vnctuosus; an oily or fatty steam believed to hold the "soul" of the matter</term>. This vapor is heavier to raise than water. Thus, the water dissolves, the air sublimates, the fire liquefies, and the earth coagulates. In this way, the four elements bring forth their effects through the medium of heat, and each is hurried to perform its office for the advancement of the generation <note>the "birth" of the Philosopher's Stone</note>.

Thus, the body is brought through itself, as has been said: It dissolves itself, it brings itself to life, and it kills itself without ceasing. In this process, all methods occur: namely sublimation, distillation, solution, coagulation, fixation, and so on. Therefore, our "grinding" <note>original: "contritio"; the breaking down of the substance</note> is not done with hands, but by the strongest boiling <note>original: "decoctione"</note>.

# Process for the tincture,

Nature alone performs all of this through the medium of its constant heat, which drives the Natural Elements so that they are separated in their transformation. For they do not depart from one another, so that the separation is nothing other than a transformation of one into the other: from Water, Air is born; from Air, Fire; and from Fire, the Earth is returned once more. <note>Aristotle says: "When you have water from air, air from fire, fire from earth, then you will have the full art." (original Latin: *Arift: Cum habueris aquam ex aere, aerem ex igne, ignem ex terra, tunc habebis plenam artem.*)</note> They are not separated for any reason other than transformation, though it is called a separation. Furthermore, Nature fixes itself back together without any discord, so that in this Work, **Body**, **Soul**, and **Spirit** are separated; for the **Spirit** is the seat and dwelling-place of the **Soul**, in which it rests.

For the moisture from the **Spirit** is like water, and the moisture from the **Soul** is like oil <note>The text notes: "an unctuous vapor is our stone" (original: *vapor vnctuosus est lapis noster*)</note>. Therefore, the **Soul** is a bond of the **Spirit**, just as the **Body** is a bond of the **Soul**; yet even then, that bond is nothing compared to the bond of Nature.

Our whole operation is nothing other than the extraction of water from the earth and the sending of this water back down upon the earth until the earth putrefies <term>putrefaction: a stage of decomposition or chemical breakdown often associated with the color black</term>. For this earth putrefies and is purified with the water. When it has been purified, the entire mastery is completed with the help of the divinity. <note>original: *Tota operatio nostra non est aliud nisi extractio aquæ à terra, & huius aquæ super terram dimissio, donec terra putrefiat. Hæc enim terra cum aqua putrefit & mundificatur : Cum mundata fuerit, auxilio diuinitatis totum magisterium perficitur.*</note> And elsewhere: "The Spirit of the Lord hovered over the waters." <note>original: *Spiritus domini ferebatur super aquas.*</note>

<margin>
Sublimation:
**Body**
**Spirit**
**Soul**.
</margin>
For just as in the creation of the world, water existed first and the Spirit of God hovered over it, so it is also at the beginning of this work in the Sublimation <term>sublimation: the process of heating a substance until it becomes a vapor and then solidifies again, used here to represent purification</term>. It moves up and down until it has entirely dissolved <note>original: "Soluiert"</note> its **Body** into a beautiful, transparent water, just like a crystal. Our water is nothing other than a vapor or mist, which is called Air, and which has gradually risen on high, departing from the corporeal water into the circle of the sphere, like dew. "The wind carried it in its belly," <note>original: *Portauit illum ventus in ventre suo*</note> and elsewhere: "It ascends from the earth to the heaven, and descends again to the earth, and receives the power of the things above and the things below." <note>original: *Ascendit enim à terra in cælum, iterumque descendit in terram, & recipit vim superiorum & infernorum* — these are famous quotes from the *Emerald Tablet*, a foundational hermetic text.</note> But through the long action and the steady, unceasing heat of its rising and falling, it becomes slightly thicker the longer it continues. Yet understand that this does not happen quickly; for the entire **Body** must first have been at the height of its circle, and only then will it begin to grow thicker and browner. And even if it were difficult for any of the **Body** to remain, the heat ultimately consumes it so that it becomes Spiritual. And I say to you in Divine Truth: the Art is nothing other than dissolving <note>original: "Soluieren"</note> and coagulating <note>original: "Coagulieren"</note> the stone, which occurs solely through Putrefaction.

# Process for the tincture,
Sig: Ll
<meta>catchword: in</meta>

The practitioner of our work must first dissolve the stone, then coagulate it <note>original Latin: *lapidem soluere, deinde coagulare*</note>, because our work is nothing other than making a perfect solution and coagulation. Unless everything is changed from earth into water, perfection can in no way be reached. Both of these—namely the dissolution of the body and the coagulation of the spirit—occur in one single operation, and one does not happen without the other. Therefore, gold and silver are dissolved; to dissolve the body and coagulate the spirit is the work of maturation.

Know also that dissolution and coagulation are different in concept, yet they have only one single operation, namely through the medium of heat. For as soon as the substance has dissolved, it has also completed its coagulation. If you diligently inspect the words of wisdom, you will easily be able to understand it, for of this they have said: that this arrangement is a change of nature and a subtle arrangement and wonderful mixing of natural things—of heat and moisture with cold and dryness.

This is that arrangement which cannot be completed by human hands alone <note>original Latin: *Hæc est illa dispositio quod manibus perfici non potest*</note>.

Now when you see here that everything begins to stand still at the bottom and no longer rises, then it has completed the conjunction <term>conjunction: the alchemical marriage or union of opposites, such as spirit and body</term>. For it becomes thicker and thicker, because the Elements, along with the Soul and the Spirit, join the spiritual Body back together into one. It is an **incombustible oil** <term>oleum incombustibile: an oil that cannot be consumed or destroyed by fire</term>, and if you dip a glowing piece of Luna <note>original: "Lunam"; the alchemical name for silver</note> into this oil, it will immediately become Gold <note>original symbol: ☉</note>. But it is not necessary to open your glass vessel if you want your work to be perfect. For know that this oil no longer leaves its various parts, because gold is nothing other than a prepared, fixed oil, so that no injury can happen to it in the fire. Therefore, the extracted fatness of the oil is a **Tincture** <term>tincture: a potent alchemical substance capable of "staining" or transforming the nature of other metals</term>, for the fatness belongs to the Soul, which extracts itself with difficulty, and only very slowly and subtly, as all philosophers write.

Its complexion is tempered and its nature directed in heat, cold, moisture, and dryness. You will find nothing superfluous or diminished in it. Air nourishes fire, just as water nourishes the earth; fix the earth with water, so that the air can be fixed into the water. For if you have "killed" the water well, you have also killed the elements, and they are dead <note>In alchemy, to "kill" a substance often means to fix it or strip it of its volatile, moving nature</note>.

Now when the oil has become lemon-brown in its fire, it takes on a fiery nature and ignites, penetrating what was hidden in its interior at the beginning. And thus it is the cause of retaining water and air <note>original Latin: *Et sic est causa retinendi aquam & aerem*</note>.

# Process for the tincture,

<margin>//</margin>All of this is accomplished by Nature alone, by means of its constant heat, which drives the natural elements forward so that they are separated in their transformation. Yet they do not truly depart from one another; rather, the separation is nothing other than a transformation of one into the other. From the Water, Air is born; from the Air, Fire; and from the Fire, the Earth is returned. <note>original Latin: "Arist: Cum habueris aquam ex aere, aerem ex igne, ignem ex terra , tunc habebis plenam artem." / "Aristotle: When you have water from air, air from fire, fire from earth, then you will have the full art."</note> <margin>//</margin> For they are not separated for the sake of being apart; it is called a "separation" because of the transformation. Nature also fixes <term>fixes: to make a volatile substance solid or resistant to heat</term> itself back together without any discord, so that in this Work, the Body, Soul, and Spirit are separated—for the Spirit is the seat and dwelling place of the Soul, in which it rests.

<margin>//</margin>Furthermore, the moisture from the Spirit is like Water, and the moisture from the Soul is like Oil <note>original Latin: "vapor vnctuosus est lapis noster" / "Our stone is an oily vapor."</note>. Therefore, the Soul is a bond of the Spirit, just as the Body is a bond of the Soul; yet that bond is nothing compared to the bond of Nature.

Our whole operation is nothing other than the extraction of water from the earth, and the sending of this water back onto the earth, until the earth putrefies <note>original Latin: "Tota operatio nostra non est aliud nisi extractio aquæ à terra, & huius aquæ super terram dimissio, donec terra putrefiat."</note>. For this earth rots and is purified with water: when it has been purified, the whole mastery is completed with the help of divinity <note>original Latin: "Hæc enim terra cum aqua putrefit & mundificatur: Cum mundata fuerit, auxilio diuinitatis totum magisterium perficitur."</note>. And elsewhere: The spirit of the Lord was carried over the waters <note>original Latin: "Spiritus domini ferebatur super aquas." A reference to the Book of Genesis.</note>.

<margin>Sublimation:
Body: Dissolve:
Coagulate.</margin>For just as it was in the Creation of the World—where first there was the water, and the Spirit of God hovered over it—so it is also at the beginning of this Work during the Sublimation <term>sublimation: the process where a solid turns into vapor and settles again, used here to describe spiritual refinement</term>. For the substance moves upward and downward for so long until it has entirely dissolved <note>original: "Soluiert"</note> its Body into a beautiful, transparent water, just like a crystal. Our water is nothing else than a vapor or steam which is called "Air," and which has gradually risen up individually. From the physical Water, it enters into the roundness of the sphere, like the Dew. The wind carried it in its belly <note>original Latin: "Portauit illum ventus in ventre suo." A famous line from the Emerald Tablet of Hermes Trismegistus.</note> and elsewhere: For it ascends from the earth to the heaven, and again descends to the earth, and receives the power of things above and things below <note>original Latin: "Ascendit enim à terra in cælum , iterumque descendit in terram, & recipit vim superiorum & infernorum."</note>. But through the long action and constant, unceasing heat of its rising and falling, it becomes a little thicker as time goes on. However, understand that this does not happen immediately; for the entire Body must first have been at the height of its circle, and only then does it begin to grow thicker and browner. And if it should happen that something of the Body remains, the process ultimately consumes it so that it becomes Spiritual. And I say to you in Divine Truth: the Art is nothing other than dissolving and coagulating the Stone, which occurs solely through Putrefaction <term>putrefaction: the alchemical stage of "blackness" or decay, seen as a necessary death before the substance is reborn and purified</term>.

...into an oil [transformed] from combustion, and an oil for the sake of retaining the tincture of moisture—which is the cause of the appearance of colors—and thus it will bring the sharp <note>original German: "spißige". And if you understand well, here lies our entire philosophy. Note that in the hidden part of our stone is heat and dryness, and in the manifest <note>The "manifest" is the outward, observable nature of the substance, while the "hidden" is its internal, potential power.</note> part is coldness and humidity. Therefore, it is necessary that the manifest be hidden, and the heat, which is in the hidden part, is the element of oil, which is dry; for this dryness fixes, and the dryness of the fire tints. However, that which is in the manifest is coldness and humidity. Therefore, one must have a proportion between these, so that the coldness and humidity are tempered by the heat and dryness that were in the hidden part. That certain coldness and humidity is a watery and burning smoke, which corrupts and gives birth to blackness. This stone is of one virtue and nature in the hidden part, and another in the manifest; but in a complete mixture, it is of the same virtue and nature. And thus the <term>Spirit: the volatile essence of the substance</term> is changed into a most noble Body, then becomes flowing and an Oil, which is a true tincture—multiplying, consolidating, heating, declaring, purging, and confirming.

Know from then on that you must govern the vapors without ceasing and not let them stand still, to be renewed over the fifth day, as you will be taught hereafter regarding the furnace. And finally, when the <term>fixation: the process of making a volatile substance stable and resistant to fire</term> begins, a small skin will form on the oil, which from day to day becomes deeper and deeper; it also finally falls slowly to the bottom, like a yellow, subtle sand. It begins to be seen more and more until it has all fallen. Let it stand thus in its warmth, and it will begin slowly to become gray-black. Then give it its fire continuously until it turns away from the black color again and changes into a pure, clear white. And when the true white comes, you will see all kinds of wonderful colors in the glass, like small streams rising up from the matter; as soon as one has barely passed, another comes in its place.
