...is converted, and after the middle stage many colors appear, and various ones at that; however, the end of all these is the whitening [dealbatio], for whiteness is the goal. Indeed, in the mixing of the Water and the Body of the prepared ferment of the body, infinite colors appear; and thus it appears that it is one mastery [magisterium], from one, and with one, and thus from four and from three, it becomes one. Likewise, whitening is the beginning of the work and the foundation of the whole Body; nor then is it varied into diverse colors except into red, in which is the ultimate goal. <note>The author is describing the alchemical "Peacock's Tail" (cauda pavonis), a stage where many colors appear before the matter settles into pure white, then finally red.</note>

When you now see that it is thus completely snow-white, then you have the noble, true, White Philosophical Stone in its white stage. Note here a great secret [Secretum]: when you have thus completed your Medicine upon the white with the help of the Almighty, you must arrange for one part Medicine, 1000 parts <term>Lime of the Moon</term> <note>original: "Calcis Lunae." This refers to silver that has been reduced to a fine powder or "ash" through calcination (heating).</note>; and to those 1000 parts of <gloss>Silver Lime</gloss> <note>original symbol: ☾, representing the Moon or silver.</note> take only one part of your white Medicine, and rub them well together on a smooth, subtle grinding stone. Put all this together into a well-luted <note>The "lute" was a paste used to seal the vessel airtight so no spirits could escape.</note> crucible and place it in a wind furnace. Give it a gentle fire so that the crucible glows a dull brown for three days and three nights continuously. When that is done, give it a strong fire and let it flow for three hours. 

Then note that no Medicine—even if it has been brought to its power and Philosophical perfection—can yet enter into any metal, neither into the perfect nor imperfect bodies, without the medium <note>A "medium" is an intermediary substance that allows the concentrated alchemical medicine to "join" with the larger mass of metal.</note>. For the "entry" must happen through the medium; for even if the Medicine is thrown onto molten metal without the medium, and you let it melt for 10 years, it still does not enter without the aforementioned medium. Because of its great purity, it floats on top like an oil on water. And note well this great secret, as just mentioned: that the Medicine glows brown for 3 days and nights, and do not let it melt before the 3 days and nights are over. For if it were to melt for 3 days and nights, the Medicine is so penetrating that it would go through the crucible. And finally, when it has flowed for 3 hours as mentioned, let it cool by itself, break the crucible, and take it out; then it is as brittle as glass, for it is still a Medicine.

Take then of this molten white Medicine and throw it again upon 1000 parts of <term>Tin</term> <note>original symbol: ♃, the sign for Jupiter or Tin.</note> or <term>Copper</term> <note>original symbol: ♀, the sign for Venus or Copper.</note>. When it flows in the flux, it tinctures <note>Transmutes or dyes the inner nature.</note> all these 1000 parts into eternally fine, stable Silver [Lunam]. Should they, however, be un-malleable [brittle] when you have thrown this Medicine in and it has flowed together for an hour, reach into the crucible with an iron wire, and whatever hangs onto it, hammer it thin on an anvil; then you will soon see whether it is still un-malleable or not.

# Process for the tincture, 269

If you wish to use it for Luna <note>original symbol: ☽ (Silver)</note>, save it; for note that the Medicine for the Cure <note>The final alchemical substance</note> requires no further preparation. But for the Tincture, you must proceed in the same way with 1,000 parts of *Gold Calx* <term>Calcis solis: gold reduced to a fine powder through heating</term> to one part of the Medicine, driven together on a clear, pure refining stone which is subtle, and placed in a well-luted <note>Sealed with clay or "lute" to make it airtight</note> crucible. Then, for 3 days and nights, just as you were taught before regarding the White Medicine, let it glow brown. Afterward, let them flow together for 3 hours, so the Medicine unites with the Gold Calx, draws it into itself, and remains brittle, breaking like glass. This is the very first thing prepared for the Tincture of the bodies.

From such melted and brittle Medicine, take one part and cast it upon 1,000 parts of Luna [Silver] or Coagulated Mercury <note>original symbol: ☿</note> which has been coagulated with Lead. When it is all in flux [molten], cast that one part of the melted and brittle Medicine upon it and let it flow and drive in flux for 3 hours. When it has flowed for that long, take a portion with an iron wire and strike it upon a clean anvil. If it is still unpliable, add more Mercury or Luna to it as mentioned before, and test it with the wire until it can endure the hammer well. When you see that it is fine and pliable, pour it into an ingot <note>original: "zaan"</note> in a single casting. Then you have good, stable Gold, which is even one degree higher than that which nature gives in the earth, namely, 25 karats <note>Standard pure gold is 24 karats; alchemists claimed their produced gold surpassed natural purity</note>.

Thus you have completed the laudable, divine, and blessed Art with the help of Nature, from one thing and in one vessel, also in one furnace and with one fire. Herewith all philosophical sayings along with the Blessed Work are completed and finished. GOD be praise, price, and honor from eternity to eternity, AMEN.

### Follows hereafter concerning the Furnace.

Now I will tell you about the furnace: how large, high, and wide it must be, and what kind of fire you should put inside it, and also how you should govern that same Philosophical Fire.

> *Rosarius* <note>Referring to the *Rosarium Philosophorum*, a famous 16th-century alchemical treatise</note> says: The fire of dung <note>original Latin: *Ignis fimi*</note> is the active agent in the work of digesting our stone. The fire of the *Bain-marie* <note>original Latin: *Balnei Mariæ*, a water bath</note> is of no use, even though it be most temperate. Whence *Alchidius* <note>A Latinized name for a medieval authority, possibly Al-Kindi</note> says: "To cook with the fire which I shall show you; our fire is to hide the matter in moist horse manure; it is the moist and dark fire of the sages, and it is hot in the second degree and moist in the first degree, the property of which fire is not to destroy the oil of the matter, but to increase it on account of its temperance..."

<meta>This page continues the technical instructions for constructing the alchemical furnace, specifically focusing on the use of "horse dung" heat to provide the gentle, steady temperature required for the transformation of the "Medicine."</meta>

# Process for the tincture, 270

...as well as moisture; for that equal and tempered heat alone is highly necessary in the generation of this art <note>original Latin: "tam humiditatem, solus n. ille calor æqualis & temperatus & talis eſt ſummè neceſſarius in generatione iſtius artis." The author emphasizes that a steady, moderate heat is more important than a violent fire for "growing" the alchemical substance.</note>.

The furnace should be made 9 measuring-feet long and 5 high; in the middle, it shall be divided so that these two parts are of equal width, namely each internal compartment 4 feet wide and 5 feet high; then it has the correct size, which may then be called a true **Philosophical Oven**. Fill these compartments with horse manure that has no straw in it; when they are full, let them stand for 5 days. On the 5th day, place the Material inside (as you learned earlier in the *Practica* <note>The practical or experimental section of the manual</note>) into one part. The other part you must **Renovate** with new, fresh horse manure. Specifically: in the middle, you must remove the burnt <note>decomposed or spent</note> manure from top to bottom, leaving about a good hand's-breadth from the floor of the furnace, and refill it with fresh manure as said above. Then it begins to heat up, and on the 3rd day, it reaches its proper warmth. When it has stood thus for two and a half hours <note>original: "drithalb Stund"</note>, make a hole so that the glass may go in, and set it right in the middle of the manure, so that it stands exactly in the center of the furnace. Close it up again neatly with the manure. 

From that hour, treat the other part in the same manner: remove the aforementioned manure as before and put fresh manure in its place. Let it stand for two and a half hours to start heating up, and then move the glass over to it. This is then called: **cook, cook, and cook again** <note>original Latin: "coque, coque, & iterum coque"</note>. Take great care that you always move it on the 3rd day and immediately renew the other part. Thus, each side of the furnace is used for 5 days at a time. Mark this: you must maintain the renovation as described above. 

When you now wish to corrupt the metals <note>To "corrupt" in alchemy means to break down a substance into its primary, blackened state (putrefaction) so it can be reborn.</note>, you must take a phial <note>original: "Viol"</note> with a long neck, as mentioned in the *Practica*, which is fused shut as follows: the neck of the phial must extend out a little, about 2 fingers or a hand's-breadth. However, if you have purged our Mercury <note>original symbol: ☿</note> and wish to set it in with its vessel and the sphere, as you learned above, then the board that lies upon the manure needs no hole. Rather, the more tightly it lies upon it, the better it is. Mark well that you must set our Mercury <note>original symbol: ☿</note> together with the wooden sphere exactly in the middle of the manure and rake the manure all around it. Also, lay a thick board over the manure in each part of the furnace so that it closes tightly and firmly; in this way, the vaporous mists remain inside the dung <note>original Latin: "Fimo"</note>. This is now the **Philosophical Oven and Fire**, and nothing else should be used from the beginning to the end.

Process for the tincture, 271

## The Seal of Hermes.

Take white amber <note>original: "Augstein," referring to succinite or amber, used here as a component for a glass flux</note>, Venetian glass, and Borax, an equal amount of each. Rub them and make them into a fine powder. When you wish to seal a vial or a glass sphere, you must have glass stoppers that are properly fitted so they cannot fall inside. When you close the stopper, sprinkle the powder thinly around it, about the thickness of a knife. Build a brick fire around the neck of the glass, which must be buried in a hollow hearth so that only the neck protrudes by about two finger-breadths. Then gradually increase the heat until the powder begins to flow. When this happens and the stopper begins to sink, quickly remove the glowing coals and immediately invert a glowing crucible <note>original: "Digel"</note> over the melted glass. Let it cool on its own; otherwise, if the crucible were not glowing hot, the glass would shatter.

Now begin, in the name of God your Creator, the Almighty, to complete the hidden secret <note>The "Secret of the Philosophers" or the Great Work of alchemy</note> which has been planted into Nature by God and given to the human race for knowledge. Through this, they may recognize how wonderfully all things are created, and how all earthly generations are born, as a testimony to all Christian believers and as a comfort to all the weak and troubled. For everything that has ever been created and is still born daily must pass away and rot, so that it may all rejoice again in its new birth—which multiplies in the future—and bring forth each from its seed its own kind and form. For everything that is born and created would have no rest, because Nature works forever to make its like and to multiply that for which it was created and ordained—all for the benefit of the human race. Therefore, learn from this and pray to GOD for wisdom and understanding, and also that He may come to your aid in your beginning of this high, Divine, and Praiseworthy Art (to the praise of GOD and the improvement of your neighbor), and that He will help to further and complete it happily with His Divine blessing.

If you wish to ask for and receive such wisdom from God, then pray from the heart as a sinner for His Divine blessing and prosperity, so that you may receive such Divine gifts all the more worthily. Do not be proud or arrogant, so that you do not bring wrath and eternal damnation upon yourself for the benefit you have received, which GOD has given you undeservedly. Instead, begin this Blessed Work <note>original: "Gebenedeyte Werck," a common term for the Alchemical Opus</note> in the name of the Almighty and for the useful service of all pious Christians, for the exaltation and building up of the Christian religion, and to be a

### CHAPTER TWO. <note>original: *CAPUT SECUNDUM*</note>

By this one may truly notice / that there is no *Tincture* <note>The "Tincture" is the active essence capable of transforming the color and quality of a base metal into gold.</note> or *Medicine* in either the Sun <note>☉, Gold</note> or the Moon <note>☽, Silver</note> / nor in any other way / unless they are first dissolved / with a metal of nature / that is nobler and better / than either of them / and the same is the key which the *Philosophers* call their *Mercury* / it is not the common mercury of the laity that is usually taken / therefore take note of which mercury I mean / as I have shown and taught you / and that is the water / of which I spoke / the same carries the *Tincture* and *Medicine* / and when the *Body* is present / it is first to receive the *Tincture* / and keeps it within itself / and whatever it then seizes. Therefore know / that all elements are against one another / therefore we seek a temperament <note>original: *Complexion*; in alchemical terms, this refers to the specific balance of the four qualities—heat, cold, moisture, and dryness—that define a substance's nature.</note> / that is of one thing / and not against one another / of this *Hermes* <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure to whom many foundational alchemical texts are attributed.</note> says, that is a balanced mixture / when the four natures or elements / that is Heat / Cold / Moisture / and Dryness / are such that one does not exceed or drive out the other.

### CHAPTER THREE. <note>original: *CAPUT TERTIUM*</note>

Now note that the beginning of the thing is two things / that is the Mercury of the Philosophers <note>original: *☿ Philosophorum*; a refined, spiritualized substance rather than the liquid metal found in nature.</note> and Sulfur / and yet it is not the common Mercury / nor their sulfur / neither in nature / nor in matter / for in these things the four elements are visible and the wise recognize them truly / and make from them through their art and mastery / Sulfur and Mercury / of which they speak / and write / for the purpose of *Tincturing* <note>original: *Tingiren*; the alchemical process of coloring or transforming a base metal into a noble one.</note>.

Therefore *Richardus* <note>likely referring to Richardus Anglicus, a medieval author frequently cited in alchemical compendiums</note>, the corrector of all foolish workers, says and writes / that all work is rejected and damned / that is done with common Mercury / regarding the Tincture of the Philosophers / so far as the *Philosophers* have a Stone / and know / which they draw out of the fire / and bring their Mercury / which is Living / and which transforms itself into the right / and true Tincture.

Therefore *Socrates* says / it must be / that you make the Stone white / otherwise you can make no true *Redness* <note>original: *Rubeum*; referring to the *Rubedo*, the final "Red Work" that signifies the completion of the Philosophers' Stone.</note> / for the two natures are nothing else / than white and red / from the white comes the red and white / and when one adds the Man to the Woman / and brings the two together / then the Woman is *coagulated* <note>thickened or solidified from a liquid state</note> / for they become fluid parts together / the Spirit / and the fixed part / the *Body* / thus they divide the Stone into two parts / one is spiritual / the other bodily / and one comes out of the other / therefore they call one the Man / the other the Woman / and one improves the other / and one increases the other / and the two parts / that is the volatile / and the stable / are one part / and have come from one / yes, from one part / and are of one nature / (as *Hermes* speaks / that which is below is as that which is above) <note>original: *es ist das underste / als das oberste*; a core axiom of the Emerald Tablet, suggesting a correspondence between the physical and spiritual worlds.</note> / therefore the error of all workers in the art / is nothing other / than that they do not use nor know the proximate Matter <note>original: *nechste Materiam*; the immediate starting material required for the specific alchemical operation.</note> which belongs to it / as written above.

### CHAPTER FIVE <note>original: *CAPUT QUINTUM*</note>

The philosophers say: let the *Matter* <note>original: *Materiam*</note> flow within itself; they call this flow the "softening" [liquefaction]. And when they see their matter turn black, they call this the "killing," the "blackening," the "breaking," the "rotting" [putrefaction], the *dissolving* <note>original: *Soluierung*</note>, *coagulating* <note>original: *Coagulierung*</note>, the "entire increase," and the "purification"—all of which happen in one vessel, cooked together. Regarding this, *Pythagoras* says: you should know that the blackness cannot come from the *Body* <note>original: *Corpore*</note> except through the *Quicksilver* <note>original: *Argento viuo*; mercury</note> and through the fire. As the philosophers have said, it is all one work, in one fire, and there is no distinction in it; for if it does not *putrefy* <note>original: *Putrificiert*; to rot or break down</note>, it is of no use. For when the *Body* <note>original: *Corpus*</note> loses its moisture, it becomes an intangible powder. Regarding this, *Hermes* speaks: when you see your *Body* <note>original: *Corpus*</note> has become black, like pitch, then you should know that you have worked well; for beneath the blackness, the white and the red are hidden or covered.

<margin>Body to Water <note>original: *Corp⁹ zu V.*; the superscript 9 is a scribal abbreviation for "us," and V often represents Water or the process of transformation into liquid.</note></margin>
Therefore the philosophers say: unless you make the *Body* <note>original: *Corpus*</note> incorporeal, and the incorporeal corporeal, you have not yet found the path to our work; and in this they have spoken truly. For first, the *Body* <note>original: *Corpus*</note> becomes water—that is, *Quicksilver* <note>original: *Argentum viuum*</note>—and thus it becomes spiritual and incorporeal; afterward, that same water, through the union, becomes a *Body* <note>original: *Corpus*</note> again. This is what some philosophers meant: in this, nature was reversed; and what you seek, you shall find—and that is true.

For in our mastery, we first make the coarse subtle—that is, from a *Body* <note>original: *Corpus*</note> a *Spirit* <note>original: *Spiritum*</note>—and make the moist dry. That is, our water into an earth, and so forth; and in this way we transform nature. For when we make that which is corporeal spiritual—and that happens in the first work of our labor—it is called *Dissolution* <note>original: *Solutio*</note>. But this is not as the ignorant dissolve the *Body* <note>original: *Corpus*</note> through *corrosives* <note>original: *Corrosiuen*; sharp acids</note> or other means into a flowing water; rather, our *solution* or *dissolving* <note>original: *Soluierung*</note> is the *dissolution of quicksilver* <note>original: *Solutio Argenti viui*</note>.

Furthermore, the first effect in the perfection of the aforementioned Stone or Elixir of Philosophy <term>Elixir: In alchemy, a substance capable of changing base metals into gold or granting long life</term> requires an elevation to purity. However, how the Mercury must be **sublimated** <term>Sublimation: Heating a substance so it turns to vapor and then solidifies again; in alchemy, this symbolizes purifying the spirit from the "coarseness" of matter.</term> or prepared, I will clearly reveal hereafter. Thus the saying will be fulfilled: "That which was above is now below, and what was below is now above." You will recognize it by the colors, and the work will show it.

# Of the Yellow and Red Man.

<margin>Sublimation:</margin>
So it lies on the ground like a black earth, and it is then called the **black Raven’s Head** <term>Raven’s Head: Known in Latin as the *caput corvi*, this represents 'putrefaction,' the stage of decomposition where the material turns black, signifying the death of the old form.</term>, or an earthy dry element. In this way, the true **sublimation** of the philosophers is accomplished, as you have heard before and as has been mentioned; also, in this sublimation is the true separation of the elements, as the masters say and speak thus: the effect of our Stone is nothing other than a separation of the elements. Therefore, the cold, watery, and moist element changes into an earthy, dry, and warm element, from which one recognizes that the same separation of the elements is in our Stone—it is not according to the common path of laypeople, but that of the Natural Masters.

<margin>Elements:</margin>
There are also only two perceptible and visible elements in our Stone, which keep the other two hidden; they are neither seen nor felt. The Earth and the Water are visible, but the Air within the Water is invisible to us, and the Fire within the Earth is also invisible, and they are neither seen nor grasped. No one perceives their power <note>original: "Tugendt," meaning virtue or inherent power.</note>, except only in the first two elements, Earth and Water; through the action of the Fire, it is changed into a true white and red.

<margin>
Mother
Names of the Stone:
mother
death
agreement
</margin>
Behold the grace of God; here is the second element in our Stone, which is the blackness and the Raven’s Head: a Mother, a Heart, a Root, from which all other things follow and are planted upon, as in a mother or the soil. It is called by many strange names by the Natural Masters, such as *laton* <note>original: "latan." Laton refers to a base metal alloy, often used to describe the "impure gold" state of the matter before it is whitened.</note>, a treasure, a black sheaf, hops, our metal, our mother, our death. It also devours Man and Woman <note>This refers to the "chemical wedding" or the dissolving of the symbolic male (Sulfur) and female (Mercury) principles into a single substance.</note>, and has many other names besides, which all signify one thing that comes from one thing. Therefore, through such sublimation, the fleeing becomes fixed, the soft becomes hard, and the watery becomes earthy. And then **the Geber** <note>Geber: The Latinized name of Jabir ibn Hayyan, a 8th-century polymath and the most influential figure in early alchemy.</note> says: the transformation occurs from one nature into the other, as cold equals itself with warmth, and dry or a spirit <note>original: "Geist"</note> to a body <note>original: "Corper"</note>, or thin to thick, or from a hidden thing to a revealed thing. Conversely, a revealed thing also becomes a hidden thing, as the masters speak in many ways; for they say the effect of our Stone is nothing else but the transformation of nature and a quickening of the elements. For thus moist turns into dry, fleeing into fixed, spirit into body, thin into thick, and watery into fiery, air into earth, whereby one element is transformed into the other; and thus you have the first chapter of this matter.

# Of the Yellow and Red Man.

<margin>White praise.</margin>
Thus, there should be prepared a fine Silver <note>symbol: $\leftmoon$</note> Calx <note>A powder produced by heating a metal; an oxide.</note> that is pure for the White Tincture, and for the Red [Tincture] a red one, as has been indicated several times above. For why? The original substance <note>original: *Urhab*</note> of Gold <note>symbol: $\odot$</note> is Gold,
<margin>Light flame.</margin>
and the original substance of Silver is Silver, because these are the two shining bodies in which the luminous flames exist and burn. These tincture [color or transform] most excellently and naturally, White and Red, above all other bodies. Therefore, make each form according to its own form, and each kind according to its own kind, such as the white with the White original substance, etc. Thus, let no work be mixed with another; otherwise, you will err in these matters.

<margin>Body, spirit, and soul.</margin>
And for that reason, the Philosophers say: our Stone is composed of three things: namely, of a **Body**, of a **Spirit**, and of a **Soul**. For the white foliated Earth <note>The "foliated earth" (terra foliata) is a stage where the material appears flaky or leaf-like.</note> is the Body, and the original substance is the Soul that gives it life, and the Living Water is the Spirit.

<margin>Tincture</margin>
Now bring these three things together upon a clean stone; grind them well, first by mixing the *aqua vitae* <note>Latin: "water of life," referring here to a purified alchemical solvent.</note>, and perform the soaking with the third part of the water and let it dry. Do this often—the more often, the better—until you have ground, saturated, and dried the excellent Stone through **graduation** <term>Graduation: A process of refining or increasing the "grade" (potency) of a substance, often through repeated heating or chemical treatment.</term>, and **fixed** <term>Fixed: In alchemy, a substance is "fixed" when it can endure the heat of a fire without evaporating or changing.</term> it, so that it swiftly transforms every imperfect body or Mercury <note>represented by the symbol $\mercury$</note> into a true body, just as it was begun.

<margin>Whitens and tinctures</margin>
It is also to be noted that the more often the Stone is **imbibed** <term>Imbibed: To soak a dry substance with a liquid until it is fully saturated.</term> and tested as stated before, the more excellently it tinctures: first to 10 parts, secondly to 100 parts, thirdly to 1000 parts <note>This refers to the "multiplication" of the Stone, where its power to transform base metals increases exponentially.</note>. Therefore, the wise praise beginning the process again often; for if one grinding and imbibing had been enough, they would not have spoken those words so frequently.

<margin>To make the White King, and divided into 2 parts.</margin>
If you now wish to take our Stone—which is called the **White King**, which has been transformed and brought into another form, and which tinctures Mercury and other metals into true Silver <note>represented by $\leftmoon$</note>—and turn it Red, so that it becomes a Red Stone and a Red Tincture, do as follows: Take the same White Stone and divide it into two parts. One part is for a "white increase," of which I spoke before, with its appropriate water. Set the other part in its own special place, in its **mortification** <note>original: "abtöwung," the chemical "killing" or breaking down of a substance to allow it to be reborn in a higher state.</note>, and increase the fire for it, continuously and more strongly, until the nature of the fire gives the same stone the name that the Masters call **Red Sulfur**. For when you see and perceive those same colors—that it is Red as dried and burnt Saffron—then take that same King with joy and keep him most diligently in a special place.

If you then desire that a Red Tincture should come from it, one that is of high quality, so that you transform Mercury <note>symbol: ☿</note> and Silver <note>symbol: ☽</note> and other imperfect bodies into true Gold <note>symbol: ☉</note>, then take 3 parts of that same stone, and 2 parts of the original substance <note>The "ferment" or starter material.</note> of Gold, and 2 parts of the water of life <note>original: *aqua vitę*; a purified alchemical solvent.</note> that belongs to it. By restarting the work from its reserved part—its very Nature—its quality is thereafter increased without limit. Do not cease until 1 part [of the medicine] in its perfection [transforms] Mercury that has been purged in a crucible; when placed over a small fire so that it simmers a little, it will tint and transform every metal into true Gold. Thus one may begin again with the Stone so that it converts Mercury and Silver into an infinite work of Gold. Then the physical secret is accomplished, which is above all secrets of the entire world and is an unspeakable treasure. For this reason, the Philosophers say our Stone has four colors: first **Black**, in the middle **White**, and finally **Red**.

Another Philosopher speaks thus: the color that is first born in the moisture is **White**, and in the White is born the **Shining Color**. For our white is nothing other than a perfect washing away of the blackness, and as much as is gathered from the White through the strengthening of the fire, there the Shining Color is born.

Another Philosopher says: when you see the white appear outwardly, you are certain that the **Red** is hidden within the white; for then it is no longer necessary to extract more material, but rather to increase the heat and apply it more strongly until it becomes Red.

<margin>First principle</margin>
Therefore, let the Most High, Almighty, Eternal GOD be praised now, who has created the most noble substance, to which He has given such a quality of virtue <note>In this context, "virtue" means an inherent power or medicinal property.</note> that can be found in no other thing than in this Stone alone, which has the might and power to overcome the conflict of the fire, and in turn strengthens all other things and ends within them.

Therefore, mark these words, identifying the secret, etc., because I have written this in the shortest possible way from all the books of the philosophers of the entire Art of Alchemy, without any concealment, and truly I have found nothing better.

Therefore, I ask you by GOD that you do not reveal this Art to any unworthy person.

## Here follows the instruction on what this blessed Stone does for Medicine.

There are several fools and blind men who say they can make <term>Aurum Potabile</term> <note>original: "Aurum Potabile"; literally "Drinkable Gold," a legendary liquid medicine believed to grant longevity.</note> out of common gold <note>symbol: ☉</note>, and that this is meant to be the best medicine for all illness. This is all against common sense; indeed, <term>Aurum Potabile</term> according to their way of healing is only good for buying sweets <note>original: "Conuect"; likely sugar-coated medicinal treats.</note> and for paying the doctor! It is true that it is quite good to have a bowl full of ducats <note>original: "Dugaten"; gold coins.</note> so that one may see them and show them to the sick person, for simply looking at gold <note>symbol: ☉</note> serves the sick well. But the true <term>Aurum Potabile</term> is in the power of a perfected <term>Elixir</term> <note>The final, concentrated form of the Philosopher's Stone.</note>, for it is a great medicine that drives out all excess and fluid-based sicknesses in the bodies of men and also in the metals. For it covers <note>transforms/coats</note> all imperfect metals and cleanses them of all impurity, and likewise the human body. Therefore, it is the noblest medicine, and this is the opinion of all the Philosophers.

But those who understand this as being made from common gold <note>symbol: ☉</note> are blind and deceived, and they deceive themselves. But our medicine is solely from Nature; therefore, it has a powerful virtue to heal the sick above all other medicines. For it gladdens the spirit, increases youth, and hinders old age. It does not let the blood rot, nor the phlegm <note>One of the four "humors" or bodily fluids in ancient medicine; an excess was thought to cause sluggishness.</note> dominate; indeed, it cleanses the blood beyond measure. It drives out all fluid-based sicknesses in the human body, for that is the noblest medicine—that is the opinion of all the Philosophers. It does not let the blood rot, nor the phlegm dominate, nor the bodies burn <note>referring to fevers</note>, nor the melancholy <note>The humor associated with black bile and sadness.</note> take hold. Indeed, it cleanses the blood beyond measure and strengthens all bodily limbs and preserves them from marring or injury. In summary: all sicknesses, Hot and Cold, it truly heals. It heals better than all the medicines of all doctors. Indeed, if a sickness has lasted for many years or a long time, it heals it in 12 days. But if it is old and has lasted a very long time, it heals it in one month. And in short, it drives out all plagues <note>original: "Pestes"</note> and dampness...

## Of the Rebis, a Stone.

You should know that in this art there are three kinds of stones that work wondrous things with God's grace, about which Aristotle has written in his books. All power lies within it according to this art, and from it one makes a powder that the masters call an elixir, which transforms all impure bodies <note>In alchemy, "bodies" refers to base metals like lead or tin that are "unrefined."</note> into Gold <note>symbol: ☉</note> & Silver <note>symbol: ☽</note>, becoming better than natural gold and silver. # Of the Yellow and Red Man.

You may look through the hole at the top, but guard yourself against the steam or the scent; otherwise, it kills. And when the water is half boiled away, you will find the <term>Rebis</term> <note>A central alchemical concept representing the "dual thing" or the union of opposites, often depicted as a hermaphroditic figure.</note> transformed into water. When the "fleeing ones" <note>likely referring to volatile substances or vapors</note> reach this water, let it cool and strain it through a cloth. Throw away the <term>dregs</term> <note>original Latin: "fæces"</note>, and that is the Stone of which the masters write. It is a stone and is no stone; you find it in all places—on the plains, and on mountains, and in the depths, and in all waters. Both the rich and the poor possess it. It is the lowliest of all things, and yet it is the most precious of all things.

Purify the water seven times, as you know how, and whatever yeast <note>original: "Hepffen"; referring to the sediment or dregs of the process.</note> remains or will remain, keep it. Then take mercury <note>symbol: ☿</note> and purge it with vinegar and salt, as you know how. If it is boiled therein for a third of a day, it will become beautiful and clear of all the filth that has mixed with it.

Afterward, take a glazed little jar <note>original: "häselein"; a small vessel or crucible.</note> with a narrow neck and put one pound of mercury into it. Add as much of the water made from the Stone and seal it <note>original: "verlutiers"; to seal a vessel with "luting" or specialized alchemical clay to make it airtight.</note> exceedingly well with good luting. Build a small, round <note>original: "Sinwels"</note> furnace of good clay and heat it until it glows. Then take the fire out, place the little jar inside, and close the furnace up well. Let it stand overnight. In the morning, you will find the mercury to be somewhat hard. Then add as much water as before and place it in the furnace in the same manner as before. Do this three times, and you will find the mercury hard and separated. 

Of this noble powder, set one part—or one <term>lot</term> <note>A historical unit of weight, roughly equivalent to 15 grams.</note>—upon 100 lots of purged mercury; that will become good and white. Of the transformed <term>copper</term> <note>original: "Veneris"; referring to the planet Venus, the alchemical symbol for copper.</note>, take one part for 50 parts of tin that has been purged; that will become better silver <note>symbol: ☽</note> than natural silver. It has been proven <note>original: "Probatum est".</note>.

**Note:** If you wish to use the work correctly for the **Red**, then take one pound of the separated mercury and the yeast <note>the sediment mentioned earlier</note> which I told you to keep during the purification. Add a twelfth part of it and rub it very well for half an hour upon a stone. Put it into the little jar and treat it in every way as you did above with the **White** work. Then you will have noble gold <note>symbol: ☉</note>. And that is the Elixir, which in one hour transforms all purged bodies <note>original: "Corpora"; the "bodies" of the metals.</note> into good gold <note>symbol: ☉</note>, tin <note>symbol: ♃</note>, and silver <note>symbol: ☽</note>.

## Miscellaneous Philosophical Matters. <note>original: "Varia Philosophica."</note>

Dear Son / in the Divine Truth I will show and share with you our Art / and the true foundation of our Blessed Stone <note>The Philosopher's Stone, the legendary substance capable of turning base metals into gold and granting long life.</note> / although you press me hard and strictly with your pleas / I will reveal to you in silence the secret of the whole world / and first point out a saying of the ancient philosophers / which reads thus: The action of the Sun <note>symbol: ☉; in alchemy, this refers both to the celestial sun and its earthly counterpart, Gold.</note> above the earth / is nothing else / than that which Nature works beneath the earth. Likewise, another says: The Sun does not bear another Sun / but the vapor held within itself / is the nature of the Sun and Moon <note>symbol: ☽; representing Silver.</note>.

Arnoldus: <note>Refers to Arnold of Villanova (c. 1240–1311), a famous physician and alchemist.</note> In the beginning of our work / there is no Sun or Moon / but only potentially. Therefore one must follow Nature / and in our composition there is a perfect body / nothing else / than that which is equal to it in Nature. Therefore it is only one thing / and yet is called twofold / it is also alone with Nature / no other thing will do it / but only the ferment / white and red / that has come into it purely and into no other thing. Therefore Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the mythical father of alchemy.</note> says: Born is our King / who has come to us out of the fire / feed and lead him with his food and drink of his own nature / until he reaches his age perfectly / for he multiplies his seed into eternity.

## A Poem.

<margin><unclear>Part of the Author</unclear></margin>
A single thing exists on Earth / which holds within it much clever cunning / and signifies the **Stone** / of the Wise and Sages alone / its name is called **Rebis** <note>original: *Rebis*; from the Latin *res bina*, meaning "double thing," representing the alchemical hermaphrodite or the union of opposites.</note> / very well known to the wise / It is found in all places / in mountains, waters, and walls / If it is such that you know it well / it shall give you much good / four words make the Stone known / **Sublimate** <note>original: *Sublimir*; to purify a substance by heating it into vapor and then condensing it back into solid form.</note> it well with its ground / Thereafter preserve it rightly / and let it often travel to Heaven / then the flash of thunder comes swiftly / and strikes down with the heat / then give it a well-made portion / lead it with heat to **fixation** <note>original: *Fixation*; the process of making a volatile substance stable so that it no longer evaporates when heated.</note> / so that it becomes firm in the fire / and fights well with its children / when it has come out of the struggle / look upon it with good piety / **dissolve** <note>original: *soluir*</note> and set it with its like-born / otherwise you have lost the labor / and seal it up entirely well / apply the **Seal of Hermes** <note>original: *Sigillum Hermetis*; an airtight, hermetic seal used to keep the "spirit" of the substance from escaping.</note> purely / do not wake it from its sleep alone / until it appears in good color / then you have found the noble Stone / which will be a great joy to you.

->To God alone the glory,<-
->No one else do I desire.<-

The philosophers say, all those who cannot kill and make alive again should not work in our Art / but whoever can / he is a master of this Art / and of our **Lead** / some call it a Stone / but only **Saturn** <note>The symbol ♄ refers to the planet Saturn, which in alchemy is the planetary correspondence for the metal Lead.</note> is to be understood / as the *Mirror of Philosophy* says / in our **Lead** is the whole Art / for just as lead is impure / so also is our <margin>4</margin> Stone / for we call the lead impure / because it is [still] in the mother's womb <note>This refers to the alchemical idea that metals grow in the earth; lead was often considered an "unripe" or "malformed" version of gold.</note> / etc. Oh, if the sellers of lead knew its power / they would no longer give it so cheaply for money.

If you sometimes want to make something from water / that are not the seven metals / such as herbs / roots / **Sulphur** <note>The alchemical principle of combustibility and soul.</note> / **Orpiment** <note>original: *Auripigment*; a yellow arsenic sulfide mineral.</note> / from all salt / **Vitriol** <note>Metal sulfates, prized for their ability to create strong acids.</note> / **Verdigris** <note>original: *Grünspan*; the green pigment or crust that forms on copper.</note> / and the like / that would not **dissolve** <note>original: *soluieren*</note> / make that first into salt / and thereafter into oil. This is spoken through a parable / if <margin><unclear>Vitriol and Copper symbols</unclear></margin> you are a philosopher / you will understand / why it is said.

### The True Preparation of Mercury.

### Table of the Greater Knowledge.

**I**nitially, the true matter and color are to be found in our **Green Lion** <note>The "Green Lion" is a famous alchemical metaphor, often representing raw mineral ore or a powerful acidic solvent like vitriol</note> / and it is called Adrop, Azot, or the green Dunech <note>These are esoteric terms for the "Prime Matter"; Azot specifically refers to the essential transformative agent or universal solvent</note>. For the 6th, one must observe / how this black earth is / and [how it] initially stood above the water / then gradually settled at the bottom of the vessel.

For the 7th, one must recognize / when the earth has become water / oil-colored / it is then called the Oil of the Philosophers <note>original: "oleum Philosophorum"</note>.

For the eighth, pay attention / how the **Dragon** <note>original: "Draco"; a symbol for the volatile or "spirit" aspect of the matter</note> is born in the blackness / and fed by its Mercury / it strangles itself / and sinks into it / so the water becomes somewhat white / and that is then the Elixir.

For the 9th, the water is entirely cleansed of the blackness / remains milk-colored / and many colors appear within the blackness.

## TREATISE.
# ON THE FIFTH
# ESSENCE
->Of Wine.<-

<margin>
//
</margin>
First, take in the name of **God** clear **Rhenish wine**, or another beautiful clear wine that has been drawn off from the **mother** <note>original: "Mutter"; refers to the lees or sediment at the bottom of the wine cask</note>, for there must be no impurity within it. As the philosophers say, one must draw our **Stone** <note>The Philosophers' Stone</note> from a single thing without adding any foreign matter. Therefore, take beautiful clear wine that is good in both smell and taste; from this, separate its **four elements** as much as is possible to do. For to separate the elements perfectly—namely, to pull the **Air** out from the **Fire**—is impossible, because Air is hot and moist. Thus, one cannot perfectly separate the moisture from the heat. Likewise, **Water** is cold and moist, so one cannot perfectly separate the cold from the moisture. Furthermore, **Fire** is hot and dry, so one cannot separate the heat from the dryness. Therefore, it is impossible to separate the elements cleanly from one another; instead, they must be mixed among each other and remain so, for in every element there are two natures: one is manifest <note>obvious or visible</note>, and the other is hidden.

Stone

Aristotle says in a small book that he wrote: everything that is in the earth is of two natures; the one is hidden, the other manifest. That which by nature shines from the outside has its opposite within; what is hot and dry on the outside is moist and cold on the inside. Therefore, let us now see how we should turn all things around, and see its interior on the outside, and vice versa <term>e converso</term> <note>original: "e conuerso," meaning "the other way around"</note>, so that we may make a perfect work, <margin>a single thing</margin> and that must happen from one single thing, without adding any foreign matter to it.

# On the Fifth Essence of Wine.

Now we wish to see how the elements may be brought back together again to make a perfect **body** <note>original: "Corpus"</note> from them, remaining eternal. You should know that in the Earth lies the perfection of the **Stone** <note>The Philosopher's Stone, the legendary substance capable of perfecting matter.</note> and the Art, for **Hermes the Philosopher** <note>original: "Hermes Philosophus," referring to Hermes Trismegistus, the mythical founder of alchemy.</note> says: In the Earth lies all the perfection of all works, for without the Earth, no thing may be perfect; for the Earth is firm and strengthens all perfection, and without the Earth no thing may be <term>fixed: rendered stable and non-volatile when exposed to heat</term>, nor can any thing gain power except from the Earth; and you should know that the Earth is very small, but of great power.

One sees from a small grain many grains spring forth; therefore, see to it well that you do not take foreign things, but rather its own Earth. For there are some who intend to make the **water of life** <note>original: "aquam vitæ," a high-proof medicinal spirit.</note> and instead make the **water of death** <note>original: "aquam mortis"</note>. This is the reason: they take foreign earth and say that such is its own Earth; others say the wine from the press or the vat with the grapes and seeds is a perfect Earth; others take grapevines, which they burn to ashes and make a lye from, which they <term>coagulate: to solidify a liquid into a mass</term> and say it is the **earth of wine** <note>original: "terra vini"</note>. They all err together and intend to make the **waters of life** <note>original: "aquas vitæ"</note>, but they become the **waters of death** <note>original: "aquæ mortis"</note>. But the **natural philosophers** <note>original: "Physici"</note> say: out of one thing you shall make that which is perfect, and add nothing foreign to it. If you, however, use grapes from the press that are not perfect for human necessity and wish to draw the **elements** <note>original: "Elementa"</note> out of them as taught before, the Earth that will then remain is its own Earth and no foreign one.

**Example** <note>original: "Exemplum"</note>: when the wine comes out of the press, it is foul and unclear, and it bubbles up every spring and its **dregs** <note>original: "Fæces"</note> and yeast stand at the bottom; it also separates its **cream of tartar** <note>original: "Weinstein," the crystalline sediment found in wine barrels.</note> from itself onto the sides of the vessel, which are also nothing but **dregs** <note>original: "Fæces"</note>. Thus, the wine thrusts away all **dregs** <note>original: "Fæces"</note> and all evil **humors** <note>original: "humores," referring to the impurities or unbalanced fluids in the substance.</note> from itself, above and below on the bottom, and on all sides. And as it becomes clear and beautiful, and has thrust all **dregs** <note>original: "Fæces"</note> from itself, it also becomes of a good smell and taste, and very lovely to drink and to take in, and then it is "one thing."

But as long as it has any **dregs** <note>original: "Fæces"</note> or lack of clarity about it, it is not "one thing," for it still has something with it that must part from it before it becomes lovely and clear. For this reason, it is obvious that one should take neither cream of tartar, nor grapes, nor wine from the press or the yeast, nor use ashes from grapevines; for all these are at once evil **humors** <note>original: "humores"</note> that the wine thrusts from itself before it becomes fit to drink; and those who [busy] themselves with such works...

# On the Fifth Essence of Wine.

...[who] wish to help themselves; they all err together, intending to make **waters of life** <note>original: "Aquas vitæ," a high-proof medicinal spirit or "the fifth essence."</note>, yet they make the **water of death** <note>original: "aquam mortis"</note>. This is because they take imperfect things—that which the wine naturally casts off from itself before it becomes fit to drink. It is as if a physician took many foul **humors** <note>In ancient medicine, humors were the four bodily fluids (blood, phlegm, black bile, and yellow bile) that governed health.</note> and **matters** <note>original: "Materien"</note> that he had purged from a person through medicine, and then took that same foul, rotten **matter** to try and make another sick person healthy. Thus it is with those who hold such **opinions** <note>original: "opiniones"</note> regarding foreign earths.

Therefore, all **physicians** <note>original: "Physici"; here referring to natural philosophers and students of the physical world.</note> say: One should make our Stone out of one thing, and never add anything foreign to it. Thus it is clear and true, for the reasons stated before, that one should take beautiful, clear wine and from it make the **water of life**, to sustain human life so that it is not corrupted by any accidental **humors** until its final **term** <note>original: "Terminum," referring to the natural end of a person's life span.</note>, and to return us to our original state of health.

Why have I said this? So that you shall guard yourselves against taking foreign earths, and for the sake of the ignorant who might put other fantasies into your head and lead you from the path of error, so that you may remain at all times in the right way without straying. Also, if you take foreign earth, you cannot know how much of that foreign earth you should or must take for the Air; therefore, stay with the prescribed **rules** <note>original: "Regulis"</note>.

You should also know that in all **medicinal** things, you should not take the element of Fire, for it is too hot; it would consume the natural moisture of the nature of the human **body** <note>original: "corporis"</note> and bring it to nothing. For the life of all humans and animals rests upon two things: namely, upon heat and moisture; and the better these are **tempered** <note>original: "temperiert"; balanced in the correct proportions.</note>, the stronger and healthier the nature is.

Therefore, in no **medicinal** work take the element of Fire. The Air is hot and moist; the Earth is cold and dry. With the coldness of the Earth, you shall **temper** the heat of the Air, and thus make a **fifth essence** <note>original: "Quintam essentiam"; the purest, most concentrated form of a substance.</note> or a clarified **body** and make the **Philosopher's Stone** <note>original: "Lapidem Philosophorum," the legendary goal of alchemy said to heal all diseases and perfect matter.</note> complete. Consider well, when it is finished, what its **complexion** <note>The specific balance of qualities (hot, cold, moist, dry) that define a substance's character.</note> or nature is and what is enclosed within it—as the Earth and Air are fixed to one another and brought to a crystal. Even if it seems terrible in the heat, when it comes into the cold it <term>solidifies: to become firm or stable</term>. And were it to stand for a hundred years in the fire, its being and nature shall not change, nor shall it lose anything of its weight. Read this lesson many times, and you will find for yourself what the **complexion** of the Stone is and what one may accomplish with it.

<summary>The author warns against using "foreign" materials or destructive fire in alchemical preparations, insisting that the "water of life" must be made from clear wine to balance heat and moisture. He explains that the final Stone must be "fixed"—remaining stable and maintaining its weight even under intense heat.</summary>

# On the Fifth Essence of Wine.

But so that we may return to our work and **purpose** <term>propositum: the specific aim or goal of the alchemical operation</term>, to gather and bring the **elements** <term>Element: the fundamental building blocks—Earth, Water, Air, and Fire—believed to compose all matter</term> together: take, in the name of the Lord, all your **rectified earths** <term>Rectificierte Erden: the purified solid residues remaining after distillation</term>. Place them in a glass vessel and pour over them just enough of its rectified water to **dissolve** <term>soluier: to turn a solid into a liquid state</term> your Earths, and no more. This should be done in a **water bath** <term>B.: abbreviation for Balneum Mariae, a gentle heating method using a vessel of warm water</term>.

Once your Earth is **dissolved** into clear water, take a small glass with an **alembic** <term>Alembick: the cap or "head" of a distilling apparatus that collects and cools vapors</term> upon it. Pour your **dissolved earths** into it. You must ensure that you pour no more water on the Earths than is necessary to **dissolve** them. Once you have placed your Earths in the glass, pour your **Air** <term>Lufft: the most volatile, gaseous spirit previously separated from the wine</term> upon it. Shake it well together by hand, then place the glass in a **water bath**, well-sealed at the top, and let it stand there for 4 or 5 days. 

Then take it out and place it on a furnace in ashes <note>A sand bath or ash bath provided more intense, even heat than a water bath.</note>. **Lute** <term>lutier: to seal the joints of the glass apparatus with a specialized paste or clay to prevent the escape of spirits</term> the **helm** <term>Helm: the top part of the still, also called the head</term> onto it, and set a **receiver** <term>Recipienten: the vessel that catches the condensed liquid</term> before it. **Distill** <term>Distilier: the process of heating a liquid to create vapor and then cooling it back into liquid to purify it</term> first with a gentle fire, and then gradually stronger, continuing until no more is **distilled**. 

Then let it grow cold. Your Earth should remain lying at the bottom of the vessel; take it out and grind it on a stone with some "wine" of your rectified water. Grind it so small and **subtle** <term>Subtil: extremely fine or refined</term> that one could paint with it using a brush. Then put your ground Earth back into the glass and pour the **Air** over it again. Stir it well together and place it back in the **water bath**, well-stopped, for 4 or 5 days, stirring it well once every day so that it mixes thoroughly. Then take it out, place it back in the ashes, and **distill** it over again **through the alembic** <note>original: "per Alembicum"</note> as was described before.

Repeat such **distillation** so often until the Earth has **distilled** itself entirely over. Note that there is yet another way to **distill** the Earth which is easier. When the Earth has finally come over, it is as the **natural philosopher** <term>Phisicus: a student of nature or a physician</term> says: "The lowest must be as the highest," otherwise no **conjunction** <term>coniunction: the chemical or mystical union of opposites</term> or joining together can happen; for the Earth must be made **spiritual** <term>Geistlich: volatile or refined into a vaporous state</term>.

Therefore, all the wise say: make the lowest as the highest, and the highest as the lowest, and so you shall have a well-made, firm work. If the Earth were made volatile and the **Air fixed** <term>Fix: non-volatile; a substance that can endure fire without evaporating</term>, and the Earth did not go over with the **Air**, they could never again unite or **fix** <term>Figieren: to make a volatile substance stable and solid</term> themselves. But when they **distill** over together, they grip one another at the bottom, and such a union occurs that they may never again be separated. It shall remain an eternal **conjunction**, just as it will be with our body and soul after the Last Judgment. For there shall be no **impurity of mixture** <note>original: "mischenheit," referring to the clashing of different elements</note> among the **elements**, but they will become a **simple essence** <term>Simbel Wesen: a perfectly unified and incorruptible state of being</term>, a single thing existing within itself.

...is as the Heaven does; it holds within it the four elements, yet there is no discord <note>original: "mischenheit", implying a confusing or impure mixture</note> in it, but only that which is simple and singular; accordingly, it holds the four elements.

So even more so is it one with our **Work** <term>Werck: the alchemical process of transmutation</term>, for the Earth has now gone forth and has been distilled over with the Air, and they are thus united so that they may now nevermore be separated. And although nothing is yet **Fixed** <term>Figiert: the process of making a volatile substance stable and solid under heat</term>, there is yet no duality <note>original: "Tuschenhait", likely referring to a lack of harmony or division between the parts</note> in it, in the elements, for they are divided equally. Behold the Air, which was hot and moist; the Earth was cold and dry. And as much as the Air had too much moisture, so much moisture did the Earth lack; and thus its dryness is tempered with the moisture of the Air. And just as the Air has too much heat, so much cold was in the Earth; and with the heat of the Air, the Earth is tempered. The Air is very light, spiritual, and volatile; the Earth is very heavy, corporeal, and fixed. Now mark what unity is here between the Air and the Earth.

These two contrary things, which are now united with one another, have thus grasped each other in their foundation, so that they have flown up together out of the **cucurbit** <term>cucurbit: the lower, gourd-shaped part of a distilling apparatus where the liquid is heated</term> into the heaven of the **alembic** <term>Alembici: the cap or "head" of the still that collects the rising vapors</term> and have become but one thing. Therefore, follow your own understanding as to what thing this may be: whether it does not contain the four elements within it, and whether they are not equally divided as was said before, and whether they are not beautiful, clear, and pure from the **separation** and **rectification** <term>rectification: the process of purifying a liquid through repeated distillation</term> that were taught before. And see whether they are now not rightly gathered, for they have risen together through the helm <note>The "helm" is the upper part of the still through which vapors pass.</note>. Think on this lesson and take it rightly into your memory, for the secret mysteries and hidden things are being revealed, which were at all times hidden by the ancients.

Therefore, thank and praise Almighty God because of His wonder-work and holy gifts, which He has given to His dear **Philosophers** <term>Philosophen: here, the alchemists who seek wisdom through nature</term>; for in this work all other secrets are enclosed. If you can otherwise understand and grasp it well and rightly, as the door to all secrets is opened to you here, then do not let it weary you to study herein, so that you may enter through this door into the **House of the Philosophers** <note>original: "domum Philosophorum"</note>, that you may see this wonderful thing; now, enough of that.

# On the Fifth Essence of Wine.

Now it is accomplished, what was previously praised; our stone shall be made—say the *physicians* <note>original: "Physici," referring to natural philosophers or alchemists.</note>—out of one thing, without adding anything foreign, and it shall have within it the four elements. This is then sufficiently taught and proven through understandings and speeches. Therefore, Hermes says: "You should not open your purse to incur great costs." And Arnold of Villanova says in his *New Testament* <note>original: "in Nouo Testamento," a famous alchemical treatise attributed to the medieval physician and alchemist Arnold of Villanova.</note>: "The Lord God has given us two stones, one for White and one for Red, which we may have for nothing where they grow; and one may have as much as one wants, and one needs to ask no one for permission." And he who knows this stone and can prepare it as described above no longer needs to spend much on the **Art** <note>Alchemical practice was often referred to simply as "The Art."</note>.

Therefore, keep well in your memory what I have shown you here; I have opened the door for you, so go joyfully now into the house of the philosophers. Set to work with your modest understanding <note>original: "kleinen verstand" (small understanding), a common humble trope used by authors of this period.</note>, and you will see and understand wonderful things. Read this lesson many times before you begin to work, so that no failure may befall your work; for I have told and written everything clearly to you, without any hidden words. I have opened the path for you which I have traveled with great care and labor, and I have also relieved you of your care and labor. I have also warned you of all failings and errors that might encounter you in the work, without obscured words or mixing in falsehoods, so that you may reach clear understanding without loss of time. And if you possess further understanding, you may understand much more from this work than I have described to you; for what one must do in the Art must all proceed along one way and path, or else one brings oneself into great cost, error, and fantasy, and becomes a cause of shame and mockery before everyone.

## Emerald Table of Hermes Trismegistus, Father of Philosophers.

Here follows the Emerald Tablet <note>original: "Schmaragdische Taffel." This is one of the most famous texts in the history of alchemy, said to contain the secret of the "prima materia" and its transmutation.</note>, which Hermes Trismegistus made, and it was found after his death in a cave where he lay buried, which he held in his hands. This Hermes lived after the **Great Flood** <term>Sundtfluß: the biblical Deluge or Noah's flood</term>; he went into the Valley of Hebron and there found the upright pillars of marble stone in which the **Seven Liberal Arts** <note>The traditional curriculum of secular education: grammar, logic, rhetoric, arithmetic, geometry, music, and astronomy.</note> were engraved. These pillars were said to have been made by the wise men who lived before the Great Flood, and this Hermes is the first who made and described the Philosopher’s Stone after the Great Flood; for this reason, he is called a father of all the wise.

E." for "Quinta Essentia," the pure celestial essence of a substance.</note> thus brought forth, as far as it may be prepared by human hands. It is the highest medicine that God has left in Nature, for it has the power to drive away all infirmities and to purify a person so they may live without decline until their final hour <note>original: "letsten Termyn," the predestined end of life</note>. And what more it can accomplish <note>original: "trincken kahn," literally 'can drink,' referring to the consumption of the elixir</note>, I will pass over in silence, for those who understand the **Work** will well know what miracles <note>original: "Miracul"</note> it can perform; I leave that to those who are meant to understand it.

<margin>v</margin>
<margin>Final signs / letting [fire] die down / Is still present</margin>
When you now see these final signs, let your **Fire** die down and the glass become cold. When it is cold, you will find a hard **Stone** at the bottom of the water, and the water stands on top of the stone. Know that if the water were not there and the stone began to fix, it would pass through the glass just as an oil passes through dry leather.

Therefore, first let the glass become quite cold before you remove the water from it, for the water ensures that the stone does not penetrate through. For as long as the glass is pure <note>heated or clear</note>, the stone is melted; for it dissolves <note>original: "Soluiert sich"</note> in hot dryness, and in cold moist air it coagulates; therefore, let it get quite cold.

Once the water is gone, break the glass and take out the **King of Eternity**, which crown and power he shall forever keep, and thank Almighty God for His holy gifts, etc.

# On the Fifth Essence of Wine.

Now is completed that which was praised before; our **Stone** shall be made, say the <term>natural philosophers</term> <note>original: "Physici"</note>, from one thing without adding anything foreign, and shall have within it the four **Elements**. This is then sufficiently taught and proven by understanding and speech; therefore **Hermes** says: You should [not] open your purse to incur great expense <note>Hermes Trismegistus often cautioned that the true Stone is made from a common, inexpensive substance, rather than costly minerals</note>, and **Arnaldus de Villa Nova** says in his *New Testament* <note>original: "Nouo Testamento"; referring to an alchemical treatise by the 13th-century physician, not the Bible</note>: **God** the **Lord** has given us two stones—one for the **White** and one for the **Red**—which we may have for free where they grow. One may have as much of them as one wants, and one need not ask anyone for permission. He who knows this stone and can prepare it as described above need no longer have great expense with the **Art**.

Therefore keep well in your memory <note>original: "memori"</note> what I have shown you here. I have opened the door for you; so go now joyfully into the house of the **Philosophers** and go to work with your modest understanding, so shall you see and understand wonderful things. Read this lesson <note>original: "Lection"</note> frequently before you begin to work, so that no failure may befall your **Work**. For I have told and written everything to you clearly, without any hidden words, and have opened the path for you which I have walked with great care and labor. I have relieved you of your care and labor, and I have also warned you—without obscured words or mixing in falsehoods—of all the defects and errors that might encounter you in the work, so that you may come to a clear understanding without loss of time. If you possess further understanding, you may understand much more from this work than I have described to you; for everything that must be done in the **Art** must proceed upon one way and path, or one brings oneself into great expense, error, and fantasy, and becomes a shame and a mockery before everyone.

Just as the hen hatches the chick:
If it is to be thus in the beginning,
Time itself will provide the evidence:
For as the fire is turned and directed,
Accordingly this **treasure** <note>The Philosopher's Stone</note> is born:
Be diligent, steadfast, peaceful, and pious,
Until God also comes to your aid:
If you attain this, then let it be your way,
That the poor are always commended to you.

->THE END.<-

## To the Friendly and Understanding Reader.

There has often been much questioning and debate regarding the art of **Alchemy** <note>The precursor to modern chemistry, alchemy focused on the purification and transformation of materials.</note>, as to whether it may and should be permitted or not. At all times, *Albertus* <note>Albertus Magnus (c. 1200–1280), a scholar who wrote extensively on nature and minerals.</note>, *Andreas* <note>Likely Andreas Libavius (c. 1550–1616), a German physician who sought to systematize alchemical knowledge.</note>, *Thomas* <note>Saint Thomas Aquinas (1225–1274), who discussed the morality of alchemical gold.</note>, and others have held that its use and practice may well be allowed—provided, however, that one primarily attributes the art to GOD alone and gives Him the honor for its revelation.

For it does not seek impossible things, as is falsely attributed to it by those who either never attained it or who were defeated and vexed by it before they could bring it to an end and achieve its effect. Indeed, it does not undertake to transform things of entirely distinct and differing species and natures into one another—such as wood into some metal, or stone into bread, etc.—which all wise men teach would be impossible. Rather, it remains within its *species* <note>original: "Specie"; referring to the natural category or classification of a substance.</note>, which is metal, and endeavors to make another metal out of one metal, one that is finer and better.

This is the purpose and end of the entire art, and it is not an impossible thing, as daily experience—to which even the ancients, such as *Pliny* <note>Pliny the Elder (23–79 AD), a Roman author known for his encyclopedic "Natural History."</note> and others, bear witness in their writings—sufficiently proves. Thus, sometimes a living thing is made from a dead thing in which there is no soul, through art and skill—as may be seen, to say nothing of other examples, in the case of silkworms <note>Early modern thinkers believed silkworms were an example of "spontaneous generation," where life could emerge from decaying matter or leaves.</note>. Indeed, all metals have but one and the same beginning from which they are first made, which are Sul-

<summary>This preface defends alchemy as a legitimate art, arguing that it does not attempt the impossible but merely refines metals within their own natural category. The author cites both theological authorities like Aquinas and classical ones like Pliny to support its practice.</summary>

### Preface.

<margin>/</margin> [Sul]phur and Mercury: as can be clearly seen when they are resolved through the Art <note>The "Art" refers to the spagyric process of chemically breaking down a substance into its fundamental components.</note>. That it becomes tin here, lead there, and in another place copper, iron, gold, silver, etc., happens through the power of the elements, which have a stronger and better influence <note>original: "Influentz"; in the context of early natural philosophy, this refers to the "influx" of celestial or elemental energies into the earth, which was believed to govern the growth of minerals.</note> in one place than in another.

<margin>/</margin> Thus it has come to pass that this art of **Alchemy** is nowhere forbidden, neither in Divine law, nor in spiritual law, nor indeed in secular law. And even if some decree were set against it, such a thing is understood to apply only to those who—because they have adopted a perverse and false aim and end for themselves in the Art—greedily seek nothing but gold, gold, gold without any foundation or understanding. In doing so, they not only waste the noble time in which they could serve the common good, but they also uselessly ruin and lose their property and goods, with which they might have otherwise helped their neighbor.

Much more could be said of this, but I will let it rest for now, because in the books of this fourth part or treatise of the *Aureum Vellus* <note>original: "Aurei Velleris"; Latin for "The Golden Fleece," a famous compendium of alchemical texts published in the late 16th century.</note>, mention is made of such matters throughout. I have brought these books together not without significant effort, labor, and expense, and I now present them to the public—since I too recognize my duty to promote the common good—in the best hope of having done you a welcome service. When I understand this to be so, I will apply myself day and night to acquiring more such hidden books and writings in the **German language** and bringing them to light, sparing no expense. Then, if I find anything of note, it shall also be shared with you, beloved reader, through the granting of Divine grace, to which I commend both you and myself.

<summary>This page concludes the preface, defending the morality of alchemy as a study of natural elements and celestial influence while condemning those motivated solely by greed. The author expresses his dedication to publishing further alchemical knowledge in German for the public benefit.</summary>

### Preface.

It is to be known / that all things come from God / and without Him nothing can be made : as you find it in Genesis 1 <note>original Latin: "Geneseos 1."</note> and in the Gospel of John 1. Therefore, in all our doing, we should call upon God / and pray for reason and understanding for this holy work : as all the philosophers say / such as Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary and mythical founding figure of alchemy.</note>, Arnoldus de Villanova <note>A 13th-century physician and alchemist known for his medical and chemical writings.</note>, Plato, etc. That all of this must be learned from God / not that we should try to push through with our own stubborn head / whether God grants that nature may endure it or not / they do not account for that / but they drive onward : One says / it is hidden in wine : another says / it is in the imperfect metals or bodies / in blood / in marcasites / in mercury / in sulfur / in urine / in vitriol / in lead <note>original: "♄ ri", an abbreviation for Saturni.</note>, in orpiment <note>original: "Auripigmento"; a deep orange-yellow arsenic sulfide mineral once used as a pigment and in alchemical experiments.</note>, and in creatures / <gloss>herbs</gloss> celandine / caper spurge / ivy / hyssop. Dear friend, tell me this / who must brew "strong water" <note>original: "Aqua fort"; refers to *aqua fortis* or nitric acid, a powerful corrosive used to dissolve metals.</note> in the mines of the earth? ## The First Part of the Book.

Now begins in God's name the Book of Wisdom, and it speaks of the origin of the noble Stone, and indicates the proportion, the color, and the form: and it speaks of its property and nature, and how we all come from it. Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear. To this, offer a prayer to the Holy Spirit: <margin>prayer to God the Holy Spirit.</margin>

->O Holy Spirit, show me that which I do not know, / And teach me that which I cannot do, / And give me that which I do not have. O Holy Spirit, teach and instruct me, / That I may live rightly, toward God and my neighbor. Amen.<-

### The First Chapter.

In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and God was the Word, and that was in the beginning with God, etc. John 1. Genesis 1. In the beginning God created heaven and earth, and the earth was waste and void, and it was dark upon the deep, and the Spirit of God hovered upon the water, etc. Now pay attention to these two texts of the New and Old Testaments, and apply your understanding to them, so that you can perform the miracles and wonders <note>original: *Miracul*</note> of an eternal thing, as *Hermes* <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy.</note> speaks. <margin>unified</margin> Thus all things are found created from a Single One, through the will and command of a Single One. The Sun is its father, and the Moon is its mother. The wind has carried it in its belly; its *Soul* <note>original: *Anima*</note> or nourisher is the earth.

And one may try it with many words, without end, that **Mercury** alone is the double, nearest matter of the metals, and not the four **elements**. And I have wanted to prove this, to say nothing of a great multitude of those in error who desire to confirm and testify to their error: that the four **elements** are the first matter of the metals.
Likewise, one may also argue against me and operate—using all my own answers against me—and say: then we are the restorers of the 4 **elements**. <margin>“ first</margin>
