# On the First Matter <note>original: "De Prima Materia"</note>

## On Composition.

Now I will proceed further
And teach you rightly how to compose:
Therefore observe with diligence, take heed of this,
That the <term>Philosophers' Mercury</term> <note>original: "☿ Philosophorum"; not common mercury, but a spiritualized "water" or essence sought by alchemists.</note> be brought
Into the running <term>Quicksilver</term> <note>liquid mercury</note> entirely,
Which was previously its earthly soil,
From which it also originated:
There you will find great benefit.
Thus the Earth will <term>dissolve</term> <note>original: "soluiern"</note> the seed,
The seed will <term>coagulate</term> <note>original: "coaguliern"</note> the Earth:
Thus from both, one shall become;
It remains as one, and nothing separates them.
<margin>Bath.</margin>
Now place the hero in his bath,
So he becomes strengthless, weary, and faint:
And let the old fool fly,
Until he finally remains lying there:
<margin>Swan: Swan.</margin>
Then a <term>Black Swan</term> <note>A variation of the "Black Raven," symbolizing the stage of Nigredo or putrefaction where the matter turns black and "dies" before rebirth.</note> will come of it,
The likes of which has not been seen on earth:
<margin>Blood: 9 imbibitions <note>original: "9. imb:"; the process of repeatedly adding liquid to a dry substance to nourish it.</note></margin>
His own blood makes him young,
When he takes the ninth drink:
After every drink he takes flight,
<margin>white:</margin>
And yet at last lies there snow-white,
And appears bright and clear.
Guard this treasure with great diligence.
It is certainly the true <term>Ferment</term> <note>A substance that, like yeast in bread, has the power to transform and "leaven" the rest of the material into gold.</note>,
Which flies up into the hands.
Also it is truly without doubt
The right Fire, and Earthly soil,
Purified to the highest degree to the end:
It still lacks two <term>Elements</term> <note>The four elements are Fire, Air, Water, and Earth; the text suggests the matter has been refined through two, but needs the remaining two—likely Air and Fire—to be perfected.</note>.
If you now wish to truly enjoy it,
Then you must pour his <term>Soul</term> into him,
So that it may live and rise,
To go toward its autumn and harvest <note>Metaphors for the final completion of the alchemical process, the Rubedo or "Reddening," when the Stone is ready to be used.</note>.

<summary>This page describes the "Composition" phase of the alchemical work, where the "Philosophers' Mercury" is reunited with its "Earth" and undergoes a series of purifications. The text tracks the transformation from a "Black Swan" to a "Snow-White" state, signifying the transition from the darkness of decay to the purity of the White Stone.</summary>

Now that the Earth is ready

<margin>The Seed. Flying mercury ☿</margin>

Here the soul makes the body healthy,

If you now understand me correctly,

It is certainly the true <term>Ferment</term> <note>The "leaven" or catalyst that, when added to the base matter, transforms the whole into the "gold" of the Philosophers.</note>.

## On Projection <note>Projection is the final stage of the Great Work, where a tiny amount of the finished "Stone" or "Tincture" is cast onto molten base metal to transform it into gold or silver.</note>.

One thing you still lack, I know it well:

<meta>This page continues the concluding portion of the alchemical treatise. # Of the Philosophers' Stone <note>original Latin: "Lapidis Philosophorum." This heading signals the culmination of the work, where the physical laboratory process is mirrored by spiritual truth.</note>

He was at once Body, Soul, and Spirit.
Consider this above all, O man.
He was more than all of us are,
Therefore He could endure such pain:
But if He had not been so <note>Referring to Christ's dual nature as both human and divine, which in alchemy represents the "Stone" being composed of both fixed and volatile principles.</note>,
We could not have been healed at all.
For when we were to be redeemed,
The Highest in heaven and earth,
Who alone is righteous, without any guilt,
Had to acquire for us His Father's grace.
He gave Himself willingly unto death,
And suffered for us great anguish and need,
So that He might redeem us—who were all corrupted—
From Adam's fall.
He let Himself be scourged, tortured, and killed,
His red blood forced out from Him:
His side opened with a spear:
That this be true, he bears witness,
The one who saw water and blood <note>A reference to the Gospel of John 19:34. In alchemy, the "blood" (red) and "water" (white) represent the two main stages or tinctures of the Great Work.</note>
Flow out for the good of us humans.
When He was now tortured and beaten,
Crucified, killed, and buried,
Then the Spirit departed from the Body;
God preserved the Soul and Spirit.
Then the elements were separated <note>In the alchemical process of "putrefaction," the substance appears to die and its components (elements) separate before they can be purified and recombined.</note>,
Each came to its proper end:
The Body remained lying in the grave,
The Soul had ascended into heaven:
And although He shed His blood,
We would not have benefited from it,
If Spirit and Soul had not returned,
And the Body had taken the Soul back to itself.
We would all have been lost.
But when Christ was born anew,
And took the transfigured soul back to Himself,
Life very quickly returned.

# Of the Philosophers' Stone <note>original Latin: "Lapidis Philosophorum."</note>

Ores, mines, and gemstones too,
Pearls of many colors, pure:
Mercury, Sulfur, Arsenic,
Alum, Vitriol, Antimony:
All have sprung from the First Being <note>original: "ersten Wesen." This refers to the *Prima Materia* or the primordial substance God created at the beginning of the world, from which all physical matter originates.</note>,
As we in the Scriptures read.
Therefore let God be praised and honored,
That He allows to grow from the Earth,
Gold and silver <note>The text uses the symbol ☽ for silver.</note> also in their seed,
May God let us also obtain it.
But the wretched, poor sophists <note>In this context, "sophists" refers to those who use clever but false arguments to justify fraudulent alchemical practices.</note>,
And the crude, ignorant alchemists,
Want to make much gold and silver,
From unstable, "flying" things <note>This refers to "volatile" substances that evaporate or sublimate when heated, which "false" alchemists mistakenly tried to use to create permanent gold.</note>,
From which then comes a color that is not <term>fixed</term> <note>In alchemy, a "fixed" substance is one that is stable and can withstand the heat of the furnace without evaporating; it is the opposite of "volatile."</note>,
And in the test, nothing is found.
Mercury is a son of disobedience,
Seldom is he brought to obedience <note>Because Mercury (quicksilver) is liquid and evaporates easily, alchemists viewed it as "rebellious" or "disobedient" until it could be "fixed" into a solid state.</note>.
Popes, Emperors, Kings, and Legates,

# Of the Preparation of the Philosophers' Stone <note>original Latin: "Lapidis Philosophorum."</note>

This living, divine stone,
Has all names in common.
It is a stone, and yet not a stone,
I mean it is something that can give birth to an animal <note>This refers to the alchemical belief that the Stone contains a "vital spark" or life force, making it more like an organic being than a dead mineral.</note>.
It is called both a stone and a bird,
Yet soon it is neither stone nor bird at hand <note>The "bird" symbolizes volatility (the ability to evaporate), while the "stone" symbolizes the "fixed" or solid state. The Great Work involves making the volatile fixed.</note>.
<margin><unclear>Jupiter</unclear> /</margin> Gold, Jupiter <note>Alchemical symbol for Tin.</note>, Mars <note>Iron.</note>, Saturn's child <note>Lead.</note>,
Mercury, Venus <note>Copper.</note>, and the swift Moon <note>Silver.</note>:
Gold, Silver, Copper, and also Tin:
Wine, Water, Blood, and Crystalline:
Soon it is called Milk, Foam, or Vinegar,
Urine and Flesh are also well known:
Now it is a salt, soon a medicine,
Orpiment <note>original: "Auripigment." A deep orange-yellow arsenic sulfide mineral used as a pigment and in alchemy.</note> is the first free form,
Purified with good Sulfur.
These names change in an instant.
The fools do not know much of this,
Therefore they stray from the right goal.
A wise man should not let himself be deceived,
But reveal this to no fool.

# OF SECRETS

### BOOK I.

<margin>Kl: Tract: page 168.</margin>
IN the Name of Jesus Christ, Son of God, Savior of the human race, born of the pure Virgin, who, when He assumed human nature, did not cease to be God: who is the true cornerstone, upon whom if anyone falls, he will be broken to pieces; but on whomever it falls, it will crush him: who is our God, blessed forever and ever, Amen. <note>original: "IN Nomine Iesu Christi Filij Dei..." ...[perceiv]ing a slight, gentle pleasure, and may feel and receive it sweetly. For this first warmth should be like the small, subtle warmth of a **brooding hen**. Now, if the warmth is too small, as mentioned above, you may take the other iron plate; or, if you do not feel the warmth with your hand even slightly, you may place the lamps with their candles directly beneath the first inner pot or vessel. For note: if you arrange and create the first warmth or **degree of fire** <note>Alchemists typically divided the heating process into four "degrees" of intensity</note> correctly and appropriately, you can thereafter create the second and third degrees all the more fittingly and easily. Thus, you must maintain a proper **regimen** <note>original: regiment; the systematic management of the fire's intensity over time</note> for this reason: so that the outward heat (which stirs the innermost warmth of the materials) shall not exceed the innermost. For the work is not as easily ruined by burning at the end as it is in the beginning of the **putrefaction** <note>original: Putrefaction; the stage of the "Great Work" where the matter rots and turns black (the nigredo)</note>.

Now, when everything is thus ordered as said, let the materials stand to undergo **solution** <note>original: soluieren; the dissolving of the solid matter</note> by means of putrefaction. For as soon as something is dissolved there, it also putrefies along with it. But such a solution does not happen as quickly as the solution of corrosive things. For the <term>Materia</term> <note>The physical substance being transformed</note> demands its proper time in both nature and operation. And so, let it dissolve and putrefy for **forty-two days**. However, through putrefaction, you make the **Body** <note>original: Cörper</note> subtle. And note: the longer you putrefy, the more certainly you will bring your work to its end. For if the body is not well dissolved, you will be unable to rightly extract its **Soul** <note>original: Seel</note> with anything in this world. And if the Soul is not drawn purely from its body—so that the body is entirely dead, without life, Soul, or **Spirit** <note>original: Geist</note>, and separated from one another—you will truly accomplish nothing in this art. Therefore, you must not spoil, destroy, or devastate this process with the putrefaction or rotting; rather, the Soul becomes subtle and volatile thereby. Thus, in our **philosophical sublimation** through **distillation**, it begins to rise upwards through the <term>alembic</term> <note>original: Helm; the cap of a still used to collect vapors</note> with a single mixing (without being held back by the body).

When it now stands thus in a moderate **digestion** of warmth, and feels the heat, the body dissolves and becomes water, and sometimes rises into the height of the glass, and then descends again to the bottom of the glass. It rises through the smoke and wind in the glass—which becomes dark—above the water, and back to the bottom. Such rising and falling eventually turns into water. After this, the material becomes fit and lays itself individually on top of the water, and finally sinks or settles into the bottom of the vessel.

### First Book.

...rise over gently and leisurely, as was said before. Now, when the yellow color and the redness begin to rise, keep the <term>recipient</term> <note>the collection vessel or flask at the end of the still</note> and leave it <term>luted</term> <note>original: "verlutiert"; sealed airtight with a paste or clay</note> as it lies, and receive the redness—which is the **Element of Fire**—together with the yellow color—which is the **Air**—so that Air and Fire come together into the recipient, and thus Fire and Air are mixed together.

Why? The reason is this, and take note: these two elements, Air and Fire, have the power and authority in such a <term>distillation</term>—which is our <term>Philosophical Sublimation</term> <note>a process of purifying a substance by heating it until it vaporizes and then solidifies again</note>—to extract the **Soul** from the **Body** without hindrance. But the first element, **Water**, does not have the strength or power in itself to extract the Soul from the Body, nor to accomplish this. Therefore, take note: if you have <term>putrefied</term> <note>original: "putreficiert"; allowed the substance to rot or break down at a low heat</note> and decayed the matter well, then the Soul will rise over much more quickly and quite gently with the reception of these two elements, the Air and the Fire. For this reason, perform all your work diligently, and your success at the end of your labor will be all the more fortunate. Although our work is called a "work of women" and a "play of children" <note>an alchemical proverb suggesting that once the secret is known, the process is as simple as domestic chores or child's play</note>, one must nevertheless apply diligence here and use a marvelous understanding if one wishes to reach a joyful and blessed end.

Therefore, once you have drawn the Air together with the Fire over into the recipient, **reiterate** it <note>repeat the process</note>: pour the Air and Fire back onto the **Black Earth**, which has remained lying at the bottom of the glass and is completely black in color; then draw it over again. But at the last, when the Fire rises, do not drive it too strongly, but rather everything quite slowly with the <term>Martial Fire</term> <note>original: "Martialischen Fewr"; a moderate, steady heat, often associated with the heat of a sand bath or the temperament of iron/Mars</note>, using a reasonable strength of warmth, so that the Earth does not clump together too hard while some of the Soul might still remain with the Body. 

Now, take this water that you have in the <term>recipient</term> and which has been drawn over—namely the Air with the Fire—and pour it back onto the Black Earth at the bottom. Always seal the **helm** <note>the "head" or cap of the distillation apparatus</note> well with paste and egg whites, and draw this water as Air and Fire once more over into the recipient. Reiterate it again by pouring it on and drawing it over. Perform such work until you see that the Earth becomes as black as black pitch or a black dry powder. And perform such repetition of the work seven times—no, not just seven times; rather, reiterate it with pouring and drawing over until you find a black dry powder at the bottom, which is its true <term>calcination</term> <note>the reduction of a substance to a powder or ash through heat</note>. For through this manifold and frequent reiteration of pouring and drawing over, the Soul becomes all the more subtle and volatile in separating itself from its Body. Thus, it is understood...

Book One. 383

Just as a child in its mother’s womb—having received its origin through the mixing of both seeds, the <term>spermatic nature</term> <note>the life-giving essence or "seed" thought to be present in both parents</note> of the man and the woman—is nourished and fed until its birth: so too, in a wondrous way, is the <term>Prima Materia</term> <note>original: "Prima Materia"; the "First Matter," the foundational, formless substance required to begin the Great Work</note> quickened, moistened, and warmed from its beginning and through its development by the element of Fire. Thus is our Work brought forth. Furthermore, this element of Fire makes everything over which it rules fixed and constant, and it raises our matter in its subtleness far higher than nature ever could within the minerals of the earth. Let enough be said of that for now.

Now we shall take in hand the <term>rectification</term> <note>the process of purifying a substance, usually through repeated distillation</note> and cleansing of the elements. Once you have separated all the elements from the earth, take first the element of Water. Pour it into a <term>flask</term> <note>original: "Kolben"; a round-bottomed glass vessel used for boiling</term> that has been well <term>luted</term> <note>original: "verlutiert"; sealed at the joints with a clay or resin paste to prevent leaks</note> at the bottom, and place an <term>alembic head</term> <note>original: "Helm"; the "cap" or top part of a still that redirects vapors into a cooling tube</note> upon it. Set the flask in a <term>bath of ashes</term> <note>original: "Capellen mit Aschen"; a vessel filled with ash or sand to provide indirect, even heat</note> and begin, with a gentle fire, to draw the element of Water over softly. Let the foul <term>phlegm</term> <note>original: "Phlegma"; the tasteless, watery, and spent byproduct of distillation</note> drip away, for it is of no use; or, if you wish, put it in a flask and keep it.

However, so that you may know how to distinguish the phlegm and separate it from the true element of Water, this is the sign: when the alembic head begins to "sweat," and after that sweating, drops run down the top of the head or "veins" appear on the inner part of the glass—as long as you see this happening, it is nothing but phlegm. But as soon as you no longer see these running drops or veins in the head, and the head becomes clear, then the phlegm has been separated from the element of Water. You must then immediately draw the Water over quite gently into a waiting <term>receiver</term> <note>original: "Recipient"; the glass vessel used to collect the condensed liquid</note> that is well-sealed at the top so that the <term>spirits</term> <note>original: "Spiritus"; the volatile, active vapors of the substance</note> cannot escape.

If you see during this distillation and drawing-over that the element of Water (which is white) finally transforms into yellow drops, and the alembic head also begins to take on a yellow tint, then take the receiver containing the element of Water away and seal it up well. This is the first labor of its rectification. Repeat this process of rectifying or cleansing the element of Water seven times upon itself; then, for this stage, the element of Water is beautifully and properly <term>purged</term> <note>original: "purgiert"; purified of all dross</note>. But mark this: when you have removed the receiver with the element of Water and the yellow drops begin to appear (as was mentioned), put another receiver in its place to catch that yellow water. Understand that this remaining yellow water is to be collected in its own glass, for it belongs to the element of Air—just as I told you before, that the element of Water is white,

### On the Philosopher's Stone by John of Padua
<note>original Latin header: "De Lapide Phil. Ioan. de Padua"</note>

The element of Air is yellow; the element of Fire is red; the fourth element is Earth, and it is black. Thus, in the division, separation, and <term>rectification</term> <note>the process of purifying a substance through repeated distillation to reach its most potent form</note> of the elements and their colors, you must pay close attention, and then the Work will proceed easily for you. Therefore, collect the remaining yellow water in its own glass vessel and preserve it. Now, when you must repeat this rectification with the element of Water, take note: you should always collect and gather the remaining yellow water into one glass. Through this labor, the yellow water—which is the Air—is separated cleanly from the element of Water. If you do this as I truthfully instruct you here, you are working correctly. And just as you have performed this labor with the element of Water in the rectification six times, repeating the same and always separating the element of Air from it, you must also do the same with the other two elements. You must proceed with the work in the same way with Air and Fire. If any of the element of Fire—which is the redness that appears in the <term>alembic head</term> <note>original: "Helm"; the top part of the still where vapors condense</note> and in the droplets—has come into the Air: understand that if any such redness has moved into the yellow water (the Air) and remained there during the ascent of the vapors, you must separate these two elements in exactly the same way as you first separated the Air and Water. Thus, rectify and purify each one individually and keep them well-protected, each being rectified six times by itself. Any remainder of Fire that has come into the Air should be separated and added to the element of Fire from which it came. Note this rectification well, for it is necessary.

Let it rise until absolutely nothing remains in the flask. Remove this receiver as well and keep it well-sealed, for this water is strong and constantly seeks to escape into the air. Thus you have now separated each element on its own; and such work is performed by...

But if the external governing and shifting qualities—not too cold from frost or heat—rule gently, so that they do not exceed the innermost (that is, the working) **Nature**, then **Nature** may complete its power to work and cannot err in its nature when put to work: for the reason that nothing resists it.

Therefore (and as follows), an excess of warmth can suddenly destroy both mother and child. For the child is nourished and fed in the mother's womb through a small, subtle warmth from the mother until its birth. Therefore, be mindful of my warning: if you wish to set something up with your understanding through haste and the agility of **Fire**, it will not happen without harm. **Nature** desires no haste, nor a greater heat than she wishes to have and can bear. For such a working **Nature** desires to have her convenient time to rule: therefore, prevent making a great fire.

As it is written in the Book of Creation <note>Refers to the Book of Genesis.</note>, when God created heaven and earth, the Spirit hovered over the waters: These He divided from the earth, yet so that it should bring forth its moist fruit, etc. Thus I now reveal to you, as to a brother, through Christian faithfulness and through my promise which I have given and pledged to you, a great **Mystery** <note>original: Geheimnuß; in alchemy, this refers to the "Arcanum" or the hidden core of the transformative process.</note>: Which I will now fulfill, provided that for the sake of my request, which I have desired in return, you do not forget, but consider it well, and in all the beginnings of your works, fear God, love Him, and in everything trust in His Divine blessing, so that you may behave toward God and your neighbor as is becoming of a Christian person: and always diligently from the heart be grateful to God for His benefit. 

Also, may you, in your prayer for this **Treasure** <note>original: Schatz; a common alchemical term for the Philosopher's Stone or the "Universal Medicine."</note> which God has given to you through me, also pray to God my Savior and Redeemer for me. For if you realized what a high treasure this God imparts: For high, powerful lords and great potentates have desired and sought such a glorious <term>Art<note>original: Kunst; here referring to the "Hermetic Art" or alchemy, the skill of transmuting base matter into spirit or gold.</note></term>, and spent a mighty sum of money on it, but it has not been God's will, nor will it yet be: For the reasons that they do not use it usefully, do not thank God for it, and establish no good work with it, but rather use it with strife, quarreling, pride, and in excess of eating and drinking, [helping] no poor or needy...

# Book Two <note>original: Liber Secundus.</note>

...[so that you] may understand and better perceive my meaning regarding the **Body**, **Soul**, and **Spirit**. For I tell you the truth: It is one **Stone**, which is called unique, and it is one thing. Just as when someone turns **Water** and **Ice** into one another, so **Water** and **Ice** become one thing, an inseparable **Water**. Therefore know, that in the separation of our **Stone** and this one [substance], **Soul** and **Spirit** are drawn out, each into its own **Water** and essence. 

Thus our **Philosophical Sublimation** <note>In alchemy, sublimation is the process of heating a substance until it vaporizes, then collecting the purified solid as it cools; here, it refers to the spiritual and physical refinement of the matter.</note> is nothing other than a separation and discarding of the superfluity of our **Stone**. Therefore, guard yourself against "foreign" sublimations <note>referring to processes using minerals not derived from the "One Thing" or the "Philosophical" source</note>; pay heed to mine. 

For our **Sublimation** is this: that one should raise the parts that are not **Fixed** <term>non-volatile; substances that do not evaporate or change when heated</term>; they will be held aloft through and with the smoke <note>original: "Rauch"; referring to the vapors or fumes within the alchemical vessel.</note>. For without this **Sublimation**, this **Work** cannot be completed. Through it, the **Elements** are perfectly separated. For this **Stone** is completed through three **Elements** primarily: with **Water**, **Air**, and **Fire**. The **Earth**, however, is a root and nourishment for the other **Elements**. 

The **Ferment** <term>a substance, similar to leaven in bread, added to the alchemical matter to trigger a transformation</term> truly whitens the **Water**, the **Air** penetrates, and the **Spirit** carries and brings. Thus understand our **Sublimation**: that the **Spirit** or **Water** cleanses the **Stone** of all impurity; the **Air** penetrates deeply, even into the root; but the **Fire** makes the **Earth** **Fixed** and constant. Thus you must learn what our **Philosophical Sublimation** may be, and the separation of the **Elements**. Oh, how very few there are who understand or recognize our **Sublimation**! For herein, and through this, the **Work** must be completed.

Within this, our work occurs: <term>Calcination</term> <note>Heating a substance to high temperatures to reduce it to powder</note>, <term>Fixation</term> <note>The process by which a volatile substance is rendered stable and resistant to fire</note>, soaking, making it liquid or hard, both for the White and for the Red <note>The "Albedo" and "Rubedo," the final two stages of the alchemical Great Work</note>. And in such a bath as just mentioned, the Stone may be nourished continually by its own power, through <term>Solution</term> and <term>Coagulation</term> <note>The process of solidifying a liquid</note>. The more diligently you practice this, the more its power to <term>tinge</term> <note>original: tingieren; the ability of the Stone to transform base metals into gold or silver</note> increases.

The <term>Solution</term>, however, happens in this way: When the Stone has been made most pure in the fire, it should then be ground as finely as possible. Understand this: it happens in glass, with our clearest vinegar <note>In alchemy, "vinegar" often refers to a potent philosophical solvent rather than household vinegar</note>; in this, it soon yields to <term>Solution</term>, becoming a pure <term>Philosophical Water</term>. Then distill the <term>Solution</term>; understand that you <term>coagulate</term> it with moderate fire. This <term>Solution</term> happens well, but almost at the very end—it must occur if the Work is to be completed. Do not think that you should distill it again in the same way you first separated the elements. Therefore, I have set down for you here that the Stone, after that same <term>Solution</term>, <term>coagulates</term> with moderate fire. Note this well: in the process of manual labor, you will understand it much better.

And so that you may know how to understand the foundation according to Nature, from which our Stone is extracted—namely, from the <term>Mercury of the Sages</term> <note>original: Mercurio der Weisen</note>. Understand this: not the common <term>mercury</term> <note>Quicksilver</note> that comes from the veins of the earth and from hollows, but rather this <term>Mercury</term> which is necessary for our Work, which is Body, Soul, and Spirit; or that which comes from and is made out of an indestructible, perfect, and entirely pure <term>Body</term> <note>original: Leichnam; literally "corpse," used here to mean the material "body" of the metal</note>. You can certainly perceive what that Body is. For that same Body is adorned by God and gives off a beautiful radiance, just like the Sun in the firmament of heaven. And just as we humans, and all animals, rejoice in the Sun’s light, so too is this to be understood. For from such a radiance, its rays shine so far and so beautifully that men and women, brothers and sisters, all rejoice. Even the little children, who are not particularly covered with good garments or clothes, exult and rejoice in the warmth of this future Sun, so that through this warmth they might also be made perfect and refreshed, so that the cold and frost, rain and wind, might no longer harm them.

For in the middle, our work begins to rise and to awaken, which is the *Whiteness* <term>Whiteness</term> <note>original: *die Weisse*; the *albedo* stage of alchemy, signifying purification and the appearance of a silver-like state.</note>: and through further requirement of its natures, perfection is brought about. And just as midday is a middle point between the rising and the setting—for the midday is neither too warm nor too cold. For on one side, in the rising, the midday has warmth; on the other side, in the setting, it has cooling. Also, all winds that come from the South come gently without great harm: thus understand that the elements in our work must also be governed gently in the middle. So note that the *Whiteness* is the middle of the work.

### Concerning the King.

Now take this King, who wears the adorned golden crown by virtue of his high, ingenious understanding and brave spirit. Strip him of all his clothing, of whatever color they may be, so that he is entirely naked and pure, free from all the colors of his manifold garments. Place him in a gently warmed bath, in which his old age and nature may rejoice. And see to it that you do not make the bath too hot for him, lest you burn or destroy his tender and pure body through the veins, flesh, and bone. Instead, make the water or bath quite soft and mild, so that the King may rejoice in such warmth. Gently rub all his veins with that same water. Through such softening and the pleasure of the bath, he will fall asleep. During this sleeping of the King, maintain the fire in a state of entirely mild, gentle warmth, so that the bath remains constantly at one temperature.

# On the Philosopher's Stone by John of Padua

If you now maintain the bath with a suitable warmth in this way, the King falls into a deep sleep; this happens because of the sweet warmth, so that he cannot wake up. And through the length of his sleep in the warm bath, he eventually becomes so weak that all his limbs—flesh and bone—open up. Thus he dies sweetly, a gentle and mild death. Leave this corpse lying in the warm bath with constant heat for as long as it takes to complete the cycle of the Moon <note>The "cycle of the Moon" likely refers to a lunar month (28 days) or the alchemical stage of *albedo* (whitening), which follows the dark stage described next.</note>, and then half as long again, ensuring that the bath completely covers the killed King; then all his strengths and bones dissolve, and the King begins to rot <note>original: *erfaulen*; in alchemy, this is the stage of "putrefaction," where matter must break down and "die" before it can be reborn in a perfected state.</note>, such that his flesh, veins, and bones start to turn completely black <note>This blackening is known as *nigredo*, the first essential stage of the Great Work, signifying the dissolution of the old form.</note>. Yet his heart and internal blood are still beautifully red, fresh, and healthy. Thus you have the beginning of the work and the death of the King, who—understand—has been turned into water <note>original: *in Wasser verkehrt*; this refers to the "mercurial water" or the "universal solvent" where the solid becomes liquid.</note> by our root.

->Must this King then be killed? Can one not take another from among his courtiers, so that such a mighty King might remain alive?<-

Yes, this King must be killed. For none of his courtiers, no matter how brave of spirit they may be, are worthy of dying this gentle and sweet death. For the King is their lord, and all others are as nothing compared to him, by reason of their lowly origin and birth <note>This highlights the alchemical belief that only "perfect" substances like Gold (the King) contain the necessary "seed" or "sulfur" to create the Philosopher's Stone; base metals are too "impure" to be the primary starting material.</note>.

->Does this King then allow himself to be killed willingly? And why does this happen?<-

This King, despite the great power and authority he has to rule, is nonetheless entirely willing to undergo this gentle death. For he knows that such a death strips away his frail old age and rejuvenates him, so that he may thereafter live eternally in health. Therefore he rejoices in the pleasant warm bath, which awakens and brings forth his internal natural heat through this death, and rejuvenates him in such a way that no youth can be compared to it.

## I cannot yet well understand, nor believe it.

I will provide a comparison with a little grain. The sower throws the little grain into the fields, where it lies for a time covered and buried with earth. And as it is attacked and broken down even to its innermost essence through rotting <note>original: *Erfeulunge*; in both agriculture and alchemy, the "death" of the seed is seen as the prerequisite for new life.</note>, yet at the same time it is nourished with the suitable moisture of a warm rain, awakened by a sweet and moderate air, and again refreshed by the mild warmth of the sun—then its innermost active power awakens, and it begins and follows its nature from which it was previously made, and it grows and bears many grains. But if its nature has no maintenance—namely of moisture, dryness, warmth, and cold—then nature (in whatever thing it might be in the world that otherwise has life or moves) would have to perish and come to nothing.

I will tell it to you even more clearly, so that you may understand it, according to the beginning of the manual work <note>Likely referring to the practical laboratory operations, the "work of the hands."</note>, as you will ultimately find it more clearly and obviously there. When the King is killed in his water and placed into <term>putrefaction</term> <note>original: *putrefaction*; the stage of decay or rotting where matter blackens and breaks down.</note> or decomposition, which is the warm bath as I have told you, then his first form is changed. Because such a body, which is thus well dissolved and rotted, still contains the four elements within itself in a chaotic mixture, just as I explained to you regarding the Creation: this is in this form, as I said there, nothing other than the creation of our blessed <term>Stone</term> <note>The Philosopher's Stone, the goal of the alchemical quest, capable of perfecting matter.</note>. And it is a change of the First Form. For if the root kept its first form, it would not be possible to create an increase from it. For notice: if the little grain does not rot, it cannot grow or bear fruit. Therefore, the body must be made subtle through the water; this <term>resolution</term> <note>original: *Resolvierung*; the process of reducing a solid body into its constituent liquid or spiritual parts.</note> some call the <term>First Matter</term> <note>original: *Primam Materiam*; the primal, undifferentiated substance that exists before taking on a specific form.</note>. Yet it is not, nor can it be, the true First Matter. For the <term>dissolution</term> <note>original: *Solvierung*</note> is nothing other than a change of the first form and a beginning of our praiseworthy Stone. Although nothing can happen without this beginning, it is nonetheless not yet time for the <term>First Matter</term> to work perfectly in its nature, although it is taken from it. For the <term>First Matter</term> cannot perform its work and prepare itself for perfection and become alive according to a generative nature <note>original: *Spermatischer Naturen*; referring to the "seed-like" or reproductive capacity of the substance to multiply itself.</note>...

### Book Three

...our First Matter <term>Prima Materia</term> <note>The primordial, formless base substance required to begin the Great Work.</note> as well. For in this the art is most hidden and most secret, obscured and transposed in their writings by all wise and sensible people. Therefore, this First Matter is still wonderfully declared and named by some who know it, and also by those who do not know it.

I will now further reveal to you concerning the four elements, as I said above, which are still in the putrefied body in a wild mixture. So keep your fire steadily at the same heat, and let your King <note>In alchemy, the "King" often represents the metallic or solar principle being purified.</note> putrefy well through the Material Fire <note>The external heat of the furnace.</note>, maintained and nourished with the same mild and gentle heat; so the four elements of the killed body awaken, which is its innermost heat and its natural acting power. When they thus awaken, they are divided—understand the elements—by the rising of distillation, each to its place.

First is the element of Water, which rises first and is not sharp-tasting, but is an aqueous moisture and flavor. It is capable and of an aqueous nature. For water is, by its nature, sweet, moist, and cold. Next is the Air, which is slightly sharper and in its nature is hot and moist; you should also separate this into a special place. Beyond that, the Fire is the sharpest of all, which in its nature, power, and effect is hot and dry, and which also separates things on its own. But the Earth, which remains lying at the bottom and is the heaviest, is a foundation and burden-bearer of the other three elements. When this division has occurred, you must preserve each element individually, as I will show you at the end during the manual labor <term>Handarbeit</term> <note>The practical, physical operations performed at the laboratory bench.</note>.

## How can I separate the elements, when they are such a mixture and wild disorder, and moreover incomprehensible to distinguish?

YOU must understand it thus: these are not the elements that rule in this world between the firmament of heaven and the ground upon which we now dwell.

# How must I then understand it?

In this way: The bath <note>The liquid medium or vessel used for the reaction.</note> in which the King <note>The "King" is a common alchemical symbol for the solar principle or the metallic substance being purified.</note> is dissolved and rots <note>original: "erfault" — referring to the stage of putrefaction or *Nigredo*, where the matter turns black.</note> is proportioned and divided into four parts.

# What are they called then?

The first part, once divided, is called Water: which is entirely sweet and is named an element. The second element is and is called Air: which is a bit sharper. The third element is called Fire: which is entirely sharp and hot. The fourth element is Earth: which is heavy and remains lying in its place, and it is cold by its nature. Therefore, the material fire <note>The external heat from the furnace.</note> awakens the internal, natural warmth of the Earth. When that same internal warmth begins to awaken, its power increases from day to day, becoming penetrating, and follows its natural course.

# Once the elements are divided and separated, what is necessary next?

When you have separated the elements, each individually, you must return the element of Water to the root in an orderly fashion—this is the moisture of the root—so that such a root does not dry out or become parched. For if its natural moisture, which was taken from the root, were not added back, the earth would become dry, hardened, and ruined, so that it could bring forth no fruit. For see for yourself: when you plant young saplings in the earth at the start, no matter how good the roots are, if those same roots are not moistened so that their power in the root receives strength from the moisture, they must perish.

# But what must I do with the Air?

You must also add the Air back to the Earth at its time and according to the order; this Air is used nearly in the middle of the work.

# Must I also proceed likewise with the Fire?

With the Fire—which is very sharp and sharper than any of the other elements—it is also added to the soil <note>original: "Erdtrich"</note> according to its order and weight. And where also of the Fire, alongside the other

## How many of them are there then?

There are no more than six colors: And when you have completed these colors and find them as such, then thank God for His blessing. And just as God the Almighty rested after His creation and sanctified the seventh day, celebrated it, and paused from all His completed labor: so it also happens in this work.

->This I would love to hear from my heart—that all things in this work occur so well and present themselves so orderly according to the creation and the work that God performed in the beginning?<-

I will tell you this quite clearly. If you bring your work to the sevenfold number! <note>The number seven is significant in alchemy, representing the seven planets, seven metals, and the seven stages of transformation, mirroring the biblical week of Creation.</note> which is compared to the seven days in which God, the Creator and Savior of us all, created and divided Heaven and Earth, man and all creatures, foliage and grass, and all wondrous works; He rested from all His performed works, and everything was set distinctly through His Divine Will and divided quite orderly to wake and to work according to its nature, in the state in which it was then created. Now, pay attention to my speech, and I will reveal to you the numbers from your Single Number, up to the tenfold number, and back into the One; so that you may understand the fourfold number and the sevenfold, within the twofold number. For in these numbers, the entire art and mastery is hidden.

First, the root at the beginning of the work is One, and is called and counted as a single number <note>The "One" represents the *Prima Materia*, the raw, unified starting material of the Great Work.</note>. ->Now I would like to hear about the six colors that are also supposed to appear in the work; what names might they have?<-

I have already named for you in part three perfect colors of our entire work, yet I will explain them to you from the beginning, how they extend according to the order of nature until the end. For there are perfect and also imperfect colors that manifest and appear in the Work.

->How many of the perfect colors are there?<-

There are four: namely **Black, White, Yellow, and completely Red**. However, it must be said that the yellow soon changes its color, becoming brown or yellowish-red, or yellow mixed with brown; and for that reason, it cannot maintain its color (namely the yellow) for its duration as well as the other three perfect colors can, of whose perfection I have already spoken a few words to you.

->How many then are the imperfect colors?<-

Of these there are two, which are called the **intermediate colors**: one is **Gray**, the other is **Red mixed with White**. These are also called "divided colors."

->Are the colors not also compared to something, as before with the comparison to God's creation and our blessed Philosopher's Stone?<-

Yes, listen diligently, and I will tell you of them in order, as they pass through the entire Work and correspond to the ruling planets, and also to the metals, which are assigned to each of these planets by nature.

## How should I understand this?

In this way: In the very beginning of our work, the **Blackness** <note>The *nigredo* stage, representing the initial "death" or decomposition of the matter.</note> appears to you. This blackness is compared to **Saturn** <note>original: *Saturno*</note> or **Lead** <note>original: *Pley*</note>, which is very unstable and blacker than all other metals. Therefore, the blackness of the color is compared to the heavy nature of lead. This is the first color and the beginning of the work.

The second color is **Gray**, which is not quite white nor completely black, being one of the intermediate and mixed colors. This color is compared to **Jupiter** and also to **Tin**. For tin is not truly white in its color, nor is it entirely black; for this reason, it is called a mixed color.

The third color is that which is entirely perfect and a beautiful **White**. This color, on account of its whiteness, is compared primarily to the **Moon** <note>original: *Luna*</note>, as pure, perfect, beautiful, white **Silver**.

The fourth color is **Yellow**, but it does not remain perfectly yellow; it becomes slightly mixed with a brownish-red. This color is compared to **Venus** <note>indicated by the symbol ♀</note> as **Copper**. For just as copper is red and yet mixed with yellow, so too is this pale yellow-red color compared to copper.

The fifth color is divided into **White and Red**, much like beautiful flowers and multi-colored little birds. Although these two are divided and mixed perfectly, because they are blended together, they are called mixed colors. These two combined colors represent the **seeds of the man and the woman**. But understand this: the man's seed is **Red** and the woman's seed is **White**, and both are perfect in their nature to perform the work. This color is compared to **Mars** <note>indicated by the symbol ♂</note> as **Iron** <note>original: *Isen*</note>. For iron is white in itself, yet within its innermost part it contains a great deal of redness. When the colors are thus mixed, it is then for the first time called its **First Matter** <term>First Matter: original Latin *Prima Materia*; the primal, chaotic substance from which the Philosopher's Stone is created</term>, as I have sufficiently told you before. From this point on, the two seeds work through the power of their nature and bring forth the branch, which is the **Tincture** <term>Tincture: a potent alchemical substance capable of transmuting metals and healing</term>, which "tinges" <note>stains or transforms the nature of a substance</note> and makes everything it touches constant and alive.

The sixth color is entirely **perfect Red**. You can have no more beautiful, lovely, or elegant color than this. This color is compared to the **Sun** <note>original: *Soli*</note> as the most beautiful **Gold** that may exist on earth. For just as gold helps against all worldly distress, such as poverty and many other countless great—

### Understand it thus.

If you wish to begin this praiseworthy and glorious Work in the name of the Lord / as I have previously shown and explained to you / first / how God created Adam / now understand / that this Adam is nothing other than the beginning and origin / which is our root. If you now take this same root or Earth / which is also called our King / which is all one and the same substance / if you now / I say / dissolve such a King in his water / and set him into <term>Putrefaction: the alchemical stage of "rot" or decay, where the matter turns black and "dies" before it can be purified</term> for rotting / so that the King is killed / and completely dissolves / just as I told you in the beginning regarding the warm bath of the King / in which he shall sleep / then the water / which comes over this King / and is poured / is the deep sleep / that came upon Adam / in such water Adam sleeps.

Now I have recently mentioned to you / and given you to understand the division and separation of the elements / how they are used. Since God the Lord then withdrew something from Adam in his body during this sleep / which was a rib from the middle of the side of his body / and made a woman from it / and closed up the place again with flesh. This example you should understand thus / Adam lies in <term>Putrefaction</term> and sleeps. Now from this Adam is taken the Woman / which is the Soul of his body / understand the elements / from which the woman is taken. For the woman / who is made / is the perfect <term>Whiteness: the stage of the work known as the Albedo, where the matter becomes a brilliant white, signifying purity</term>. Now such Whiteness cannot appear / except through the action and addition of the elements / which are joined back to Adam / as the body / in an orderly fashion: that is / that the place / from which God took the woman / be closed again with flesh. For if Eve is to live / she must indeed participate in the Soul / which Adam possesses. Which you should perceive thus: that Soul and Spirit / are withdrawn from the body / through and in the elements / which Soul and Spirit / having been taken from the body / are returned and given to it again. All of which / however / happens in a discreet and measured manner. For from this the Woman's Seed gains its origin / and is thus taken from the Man / which is an eternal root. Yet they still stand distinctly in a twofold number / although they are mixed. For just as Man and Woman / according to God’s command / and Christian order / were given to one another / which are two bodies and one soul: understand / it is also thus in our Work. For Adam was first made of Earth / and from him the woman was taken and created.

## How can I recognize that the Woman shall be taken from the Man?

I will tell you this briefly: that this consists in the division of the Man and the Woman, and thereafter in the mixing of the Man's and Woman’s Seed, which is a Secret of all hidden things in this Art. For through both Seeds, an invincible Fruit is born, which has wonderful power to act. But take note: when you have added and returned the Water and the Air to the Earth from which Adam was made—that is, once **GOD** had already made the Woman and closed the place with flesh—you should understand it in this way: When you have added these two elements, the element of Water and of Air, to the Earth, then you have a perfect, stable Whiteness. Such Whiteness is the Woman or the Woman’s Seed of which I have told you; and such a Woman rules over the Man with her reason. Why? For these reasons: because when you first began your Work through the Man—understand our <term>Root: the starting material or "Prima Materia" of the alchemical process</term>—it was nothing other than bare Earth and a desolate mixture, just as when the elements were still together before their division, as you heard from me in the beginning.

But now, since such Earth has come to Whiteness, it is perfect, and it allows for a fair <term>Projection: the process of casting the alchemical substance onto base metals to transform them into silver or gold</term>, which was impossible for the Man or Earth at the beginning of the Work. This is because the Whiteness provides more utility than the Man or Root did at first. For since this is a projection, the Whiteness provides the utility of its first perfection. Therefore it is said that the Woman rules over the Man. But shortly following this, I will tell it to you more clearly. I must also reveal this to you, so that you do not misunderstand the little word "Perfect" to mean it is a perfect and completed <term>Tincture: the final medicinal or transformative liquid; here the author warns that the white stage is not yet the final red goal</term>, which it is not. She can employ all labor and virtue for her benefit, such as weaving, embroidery, etc. It is said that the Woman rules over the Man; so that you may grasp it well in your understanding, I will tell it to you even more clearly through an example.

### What is the Garden, or Paradise?

<margin>perfection</margin>
<margin>perfection</margin>
<margin>garden</margin>
The Garden is the vessel, along with the water and the entire *Materia* <note>original: "Materia", the physical substance or "first matter" used in the alchemical work</note>, in which our Work is brought forth until the joining of both the female and male seeds. For at the very least, you will need three glasses in your Work. In the first one, however—in which vessel the creation of the man occurs in the beginning—the woman is taken and made from such a man; in which creation and division of these two seeds, there is added to them in such a garden (in which they have their pleasure according to the demand of their natures) water, air, and fire, so that such a garden may not perish with its fruits, especially the tree in the midst of the garden which surpasses all else.

This I will show you in our Work; understand it thus: Our Work is pure in its root, and constant in its color within the fire. Now when the Work has begun, such an Adam (or Earthly male seed) is indeed present, but he is dead in the first stage of his mixing in the *Solution* <term>Solution: the chemical process of dissolving a solid into a liquid, often representing the first stage of the Great Work where the "body" is broken down</term>. Not that I say the body is dead in its effect; nonetheless, it can no longer work in this form in which it first begins beyond its power, for no *projection* or *Tinctur* <term>Tincture: a potent alchemical substance or "medicine" capable of transforming and coloring base metals into gold</term> has yet been brought about in him. 

But if such male seed is driven forward through the power and effect of the elements, as its nature demands—such as through the element of Water—the <gloss>Blackness</gloss> <note>original: "Schwerze", referring to the Nigredo stage of decay and fermentation</note> is completed; through the Air, the <gloss>Whiteness</gloss> <note>original: "Weisse", referring to the Albedo stage of purification</note> is completed, which Whiteness is the Woman and a fair *projection*. Now since the Woman is understood through the Whiteness and has come to a modest *projection*, you must indeed recognize that the Woman rules more than the Man, although the Woman works or exists having been taken from the Man. For in the beginning and in the middle of the Whiteness, the Man (who is the root) could bring about no increase, as the Whiteness is now able to do. 

Therefore it is said that in the [Tree] <note>original: "I. H.", likely an abbreviation for the Tree of Knowledge or a specific alchemical vessel</note> which **GOD** had forbidden them; but such a garden and Paradise was well-secured all around with a strong fortification, by which you should understand the vessel or glass that protects our entire *Materia* from all other impurity and holds it together. For the more pleasant and fragrant, and of lovely taste and smell a garden is, the more vermin tend to gather there. <note>This serves as a warning to keep the alchemical vessel hermetically sealed to prevent contamination by "impurities" or "vermin."</note>

To bring this to a close, I will explain to you briefly why this garden is called a Pleasure Garden <note>original: "Lustgarten"; in alchemical terms, this refers to the ideal environment within the vessel where the "Great Work" flourishes</note>, using beautiful examples; and pay diligent attention to this.

First, a Pleasure Garden should be well-adorned with wondrous and healing herbs, which must possess a noble, precious, and lovely scent.

Second, that there should be planted within it beautiful and pleasant fresh trees, which do not produce worm-eaten or bad fruit.

Third, that the soil <note>original: "Erdrich"; representing the base matter or "salt" of the work</note> in which the seeds are planted—or whatever one intends to gain good fruit and use from—must be well-worked.

Fourth, that the same garden must be traversed by a fresh, sweet watercourse, divided into four parts, yet neither too much nor too little. For where there is an excess of water, the fruit would be drowned by the abundance of moisture and come to nothing. Likewise, if there is too little moisture, it would perish from dryness. For Nature cannot, in any way, fulfill its work without proper moisture.

Fifth, such a Pleasure Garden should stand or be situated in a level and open field, free from the obstruction of any foreign trees standing outside the garden, so that a gentle and fruitful air may pass through the said garden.

Sixth, that such a Pleasure Garden should lie and extend toward the rising of the sun <note>the East; representing the application of heat and the beginning of the alchemical "illumination"</note>, so that all the fruit—which is to reach its perfect effect—may be refreshed by the warmth and heat of the sun. If a garden is assigned such a proper place, location, and orientation, as active Nature requires, it is at this time well-made and proportioned.

I will better reveal the Garden of Paradise, so that you may learn to better recognize the Work. First, I will tell you what the tree in the middle of the garden is. Second, I will tell you what the earth is in which the tree is planted. Third, I will tell you what the poisonous serpent is that gave Eve the advice to pluck the apple. Fourth, I will tell you what the four waters are that run and flow through the Garden of Paradise. And mark well what I say.

## The Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil, which stands in the midst of Paradise, signifies as follows.

This Tree, which stands in the middle of the garden of Paradise, signifies our Root <note>the primary matter or starting substance of the alchemical work</note>. For just as the middle point is found in the perfection of the metals, so this tree is to be compared to that middle point; it may also rightly be called the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil. For as our Tree—understand, our Root—is prepared, it distinguishes the Truth from Falsehood, and the Good from the Evil. Also, just as the beautiful, bright Sun in the firmament is a middle point between the other ruling planets, both above it and below it: so also is our Root, from which Eve plucked the apple and ate half of it, and gave the other part to her husband Adam. <note>In alchemy, Adam and Eve often represent the masculine/sulfuric and feminine/mercurial principles that must be joined.</note>

### What now is the Earth, in which the Tree is planted?

<margin>pink/rose-red</margin>
Such Earth is the red *Mercury* <note>original: *Mercurius*</note> (but not the common red mercury found in shops), through which, and in which, our Root brings forth its perfect *Tincture* <term>Tincture: the potent liquid or powder capable of transmuting metals and healing the body</term>. For the Earth receives our King. Not that I say that the *Mercury* accomplishes anything on its own, which is not the case: rather, the *Mercury* is only a helper to our Root, and as our Root gains strength, the Mercury is in part retained by it and made fixed <term>fixed: rendered solid and resistant to the heat of fire</term>. For our Root remains in its natural action, unhindered by its mixture with the *Mercury*. For it is our Root that brings forth the two seeds, and not the *Mercury*.

Thus you see that the *Mercury*, which is our *Resolved Water* <note>original: *Resolvirt Wasser*; a substance reduced to its liquid, primal state</note>, is used in our Work for no other purpose than as a help. Just as the planet Mercury in the heavens always stays near the Sun, so too is it joined to our Root. For you well know that no earth may bring forth fruit, even if you have performed all possible and proper labor with it, if you do not first cast seeds into it. If you do not, you certainly have no fruit to hope for in return; but if you sow seeds into the Earth, you can expect to receive seeds again from the fruit it will bring in the future. Thus understand that the Earth—that is, the *Mercury*, our water—which encompasses our Root, is nothing other than a helper, receiving the action of the elements,

### What then does the poisonous serpent signify?

The serpent that advised Eve to eat from the tree, so that they would know Good and Evil and be like the gods, is our **Resolving Water** <term>Resolving Water: an alchemical solvent used to break down or "resolve" solid matter into its liquid, primary state</term>, known as *Mercury* <note>original: *Mercurius*</note> (understand it as the "Living" or "Philosophical" Mercury), which is the poisonous serpent. For through it, the **Resolution** <note>original: *Resolvierung*</note> occurs, which is the beginning of the work. For through this serpent, as a helper, our **Root** is able to work its natural progress and bring forth a fruit. For if the first transformation of the **Solution** <note>original: *Solution*</note> does not happen, then our Root remains unchanged in its first form, and in that state, it is unable to bring forth any fruit. This serpent is also the **bath** in which our King rests and is dissolved, just as I told you at the beginning concerning the warm bath of the King. Therefore, understand and note that this serpent signifies and is our **Solvent Water**, in which Adam lay when God let a deep sleep fall upon him, and from whom the Woman was subsequently made.

I will tell it to you a little more clearly. The crafty serpent, which is much more cunning than other animals, signifies our **Mercurial Water**, in which our King is dissolved and killed. For God the Lord spoke to the serpent: "Because you have done this, you are cursed above all cattle and above all animals in the field; upon your belly you shall go, and earth you shall eat all the days of your life. And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between her seed and your seed. For the seed that is born of the woman shall crush your head, and you shall bite him in the heel."

Understand this example in this way: The serpent is the *Mercury* from which our **Resolving Water**, as I have said, was prepared and made (understand: the "body" is dissolved through its own *Mercury* <note>original: ☿</note> alone, through **digestion** <note>original: *zerdaüwung*</note> and **putrefaction** <note>original: *erfäulung*</note>). The curse of God upon the serpent refers to how *Mercury*, as you can see, rolls and runs back and forth on its belly. For all other metals are actually **coagulated** <term>Coagulated: thickened or solidified through heat or chemical action; the opposite of being dissolved</term> in their natural "cooking." God also says, "You shall eat earth all your life": that is—

Now hear further regarding **Adam and Eve**; I must tell you one more thing so that you may notice that all four rivers signify one main river. But understand that the four rivers that divide from it are the **four elements**, just as I have now told you.

From our water / in which the body is dissolved / and from which the soul is drawn out of the body.

### What is our water called?

Our water is called / when it is prepared / an eternal, everlasting / and stable water: which cannot be drawn out except from an eternal beam / as beautiful as the brilliance of the sun.

## Into how many parts is our water divided?

Into two parts: Namely / into the Heaven and into the Earth / into the Highest and into the Lowest / into a Gross and into a Subtle / into a spirit and into a body <note>original: *Leichnam*; while this literally means "corpse," in alchemy it refers to the solid, material residue of a substance after its volatile spirit has been removed.</note> / and from the body into a spirit. ## Our Stone / in how many kingdoms is it named and recognized?

In three. For it is Vegetable / Animal / and Mineral.

### Why Vegetable?

Because / it is strengthened and changes like the trees and vines / and other growing things / which Nature brings forth through her growth.

### Why Animal?

For it has a conjoined body / along with its spirit / for the wind carries it in its belly <note>This is a famous allusion to the *Emerald Tablet of Hermes*, which describes the "wind" as the carrier of the life-force or "spirit" of the Stone.</note>.

### Why Mineral?

Because it has come from metallic things.

## How the Vessels Should Be.

For your needs, five or six glasses are enough. For it is not necessary that you have more glasses, provided they are strong, as the manual labor will teach and show you. ### Must the warmth also rule around the top of the glass in which the matter is contained?

Therefore, the inner part of the furnace has a reception and a reflection <note>An architectural feature of the furnace designed to bounce heat back onto the vessel.</note>, so that the warmth must remain and rule around the entire glass.

# What should he do, to whom Almighty God communicates this incomparable treasure through His blessing?

He should praise and glorify God daily in all his actions and omissions, and be grateful to Him for the high and unspeakable gifts of His Divine blessing, leading and showing an honorable and modest conduct toward everyone, to help the poor therewith. For what you do to these, you have done to God.

# If God has given you this blessed treasure, how should you further conduct yourself?

God has given you such a treasure to use with sensible and good reason, to be grateful to God, not to wastefully misuse it with any pride or pomp of eating and drinking, or other extravagant pastimes. Rather, fear God above all things and remember what a high treasure God has bestowed upon you above other men, wherein much secret wisdom is hidden, so that you see and recognize wonderful effects, how Nature governs and indicates God's gracious will. Therefore it is an inexhaustible treasure, so that you may help poor, needy people, as fellow-brothers of Christ, therewith. Thus understand, that God has placed all His gifts or goods in your hands as a <term>steward</term> <note>original: "Factor." In this period, a "Factor" was a business agent or manager entrusted with the goods and capital of another.</note>, and that on the <term>Last Day</term> <note>The Day of Judgment.</note> you must give an account of such bestowed gifts, and of your life and conduct. For God, who gave you such gifts, also wants to be honored for them, for He is the Lord who created and gave everything.

# Should one then not be joyful with such a treasure, but rather fear God too much?

Almighty God forbids no joy; rather He commands joy in the Lord Jesus Christ. But to be joyful in shame and vice, and other immodest conduct, does not please God. But to be joyful with reason, observing God's commandments therein, not to offend your neighbor with bickering and quarreling, but to do everything with patience and joyful steadfas-
tigent <note>The word continues as "steadfastness."</note>

Therefore guard yourselves, that you be a cause of evil to no one, nor ever let anyone come upon your work and secret. And if you do this, know that you shall gain great praise and honor from the art, for it has everywhere humbled the wicked and has also ruined the ignoble without measure.

### Of the Key of Chemical Philosophy.
<note>original: "De Clavi Philosophiæ Chemicæ"</note>

Lll 2

In the beginning, all <term>metallic bodies</term> <note>original: "Leichnam" (literally "corpses"); in alchemy, this refers to the solid, physical form of a metal.</note> were intended to be made into <term>Gold</term> <note>symbol: ☉</note> and <term>Silver</term> <note>symbol: ☾</note>. And that this does not happen is due perhaps to impure sulfur that is mixed with the quicksilver, or from the foul earth in which they come together. In the same way that a child in its mother’s womb contracts a sickness, either from impure seed, or, if the <term>matrix</term> <note>the "womb" or environment where the metal forms</note> is already quite clean, the child nevertheless becomes sick from the place where it lies in its mother’s body, which is foul and impure. It is exactly the same with the metallic bodies that come out of the earth.

<margin>Note: <term>Saturn</term> <note>symbol: ♄</note> <unclear>This is further detailed</unclear> on page 458.</margin>
Now you should know that there is a distinction between all metallic bodies; this comes from various types of sulfur, which is nothing other than the moisture of the earth. If the sulfur is black and soft, and is transformed during the maturation in its veins, then a mixture occurs through the power of a star called Saturn. This star governs Lead; for from this mixture and the influence of the star, Lead grows in the earth.

<margin><term>Jupiter</term> <note>symbol: ♃</note></margin>
If the sulfur is white and cloudy, and remains in maturation in its veins, then a mixture occurs from which Tin grows in the earth, by the power of a star called Jupiter.

<margin><term>Mars</term> <note>symbol: ♂</note></margin>
If the sulfur is black and hard, and is processed during maturation in its veins, then a mixture is formed by the influence of the planet Mars, and it becomes Iron.

<margin><term>The Sun</term> <note>symbol: ☉</note></margin>
If the sulfur is red, clear, transparent, and pure, and is transformed during the pure maturation in the veins of the earth, then a mixture occurs by the influence of the Sun, and Gold grows in the earth.

<margin><term>Venus</term> <note>symbol: ♀</note></margin>
If the sulfur is red and cloudy during the maturation through the mixture of the star Venus, then Copper grows in the earth.

<margin><term>Mercury</term> <note>symbol: ☿</note></margin>
You should also know that <term>Quicksilver</term> <note>original: "Koch"; likely a shorthand or dialect for "Quecksilber" or the process of "coction" (cooking/maturation).</note> also grows in the earth by the power of a star called Mercury.

<margin><term>The Moon</term> <note>symbol: ☽</note></margin>
But if the sulfur is white, clear, and transparent, and is transformed during the pure maturation in the veins of the earth, then a mixture arises from which Silver grows in the earth, by the power and dominion of a star called the Moon.

These are the seven planets, by whose power and dominion the metallic bodies in the earth are born and created.

Up to this point, I have spoken of how the metallic bodies in the earth come to be, and how they differ from one another in *accidental form, and not in their innate nature* <note>original: "forma accidentali, & non in innata"; this means that while they look different (accidental), their internal "metallic essence" is the same.</note>. Now I will instruct you further, so that the noble art may be proven true, in order that we may counter those who say the art is false.

### Of the Key of Chemical Philosophy.
<note>original: "De Claui Philosophiæ Chemicæ"</note>

There are several who do not rightly recognize or understand the true Art <note>Alchemy</note>, and yet contradict it, not rightly knowing what its nature is, outwardly or inwardly. They throw at us <term>Aristotle's</term> <note>The Greek philosopher whose theories on the four elements and the "permanence of species" were often cited by critics to argue that one metal could not become another.</note> opinion that the **Form** <note>original: "Forma"; the essential identity or soul of a substance in Aristotelian philosophy.</note> cannot be truly transformed. But this is spoken by those who think they want to transform the **bodies** <note>original: "Corpora"; the physical metals.</note> while they are still impure, which undoubtedly cannot happen. These same people hear a word that follows, which is: that "un-malleability" <note>original: "unschmeidigkeit"; brittleness or lack of ductility.</note> destroys the form of these things, especially in the **metallic bodies**. <note>original: "Leichnamen" (literally "corpses"); the solid, physical state of metals.</note> That is true, when an

<margin>Ash</margin>
**body** is reduced to ash and well washed with sharp water <note>original: "scharpffem Wasser"; likely an acid or corrosive solvent.</note>, and ground small, and so often drenched and dried until it becomes like white

<margin>white, living lime</margin>
snow and a **living lime**: <note>original: "lebendiger Kalch" (quicklime); a chemically reactive state of a mineral.</note> Thus, from the ashing and various washings, the bodies lose their corrupt moisture and gain a foreign and purified moisture which directs and cleanses the metallic body; and from this, the purified ash is brought back to a hard, flowing water <note>likely referring to a molten state or the 'mercury of the philosophers'</note>, which may then receive white and red color. <note>White and red are the two final stages of the Great Work, representing Silver and Gold.</note>

Now it is also true that at various times things also receive **Form**. This is well demonstrated to us by **Realgar** <note>original: "Ruschgelb" (arsenic disulfide); an orange-red mineral.</note>, which appears red, and when one roasts it, it becomes black, and when one separates it according to the teachings of the Art, it becomes white—and yet it remains that which it was before.

We also see that **Vitriol** <note>original: "Atrament"; a sulfate mineral used to make ink and acids.</note> has a black color, and when one roasts it, it becomes red, and yet it is still Vitriol. Some may say that such things easily transform from one color into another, but that it is impossible for the metallic bodies. To them I answer: with an obvious matter and with many proofs, I shall nullify their speech.

Now we see openly that from **Silver**, fine **Azure** <note>original: "Lasur"; a blue pigment. The author argues that if silver can become blue, its "form" has been altered.</note> is made, and yet it is pure in its nature from all filth; and the form derived from it is more easily destroyed than the unborn form.

Also, we see well that **Copper** takes on a gold color and becomes **Brass**, and yet is neither copper nor gold perfectly, for the fire destroys them both.

Now we see that **Tin**, from great and excessive fire, receives a gold color, and yet it would more rightly receive a silver color, for its nature is shaped similarly to it.

So we also see that **Iron** transforms into **copper** <note>original: "Koch"; likely referring to the alchemical observation of iron "turning" into copper when placed in vitriol solutions.</note>, which seems unjust to many. For why should that not be possible? Have I not told you before that all metallic bodies here in the earth are created from **Sulfur**

...other things. During wintertime it is not fit, because of winter's frost. But whatever other work there is, that is fit at all times: But what that may be, I will tell you in its stead.

The fourth commandment is: that the master craftsman be constantly and diligently at his work, and let himself not be weary, but complete his work until the end. And if he does not complete it to the right end, he loses both expense, time, and labor. And if he works one week and goes idle the next, and thus puts it off from year to year, he will never finish it.

<margin>5.</margin>
The fifth commandment is: that he works according to the teaching of the Art, and not place one task before the other, except as is fitting or proper. For if he wishes to cast his **spirit** upon the **bodies** <term>Leichnam</term> <note>literally "corpses"; the solid, metallic state before being "vivified" by the alchemist.</note> after their purification, before he has confirmed them, and if he wishes to harden unpurified **water**, he loses his **powders**. For if he throws them in, they do not remain and vanish quickly. Or if he wishes to throw **powders** upon the **body** with steady **spirits**, which have not been brought to **water**, nor purified in the manner of **water**, they do not enter into the **body** <term>Corpus</term>, nor do they mix in any way.

<margin>6. vessels</margin>
The sixth commandment is: that all the **vessels** <term>Vasa</term> <note>Latin: "vessels."</note> that the master craftsman must use should be glass, or glazed. For if he put **sharp waters** <note>archaic term for acids or corrosive solvents.</note> into **copper** vessels, they would become green; if one put them into **iron** or **tin**, they would become black and impure. But if one puts them into earthen vessels, then the **sharp waters** strike through and spoil.

<margin>7.</margin>
The seventh commandment is: That no one should undertake, above all things, to reveal anything to **princes** and **lords**, or presume to perform any work before them. For if he undertakes work for them, they will question him from one time to another and say: "Master, how goes it? When shall we see something?" and they cannot wait for the proper end, and will say: "It is nothing; he is a **deceiver**," <note>original: "Trieger".</note> etc. This will then become a misery, and if he does not bring it to the right end, he has eternal enmity. But if he brings it to a good end, then they will seek how they may lock him away eternally and never let him out. Thus he has trapped himself with his own mouth.

<margin>8.</margin>
The eighth commandment is: that no one should undertake this Art unless he has provisions for two years, so that he may procure all that which he needs for the Art. For if he undertakes the Art and begins to work and lacks the means, then he has lost both expense and time.
