### Concerning the Key of Chemical Philosophy.
<note>original: "De Claui Philosophiæ Chemicæ"</note>

Now is the time for us to write further concerning the beginning of this noble Art. And first, I will teach you how to build the furnaces that are required for this Art, and how many of them there should be, or how they should be made. One thing you should know is that you must build your furnace according to the size of the Great Work you intend to perform. If you are undertaking a large work, make the furnace accordingly larger; but if you have only a little, make them small in proportion. Nevertheless, I will give you instructions for making a moderate furnace that would suit both the rich and the poor.

<margin>The first furnace.</margin> First, I will teach you how to make a masterly furnace, which you shall build in this way: You should build it by a wall, about one ell <note>An "ell" is a historical unit of length, roughly 24 to 45 inches depending on the region.</note> or a little further from the wall. There, dig a pit, which you should coat well on all sides with the **Lute of Wisdom** <term>Luto Sapientiæ</term> <note>A heat-resistant paste or cement used by alchemists to seal vessels and line furnaces.</note>. In this pit, there should be a wind-vent passing through the earth, and the air into the pit should be narrow at the opening in the pit, but a span wide on the outside by the wall where the wind and air enter; this should also be well-coated with the **Lute of Wisdom**. After this, build a wall over the pit using pure, common clay, adding a fifth part of potter's clay and a little fine sand, mixing it all together exceedingly well. With this clay, build a wall upwards over the pit, two feet <note>original: "Schuch," an archaic spelling of "Schuh" or foot.</note> high and a span thick, and make it round <note>original: "sinwel," an archaic term for circular or spherical.</note>; let it dry thoroughly. Then, have a potter make a disc from noble earth that can well withstand the fire, according to the dimensions of the furnace. This disc should have 50 or 60 holes throughout; these should be narrow at the top and wide at the bottom, so that one might poke their smallest finger through them, so that the coals, ashes, and small stones that fall into them may better pass through. Place the disc upon the furnace so that the narrow end of the holes faces upward. Afterward, build a wall over the furnace disc, nearly an ell high in thickness. Below, above the disc, make a moderate hole through which to pour coals, and at the top of the furnace, also make a hole where one puts in whatever is to be calcined <note>To "aschen" or calcine: to reduce a substance to powder or ash through prolonged heat.</note> or burned. For this same hole, you should make a lid of good potter's clay, well-tempered, so that you may cover the hole with it; the furnace, however, should remain round. And at the top, make three or four holes around the furnace, two fingers wide, to give the furnace air.

Furthermore, know that you should place a tripod upon the disc, or a stand made of good clay, so that one may set the vessels upon it in which one intends to burn or calcine. And beneath it, make a coal fire <term>Kolfewr</term>, for a coal fire burns or calcines more purely than one made of wood.

# Concerning the Key of Chemical Philosophy.
<note>original: "De Claui Philosophiæ Chemicæ"</note>

<margin>Elixir</margin>
A powder that the masters call "Elixir." Elixir is an Arabic word, and in English it means as much as a leaven or yeast <note>original: "Urhab oder Gerben." Just as leaven causes dough to rise and transform into bread, the alchemical elixir transforms "base" metals into gold.</note>. For just as bread improves and rises from good yeast, so too do the bodies <term>Corpora</term> <note>The "bodies" refer to the seven basic metals: gold, silver, copper, iron, tin, lead, and mercury (though mercury is often classed as a spirit).</note> rise and transform into gold and silver through these five spirits <term>Spiritibus</term> <note>The "spirits" are the volatile substances: mercury, sulfur, orpiment, sal ammoniac, and sometimes others like marcasite.</note>, and most of all by mercury <term>Koch</term> <note>original: "Koch," literally "Cook." Here it is used as a technical name for quicksilver/mercury, the primary "cooker" or maturing agent of metals.</note>, for it is the origin of all bodies.

<margin>Mercury</margin>
I will instruct you about several others which do not have the power to transform the bodies on their own, but rather they help the five spirits so that they are prepared and can be more easily turned into liquid <note>original: "zu Waſſer macht," literally "made into water," referring to the process of liquefaction or dissolution.</note>. With their liquids, one mixes the ashes of the "corpses" <note>In alchemy, a "corpse" or "carcass" refers to the solid residue—the metallic oxide—left after a substance has been burned or calcined.</note> so that they gain a moisture that restores the corpses. And I will teach you one after the other how each should be prepared or made.

<margin>Mercury</margin>
Quicksilver or mercury <term>Koch</term> is nothing other than a viscous and refined water, gathered through the earth and well-tempered heat, collected within the veins of the earth until the moisture is mixed equally with dryness. And for this reason, it flees away so easily in the fire, yet it does not cling to anything, as its refined nature is well-tempered by dryness and does not allow sticking. Together with sulfur, it is a mother of all "corpses" (metals). It is found in the mountains and sometimes in ancient lakes. Its nature is warm and moist, and it is the root and origin of all bodies <note>original: "omnium Corporum"</note>; they all come from it and all mix with it—though with iron only very harshly—and without it, no other metal can be gilded.

<margin>$\triangle$ is moisture p. 451</margin>
$\triangle$ Sulfur <note>The triangle symbol usually represents the element of fire, but here the margin and text associate it with Sulfur.</note> is the earth's moisture, which is produced in its veins with well-tempered heat until it becomes hard and dry. And when it becomes dry, it is called sulfur. It is of a strong nature and of the same substance as its oil. Therefore, one cannot take its oil from it as one does with others that contain oil, except with strong and sharp waters <note>This refers to corrosive acids like sulfuric or nitric acid used to "extract" the essence of a mineral.</note> by boiling it in them. It is found in the earth, sometimes in mountains or in lakes, and it is of various kinds: one is called the "living" <term>Sulphur Vivum</term>, the other the "dead." The living sulfur is as it is brought out of the earth; the dead is that which has been melted and cast into tubes, as it is found for sale.

<margin>Orpiment</margin>
Orpiment <term>Auripigmentum</term> <note>Orpiment is a deep yellow-orange arsenic sulfide mineral once used as a pigment and in alchemy; its name literally means "gold pigment."</note> is a yellow stone grown in the veins of the earth. It is heated and boiled repeatedly from the earth's refuse and flames until it transforms into orpiment. How one should prepare and make it, however, I will teach later in its proper place.

<margin>Alum <note>original symbol: $\ominus$</note></margin>
I will not keep **alum** from you, for it is also quite useful for this art; prepare it thus: Take as much of it as you find for sale and put it in a pot until it is half full; seal the pot very well, place it in the furnace, and give it a gentle fire until it warms up. ### CALCINATION
<note>original: "CALCINATIO"</note>

Thus, **calcination** <term>calcination: the process of heating a substance to high temperatures in air to cause thermal decomposition or to remove volatile fractions</term> or "ashing" is nothing other—to speak plainly—than a pulverization of any thing through the power of fire, by depriving it of the moisture that it previously held and which bound it together. One powders the **bodies** <term>bodies: the solid, physical matter of a substance, as opposed to its volatile "spirits"</term> so that they become clean of their impurity. Likewise, one powders the **spirits** <term>spirits: volatile substances that easily evaporate or "flee" the fire</term> for this and many other reasons. Firstly, so that the bodies lose their impure taste <note>in early chemistry, "taste" often referred to the chemical essence or reactivity of a substance</note>; and without this, it cannot be. Thus, pulverization was discovered so that one might harden moist bodies therein. For one sees obviously that they become hard by this method, and most especially tin. But as to why one powders the spirits: that is done so that they might become stable all the sooner and transform all the better into water. For certain burnt things are stable in the fire and also turn to water sooner than unburnt ones.

### COAGULATION
<note>original: "COAGVLATIO"</note>

Thus, purification and hardening is nothing other than a deprivation of the watery or moist thing, a restoration of the moisture into a hard mass. For it is often found that mercury is hardened and purified, and that one drives the watery things it has from its moisture out of it and makes it hard. The **mercury** <note>original: "Koch," likely a variant of "Quick," referring to Quicksilver/Mercury</note> is hardened in this way, and one **kills** <term>kills: also known as "mortification," the alchemical process of changing a substance's state or stripping it of its "living" volatile qualities</term> it, by burning it thick with force. For the power of this fire takes away its moisture. And this is done in such a vessel, elongated and narrow in shape, like a canister or an iron pipe.

### FIXATION
<note>original: "FIXATIO"</note>

Thus, **fixation** <term>fixation: the process by which a volatile substance is rendered stable in fire so that it no longer evaporates</term> is nothing other than a companionable purification of fleeing things by the fire. But the reason this was discovered is so that every transformation and change of one thing into another may be complete and stable, and not revert. The imperfect bodies...

### SOLUTION AND LIQUEFACTION
<note>original: "Erlösung und Fliessiung"</note>

Thus, **solution** <note>original: "Erlösung," literally "release" or "redemption," here meaning the dissolving of a solid</note> and **liquefaction** are nothing other than the transformation of any thing that is or will be powdered into water. The reason this was discovered is so that its outer nature might become its inner nature, and also so that one might better **purify** the bodies and the spirits; and thus all its filth is purified and cleansed from it.

Take note that one may turn a thing into water in two ways. Either with heat, or with moisture, such as in a cold pit or in a cellar, as I will teach you hereafter.

### PURIFICATION
<note>original: "Leuterung"</note>

Thus, **purification** <term>purification: in this context, refers to distillation, sublimation, or filtration to remove impurities</term> is nothing other than the raising of an aqueous vapor in its vessel. The preparation is of many kinds: Some purifications are done with fire, some without fire. Those done with fire are of two types: One is upward, as through a cap <note>the "helm" or top of a still</note> or through an **alembic** <term>alembic: a classic distillation apparatus consisting of two vessels connected by a tube</term>, so that one burns something out together. 

But why each was discovered is so that a water might be purified from its dregs or tannins <note>original: "Heffen oder Gerben"</note> and that one might keep it so that it does not rot. For we see that every pure thing remains beautiful and clear. Especially also it was discovered so that one might dry the spirits and the powders, if this be needed, while having pure and clear water that afterward has no dregs or filth from which the spirits or powders might receive impurity. 

But as to why it was devised to purify downward <note>referring to *distillatio per descensum*, where the vapor is forced downward, often used for heavy oils</note>, that is because of what is pure oil in its nature, or has an expressed nature, which one cannot subdue upward in its flowering nature, as is seen with **petroleum** <note>original: "Petroleo"; referring here to naturally occurring rock oils</note>.

Thus, purification with or through the **felt** <note>filtration through cloth or felt</note> is nothing other than a preparation of hard and unfluid things into something like a soft wax. From this one may note that it was devised so that, due to thirst, nothing may enter the bodies that desires to transform until it is "born" <note>produced or brought into a new state</note> so that it becomes fluid and can enter the bodies.

Thus some believe that the preparation should be with oil and with **sharp waters** <term>sharp waters: strong acids or corrosive chemical solvents</term> <note>original: "scharpffen Wassern"</note>, yet that is nothing, for in no way does one find the truth there. If you now wish to separate **mercury** and turn it into a snow-white powder: take 1 part **quicklime** <term>quicklime: calcium oxide, a caustic alkaline substance produced by heating limestone</term> <note>original: "lebendiges Kalchs"</note>, and 1 part powder made from **eggshells**, or 1 part **verdigris** <term>verdigris: a green pigment and chemical prepared by exposing copper to vinegar vapors</term> <note>original: "Kupffergrün"</note>, and one quarter-part **sal ammoniac** <term>sal ammoniac: ammonium chloride, used as a flux in metallurgy and alchemy</term> <note>original: "Salarmoniac"</note>. And this is a sign when it has been rubbed enough: take a little of it and rub it firmly against a silver penny with your fingers; if it sticks to the penny, it has not had enough. <note>Mercury forms an amalgam with silver; if the silver turns white or "sticky," it means the mercury is still in its raw, metallic state and not yet "fixed" or "killed."</note> Thus one shall rub it again with **vinegar** and dry it for as long as it takes until it no longer sticks to the penny when one rubs it thereon.

When you now see that it has had enough, rub it out exceedingly well and small, and make it as dry as you can. Put it into the vessel in which one separates the spirits, and cover it with its lid. And when you lay the prescribed powder into the vessel, level the powder across the top, and close the glass, and seal it well with **lute** <term>lute: a clay or cement paste used to seal alchemical vessels airtight</term> <note>original: "Luto"</note> so that it has no air. And place it in the furnace and give it at first a gentle fire for nearly half a day, until its moisture entirely smokes out through the hole that goes through the cap.

You shall note it thus: take a knife blade or other piece of sheet metal and lay it over the hole. If it becomes black or damp, it has not had enough. But when it no longer sweats, then seal the hole above well with **lute**, and increase the fire more and more. And at the last, make a strong fire.

And if it happens / that something has remained in the salt / then take new salt / and separate it again as before / for the fourth time / and for the fifth time / Then keep it / until I will teach you later / how you shall make it **fixed** <term>fixed: a state where a substance is stable under heat and no longer evaporates or sublimes</term> <note>original: "stät"</note>.

<margin>//</margin> Now I will teach you / how you shall separate the **sulfur**. Take it / and grind it very small / and boil it in strong vinegar for a whole day / and skim it off beautifully at the top. The next day boil it in pure **urine** <note>distilled urine was a common source of ammonia and phosphates in early chemistry</note> / and skim it very well / After that let it dry / then also grind it very well / and take as much prepared **alum** <term>alum: a double sulfate of aluminum, used as a mordant and astringent</term> <note>original: "Alaun"</note> with it / and lay it in the separation-vessel / and separate it like the **cook** / except that you do not need such a great fire / And separate it for a whole day. In the morning take it out / and so you will find the sulfur separated / black / And so separate it with the same dregs the next day / then it will become whiter / And separate it on the third day with prepared salt / then it will become quite white / After that separate it for the fourth time with salt / then it will become snow-white. Then keep it until I will teach you / how you shall keep it in your fire / and make it fixed.

But when you wish to separate **Orpiment** <term>Orpiment: a deep orange-yellow arsenic sulfide mineral formerly used as a pigment and in alchemy</term> <note>original: "Operment"</note> / then you shall grind the Orpiment exceedingly well / and boil it thoroughly in vinegar and urine for two days / just as you did the sulfur / and skim it well. **Sal ammoniac** <term>Sal ammoniac: ammonium chloride, a volatile salt used to "cleanse" or "spiritualize" metals</term> <note>original: "Salarmoniac"</note> you shall make stable thus : Grind it quite small and well / with just as much prepared salt without any moisture / and lay that in the separation-vessel / and separate it with a gentle fire for a good quarter of a day / Thereafter with a strong fire through the day until the morning / Then open it up / and whatever is separated, keep that / And do to it in all things / as I taught you with the mercury / and separate it with the **Hessian [additive]** <note>original: "Hessen"; likely referring to the refractory clay or materials used in Hessian crucibles, or a specific additive from that region used for purification</note> thus for 2 or 3 hours.

Now know / that it should be a **charcoal furnace** <note>original: "Kolferor," likely a dialect variant of "Kohlenfeuer" (coal-fire) or a specific alchemical furnace type</note> / for two reasons : The first reason is / that it is less work to stoke coals / than wood : The other reason is / that the fire from wood smokes more / than from coals. And therefore one cannot easily burn with it / because the vessels may flow and crack / which then often happens. For they are sometimes made of poor clay / or are not well-fired. And when one of the vessels cracks / then white smoke immediately comes out of the vent / which one sees very quickly on a charcoal furnace. When you see that / then take it immediately from the fire / or you lose your work / and coals / and whatever you lay upon it.

And sometimes it is accustomed to harden in the lower vessel / so that one cannot retrieve it / and it will not separate. Therefore you shall not despair of your work / but take it out / and grind it better / and add more of the Hessian [additive] to it / and separate it with a diligent fire / so it will be well-separated.

Do this as often as necessary until it becomes entirely clear. Then boil it over a gentle fire until it has boiled down thick, and refine it quite purely, and strain it through a felt or through a hat <note>a common method of filtration using a felted wool hat</note>, which is better. Keep it in a glass vessel until you need it.

### PRACTICE.

In the name of God, take red sulfur and <term>orpiment</term> <note>arsenic trisulfide, used for its yellow color; original: "Rauschgelb"</note> that have been separated and fixed <note>referring to substances that have been purified and rendered non-volatile by fire</note>, of each an equal weight. Add to them half as much "water of silver" <note>likely a solution of silver in acid, such as silver nitrate</note> as there is of one of the others. Put these together into a glass with a narrow neck and <term>lute</term> <note>to seal a vessel with an airtight clay or paste; original: "verlutier"</note> it well so that no air may escape. You must do this with fire or with a glowing iron until it melts and fuses together. Then set it in the ashes <note>a sand bath, which provided a gentle, even heat</note> and give it a soft fire, and melt it once it coagulates and becomes hard. Thus it will become a fixed color <note>a tincture or pigment</note> which penetrates and mixes with the <term>body</term> <note>the base metal being transformed; original: "Leichnamb," literally "corpse"</note>, joining and uniting with it, and it remains eternally. Of this powder, place one part by weight upon 100 parts of well-prepared <term>copper</term> <note>original: "♀"</note> or <term>iron</term> <note>original: "♂"</note>; without doubt, it will become white, pure, and good in every test, color, and work, and it remains eternally without end.

If you wish, however, to make another powder that is also certainly good: Take <term>salt</term> <note>original: "Koch," likely referring to common salt or sal-gemme</note>, separated and fixed, one part; sulfur, separated and fixed, also one part; and powdered silver, also one part. Rub these exceedingly well together upon a stone and saturate them with <term>sal ammoniac water</term> <note>ammonium chloride solution</note> three or four times—rubbing, saturating, and drying. Then lay this upon a stone in a damp place and let it turn to water <note>the process of deliquescence, where a substance absorbs moisture from the air until it dissolves</note>, as I have taught you. Keep that which becomes water; the rest you should rub further and saturate more with sal ammoniac water, and lay it again upon the stone in a damp place until it all becomes water. Draw this water through the <term>clarifying-cap</term> <note>a filtration or distillation apparatus; original: "Leuterhut"</note> as I have taught you before. Place the water in a water bath <note>original: "setz das Wasser in Wasser," a bain-marie</note> and not in the ashes, for otherwise it will become too hard for you to purify, and you will lose your labor. And when you have clarified it thus, put it in a glass and seal it as I have just taught you, and melt it with a gentle fire. Then it will become a white and hard matter, as transparent as crystal, which melts in the fire like wax and penetrates the metallic bodies and remains with them. Place one part of this powder upon a hundred parts of any calcined and purified body; it will endure and remain always white and good.

However, I advise you not to use it upon impure <term>copper</term> <note>original: "♀"</note> or bodies, for after the third or fourth test, it will vanish and come to nothing.

# A L C H E M Y
## A Thorough Report /
### concerning what the true Art

->contains and is capable of /<-
->In the Universal and Particular Way,<-
<note>original: "In Via Vniuerfali & Particulari"</note>
->Drawn together<-
->from all the Philosophers.<-

<margin>Calcination of the Imperfect Metals. <note>original: "tio Imperfectorum"</note></margin>
First and foremost, you must know how the four <term>imperfect metals</term> <note>metals that were believed to be "unripe" or chemically unstable compared to gold and silver; original: "Imperfecta Metalla"</note> are <term>calcined</term> <note>reduced to powder through heat or chemical action; original: "calciniert"</note>. Namely: <term>Saturn</term> <note>lead; original: "Saturnus"</note> and <term>Jupiter</term> <note>tin; original: "Iupiter"</note> are calcined in one way through salt, and from Saturn comes <term>minium</term> <note>red lead; original: "Menig"</note> and <term>ceruse</term> <note>white lead; original: "Cerussa"</note>. <term>Venus</term> <note>copper; original: "Venus"</note>, however, is calcined through sulfur, and becomes <term>burnt copper</term> <note>copper oxide; original: "Aes vstum"</note>. <term>Mars</term> <note>iron; the OCR "Meeß" is likely a transcription error for "Mars" or "Marß"</note> is calcined through vinegar, and becomes <term>Saffron of Mars</term> <note>iron oxide; original: "Crocus Martis"</note>. However, the calcination of <term>Sol</term> <note>the Sun, representing gold; original: "Solis"</note> and <term>Luna</term> <note>the Moon, representing silver; original: "Lunæ"</note> you will find in the <term>Greater Work</term> <note>the quest for the Philosophers' Stone; original: "Opere Maiori"</note>.

### First follows the Particular Work.

<margin>Which calxes are to be taken. <note>original: "Qui Calces sumendi"</note></margin>
If you now wish to make a <term>Particular</term> <note>a limited alchemical process aimed at a specific result rather than the universal stone; original: "Particular"</note> from the imperfect metals and work toward the "red" <note>the final stage of transmutation</note>, then you must take the <term>calxes</term> <note>metal powders; original: "Calces"</note> of Copper, Iron, or also Lead, which are red in themselves, that is, <term>minium</term> <note>original: "Minia"</note>. But for the "white," take the calxes of Tin or Lead, that is, <term>ceruse</term> <note>original: "Cerussam"</note>.

### What is the Mercury of the Philosophers?
<note>original: "Mercurius Philosophorum quid?"</note>

Next, you must know what the <term>Mercury of the Philosophers</term> <note>not common quicksilver, but a theoretical "first matter" or essential solvent; original: "Mercurius Philosophorum"</note> is, through which all metals, <term>perfect and imperfect</term> <note>gold/silver and base metals respectively</note>, are dissolved and reduced into <term>First Matter</term> <note>the primordial substance from which all things are made; original: "Primam Materiam"</note>. Regarding how it is prepared, you will find good instruction in the Second Part, "On the Greater Work," "On the Matter of the Stone," in the first chapter. For the <term>Matter of the Stone</term> <note>the raw materials for the Philosophers' Stone; original: "Materia Lapidis"</note> is the same in <term>Universal</term> and <term>Particular</term> works. The Particular works are the same as the Universal, except that the Universal must be worked more subtly and with more effort and time than the Particular. This is because their entire <term>composition</term> <note>original: "Compositum"</note> is nothing but pure gold and silver, and its <term>power</term> <note>original: "Virtute"</note> extends much further—and almost infinitely—as a medicine for human and metallic bodies than the Particular works.

It introduces the "Mercury of the Philosophers" as a universal solvent and explains the difference between the "Particular" and "Universal" alchemical works.</summary>

# Report on Alchemy
### [continued]

But they do not extend themselves further / except for a time / until they are aided in their **Multiplication** <note>The alchemical process of increasing the quantity or potency of the Philosopher's Stone; original: "Multiplication"</note> / with great caution. And the **Matter of the Stone** <note>The essential substance used to create the Philosopher's Stone; original: "Materia Lapidis"</note> must be worked in all works for the **Red** <note>The final stage of the Great Work (rubedo), associated with gold; original: "auff Roth"</note>, **from the Sun** <note>Gold; original: "ex Sole"</note>: and for the **White** <note>The penultimate stage of the Great Work (albedo), associated with silver; original: "auff Weiß"</note>, **from the Moon** <note>Silver; original: "ex Luna"</note>.

<margin>**Putrefaction** <note>The stage of decomposition or "rotting" necessary for transformation; original: "Putrefactio"</note>.</margin>
<margin>**Separation of the dissolved from the undissolved** <note>original: "Separatio Soluti a non Soluto"</note>.</margin>
Once you have the Matter of the Stone / take the **calx** <note>The fine powder or oxide left after a metal has been burned or corroded; original: "Kalchs"</note> of whichever **imperfect metal** you wish / and when it is most subtly prepared / put it into a **vessel** <note>A lamp-shaped glass container; original: "Ampel"</note> with a long neck / and pour enough of your **Lunaria** <note>Literally "Lunar Water," a specialized alchemical solvent or "mercurial water" used to dissolve metals; original: "Lunariæ"</note> over it / so that it rises four fingers above the **calces** <note>The powdered metal; original: "Calces"</note>. Quickly place a **blind alembic** <note>A still-head without a spout or "nose," used to keep vapors inside the vessel for digestion rather than distillation; original: "blinden Helmen"</note> upon it / and seal it well / so that nothing may smell or escape / Place it day and night in warm sand. After that, place it in an unsealed vessel in a **water bath** <note>A gentle heating method using a container of boiling water; original: "Balneum Mariæ"</note> for 6 days and nights. When the time is up / take the vessel out / and pour that which has dissolved / and is clear water / into a **cucurbit** <note>A gourd-shaped chemical flask; original: "Cucurbitam"</note> which is similar in shape to the first vessel / except the belly should not be so flat / and the bottom not so wide. Also, the cucurbit should be twice as large in proportion as the vessel. In this way, one may always pour from two vessels into one cucurbit. But in the pouring, one must take care / that it is not made cloudy. Afterward, pour as much **Lunaria** over it again / four fingers high / but let it stand for 6 days and nights / as before / in **putrefaction** <note>original: "Putrefactione"</note>. Continue this pouring / putrefying / decanting / and closing of both glasses / with the blind alembics / until the **body** <note>The solid material; original: "Corpus"</note> is evacuated of its **spirits** <note>The volatile, "life-giving" essence of the metal; original: "Spiritibus"</note>. The decanted liquid / should also be well-sealed / and kept in a **warm and moist place** <note>original: "Calido & Humido"</note>.

If, however, you should lack enough **Lunaria** for this / take the cucurbit in which all the **liquefactions** <note>The dissolved substances; original: "Liquefactiones"</note> are held / place an alembic with a spout upon it / place a **receiver** <note>A vessel to catch the distillate; original: "Recipienten"</note> before it / and distill it in a **water bath** <note>original: "Balneo"</note> with gentle heat. Take off two-thirds of the water / and put that same **Lunaria** back onto the calx / as before. Repeat this until no more of the **spirit** <note>original: "Spiritu"</note> remains in the **earth** <note>The solid residue; original: "Erden"</note>. # Now Follows the Second Part
->Concerning the Universal Way, or the Great Work of the Philosophers’ Stone.<-
<note>original: "De Via Vniuersali, siue Opere Maiori Philosophici Lapidis."</note>

This treatise is divided into three parts. First, it tells what the <term>Matter of the Stone</term> <note>original: "Materia Lapidis"; the physical substance used as the starting point</note> is and how it should be prepared. Second, what the <term>Form of the Stone</term> <note>original: "Forma Lapidis"; the essential character or "soul" of the substance</note> is. Third, after the Matter and Form are prepared, how one should put them together according to their proportion and cook them properly, so that the <term>Philosophers’ Stone</term> <note>original: "Lapis Philosophorum"</note> may be finished from them.

## CHAPTER ONE,
## Concerning the Matter of the Stone.

Initially, it is necessary to know that this gold, which one intends to use for this purpose, must be prepared through <term>antimony</term> or <term>Aqua Regis</term> <note>literally "Royal Water," a powerful mixture of acids capable of dissolving gold</note>, and thereafter <term>cemented</term> <note>A refining process where metal is heated with powdered additives to remove impurities</note> two or three times, and made as fine as possible. Furthermore, you should beat it into round discs or plates; specifically, if it weighs four <term>Loth</term> <note>A historical unit of weight, roughly equivalent to 2 ounces or 60 grams</note>, let it be somewhat wider than a <term>Thaler</term> <note>A large silver coin common in the Holy Roman Empire</note>, then it is correct.

Then take a thick glass, shaped like a <term>urinal</term> <note>A common alchemical flask with a wide body and a neck, named for its resemblance to medical vessels</note>, not very tall. Into it, put twelve times as much weight as the gold plates of <term>Magnesia</term> <note>In this context, an alchemical mineral or flux, not the modern chemical element magnesium</note>, crushed into pieces the size of a hazelnut, or as it pleases you, provided that it can fit into the glass. Thereafter, place the gold plates upon the urinal and fit a <term>helm with a nose</term> <note>An "alembic" or still-head with a protruding spout for distillation</note> that fits correctly onto it. Seal it with <term>lute</term> <note>A specialized alchemical paste or cement used to make joints airtight</note> up over the beak to protect it from the heat so that it does not crack. Have a fine earthenware "hat" made of two pieces to go over it, so that you can surround the little furnace...

# Report on Alchemy

->Rectification of the Water and the Oil.<-

Now that you have separated these things in this way six times, rectify both the Water and the Oil as follows: Take your water in a clean new glass vessel and place a helm <note>the cap or "head" of a still used for distillation</note> upon it, and set it in **Mary’s Bath** <note>original: *Balneum Mariæ*; a water bath used to provide gentle, even heat</note>. Distill the water with gentle warmth, so that one drop falls out between every 20 and 30 beats <note>likely referring to the pulse or a slow count</note>. Place that again in a fresh glass, as before, and do this four times, so that it reaches **a crystalline clarity** <note>original: *ad Cristallinam Serenitatem*</note>, and then it is prepared correctly. Do the same for the oil. However, you must distill the oil in the ashes <note>an ash-bath, which allows for higher temperatures than a water bath</note>. And pay close attention in all your work that it does not leak its scent <note>this warns against the evaporation of the volatile "spirit" of the substance</note>, for that would result in a great loss to you. The water you have made, call **Lunaria** <note>Moon-water</note>, and the oil, call **Water of Life** <note>original: *Aquam Vitæ*</note>.

Keep both in good glass vessels, well-secured with the **Lute of Wisdom** <note>original: *Luto Sapientiæ*; an airtight alchemical sealant made of clay, lime, and other binders</note>, so that nothing leaks out. These two, oil and water—**that is, Air and Water**—or **Lunaria** and **Water of Life**, smell foul. And this is the entire preparation of the **Matter of the Stone** <note>original: *Materiæ Lapidis*</note>.

## CHAPTER TWO,
### Concerning the Form of the Stone.

The Form of the Stone is nothing other than Gold with Magnesia for the red <note>the "Red Work" or Rubedo, the final stage for making gold</note>, and Silver with Magnesia for the white <note>the "White Work" or Albedo, for making silver</note>. Nor should anything else be added to the Stone that is meant to remain with it, for it must be worked from these things from the beginning until the end; otherwise, all effort and labor would be lost.

For the Form of the Stone <note>likely "Lapidis"</note>, take the gold that you previously covered over the "judgment" <note>this may refer to gold purified by cupellation or a specific test</note>, or another that is similar and of very good quality, and beat it thin. However much gold you take, always take for every 1 *Loth* <note>a German unit of weight, roughly 14.5 grams</note> of gold, one and a half *Loth* of Mercury (☿) or **raw Quick-silver** <note>original: *Argenti Viui Crudi*</note>. Amalgamate them and pour it out into cold water; it will then be somewhat harder than the mixture used for gilding. Weigh it, and take a fourth part of its weight in white salt. Rub the salt into the amalgam so that it becomes a pure black mass. Put it in a crucible and set it to the fire; let the mercury evaporate gradually so that nothing of it remains. Then take it out of the crucible and put it into a glazed vessel. Pour boiling pure water on it, stir it, let it settle again, and carefully strain the water away. Do this three or four times, so the salt is also removed and the gold is refined. Calcinate the "lime" <note>the resulting fine powder</note> and dry it in the sun.

<meta>This page continues the specific instructions for the chemical preparation of the "Stone." ->**On the Universal and Particular Way**<-

After this drying, take according to the proportion: for every 1 **Loth** <note>a historical unit of weight, approximately 1/2 ounce or 15 grams</note> of this **Gold Calx** <note>gold reduced to a fine powder through chemical means</note>, take 4 **Loth** of **Lunaria** <note>literally "Moon-water," a prepared alchemical solvent</note> made from the **Magnesia** <note>a term for a foundational alchemical mineral, not modern magnesium</note>. Or, what is most certain: if there is a large amount of the gold powder, ensure the Lunaria rises four finger-widths above it. Place it in a flask with a long neck, set a **blind helm** <note>a still-head without a spout, used to keep vapors inside for "digestion" rather than collection</note> upon it, and let it stand in **Mary’s Bath** <note>original: *Balneo*; a gentle water bath</note> for six days and nights. Pour it off as you did before into the already collected water, and secure it again. Do this until you have performed the process 7 times. Whatever of the powder is not dissolved by the seventh time, keep that separately.

Afterward, take the cucurbit containing all the **liquefactions** <note>original: *Liquefactiones*; the dissolved liquid extracts</note>, set a helm upon it, place a receiver in front, and draw the water over in the water bath with gentle heat until it looks like **melted wax** at the bottom. Then stop, and pour fresh Lunaria over it again. Secure it with the blind helm and set it in the water bath to **putrefy** <note>original: *putreficieren*; a process of warm digestion meant to break down the substance</note> for 6 weeks. Whatever is then dissolved, pour the clear water into a fresh glass, set a blind helm upon it, and keep it in a warm and moist place, as before. Over the glass from which you poured this, set a helm and draw down the moisture with the gentlest heat in the water bath, and dry it gently. Add fresh Lunaria to it again (as before) so that it rises four finger-widths above it, and let it stand in putrefaction for six days and nights. Pour off the clear liquid that has dissolved and dry the **dregs** <note>original: *Fęces*</note> again as before. Continue this pouring on, pouring off, and drying until the material entirely turns to water. Keep this second liquefaction constantly in the warm water bath, well-secured with a blind helm, just as you did with the first.

When it has all turned to water, set it again for six days and nights in the water bath under a blind helm to putrefy; then take it and separate the elements.

### The Separation of the Elements Follows

Draw the Water down in the water bath with gentle heat, and the **Air** <note>original: *Aërem*; referring to a more volatile "spirituous" fraction of the liquid</note> in the ash bath. Pour the water back onto the dregs, and let it putrefy again for 6 days and nights. Then draw the water off again with low heat...

### Report on Alchemy

...down in a **water bath** <note>original: *Balneo*; a gentle heating method using water to maintain a constant, low temperature</note> and the oil in **ashes** <note>original: *Cinere*; a method of dry heating where the vessel is placed in hot ashes</note>. Do this 25 times, so that the greater part of the water is converted into **air** <note>original: *Aërem*; here meaning a gaseous or highly volatile state</note> or oil. And repeat this until the **dregs** <note>original: *Fæces*</note> or **earth** <note>original: *Terra*</note>, when dried, no longer smoke upon a glowing metal plate and are like an intangible powder.

As much as you collect of this oil or air, put it into a **luted** <note>original: *verlutiert*; sealed with alchemical paste or clay to make it airtight</note> little glass and **rectify** <note>to purify a substance through repeated distillation</note> it once or thrice, just as you did with the oil earlier in the **preparation of the matter** <note>original: *præparation Materiæ*</note>, and keep it well secured.

Then weigh the intangible powder and take half its weight of the aforementioned oil. Put it in a glass, place a **blind helm** <note>a still-head without a spout, used to keep vapors inside the vessel for "digestion" rather than letting them escape</note> upon it, and set it in a water bath to **putrefy** <note>original: *putreficieren*; a stage of alchemical breakdown where the matter is allowed to rot or decompose in gentle heat</note> for six days and nights. Thus the matter will be moist. Put a helm <note>a standard distillation head with a spout</note> upon it and dry it with gentle heat. Pour the oil back in—half as much as there is powder—putrefy it and dry it again as before. And every time you dry the **earth** <note>original: *Terram*</note>, you must always weigh it so that you do not fail in the proportion of the oil. Do this until it drinks in much oil, namely four times as heavy as it was in the first drying or at the beginning. Then test it to see if it has enough: take a little of this dried powder and throw it on a glowing metal plate. If it vanishes entirely in smoke, then it has enough; if not, repeat it with the oil until you have the complete sign.

After this powder is thus well dried, put it in a **sublimation vessel** <note>original: *Sublin-torium*; a vessel designed to heat a solid until it vaporizes and deposits as a purified solid higher up</note>, put its cap on, give it a gentle fire at first, then increase it until the matter **sublimates** upward. Then take what has attached itself to the cap and the sides of the **sublimator** <note>original: *Sublimatorij*</note>; keep it cleanly together, for it is the perfect **Mineral Stone** <note>original: *Lapis Mineralis*</note>.

The black **dregs** <note>original: *Fæces*</note>, however, which remain at the bottom after the third sublimation, are no good; one need not regard them. But what hangs in the cap and on the sides of the glass, take that and put it in a clean little glass; add a little **Water of Life** <note>original: *Aquæ Vitæ*; high-proof distilled alcohol or a potent alchemical solvent</note>—though the **Ointment of the Philosophers** <note>original: *Vnguentum Philosophorum*; a specific refined alchemical preparation</note> is better. Seal it with its blind helm, set it for 8 days in a water bath to putrefy; thus it will become a pure oil. Keep that, for the **Form of the Stone** <note>original: *Forma Lapidis*</note> is then also prepared. And what was mentioned before regarding gold shall also be understood for silver if one wishes to work toward the **white** <note>the *albedo* or "whiteness" stage of the Great Work, which results in the ability to transmute metals into silver</note>.

# CHAPTER THREE
## On the Composition of Matter and Form.

Now that you have prepared and finished the **Matter and Form** of the Stone (as has been shown), take 1 part of this last oil that you obtained from the **sublimated powder**. Put it into a new, clean little flask or glass bulb. Add to it many times as much <term>Water of Life</term> <note>original: *Aquæ vitæ*; here referring to highly distilled and purified alcohol</note>, which has been highly **rectified** <note>purified through repeated distillation</note> as described above. Seal the little flask well at the bottom with <term>Clay of Wisdom</term> <note>original: *Luto Sapientiæ*; a specialized airtight sealant used by alchemists, often made of clay, lime, and organic binders</note>, as is the custom. Place it in reasonably warm **ashes** <note>a "sand bath" or ash bath for indirect, even heating</note> and let it become quite warm, ensuring the glass is well-protected against the escape of vapors. Mix it well in this manner and immediately place its **blind helm** <note>original: *blindes Helmlein*; a distillation head without a spout, used to force vapors to condense and fall back into the mixture (reflux)</note> upon it. This helm should be coated with a mixture of **egg white and quicklime**, with a small ring of good <term>Clay of Wisdom</term> carefully applied over the joints and further secured with egg white.

Place this in a <term>Furnace</term> <note>original: *Fornacem*</note> that maintains a steady heat and is easy to control. Regulate it with a low heat. In this way, the oil and the <term>Water of Life</term> will dissolve into one another so that in 12 days—if one proceeds correctly—the **black color** appears. With the same fire or heat, during the next 8 days, the blackness turns to **white**, and after another eight days, it turns into **yellow**. If the heat is strengthened slightly, the yellow color also turns into **red** within eight days, looking like an egg.

Afterward, one must remove the little glass with the **Stone**, and clean the Stone of the filth and impurities that cling to the glass around it. Place the cleaned Stone into another clean little glass, just like the previous one. Regulate it in the furnace again for 6 days and nights, but with a slightly stronger fire—specifically, so hot that one cannot easily bear to keep a hand in the ashes where the glass stands. When you remove it after 6 days, the <term>Animal Stone</term> <note>original: *Lapis Animalis*; a stage of the alchemical work associated with a more "animated" or potent state of the matter</note> is completely finished.

->The Vegetable Stone follows.<-

To make the aforementioned **Animal Stone** into the <term>Vegetable Stone</term> <note>original: *Lapidem Vegetabilem*; in alchemy, the "Vegetable" stage often refers to the Stone's ability to "grow" or multiply its power</note>: Take again, for example, if you had four <term>Loth</term> <note>a historical unit of weight, roughly 1/2 ounce or 15 grams</note> of the oil from the sublimated powder, and add three times that weight—which is 12 <term>Loth</term>—of <term>Water of Life</term>, and 1 <term>Quintlein</term> <note>a small unit of weight, about 4 grams</note> of the newly made <term>Animal Stone</term>. Put them together, mixed as before, and let them stand for 30 days, passing through the **colors** <note>original: *Colores*; the sequence of color changes (black, white, yellow, red) indicating the progress of the Great Work</note>. Thus you will have the <term>Vegetable Stone</term>.

## Following: Multiplication of the Stone.

If you then wish to multiply the <term>Stone</term> <note>original: *Lapidem*; the Philosopher's Stone</note> in <term>Virtue</term> <note>original: *Virtute*; referring to its inherent power or "potency" rather than moral virtue</note>, take as much of the aforementioned Stone as you wish and a third part as much <term>Water of Life</term> <note>original: *Aquæ Vitæ*; highly distilled alcohol or a specialized solvent</note>, and mix them as before. Set it in the heat and let it pass through the <term>Colors</term> <note>original: *Colores*; the characteristic color changes (black, white, yellow, red) that signal progress in the alchemical process</note>. Or, take the finished Stone and place it with a little Water of Life in a <term>Water Bath</term> <note>original: *Balneum*; a gentle heating method</note> to purify and congeal it, as mentioned above; this is better than setting it in as a powder. You may do this as often as you wish, and the Stone will become better the longer it is worked. For the more it is multiplied, the more it <term>tinges</term> <note>original: *tingirt*; the alchemical ability of the Stone to "dye" or transform the nature of a base metal into gold</note>. Namely: if it originally transmutes 10 parts and is multiplied once, it will then transmute 100 parts. The second time, 1,000 parts, and so on.

For the **White Work** <note>original: *Auff das Weiß*; the process of creating the Silver Stone</note>, one uses exactly the same labor, except that in the beginning, one requires no <term>Antimony</term> <note>original: *Antimonium*</note> or <term>Cement</term> <note>a corrosive powder used in refining</note> to finish the silver. Instead, one refines the silver two or three times on the <term>Cupel</term> <note>original: *Capellen*; a shallow porous vessel used in assaying and refining precious metals</note> to the highest degree, makes it fine, and beats it into a round plate. The colors come again: the first color is **Green**, the second **Red**, the third **White**, and the fourth is the metal, white as silver. Otherwise, the process is the same for one as it is for the other.

## Following: The Projection.

Now you should know that when you wish to <term>cast upon</term> <note>original: *auffwerffen*; the act of "Projection," adding the Stone to molten base metal</note>, you will find no metal that accepts the substance of the <term>Blessed Stone</term> <note>original: *Lapidis Benedicti*</note> into itself more readily than gold (where the Stone has been prepared for the **Red Work**). For the **White Work**, however, silver is most pleasant to it. Therefore, upon whichever of these two you wish to cast, throw 1 part of your **Medicine** upon 100 parts of gold flowing in the crucible. Then, throw one part of that same gold again upon 100 parts of gold flowing in the crucible, and so on as long as it pleases you. When you have sufficiently multiplied it in the gold—for this is the **Multiplication in Quantity**—then throw 1 part of this same gold (which is now also Medicine) upon 100 parts of <term>Imperfect Body</term> <note>original: *Corporis Imperfecti*; a base metal like lead or tin</note> or <term>Raw Quicksilver</term> <note>original: *Argenti Viui Crudi*; mercury</note>, and refine it on the test. Then you will truly have gold, equal to all proofs and eternally lasting.

## To make Drinkable Gold from the Stone.

If your Stone is multiplied to the <term>Highest Perfection</term> <note>original: *ad summam Perfectionem*</note> in virtue, or also in quantity, multiplied in gold alone, then you may dissolve it again in a <term>Water Bath</term> <note>original: *Balneo*</note>. It is then **Drinkable Gold** <note>original: *Aurum Potabile*; a legendary alchemical medicine believed to have restorative and life-extending properties</note>. Not only all imperfect...

Metals are good to transform into true Gold and Silver through **Projection** <note>The act of casting a small amount of the Stone onto a large mass of molten base metal to effect transformation</note> alone, as mentioned; moreover, it is the highest **Medicine** <note>original: *Medicin*; in alchemy, the "Medicine" refers to the Stone’s ability to "heal" base metals into gold or human bodies into health</note> for metallic bodies that exists on Earth.

But if you cast it on dry, the greater part of your Medicine flies away <note>The alchemist is concerned about "volatilization," where the precious powder turns to smoke and escapes before it can react with the molten metal</note> before it enters. For this Medicine has the greatest attachment and affinity for metals.

If it is dissolved entirely into water, or much better into oil, then it has its greatest effect in human **bodies** <note>original: *Corporibus*</note>, or other living animals; for this reason, **inceration** <note>original: *Inceratio*</note> was also invented.

### The First Part.

When you have now prepared the **Lunaria** <term>original: *Lunariam*; likely a silver-based solvent or "moon-water"</term> and the **Water of Life** <term>original: *Aquam Vitæ*; usually distilled alcohol or a potent solvent</term> (as mentioned above in the Second Part), it is not yet entirely finished as it should be. Then take the pregnant Earth, lay it in a **Sublimatorium** <term>a vessel used for sublimation—turning a solid into vapor and back to solid</term> made of clay, well-sealed for 24 hours; **sublimate** it, so that the pure may be separated from the impure. And calcine the Earth, imbibe it, and putrefy it again; distill and calcine it as before, and do this four times. Then set it by itself in a water bath to dissolve, and congeal it again; do this also four times, then you have the true **Salt of Tartar**, or **Vegetable Salt**. But the water drawn from it is the **Lunaria** <note>original: *Lunaria*; literally "moon-water," a solvent believed to be related to the powers of silver or the moon</note>, sharpened with the gold, which you should **rectify** <note>the process of purifying a liquid by repeated distillation</note> twice.

With this sharpened Lunaria, dissolve the **Sulfur of Nature** <note>original: *Sulphur Naturę*; the inherent vital energy or essence within a substance</note> which you produced in the **sublimation** <note>the process where a solid turns directly into a gas and then back to a solid, used to purify substances</note>, into a pure poured-off water, just as you initially did with the calcined gold. Then separate the elements in this way: set it to putrefy for 16 days. When those are over, set it in warm ashes; take the moisture from it with a gentle fire, as much as you can extract. Take this entire moisture and set it immediately, without any further putrefaction, into the **water bath** <note>original: *Balneum*; a method of heating using a container of water to ensure gentle, even warmth</note>. Draw the water down with the very gentlest heat, so that the **Air** <note>original: *Aër*; the alchemical element of volatility and movement</note> remains at the bottom. But over the dregs, which previously remained in the glass in the ashes during the distillation, put the water again—the water you just drew from the Air—and putrefy it for two days. Distill it again in the ashes and take the water in the water bath. Begin this process again, repeating it twelve times. And when you have brought all the Air together, rectify it seven times in **ashes** <note>original: *Cinere*; using warm ash as a heat source for distillation</note>. The dregs that it leaves behind in each rectification should be added to the dregs that remained from the twelve distillations in the ashes mentioned above. These same dregs, in which the **Fire** <note>the alchemical element of heat and transformation</note> is contained, should be rubbed small on a glass plate. Pour the whole water that you drew from the Air onto it. Set it to putrefy for three days, distill it in sand, and dry it out well so that all moisture comes out. Set this same moisture in the water bath and draw the water from it with the gentlest warmth; what then remains at the bottom of the glass is the Fire.

Place the water over the dregs again, putrefy it again as before, and treat it in all things as you did previously. Do this eight times. And whatever you have extracted from the Fire, rectify that also seven times. Likewise, the dregs that the Fire always leaves behind should be added to the **Earth** <note>original: *Erdtrich*; the solid, fixed residue</note> or dregs that remained behind. But the water drawn from all these separations must also be rectified seven times in the water bath. Keep these three **liquors** <note>original: *Liquores*; alchemical liquids or essences</note>, each individually in well-secured glasses, and mark them so that you do not take or grasp one for the other when you wish to use them.

# In the Universal and Particular Way.

...is just as heavy, and a third part as heavy as the **calcined gold** <note>gold reduced to a fine powder through intense heat</note>, or **sulfur**, and likewise of the oil—that is, the **Philosophical Ointment** <term>Vnguenti Philosophici</term>—is also as heavy as the **earth** <note>the solid residue remaining at the bottom of the flask</note> is. Put it all together in a glass for **putrefaction** <note>the process of breaking down a substance through gentle warmth and moisture</note> for twelve days. After twelve days, add as much water again by weight; let it putrefy again, and continue doing this until the twelve parts of water have been added. 

Afterwards, take the **Air** <note>original: *Aërem*; likely referring to a volatile distilled fraction</note>, divide it into eight parts; put one part into the glass with the previous mixture and let it putrefy for eight days. Thereafter, add another part, and so on, until all eight are in. Then divide the **Fire** <note>another distilled fraction or perhaps a specific grade of heat</note> into five parts; add one part, let it putrefy for eight days, and so on until all five parts have been added. When all this is done, place a **helm with a nose** <note>a distillation lid or alembic with a pouring spout</note> upon it, and take from it approximately four or six parts of the moisture. Take the remainder that stays in the glass and put it into its **fixing-glass** <term>Figier Glaß</term>. Give it twenty-two days, or as long as necessary (as you will see by the colors), with a gentle fire. Thus it congeals into a **red, transparent, round stone, like a ruby**.

### Multiplication.

Afterwards, take this stone and dissolve it with three times its weight of **Lunaria** <note>the alchemical solvent "moon-water" previously prepared</note> which has been sharpened with gold. Also add a third part, by weight of the **stone** <term>Lapis</term>, of calcined gold—which is called sulfur—and let it putrefy in a **water bath** <note>original: *Balneo*</note> for twelve days. Put it again into the fixing-glass, as before, and let it pass through the **colors** <note>the sequence of color changes—black, white, yellow, red—indicating the progress of the alchemical Work</note> with a gentle fire for twelve days, or until it is finished. And in this way, you may multiply it **in power** <note>original: *in Virtute*</note> as often as you wish.

You may also multiply it **in power and quantity** <note>original: *in Virtute, & Quantitate*</note> together, namely: if you put four parts of calcined gold or sulfur, and one part of the prepared **stone** <term>Lapide</term>, as well as twelve parts of the sharpened Lunaria together into putrefaction, it will dissolve in four days. Then, as before, take the fourth or sixth part of the moisture through distillation with the "helm," and afterwards fix it as before. And the more often such **multiplication** is repeated, the more useful the stone is in **projection** <note>the final act of alchemy: throwing the finished stone onto base metal to transform it into gold</note>.

This multiplication may also be done in another way, namely: take **amalgamated gold**, made from one part gold and five parts **raw mercury** <term>☿ Crudi</term>; add four parts of the **amalgam** <term>Amalgamæ</term> to one **lot** <note>a historical unit of weight, roughly 15-16 grams</note> of the stone. Dissolve each separately, mixed with Lunaria, place it into the **Vessel of Hermes** <term>Vaß Hermetis</term>, and multiply it as often as you wish. With this, you produce just as much gold in proportion as otherwise.

# The Fourth Part.
## Preparation of the Mineral Stone.

To assemble the **Mineral Stone** in a short time, proceed as follows: Make an **Aqua fort** <term>Aqua fortis</term> <note>literally "strong water," usually nitric acid</note> from two pounds of **calcined vitriol** <note>iron or copper sulfate heated until it becomes a dry powder</note>, one pound of **saltpeter**, and one and a half pounds of **cinnabar** <note>mercury sulfide</note>. When it has been distilled as is customary, always add one and a half pounds of fresh cinnabar to each pound of the resulting water, and distill it again. Do this five times, so that you bring three pounds of cinnabar into one pound of water. Once this is done, take for every one pound of *Aqua fort*—thus sharpened with the cinnabar—one pound of **Lunaria** <note>original: *Lunariæ*; likely a reference to a specific alchemical liquor or "moon-water"</note>, which has been best sharpened with **Salt of Tartar** <term>Sale Tartari</term> <note>potassium carbonate</note>. Mix these together very gently, let it stand for one or two days in a warm **water bath** <term>Balneo</term>, so that it may be well incorporated, and afterwards distill it all together.

<margin>This salt is nobler than the Salt of Tartar.</margin>
If you now wish to make the **Vegetable Salt** <term>Sal Vegetabile</term>, then let it circulate for 16 days in the water bath; it will then unite at the bottom of the glass like a crystal glass. Keep this and use it in the Mineral Stone instead of the **Philosophical Ointment** <term>Unguenti Philosophici</term>. When you put your **calcined gold** into it, add one ounce of gold for every twelve ounces of the salt; set it to **putrefy** <note>to break down through gentle heat</note> for 20 days. Add also one ounce of the Philosophical Ointment, and everything will become pure water. Afterwards, place a **distillation lid** <note>original: *Helm*</note> upon it, and draw the water off in the water bath so that only the gold and what the water leaves behind remain at the bottom. **Congeal** <note>solidify</note> this in the ash-heat. When it has cooled well and you have opened the glass, weigh the material, and add exactly the same weight of the aforementioned mixed water and a very little of the Philosophical Ointment; dissolve it again in the water bath and **regulate** <note>original: *guliers*; likely *reguliers*, meaning to process or fix</note> it in the ash-heat. Do this ten times. Then take your dissolved powder; for every one ounce of powder, add twelve ounces of the best rectified *Lunaria*, sharpened with Salt of Tartar and Gold, and one ounce of calcined gold or sulfur. Circulate it all through the stage of putrefaction; put it into a **Hermetic Vessel** <term>Vas Hermetis</term> <note>a glass flask sealed with heat</note>, let it pass through all the **colors** <note>the traditional sequence of black, white, and red in the alchemical process</note> for 22 days, and **fix** it <note>render it stable under heat</note> if it is not finished before that time. However, I expect you will accomplish it in 10 or, at the longest, 12 days.

When this has been done, take this **medicine**; namely, when there are 12 ounces, add half an ounce of Philosophical Ointment. Putrefy them together for nine days in the water bath, then congeal it in the ash-heat. Dissolve it again by itself without any addition, and congeal it. Continue this until it no longer wishes to be congealed; then you have enough, and you can finish this medicine in 80 days.

# Multiplication of the Medicine. <note>original: *Multiplicatio Medicinæ*; the process of increasing the quantity and potency of the alchemical substance</note>

Multiply this medicine in this way: Take one ounce of this Stone in a glass and place upon it half an ounce of the **amalgam** <note>a blend of metals, usually involving mercury</note> made from one part gold and five parts **mercury**. Seal the glass with a **blind helm** <note>a distillation cap without a pouring spout, used to force vapors to condense and fall back into the vessel</note> and place it in warm ashes for six hours. When the material appears like gold, then stop; if not, continue with the fire until you see the sign, or until it turns into a red powder. Then take again a little of the **Philosophical Ointment** <term>Vnguento Philosophico</term> <note>a specialized alchemical substance used as a solvent or binder, previously described in the text</note>, use it to dissolve this powder, and congeal it again in the ashes. Repeat this until it will no longer allow itself to be congealed.

Then take one part of this final medicine; add it again to ten parts of amalgam in a sealed glass; dissolve it and congeal it. From that same medicine, take one part again, add it to ten parts of amalgam or common mercury, and proceed as before. Continue with this repetition for as long and as many times as needed until it no longer becomes a red powder but rather a hard, brittle **mass** <term>Massa</term>. Then cast some of it out and observe how much it **tinges** <note>original: *tingiere*; the act of the medicine "dyeing" or transforming a base metal into a noble one</note>. In this way, you will find the correct proportion—how many parts of mercury or imperfect metals you may transform with one part of this medicine—so that it becomes eternal, stable gold, as good as that which comes from the mines.

But if you wish to perform a **multiplication** that proceeds forever without end, then take some of the last medicine or "congelation" where the mass has become hard. Grind it, then take 50 parts by weight of common mercury (relative to the weight of the mass) and put them together in a well-secured glass. Let it stand in a constant, small, gentle heat for 30 days. It will then again be a hard, congealed mass; take this out. Take as much of it as the mercury you added to it, and use it to transform metals according to your pleasure. And when the mass is ground down, add the same amount of mercury again—namely, the 50th part—and keep it again for 30 days in the heat as before. Then take the medicine out again and add mercury once more. Carry this on for as long as you live, and you shall have an **increase** <term>Augment</term>, a refuge for performing **projections** <note>original: *proijcieren*; the final transformation of base metal into gold</note> in your time of need.

## The Fourth Part.
### The Precise Preparation of the Mineral Stone. <note>original: *Accuratio Lapidis Mineralis*</note>

To assemble the **Mineral Stone** quickly, proceed as follows: Make a **strong water** <term>Aqua fortis</term> <note>a powerful acidic solvent, usually nitric acid</note> from two pounds of calcined **vitriol** <note>iron or copper sulfate used to create acids</note>, one pound of saltpeter <note>OCR cut off: *Salpeter*</note>, and one and a half pounds of **cinnabar** <note>a bright red mineral consisting of mercury sulfide</note>. When it has been distilled as is customary, always add one and a half pounds of fresh cinnabar to each pound of the water and distill it again. Do this five times, so that you have incorporated three pounds of cinnabar into one pound of water. Once this is done, take one pound of the strong water that has been sharpened with cinnabar, and one pound of **Moonwort** <term>Lunariæ</term> <note>an alchemical herb or substance often associated with silver or lunar properties</note> that has been purified in the best way with **Salt of Tartar** <term>Sale Tartari</term> <note>potassium carbonate, used as a flux or purifying agent</note>. Mix these together very gently; let it stand for one or two days in a warm **water bath** <term>Balneo</term> so that they incorporate well with one another, and then distill them together.

This salt is more noble than the Salt of Tartar. <note>original Latin: *Hoc Sal nobilius Sale Tartari*</note>

If you now wish to make the **Vegetable Salt** <term>Sal Vegetabile</term>, circulate the mixture for 16 days in the water bath until it unites at the bottom of the glass like a crystalline glass. Keep that and use it in the Mineral Stone in place of the **Philosophical Ointment** <term>Vnguentum Philosophicum</term>. Put your calcined gold into it—add one ounce of gold for every twelve ounces of the salt—and set it to **putrefy** <note>the stage of "rotting" or breaking down the material, often resulting in a black color</note> for 20 days. Also add one ounce of the Philosophical Ointment, and it will become pure water. Afterwards, place a distillation head <note>original: *Helm*</note> upon it and draw off the water in the water bath, so that only the gold and whatever the water leaves behind remain at the bottom. Congeal <note>solidify</note> this in the **ashes** <note>a sand or ash bath used for gentle, even heating</note>. When it has cooled well and you have opened the glass, weigh the material and add an equal weight of the aforementioned cinnabar mixture and a very little Philosophical Ointment. Dissolve it again in the water bath and congeal it in the ashes. Do this ten times. Then take your dissolved powder; for every one ounce of powder, add twelve ounces of the best rectified Moonwort, prepared with Salt of Tartar and gold, and one ounce of calcined gold or sulfur. Put it all through the process of putrefaction; place it in a **Hermetic vessel** <term>Vas Hermetis</term> <note>a glass flask sealed airtight by melting the neck</note>, let it pass through the **colors** <note>the sequence of color changes—usually black, white, and red—that signal progress in the Alchemical Work</note> for 22 days, and fix it <note>render it stable and non-volatile</note> if it is not already finished by that time. However, I expect that you will complete it in 10 or, at the longest, 12 days.

When this is done, take this **Medicine** <note>another term for the Alchemical Stone or its intermediate stages</note>: for every ounce, take half an ounce of the Philosophical Ointment and putrefy them together for nine days in the water bath. Afterwards, congeal it in the ashes, then dissolve it again by itself without any addition, and congeal it. Continue this until it no longer allows itself to be dissolved. Then you have enough, and you can finish this Medicine in 80 days.

# On the Universal and Particular Path <note>original: *In Via Vniuersali & Particulari*</note>

### Multiplication of the Medicine <note>original: *Multiplicatio Medicinæ*</note>

Multiply this **Medicine** <note>in alchemy, the "Medicine" refers to the Elixir or the Philosopher's Stone, capable of "healing" base metals into gold</note> as follows: Take one ounce of this **Stone** in a glass, and lay upon it half an ounce of the **amalgam** <term>Amalgama</term> <note>a blend of metals, in this case gold and mercury</note> that is made from one part gold and five parts **mercury** <term>Mercurij</term>. Seal the glass with a **blind helm** <note>a still-head without a spout, used for refluxing or circulating vapors back into the vessel</note>; place it in warm ashes for six hours. When the material looks like gold, then stop; if not, then continue with the fire until you see the sign, or until it turns into a red powder. Then take again a little of the **Philosophical Ointment** <term>Vnguento Philosophico</term> <note>a fatty or oily substance produced during the alchemical process, used as a solvent</note>, add it to this powder to **dissolve** <term>solvieren</term> it, and **congeal** <term>congeliers</term> <note>turning a liquid back into a solid through cooling or evaporation</note> it again in the ashes. Repeat this until it will no longer allow itself to be congealed.

Then take one part of this last **Medicine**; add it again to ten parts of the **amalgam** in a sealed glass; dissolve it and congeal it. From that same Medicine take one part again, add it to ten parts of the amalgam, or to common mercury, and do with it as before. Continue with this repetition for so long and so many times until it no longer becomes a red powder but rather a hard, brittle mass. Then cast some of it <note>perform a "projection" or test</note> and pay attention to how much it **tinges** <note>the transformative power of the stone to "color" or change the nature of another metal</note>. Thus you will find the right **proportion** <note>original: *Proporß*</note>: how many parts of mercury or of the **imperfect metals** <note>base metals like lead, tin, or copper</note> you may tinge with one part of this Medicine, so that it becomes eternal, stable gold, as good as that which comes from the mines.

But if you wish to perform a **multiplication** that proceeds forever without end, then take some of the last Medicine or **congealment** <note>original: *Congelation*</note> where the mass has become hard. Grind it up, then take 50 parts by weight of common mercury (relative to the weight of the mass), put them together in a well-secured glass, and let it stand in a steady, small, gentle heat for 30 days. Then it will once again be a hard, congealed mass; take this out. Take as much from it as the mercury you added to it, and **tinge** with it according to your pleasure. And when the mass is ground up, then add as much mercury to it again—namely, the 50th part—and keep it again for 30 days in the heat as before. Then take the Medicine out again and add more mercury. Continue this for as long as you live, and you shall have an **increase** <note>original: *Augment*</note>, a refuge to **project** <term>proijcieren</term> <note>the act of casting the stone upon base metal to transform it</note> in your time of need.

# Report on Alchemy <note>original: *Bericht von der Alchemey*</note>

...half a pound of cinnabar <note>original: *Zinober*; mercury sulfide</note>; putrefy it day and night in a water bath <note>original: *Balneo*</note>, then set it in sand and burn it into a strong water <note>original: *Aqua fortis*; usually nitric acid</note> as is customary. Afterward, add fresh vitriol <note>sulfate minerals</note> and cinnabar in the previous proportion to the water; treat it as before. Do this five times. Then take one ounce of gold, which has been calcined <note>reduced to a fine powder through heat</note> most subtly by means of common mercury <note>original: *Mercurium Vulgi*</note>, and afterward made volatile by the calcined volatile water <note>original: *Wasser Volatile*</note>. After such time, take it out, and thus it is resolved <note>dissolved into liquid form</note>. Take that, place a helm <note>a distillation cap</note> upon it, and gently draw off the water so that nothing remains behind but the gold and what the water leaves behind—a mass as large as the gold—remaining in the glass. To this, add one ounce of **Philosophical Ointment** <note>original: *Vnguenti Philosophici*; a refined alchemical substance, often fatty or oily in consistency</note>; set it for two days in putrefaction, then dry it in ashes <note>original: *in Cinere*; a gentle heat source</note>. After that, add some of the aforementioned strong water—no more than the amount of powder remaining in the glass—putrefy it for one day and night, and dry it in the ashes. Do this ten times.

After this, add twelve ounces of strong water, an ounce and a half of **Philosophical Ointment**, and one ounce of calcined gold or sulfur <note>original: *Sulphuris*</note> to the aforementioned powder. Set it for six days in a water bath to putrefy, then afterward in a circulating vessel <note>original: *Circulatorium*</note> or Hermetic vessel <note>original: *Vas Hermetis*; a glass vessel sealed with heat</note>. Let it stand in the ashes for ten or twelve days until it remains at the bottom like a stone and no longer rises upward. Then dissolve it by itself, or with a little **Philosophical Ointment** in a water bath; congeal it in ashes, dissolve it again, and congeal it. Do this three times, or until it no longer allows itself to be congealed but remains like an oil. Thus you have perfectly made the **Medicine**, which is a mixture of mineral and vegetable; with this, you may tincture <note>transform base metals into gold or silver</note> as mentioned above. And this Medicine, which the authors have made before, is prepared in eight days.
