# In the Universal and Particular Way <note>original: *In Via Vniuersali & Particulari*; refers to two different paths of alchemical work—one for a general medicine and one for specific metals</note>

...in a **water bath** <note>original: *Balneum*; a vessel of warm water used for gentle, even heating</note> for two days / then it dissolves into a small amount of water / which is clear / and is called **Fermentable Water** <note>original: *Aqua Fermentabilis*</note>, in which our Stone is fermented / and drawn toward the nature of the metals. Divide this same water again into two parts. Place one part in a glass to congeal <note>solidify</note> in the fire / afterward take one part of **mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note> / which is amalgamated with mercury twice its weight / and take from the congealed **mass** <note>original: *Massæ*</note> a fourth part as heavy as the **amalgam** <note>original: *Amalgama*; a blend of mercury and another metal</note> weighs / rub the two together / so that they become one **Body** <note>original: *Corpus*</note> / After that, imbibe <note>slowly saturate a solid with liquid</note> it again gently / and give it a little **Fermentable Water**, and yet a little more / until it enters into it / Then place it in a **fixing glass** <note>original: *Figier Glaß*; a vessel designed to withstand long heat while stabilizing volatile substances</note> / with a mild fire to congeal / then the vapor from the **Stone** <note>original: *Lapide*</note> will penetrate the vapor of the **amalgam** / and be turned into a true **Medicine**. The more often you reiterate <note>repeat</note> the **Medicine** / the more you multiply it **in power and virtue** <note>original: *in Potentia & Virtute*</note>. Thus / when your **Medicine** tinctures <note>transforms</note> 100 parts the first time / it tinctures 1,000 the second time / 10,000 the third time / and so on. Therefore, do not despise this multiplication: For the more often a **Medicine** is placed into **digestion** <note>prolonged gentle heating</note> / the more perfectly it acts in the **projection** <note>the final step of throwing the medicine onto base metal to transform it into gold or silver</note>.

### Fixation of the Air <note>original: *Fixatio Aëris*; the process of making a volatile substance stable under heat</note>.

But if you wish to fix the **Air** <note>original: *Aërem*; here referring to the volatile gaseous spirit or "tincture"</note> in which the entire tincture resides / then take the **Earth** <note>the solid residue</note> which you set aside / and a little of the **Mercurial Water** <note>original: *Aqua Mercuriali*</note> / let it **putrefy** <note>decompose or rot under gentle heat</note> for a day or two / Then **distill** it in a **water bath** <note>original: *Balneo*</note> with a mild fire for so long / until nothing more will come out in the bath. Then place the glass in **ashes** <note>original: *Aschen*; a hotter method of indirect heating than a water bath</note> / **distill** it / and receive the **Air**, which will be dark blue / Drive out as much of it as you can / and when nothing more will **distill** / then place the water in a well-secured place. Take the **Earth** that remains at the bottom of the glass / rub it on a glass plate / to this, add a little of the previous **Stone** with the **Earth** / imbibe it with the water that you drew off from the **Earth** / until it becomes like a pulp / Set it to **distill** in **sand** <note>a sand bath, providing higher heat than ashes</note> / fire it with the **third degree** <note>a specific level of alchemical heat, usually quite strong</note>. For the more difficult it is to separate the moisture from the **Body** / the nobler and more powerful it is: Reiterate this imbibing and **distilling** / until you draw the **Soul** <note>the vital essence</note> entirely from the **Body** / and nothing more will come out in the **distilling**.

Set this **liquor** <note>original: *Liquorem*</note>, in which the **fire** is / into the glass with the **Air** that is dark blue / **rectify** <note>purify by repeated distillation</note> that by itself with the **distillate** in the **sand** one time / then you have your **Air** perfectly mixed **with Fire** <note>original: *cum Igne*</note> / with which you shall fix your **Stone** in the following way:

# Report on Alchemy in the Universal and Particular Way <note>original: *Via Vniuersali & Particulari*; refers to the two paths of alchemy—the "Universal" which creates a medicine for all things, and the "Particular" which works on specific metals.</note>

Take the aforementioned congealed **amalgam** <note>a mixture of mercury and another metal</note>, and a little of the **Philosophical Ointment** <note>original: *Unguento Philosophico*; likely a refined fatty or oily alchemical substance</note>, or of the other **Vegetable** <note>original: *Vegetabili*; refers to a substance derived from plants rather than minerals</note> substance; rub it very finely upon a glass plate / then imbibe <note>slowly saturate a solid with liquid</note> it with the prepared **Air** <note>original: *Aëre*; here referring to a volatile spirit or gaseous substance</note> a little / and then a little more / until it looks like a thin paste / then let it **putrefy** <note>original: *putrificiren*; the process of breaking down or "rotting" a substance to its base components</note> for 6 days / set it in to **fix** <note>original: *figieren*; to make a volatile substance solid and resistant to heat</note> with a gentle fire / until it congeals / just as you did above with the **Fermentable Water**. Repeat this / until it becomes half again as heavy / as it was before. Of this, place some upon a copper plate: If the **Medicine** melts like a wax / without smoke / then it is correct: If not / then repeat the process so long and so many times / until you attain the sign.

You may also compose your **Elixir** <note>a potent alchemical liquid or powder used for transformation</note> well in the following way. Take twelve and a half parts of the **Water of Silver** <note>original: *Aqua Argenti*; often used to refer to mercury or a mercurial solvent</note> mentioned above / dissolve one part of the congealed **Stone** <note>original: *Lapidis*</note>, as is recorded above / add one and a half parts of **Philosophical Ointment**, or of another **Vegetable Salt**, and 2 parts of the mixed upper **Air** / this will be dissolved in a **water bath** <note>original: *Balneo*</note> into pure water in two days. Draw the sixth part of the water out in the water bath through distillation / afterwards congeal it with a mild fire / dissolve it in the water bath, and congeal it again in **ash** <note>original: *Cinere*; using a bed of hot ashes for gentle, indirect heat</note>. Continue this / until it will no longer allow itself to be congealed / then you have a very good Elixir or Medicine. The same is also to be understood regarding **gold**.

# Garden of Riches <note>original Latin: *Hortus Diuitiarum*</note>

Seeking the art receptively; this part, which primarily deals with the secrets and the most hidden mysteries of the other **Astronomy** <note>In alchemy, "Astronomy" often refers to the study of "celestial" or volatile influences within chemical substances.</note> and the other **Philosophy**, likewise the experience of **Blessed Alchemy**: how through the help of this art, natures are to be brought to perfection. You children of wisdom, you should know that the **Philosophers** <note>Refers to the ancient and medieval alchemists, the "Philosophers of Nature."</note> have written of this Divine Art and its **mode or practice** <note>original: *Modum oder Practick*</note> in the most secret manner, with confused riddles, using various figures and contradictory words. It would be a wonder if a person who had an **angelic understanding** <note>original: *Englischen Verstand*; "Englisch" here is an archaic form of "Engelisch," meaning the intellect of an angel.</note> could grasp it, unless they are a **highly enlightened Philosopher** who has meditated upon or researched this art to its deepest foundations. I will reveal such manipulations with the help of God, and I will so faithfully instruct our children who are suitable for it, that no one may fall into error in their work.

Come here, you children of **Philosophy**; I will lead you into the **Garden of Riches** and the experience of all joy and welfare. Therein I will show you flowers of all kinds of colors in this whole world, such as you might ever imagine. And in particular, I will teach you to assemble and mix certain roots of nature—the noblest of all—and the herbs which are the most secret in the art of the **Philosophical Mastery** <note>original: *Magisterij*; the "Great Work" or the achievement of the alchemical goal.</note>. I will teach you to separate and preserve their fragrant flowers, and also to extract their delicious juice and marrow in the purest way. And lastly, I will teach you to perfectly confirm and **fix** <note>original: *figieren*; to make a substance stable so it no longer evaporates or changes when heated.</note> all of this, so that henceforth no element can harm or spoil it. Rather, let it be something that takes root in the fire, grows in the air, shows its leaves in the water, and turns green in the earth, and multiplies itself at all times so that none of its power is lost.

Once you have collected these and tasted their sweetness, they will protect you from hunger and thirst. They will give you an abundance of **riches** which will never again be lacking. They heal and **preserve** <note>original: *præservieren*</note> you from all diseases and keep your life in a healthy state for a long duration, according to the will of God.

# Chapter One

## On the Knowledge and Revelation of the Matter and substances of the Philosophers, from which the highest Masterpiece <note>original: *Magisterium*; in alchemy, this refers to the ultimate goal or the completed Philosophers' Stone.</note> of the Philosophers’ Stone is made.

Take heed, you sons, and recognize the natural roots and the noblest herbs of the Philosophers. Their roots are green, mixed with a whiteness; but their herbs are of brown, red, and white color, while some are yellowish. Their flowers, scent, and taste are so noble that nothing sweeter, nothing stronger, or more precious in this world can be found that might equal them in goodness. Their extracted juice also takes on various colors, for it becomes red in the sunlight, and in the brightness of light, it turns to the whiteness of the moon <note>In alchemical symbolism, "the moon" represents Silver or the "White Work" (Albedo).</note>. And these herbs are quite common—a heavenly gift found at all times and in all places, possessed by the rich as well as the poor. They are simple and rejected, and are used least of all for our medicine; for their virtues are hidden. The ancients never wished to reveal anything about them, but instead kept them most hidden. Whose names I have fully stated, and I swear by the Creator of Heaven and Earth that from them alone the Art is completed, and from no other thing in this entire world.

Therefore, I most earnestly plead with all those who, through God's grace, shall draw understanding from this book and receive its fruit, that they do not use or enjoy such a Divine gift for evil, haughtiness, pride, or a tyrannical life. But rather, praise and honor God, and share it for the benefit of the body and the salvation of the soul, so that the poor and needy may receive comfort and help, and thus cry out together to the Heavenly Almighty God. This I ask so that I might not be found among those of wicked life at the Last Judgment, and that the wrath of the stern Judge does not crush me along with them, but that I may hear His lovely voice with the chosen ones: "Come here, you blessed of my Father, receive the kingdom," <note>Matthew 25:34; a common scriptural citation in alchemical texts to emphasize the practitioner's moral duty.</note> etc.

# The Second Chapter
## On the Labor of the Blessed Stone.

My son, now lay your hands to the work, and say in the name of GOD: O GOD, help me, protect me, and grant me your grace.
Therefore, take all herbs that are known to you, with their roots and flowers, and extract from them the four elements in this way. Take a good portion of the mentioned herbs, of each an equal part <note>original: *ana*; a medical and alchemical term meaning "of each an equal amount"</note>. Cut them or pound them as finely as possible, and place them in a philosophical vessel <note>An alchemical flask, such as an alembic or retort</note>. Extract from them the four elements: first the water, second the airy oil, third the fire, and the earth remains at the bottom <term>in Fundo: at the base or bottom of the vessel</term>. Grind this earth finely, pour over it its own extracted water, and sublimate it again as at first. <margin>7 times</margin> Do this seven times—that is, let the dead rise seven times; meaning they kill themselves seven times through rising <note>In alchemy, "rising" or evaporation is often equated with the spirit leaving the body, or "dying"</note>, and become living again seven times through descending. For when Father Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy</note>, who was a King of the Greeks, was asked what the most important thing in the Art was, he said: "That the dead rise seven times, and the living descend seven times." Thus you will have what you seek. For in this way, the power of each is indissolubly bound within them, and such a firm bond of the Bridegroom and the Bride—namely, of the water and the powder—is made. And in this degree, the Water of Life <term>Aqua Vitæ</term> receives seven Fifth Essences <term>Quintas Essentias: quintessences, or the purest spiritual essence of a substance</term>, and drinks in all the substance, nature, and life of the aforementioned herbs during these seven sublimations.

This venerable water, which is called a Fountain of Life, you shall sublimate by itself <note>original Latin: *per se*</note> two or three times. Cast away the earth or dregs <term>Fæces: the solid waste or residue left after distillation</term> which it leaves at the bottom in each sublimation. Thereafter, sublimate it again by itself, slowly, with a mild fire, until the substance of the water is entirely extracted. But when the oil begins to rise, put forth another vessel to catch such precious oil. Then, strengthen the fire gradually and gently until no more of said oil rises. Keep this blessed oil and liquid <term>Liquor: a fluid substance</term> of the philosophers in a clean vessel, well-sealed.

## The Fourth Chapter.
### On the Form and Shape of the Vessel in which the Material is Cooked.

For the Stone there is only one vessel in which the entire Great Work <note>original: *Magisterium*, referring to the completion of the Philosopher's Stone</note> is perfected. This is a blind cucurbit <note>term: A gourd-shaped glass vessel; "blind" means it has no opening at the top or its opening is sealed</note> which has no lid. It is a single vessel made of glass, thick and well-annealed <note>The process of slow cooling to toughen the glass</note>: sealed on all sides, half a cubit <note>roughly 9 to 12 inches in this context</note> long, and round or flat at the top, of a good width. It should be slightly curved at the bottom, and the sides should be brought up straight, far enough apart from each other so that whatever is sublimated <note>term: Sublimation is the process where a substance is heated into vapor and then solidifies again at the top of the vessel</note> can rise and fall without hindrance.

## The Fifth Chapter.
### How to Seal the Vessels.

<margin>
retained p.
filled V.
p. 504.
</margin>
The way to seal <note>original: *sigillieren*, likely referring to the "Seal of Hermes" or an airtight glass seal</note> the vessel is as follows. First, take the previously mentioned *Philosophical* divided water, well mixed with its noble earth and its fresh blood, and place it into its suitable glass, the shape of which has been described. Then close the mouth of the glass in this manner: Take a glass ball and place it upon the mouth of the glass vessel; around it, sprinkle crushed glass. Then place the glass or flask into a pot and put ash around it so that the ash is two finger-breadths thick on all sides. The flask should extend about two fingers' width above the ash, or a little more. Then surround it with coals and let them catch fire. When the neck of the glass glows red, sprinkle a little borax <note>original: *Burras*; used here as a flux to lower the melting point of the glass</note> onto the ball, and the glass will flow immediately <note>fusing the ball to the neck to create a permanent seal</note>. Then let it cool and take out the vessel with the material inside. Note always that you should weigh the glass before the material is put inside, so that you know how to adjust your measurements if you wish to add more.

For the Stone <note>the Philosopher's Stone</note>, there is only one vessel in which the entire <term>Magisterium</term> <note>the "Mastery" or the completed alchemical process</note> is perfected. And it is a blind <term>Cucurbit</term> <note>a gourd-shaped glass vessel</note> which has no lid. It is a single vessel made of glass, thick and well-annealed <note>cooled slowly to remove internal stresses</note>: sealed on all sides, half a cubit <note>about 12 inches or 30 cm</note> long, and round or flat at the top. It should be of a good width: the bottom should be slightly curved, and the sides should be brought up straight and far enough apart from each other so that whatever is sublimated <note>turned into vapor by heat</note> can rise and descend without hindrance.

***

# The Fifth Chapter /
## How to Seal the Vessels.

<margin>retained e. divided W. p. 504. <unclear>Beit</unclear></margin>
The way to seal <note>original: *sigillieren*; to hermetically close</note> the vessels happens thus. First, take the aforementioned Philosophical divided water, well-mixed with its noble earth and its fresh blood; place it into its suitable glass, the shape of which has been described, and then close the mouth of the glass as follows: Take a cast sphere, lay it upon the mouth-hole of the glass, and strew crushed glass around it. Then place the glass or flask <note>original: *Kolben*</note> into a pot. Put ashes around it so that they are two finger-breadths thick all around. The flask should extend about two finger-breadths above the ashes, or a little more. Then surround it with coals and let them catch fire. When the neck of the glass glows, strew a little <term>Borax</term> <note>original: *Burras*; used as a flux to help the glass melt together</note> onto the sphere, and the glass will flow immediately. Then let it cool and take out the vessel with the matter inside. Always remember to weigh the glass before you put the matter in, so that you know how to proceed if you wish to add more.

# The Sixth Chapter /
## On the Philosophical Furnace / and how the vessel should be placed.

Have a vessel made for yourself out of good fire-resistant clay, in which you will arrange our Old One <note>a symbolic name for the prime matter or the Stone</note> or Stone, or Sealed Water. This clay vessel should be of such a width that the glass fits comfortably inside, and so that about three finger-breadths of ashes can be filled in all around it. Over the mentioned vessel, have a lid made of the same clay, so that the fire does not touch or strike the glass vessel containing the Matter; set this one atop the other. At the top of this lid, have another small lid made with a handle, which you can lift off if it becomes necessary to look at the Matter. Now, we place the Matter into the coated <note>original: *beschlagenen*; likely "luted" or coated with a protective layer of clay</note> glass, and then into the aforementioned earthen vessel. The glass should be three or four parts empty, and only one part full.

Construct the furnace in the following way: Prepare a good loam <note>a mixture of clay, sand, and straw</note>, mixed with horse manure and sand, and well-worked so that it may better hold the heat. Make a round structure, two spans <note>about 18 inches or 45 cm</note> in width and two spans in height. In the middle of this, a base should be placed which has a hole in the center, through which you can slide a fist, so that the air may draw through it. Above the mentioned base, an iron piece should be inset with a cross, from which the lamp <note>original: *Ampel*; a steady oil lamp used as a heat source</note> shall hang. This should be in a gap where, between the lamp and the furnace walls, a fist may be pushed through on all sides, or four finger-breadths, so that the air can circulate.

Upon this furnace, set another furnace, into which iron bars are placed so that the earthen vessel (containing the glass with the Matter) can be set upon them. Such bars should be set one standard foot <note>original: *Werckschuch*</note> high above the base. The height of this furnace should be raised up to the lid of the lower earthen vessel that stands on the bars: the reason for this is so that when you want to look at the Matter to see how the <term>signs</term> <note>original: *Signa* or *Warzeichen*; the specific color changes, like the Black Sun or White Swan, that indicate progress</note> manifest themselves, there is no hindrance as there would be if the furnace were too high. The width of this part of the furnace should be such that there are four finger-breadths of space between the vessel and the walls, so that the heat of the fire does not only strike the bottom of the lower vessel in which the glass with the Matter stands, but rather [spreads] itself all around

# The Seventh Chapter /
## On the Philosophical Wick.

The lamp should be placed under the glass, and it must burn without ceasing. For <term>the</term> <note>original: *dz* (abbreviation for *das*)</note> Philosophical Fire is made with a wick of three threads, and no more: they should also not be too coarse. But the Philosophical Wick <note>often described in alchemical texts as an "asbestos" or "everlasting" wick that does not consume itself</note> never burns away, nor is it consumed, so that the worker needs to do nothing else but pour in more oil. With such a fire our work is completed, and not otherwise. Therefore, take care that it does not go out.

---

# The Eighth Chapter /
## On the Degrees of Fire, how they are to be governed throughout the entire work.

Maintaining the governance of the fire is no small skill. For in the <term>Solution</term> <note>the process of dissolving a solid into a liquid state</note>, the fire should always be gentle; in the <term>Sublimation</term> <note>the process of heating a substance until it vaporizes and then collects as a solid again</note>, moderate; in the <term>Coagulation</term> <note>the thickening or hardening of the liquid matter</note>, tempered; in the Whiteness <note>the *Albedo* stage</note>, increasing; and in the Redness <note>the *Rubedo* or final stage</note>, strong.

If you err in these through ignorance, you will often regret your loss. However, the more the colors change, the more the fire is to be increased gently, until it attains the signs of Whiteness. This Whiteness requires much fire because it is moist and cold, and is poorly "cooked." <note>Alchemists viewed the transformation of matter as a process of "digestion" or "cooking" driven by heat</note> For this reason, the female figures...

# The Tenth Chapter /

## Concerning the Transmutation of the Stone / from one nature into another / and from one color into another.

<margin>
one glass / one cooking /
7 orders
to the whole
</margin>
Be told, dear son, you should know that in this single closed glass, in a single cooking, seven dispositions and orders are accomplished for this **Great Work**. The first is **Decay** <note>original: *Putrefactio*</note>, so that you may extract a pure, subtle substance; The second is **Dissolution** <note>original: *Solutio*</note>, so that the entire matter is dissolved into a water; The third is **Decay** <note>original: *Putrefactio*</note>; The fourth is a **Washing** or **Purification** <note>original: *Ablutio*</note>; The fifth is **Coagulation** <note>original: *Coagulatio*</note>, which is to gently dry the water into our Sun; The sixth is **Calcination** <note>original: *Calcinatio*; reducing a solid to a fine powder using heat</note>; The seventh is **Fixation** <note>original: *Fixatio*; the process of making a volatile substance stable in fire</note>. But in these seven orders, seven other common changes of nature manifest, which appear wonderful to the sight. For when our stone is placed in our vessel and finds the warmth of the sun, it immediately dissolves itself into a water. At times it rises upward into the height of the vessel, and thereafter it falls back down again to the **bottom of the vessel** <note>original Latin: *ad Fundum deß Geschirrs*</note>; And through
<margin>wind/vapor</margin>
the wind—that is, the vapor—it raises itself. Such a rising thing turns into a water, and in the beginning a thickness will stand over the water, which gradually thickens into an earth that sinks into the water and lies at the bottom <note>original Latin: *in Fundo*</note>.

# The Eleventh Chapter /
## Concerning the manifold colors which appear during the governance.

NOTICE, there are three principal colors which appear in the Work: **Black**, **White**, and **Red**. Alongside these, there are also other colors that allow themselves to be seen in the Work: The first is silver-colored; the second, Black; the third, Multi-colored; the fourth, Brown; the fifth, Green; the sixth, Mirrored, like the **Peacock’s Feathers** <note>known in Latin as the *Cauda Pavonis*, this stage of shimmering colors indicates that the "Blackness" is breaking and the transition to "Whiteness" is beginning</note>; the seventh, toward silver-white; the eighth, the highest perfect Whiteness; the ninth, Brown; the tenth, Saffron-colored; the eleventh, the perfect Redness; and many other colors come in between, to which one need not pay much attention.

---

# The Fifteenth Chapter
## On the Fermentation of the Blessed Stone.

Take five or six parts of the completed and perfectly fixed white or red **Medicine** <term>Medicine: a common alchemical term for the Philosopher's Stone in its potent, transformative state</term>, and one part of the white or red **prepared Body** <note>original: *præprirten Corporis*</note>, most purely and well **calcined** <note>calciniert: the process of heating a substance to high temperatures to reduce it to a fine powder</note>. Place them together in a **Fixing-Glass** <note>original: *Figier-Glaß*</note> to **putrefy** <note>putreficieren: to rot or decompose, a necessary stage of breakdown before rebirth</note> in the **Mary’s Bath** <note>original: *Balneo Mariæ*; a water bath used for gentle, indirect heating</note> within the **Philosophical Oven**; govern the fire with due measure until that which was first made **volatile** <note>Volatile: a substance that easily evaporates or changes state</note> takes unto itself the **fixed Body** <note>Fix Corpus</note>, so that the **fixed becomes volatile**, and the **volatile becomes fixed**. And when you see the appearance of many colors, strengthen the fire until you find everything **fixed** in the form of an oil; then you have the true **Elixir**, with which you can **tincture** <note>tingieren: to transform or "dye" base metals into gold or silver</note> whenever you wish.

And note that you do not need to perform this **fermentation** more than once. For the entire **matter** <note>Matery</note> transforms itself into a **ferment**; therefore you do not need to start anew again. For just as the **leaven** <note>Heffel: yeast or sourdough starter</note> of bread changes or sours the whole dough, so from this **paste** <note>Past</note> a portion is kept as a **ferment** to again **ferment** another **paste**, and this is again as noble as before. That is the property in the **philosophical matter**.

---

# The Sixteenth Chapter
## That the Tincture is increased through Solution, and also through Fermentation.

Our **Medicine** is increased through **solution** <note>Solution: the process of dissolving a solid into a liquid</note> and also through **fermentation**. Through **solution**, it is somewhat slower; but through **fermentation**, our **Medicine** is much more quickly **augmented** <note>augmentiert: increased in quantity or potency</note>. For if it is not **dissolved** <note>solviert</note>, it does not **operate** <note>operiert</note> well, unless it be fixed in its ferment. It

## The Seventeenth Chapter,

### That the Tincture can be augmented in two ways: in quantity and in quality. In quantity, it is augmented thus.

<margin>
Of the red water reserved. See page 511.

It is likewise to be noted that the **Elixir** can be **augmented** and increased in two ways, namely in volume and quantity, and in quality and power. In volume or quantity, it is **augmented** as follows: Take one part of the red reserved water and three parts of the **Elixir**; put them together and arrange everything in its proper philosophical vessel, and place it again over a gentle fire until it turns into a **Stone** <note>original Latin: *Lapidem*</note>.

Some arrange it in a **cucurbit** <term>Cucurbit: a gourd-shaped glass vessel that forms the lower part of a distillation apparatus</term>, pouring over it the first **rectified** <note>purified through distillation</note> water, with its **helm** <note>the cap or "alembic" that sits atop the cucurbit</note> placed upon it and well **luted** <note>sealed with an airtight paste or clay</note>. Then they pour the water back over it and draw it off again, repeating this so often until they see the aforementioned **matter** at the **bottom** <note>original Latin: *in Fundo*</note> of the vessel shining brightly, like a naked sword, and brought back to its former Whiteness or Redness, according to how the **matter** was **prepared**. And this is a higher and more hidden **secret** than can be believed.

-># Garden of Riches.<-

## The Eighteenth Chapter,
### How the Medicine is augmented in quality.

In quality, the **Elixir** is augmented thus: namely, that one takes <note>original: *ne-* / *nehme*</note> of the **volatile Stone**, which has the **nature of a woman** <note>In alchemical theory, "female nature" refers to the volatile, cold, or moist principle, typically associated with Mercury</note>, three [parts], and of the **Elixir** one part. Put these together as is necessary; place them in a **cucurbit** <term>cucurbit: a gourd-shaped glass vessel used in distillation</term>. Over this, if you wish, pour some of the [red] water so that it swims above it. **Seal** <term>seal: hermetically sealing the vessel (often called the Seal of Hermes) to prevent the spirit from escaping</term> it according to custom; arrange it in the furnace with its **receiver** <note>the vessel that catches the distilled liquid</note>, the joints also being well **luted** <term>luted: sealed with a specialized airtight clay or paste</term>. **Distill** the water with a gentle fire, and when it has completely come over, then strengthen the fire so that everything that wishes to **sublime** <term>sublime: the process where a solid substance is turned into vapor by heat and then cools back into a solid at the top of the vessel</term> may rise up.

That which is **sublimed**, add it back to that **at the bottom** <note>original: *in Fundo*</note>, as was previously reiterated and [sublimed?], as many times as necessary, until through such repeated **sublimation** [the whole] remains **at the bottom**.

When it has all become **fixed** <term>fixed: a stable state where the substance can no longer be evaporated or changed by fire</term> in this way, then add again its quantity of the **volatile Stone**, and **imbibe** <note>to "imbibe" is to gradually add liquid to a dry substance until it is saturated</note> it in the aforementioned way, until everything rises up again and finally becomes fixed once more. Continue this until it flows quite easily, exactly like wax. This **Medicine** is constant; it **tinges** <term>tinge: the transformative power of the Stone to color and change the nature of a metal</term>, penetrates, consolidates, and makes [the metal] resistant [to fire]. One part of this **transmutes** a thousand times a thousand parts of any **body** <note>original: *Corpore*</note> into true **Gold** or **Silver**.

---

## The Nineteenth Chapter,
### How the Medicine shall be fermented at the last,
### so that it may perfectly tinge.

But when you wish to **tinge**, take of the same **body** <note>original: *Corpore*</note> with which you have **fermented** in your work—namely, whether it be **White** <note>for making silver</note> or **Red** <note>for making gold</note>. Bring this **body** into a **subtle lime** <note>a fine powder produced through calcination or heating</note>; lay it in a **luted** dish or in a crucible over the fire, and drip the **oil of the Elixir** onto it little by little, so that the powder may take it in, and together they may become a **subtle powder**. Take care that not too much of the oil is lost upon it. This **Ferment** is the **Elixir**, with which you can **tinge** all metals and **quicksilver** <note>original: *Argentum uuum* / *vivum*</note> into **Silver** or **Gold**, according to how the **Medicine** has been prepared.

# The Eighteenth Chapter/
## How the Medicine is augmented in Quality.

Regarding its quality, the **Elixir** <term>Elixir: the perfected alchemical substance, also known as the Philosopher's Stone</term> is augmented in this way: namely, take three parts of the **Volatile Stone** <note>In alchemy, "volatile" refers to a substance that easily vaporizes or rises when heated. Here it is associated with the "female" principle, often representing Mercury</note>, which is of a female nature, and one part of the Elixir. Put them together as is required and place them in a **cucurbit** <term>Cucurbit: a gourd-shaped glass vessel used for distillation</term>. Over this, if you wish, pour some of the "first water" so that it floats upon it. Seal this vessel with **lute** <term>Luting: sealing a vessel with airtight clay or wax to prevent vapors from escaping</term> as is the custom, and set it in the furnace with its **recipient** <term>Recipient: the vessel that collects the condensed liquid during distillation</term>, making sure the joints are well sealed. Distill the water with a gentle fire; and when it has completely come over, then strengthen the fire so that everything that wishes to **sublimate** <term>Sublimation: the process where a solid is heated into a vapor and then collected again as a solid</term> may rise up.

Take that which has sublimated and return it to the residue at the **bottom** <note>original: "in Fundo"</note>, repeating and sublimating as before, time after time, until through such repeated sublimation everything remains at the bottom.

When it has all become **fixed** <term>Fixation: the process of making a volatile substance stable under heat so it no longer evaporates</term> in this way, then add again its quantity of the Volatile Stone and **imbibe** <term>Imbibition: the slow addition of liquid to a dry substance until it is fully saturated</term> it in the aforementioned way, until it all rises again and finally becomes fixed once more. Continue this until it flows as easily as wax. This **Medicine** is enduring; it **tinges** <term>Tingeing: the alchemical transformation of a metal's color and nature into gold or silver</term>, penetrates, consolidates, and makes stable. One part of this transmutes a thousand times a thousand <note>i.e., one million parts</note> of any body into true gold or silver.

# The Nineteenth Chapter/
## How the Medicine is finally fermented, so that it may perfectly tinge.

However, when you wish to perform the transmutation, take some of the same **Body** <note>The "Body" refers to the specific metal (Gold for the Red work, Silver for the White work) used to "tune" the medicine</note> with which you fermented in your work, namely either the White or the Red. Bring this Body into a subtle **calx** <term>Calx: a fine powder produced by heating a metal to a very high temperature (calcination)</term>; place it in a luted glass dish or in a crucible over the fire, and drip the **Oil of the Elixir** onto it little by little, so that the powder absorbs it and they become one subtle powder together. Guard yourself against using too much of the oil. This **Ferment** is the Elixir with which you can tinge all metals and **Quicksilver** <note>original: "Argentum Vivum"</note> into silver or gold, according to how the Medicine was prepared.

### Here begins
# a Work of Alchemy,
## which is a gift of Almighty GOD,
### and is divided into Twelve Chapters.

## The First Chapter,
### How one should sublimate the Mercury for the Art.

Also take 2 pounds of <term>Vitriol</term> <note>Sulfate minerals, usually green or blue vitriol, used as acidic reagents</note>, one pound of <term>Mercury</term> <note>Quicksilver</note>, and one pound of common salt. Sublimate it thus for the first time, and for the second and third times. For the fourth time, through common salt, and for the fifth time, by itself alone.

## The Second Chapter,
### How one should turn the prepared sublimated Mercury into water.

<margin>
<unclear>Mercury sublimate Tin</unclear>
<unclear>Mercury Tin Mercury</unclear>
</margin>
Also take pure, fine <term>Tin</term> <note>Represented by the symbol ♃</note> and common Mercury, one pound of each; from these, make an <term>Amalgam</term> <note>A mixture or alloy of mercury with another metal</note>. Wash the amalgam thoroughly until the blackness is removed, and dry it well over gentle heat. And take two pounds of the <term>sublimated Mercury</term> <note>The mercury purified in the previous chapter</note>, or as much as the weight of the amalgam, and grind them together on a smooth stone. Place it on a glass plate in a damp cellar that is warm; thus, a "water" [liquid] will form from it. Distill this—if it comes down cloudy—through a filter, and put it into a glass vessel. Place it in horse manure <note>A common alchemical method for providing gentle, consistent biological heat</note> or in a <term>Bain-marie</term> <note>original: "Balneum Mariæ," a water bath</note> for one month. Seal the glass very well so that it does not <insert>evaporate</insert> <note>original: "verrieche," literally "smell away" or lose its potency through scent</note>. Afterward, distill it through an <term>Alembic</term> <note>A distillation apparatus consisting of a gourd-shaped vessel and a cooling cap</note> into a glass receiver that is well <term>luted</term> <note>sealed with airtight clay or paste</note>. Distill it from the water bath, and then distill it further from the ash [an ash-bath] with gentle fire, and keep this well-sealed for your work. And the <term>residue</term> <note>original: "Fæces," the solid remains left after distillation</note> that remained in the glass, keep that also well-protected and <term>calcine</term> <note>heat to a high temperature to reduce to a powder</note> it, as will be seen hereafter in the Sixth Chapter.

<margin>p. 523.</margin>

# A Work of Alchemy. 530

...[management] too [quickly] or slowly. But I want you to act in such a way that your thoughts follow Nature. If you manage your work thus, you will achieve a perfect art; the water, through its good operations, makes things White, and that same Whiteness then becomes Red. <note>In alchemy, the transition from the White stage (albedo) to the Red stage (rubedo) marks the final perfection of the Philosopher's Stone.</note>

Therefore it is necessary that our Stone be extracted from the nature of two types of metallic earths. From this, a perfect Elixir will be produced—more nourished or purified—and it signifies more than the Sun <note>symbol: ☉, referring to Gold</note> or the Moon <note>symbol: ☽, referring to Silver</note>. This is because it can turn or transform all things and make perfect the lesser things into Gold or Silver, which the metals themselves cannot do. For if they were to give their perfection to another, they would become imperfect themselves, because they cannot "tinge" <note>To "tinge" or "tincture" means to transform the very nature of a base metal into a noble one.</note> except as far as they can extend and distribute themselves. For nothing makes things white except by its own whiteness, and nothing makes things Red except by its own redness. And therefore, we work upon our Stone so that its tincture <note>The active transformative essence</note> is improved within it, more than in its own nature, and thus the Elixir is established; that is, according to a secret and hidden understanding.

<margin>1.</margin>
First, the right, true nature is obtained, and what color it is; and it is called **Atrop**, or **Alat**, or **Tapar**, or **Dunath**. <note>These are likely specialized "deck-names" or encoded terms for the primary material used at the start of the work.</note>

<margin>2. 3.</margin>
Second and Third, it is understood how the metals are dissolved in the water, and a new <term>Corpus</term> <note>Latin: "Body"</note> or metal is made.

<margin>4.</margin>

<margin>5.</margin>
Fifth, it is understood how the greater part of this water has become a black and stony earth, of which all the Philosophers speak.

<margin>6.</margin>

<margin>7.</margin>

<margin>8.</margin>
Eighth, how a <term>Dragon</term> <note>original: "Track." <margin>9.</margin>

<margin>10.</margin>

Therefore, if you have them / the white roses appearing in all things / then you shall be certain / that in the same the redness of the <term>tincture</term> <note>The potent alchemical liquid or substance capable of transmuting metals.</note> is hidden. After that, one must not take out those same white roses / or add more water / but give a strong fire / until it becomes quite pure red. This is then the Red Rose / or the Red Tincture.

### **Red Rose** <note>original: "Rosa rubra"</note>, that is / the Red Roses.

I am an elixir for red / I change all imperfect metals into the purest gold / better than that which is made from the mine. For if one part is cast upon 1000 parts <term>☽</term> <note>Silver</note> or ☿ <note>Mercury</note> / it has turned it into the very purest gold.

# A Work of Alchemy.

## Hermes speaks:

<margin>Entry <unclear>e</unclear></margin>
**H**e who makes me White / also makes me Red. For the White and the Red / they come from one root / and the root is the <term>Mercurial Water</term> <note>The "water" of mercury, often referring to a solvent or the "soul" of the metal.</note> / That is our root for Red and White.
Therefore / Son / if you act according to the counsel and opinions of the wise masters / and do not overstep the goal in the work / then you are blessed: But if you perform these things quickly and hastily / then hindrance / fear and terror will come to you.

->T H E   E N D.<-

Throw away the ninth water, and leave it under the blind alembic in the ashes, and maintain it in every way as before. Do this three or four times, until the water consumes itself without any boiling or bubbling, and let it stand under the blind alembic with a gentle fire, like the heat of the sun. Then the **Oil of the Stone** will be ready, with which one <term>tinctures</term> <note>To "tincture" means to transform or "dye" a base metal into a more perfect state, such as gold or silver.</note> the Mercury until the end.

### Another method, regarding Marcasite.

Take a measure of good vinegar and distill it. Take the <term>dregs</term> <note>original: "Fæces"; the sediment or remains left after distillation.</note> that remain behind and take four <term>Loth</term> <note>A traditional German unit of weight; 4 Loth is approximately 60 grams or 2 ounces.</note> [of another substance] <insert>likely more dregs or a specific salt</insert> with it, and pour the distilled vinegar upon it, and distill it once more; thus it is ready for the work. Afterward, take a fire-resistant **marcasite** or **gold pyrite** <note>original: "Goldkiß"; iron pyrite or "fool's gold," often used in alchemical attempts to extract or "grow" gold.</note> and grind it into a fine powder, and put it into a flask, and pour the vinegar upon it. Let it stand in warmth until it turns yellow. Then pour off the yellow vinegar and pour another [fresh batch of vinegar] onto it. Do this until it no longer turns yellow. Afterward, take **calcined silver** <note>represented by the symbol ☽ (Moon/Silver).</note> and boil it out well, and pour the yellow vinegar upon it. Let it stand in warmth for 14 days; afterward, reduce it with **borax** <note>original: "Burraß"; used as a flux in smelting.</note>. Thus you have good **gold** <note>represented by the symbol ☉ (Sun/Gold).</note>.

<meta>This page transitions from the completion of the "First Tincture" and a brief mention of marcasite to the introduction of the "Second Tincture." It uses a detailed botanical metaphor to explain how base metals are "grafted" with noble ones to bear fruit.</meta>

-># The Second Tincture for White and Red.<-

The blessed Stone of the Sages, according to the content and the true natural way of the philosophers, as the same is prepared in the correct manner, art, and intention from the beginning until the end; also in every measure with complete truth, as I myself personally and quite truthfully found it to be in the Work. For the same is [not] prepared with sharp waters <note>Referencing corrosive acids like aqua fortis.</note> or substances contrary to nature, but only with, in, from, and not without the metals. For it must come from metals, from which metals are made, and from which metals can grow. For every tree brings forth its own seed and blossom, from which many beautiful apples or pears then grow and spring forth. Likewise, small branches are cut off which are fertile and have borne beautiful little growths, and come from a good tree. These are then set, planted, and grafted onto a wild, infertile trunk and stem; nevertheless, they are fertile as before, and teach that same infertile stem and trunk along with them, so that it becomes like them and likewise bears such fruit, just like these small branches. Thus, in the same manner, is it to be understood regarding the metals.

If you have a decayed, infertile, worthless metallic stem, and yet would like for that same stem not to perish entirely on account of its growing roots, then seek first for a small branch which bears beautiful and tasty fruit, either apples or pears. Take that same small branch and graft it very subtly, and at the right time, onto that stem—which usually happens in the spring—so that in summer it may bring forth its first green little leaves, grow in a little during the second summer and receive a strong trunk, but in the third summer it may usually bring its first fruit. Even if there is not much fruit, it is all the more flavorful and lovely to look upon, because it is the first fruit. Thus, henceforth, this tree of metals can bear more and more fruitfully as time and years go by, until at last its fruit becomes without number.

# OF THE STONE
## IN MERCURIAL
### W A T E R

In the Name of the Holy Trinity. If you are not working on <term>Copper</term> <note>original: ♀</note>, you do not need this test.

# On the Stone in Mercurial Water

If you see forks or streaks appearing in the helm <note>The "helm" or *alembic* is the cooling cap of a still where vapors condense.</note>, stop immediately and discard what remains in the flask. Take fresh distilled wine again and proceed as before. Continue this until you have enough of the Quintessence <note>original: *Quint. Essent.*; the "fifth essence" or most purified spirit of a substance, in this case, highly concentrated alcohol.</note>.

Take the Quintessence you have just prepared and throw a good handful of dried salt into it. Distill it as before until you feel "sweet water" <note>This likely refers to a neutral taste, indicating that the spirituous part has already passed over.</note> on your tongue; then stop. Discard what remains in the distilling vessel. Take what you have distilled over, add another handful of salt, and distill it a third time until you feel sweet water; then stop. Again, discard the residue. Pour what has distilled over into a flask, add a handful of fresh Salt of Tartar <note>original: *Salis 🜖ri*</note>, and distill it completely over the "eighteenth stroke" <note>likely referring to a specific setting on a furnace or a measure of time</note>. Perform this process five times in succession.

---

->Salt of Tartar<- <note>original: *Sal 🜖ri.*</note>

Place Tartar <note>original: *Weinstein*; the potassium bitartrate crusts found in wine barrels.</note> upon a stone and place glowing coals on top of it until the Tartar <note>original: *🜖m*</note> turns white. Then remove the coals and place them on the other side so it turns white there as well. Then grind it, dissolve it in a warm fire, and distill it—filtering it through a cloth or straining it cleanly. Afterward, boil it back into salt. First, let it flow <note>This refers to deliquescence, where a salt absorbs enough moisture from the air to become a liquid.</note> on a "flowing stone" in a cellar, then boil it hard again, grind it, dissolve it, and boil it once more. Thus you have good Salt of Tartar. If you let this salt flow on the stone, you have good Oil of Tartar <note>original: *Oleum 🜖ri.*</note>.

Afterward, pour five ounces <note>original: *Unß*</note> of Oil of Tartar into two ounces of Quintessence. Put them together in a flask and place it in a cellar. Then "little stones" <note>original: *Lapilli*; crystals.</note> will form. Place these in a flask, seal it well, and let them become warm in the flask. They will become an oil in which you can dissolve Gold <note>original: *☉*</note> or Silver <note>original: *☽*</note>. This is called the Quintessence of Tartar <note>original: *Q. Ess. è 🜖ro*</note>.

Once you have filtered it, distill it afterward using an alembic, in which it is not thinned out, then in warm or thin ashes. Finally, distill it in a sand bath until the moisture is completely gone. Then let it cool by itself. Pour the distilled water back onto the dry dregs <note>original: *Fæces*</note> and distill it off again. Pour it back on until nothing more will distill. Repeat this as often and as long as necessary until a clear stone forms in the glass.

## The Work upon the Mercury of Silver

### The Joining of the Two Waters

Likewise, take the water in which the mercury <note>original: *☿*</note> was dissolved, and pour it into the golden water in which the gold was dissolved, mixing them together. Seal the glass well with wax so that nothing may smell or leak out, and place it in a water bath for 40 days. And watch very carefully that the bath does not grow cold. Thus it <term>digests</term> <note>original: *digeriert*; a process of slow, gentle heating to mature a substance.</note> itself with the mercury and becomes one nature and property.

## Also, how to separate or divide the four elements from one another.

Also, take the glass and place an <term>alembic</term> <note>A cap or lid used in distillation to collect and direct vapors into a receiving vessel.</note> upon it, and place it in a hot <term>water bath</term> <note>original: *B. M.* or *Balneum Mariae*; a vessel of hot water used to heat substances gently and evenly.</note>. Distill the first element from the <term>matter</term> <note>original: *Materia*; the physical substance being worked upon.</note> for three days and nights. This is the <term>Element of Water</term> <note>original: *Element Aqua*</note>, and it is a beautiful, pure, clear water, measuring one and a half <term>drinks</term> <note>original: *Trünckel*; a liquid measure roughly equivalent to a cup or glassful.</note>. Thus, half a small drink remains in the glass, which is entirely golden-red. Keep this Element of Water separate in a glass, well-sealed with wax.

Afterward, take the glass in which the half-drink of golden liquid remains and <term>seal it tightly</term> <note>original: *verlutiere*; to seal a vessel with "lute," a paste made of clay or other materials to prevent the escape of vapors.</note>. Place an alembic upon it, and set it on a <term>furnace</term> <note>original: *Capellen*; here referring to the heating chamber or cupel-stand of a furnace.</note> in ash or sand, and distill it with a strong fire. Thus an oil will distill over; this is called the <term>Element of Air</term> <note>original: *Element Auræ*</note>. This is the second element, the Air. Keep this element also separate in a <term>flask</term> <note>original: *Kolben*</note> well-sealed with wax.

Now you have two elements separated from each other. At the bottom of the glass from which the Element of Air was separated, you will find a dry mass or matter, which is called a <term>Body</term> <note>original: *Corpus*</note> or an Earth. This is the third element. Grind this same Body into powder upon a marble stone; it will become a black powder. Keep the powder separate in a flask, well-sealed, until you have need of it.

### Note here how one should purge and purify the two elements of their impurities.

Take the first element, Water, and place it in a water bath for eight days. Likewise, take the second element, Air, in its flask, and place it in a water bath for eight days, ensuring that the flasks are well-sealed at the top with wax.

Afterward, take each one separately and place it on a furnace in ash, and distill each element separately with a good fire. You shall <term>dissolve</term> <note>original: *ſolvieren*</note>, distill, and <term>purify</term> <note>original: *pureficieren*</note> these two elements seven times in this manner, always each one separately. Then they are purified and well-prepared for the <term>tincture</term> <note>A potent alchemical substance used to transform or "color" base materials into a higher state.</note>.

Now take the Earth, or the powder, and put it into a flask, and pour upon it a little water from the first Element of Water, thus

## Note now how one should ferment the blessed noble stone, so that it may transform all bodies into good gold.

Take four **Loth** <note>A traditional German unit of weight, roughly equivalent to 14-15 grams or half an ounce.</note> of mercury that has been well-purified with salt and vinegar three times. Then take 2 Loth of thin, beaten gold and make an **amalgam** <note>original: *Amalgama*; a mixture of mercury and another metal, often used as a starting point for further chemical work.</note> of it, just as goldsmiths do when they wish to gild. When that is done, take the amalgam and lay it upon a marble stone, and add to it one Loth of the red sulfur—the blessed stone—and grind them together very well.

Then take the matter thus ground together and put it into a **small flask** <note>original: *Kölbel*</note>, and pour over it four Loth by weight of the **Element of Water** <note>The clear liquid distilled in the previous stage of the process.</note>. Place the flask in ash upon a **furnace** <note>original: *Capellen*</note> and distill the water back over from the matter with a gentle fire.

Afterward, take the flask out with the matter, and if anything has sublimated, add it back to the matter remaining at the bottom. Grind it small again upon a stone as before, put it back into a flask, give it another four Loth of water from the Element of Water, place it back in the ash, and distill it again as before. Perform this work **seven times**; thus the matter will become entirely **fixed** <note>original: *fix*; meaning the substance has become stable and will no longer vaporize or change when exposed to heat.</note> and constant in any fire.

# Observe here now how one should soak and incorporate the fixed materials, as mentioned above, with their oil—that is, with the other element, the element of air.

Take the material and grind it small on a stone, as before. Place it once again into a glass and pour three **Loth** <note>A traditional German unit of weight, roughly 14–15 grams or half an ounce.</note> by weight of the element of air over it. Place this on a **cupel in ash** <note>original: *Capellen in ein Aschen*; a method of heating a vessel by surrounding it with hot ashes to ensure even temperature.</note> and give it a good fire. Thus the material will also melt at the top of the glass like wax, and many beautiful colors will rise and fall in **circulation** <term>Circulatu: the alchemical process where a substance is heated so it evaporates and condenses repeatedly in a closed vessel, mimicking the natural cycles of the heavens</term>. Let it soften together in this way for three days and nights. Afterward, take the material out and grind it small as before. Add three more **Loth** of the oil, or the element of air, and place it back on the cupel in the ash. Give it a strong fire for three days and nights, as before. In this way, many kinds of colors will again rise and fall in circulation, and it will flow up and down within the glass. Thus is proven the saying of all philosophers: "Our stone rises into heaven and descends again from heaven to the earth." <note>This is a famous quote from the *Emerald Tablet*, an ancient foundational text of alchemy, describing the movement of the "Life Force" between the spiritual and physical realms.</note>

Continue this rising and falling until the material completely **coagulates** <note>thickens or solidifies from a liquid state</note> again into a beautiful red powder, like scarlet. Thus the **tincture** <term>Tinctur: a potent alchemical substance used to "dye" or transform the properties of base metals into gold</term> is now prepared, and one part now transmutates a thousand parts into well-proven gold. And I, Doctor Niclauß Melz, have worked this with my own hand and tested it before an honorable Council in the Royal City of Kronen <note>Likely Kronstadt or a similar city with "Crown" in its name</note>, for which I have a seal and letter addressed to the Holy Father, the Pope.

## Note how the projection and multiplication should occur upon the mercury or tin for which the medicine is prepared.

Take one hundred **Loth** of quicksilver or tin that has been well purified with salt and vinegar three times. Then place the **mercury** <note>original: *Mercurium*</note> in a crucible and set it on a fire until it begins to smoke. Then take one **Loth** of the aforementioned medicine and throw it into the crucible onto the mercury, and blow upon it well <note>using a bellows to increase the heat</note> for a good hour. Thus the quicksilver will transform into a beautiful red powder, just as the first was. Thus has the **multiplication** <term>Mehrung: the process of increasing the quantity of the alchemical "medicine" or "stone" without losing its potency</term> now occurred; from one **Loth**, you have one hundred **Loth** of medicine.

Afterward, take one **Loth** from those hundred **Loth** and throw it upon a thousand **Loth** of quicksilver or tin, as mentioned above, and blow upon it very well for a whole hour. Thus you have good, precious, proven gold, better in all tests than natural gold.

**Also:** Take half a pound of **saltpeter** <note>Also known as nitre, a key ingredient in making acids and gunpowder.</note>, let it melt in a new pot, and keep it slowly in a **circular fire** <term>Circul Feuer: a fire that surrounds the vessel to provide even, consistent heat</term> for two hours. And when the saltpeter begins to crust over the top in the pot like ash, then pour it out into a basin that stands in a vessel of cold water. And when the saltpeter has properly cooled and begins to attract moisture, crush it fine in a mortar and put it immediately into a **bladder** <note>Likely a pig's bladder, used here as a semi-permeable membrane for a primitive form of osmosis or filtration.</note>. Hang the tightly tied bladder in ordinary warm water, and place that water in a clean vessel; this is done so that you may notice how many **Loth** <note>A traditional unit of weight, approximately 14.5 grams.</note> of the half-pound of <term>🜔</term> <gloss>Saltpeter</gloss> have turned into water. If some saltpeter passes through the bladder into the surrounding water, you must let it **crystallize** <note>original: *schiessen lassen*; to let crystals "shoot" or form out of a saturated solution.</note> therein, and afterward weigh how much of it there is. Keep that until the end. Afterward, take the water that remained in the bladder, filter it twice in succession, and then put that water immediately into a **receiver** <term>Recipienten: a glass vessel used to collect the products of distillation</term>.

And then take fresh materials: one and a half pounds of saltpeter, finely ground, and one pound of **brick dust**. Mix these two powders well together and put them into a **flask** <note>original: *Kolben*; a long-necked glass vessel used for distillation.</note> that is well **luted** <term>verlutiert: sealed with a paste made of clay or lime to make the joints airtight</term>. Place it over a lively fire and attach the receiver containing the first water. Drive the **spirits** <note>The acidic vapors or fumes.</note> through the bricks over into the water—first with a gentle fire, and afterward like **Aqua Fortis** <term>Aquafort: "Strong Water," or nitric acid, capable of dissolving most metals</term>, for as long as a day and a night, until no more red spirits come over and the **distillate** <note>original: *Olemicum*; likely referring to the oily appearance of the concentrated acid vapors.</note> turns white. Then stop; it is enough.

**Also:** afterward, take that same water in which the spirits are contained and put it into another luted glass. Distill it over again gently into the receiver. Some saltpeter that has melted will remain in the flask; take it out and weigh it along with the saltpeter that first passed through the bladder. Thus you will realize how much of the half-pound of dissolved saltpeter has turned into "warm water." And see to it that it does not evaporate, for it is very strong. Afterward, take that same water and apply it again, driving more spirits from saltpeter through the bricks into it, two or three times, always using new bricks. After this, the water is ready and will dissolve <term>☽</term> <gloss>Silver</gloss>; it even strengthens the yield significantly. It also **precipitates** <term>præcipitiert: causes a substance to settle out of a solution as a solid</term> <term>♄</term> <gloss>Lead</gloss> completely, turning it either red or white.

# If you wish to fix all things, do it with glass.

**Also:** Make an alkali salt <note>original: *Salalcali*</note> from quicklime <note>original: *Calce viua*</note> and willow ashes; then take the white, transparent pebbles <note>original: *Kißlingstein*; likely quartz or flint</note> that have been calcined <term>Calcined: heated to high temperatures to drive off volatile matter, leaving a crumbly powder</term>, crush them fine, and mix the alkali salt into them. Let them melt together with a strong fire, and a substance remains shaped like glass; this serves highly in the workings of nature.

**Also:** To this glass you may add calx of lead <note>original: *Calcem Saturni*; Saturn is the alchemical name for lead</note> to 24 parts, or of copper <note>original: *ad Veneris*; Venus is the alchemical name for copper</note>, which is burnt copper <note>original: *Aes ustum*</note> or antimony, or all these materials in equal parts <note>original: *e. a.*, likely *equales partes*</note> according to your will. Thus the glass takes the color from them and the power of the metals. And if one lets silver <note>original: *Lunam*</note> melt with it for 24 hours, see then what it has accomplished and what degrees [of purity or color] appear there; they remain through the lead or the cement <term>Cement: a dry refining mixture used to purify precious metals at high heat</term>.

# Concerning the white ore.

Furthermore, take two pounds of saltpeter, one pound of alum, and one pound of arsenic. From these make an aqua fortis <term>Aqua fortis: "Strong water," a name for nitric acid used to dissolve metals</term>. Place the white ore into it, and it will dissolve in a day and a night. Take that calx <note>the resulting precipitate or powder</note> out and let it dry. Afterward, mix it with borax <note>original: *Purraß*</note> and melt it, and then refine it upon the cupel <term>Testen: a porous clay bowl used to separate precious metals from impurities like lead</term>. Thus you will find in one pound of ore the value of one guilder of gold <note>original symbol: ☉</note> and half a *loth* <note>a unit of weight, roughly 7.5 grams</note> of silver <note>original symbol: ☽</note>.

->Oil of Sulfur.<-

Take alum and sulfur; distill it by descent <term>per Descensum: a method of distillation where the heat is applied from above, forcing the liquid to flow downward into a receiver</term>, just as you do with vitriol; thus it will be crystallized.

->Oil of Vitriol.<-

Take two pots, as you know how, and in the upper one make many holes. Place the vitriol <note>Iron or copper sulfate</note> inside and seal it well. Bury the lower pot in the earth, and around the upper one make a fire of coals. Strengthen the fire until the pot glows and becomes white-hot. Then stop and let it cool. You will find in the lower pot an oil, green as grass, which is called the Milk of Mercury <note>original: *Lac Mercurij*</note>.

->Fixation of Cinnabar.<-

Furthermore, to boil the cinnabar <note>original: *Zinober*; mercury sulfide</note>, make a lye. Take one part willow ashes and one part quicklime <note>original: *Calcis viui*</note>, and pour urine upon it, and let it boil. Filter these powders through a felt until it comes out clear. Then take the lye in a glazed vessel and put the cinnabar into it,

# Beautiful Particular Works.

->Regarding Gold.<-

Take here one pound of *Aqua Regis* <term>Aqua Regis: 'Royal Water,' a mixture of nitric and hydrochloric acids capable of dissolving gold</term>, which has been made with salt / dissolve in it two *loth* <term>Loth: a unit of weight, approximately 15-16 grams</term> of fine gold <note>original: ☉</note> / pour into it two measures of Augsburg water <note>A regional reference likely referring to a specific local quality of spring or distilled water</note> / so that it becomes weak / Then put into it eight *loth* of common salt <note>original: 🜔</note> / and place it in the heat for 14 days / In this way, citron-yellow scales will grow / which should weigh 10 *loth* / and be gold <note>original: ☉</note> / but the water shall become white and clear. ->The Conversion of Silver into Gold.<-

Also / Take Hungarian vitriol <term>Vitriol: a sulfate of a metal, often iron or copper</term> / put it into an earthen retort / and place it in the side of the intense furnace <note>original: *Hellofen*</note> / and attach a receiver containing water to it / and drive off the oil strongly for 8 hours / until no more oil or spirit will come forth. Make plenty of this oil / draw off the phlegm <term>Phlegm: the watery, inactive part of a distilled substance</term> in a water bath <note>original: *Balneo Mar.*</note> / and keep it well. From the vitriol, extract its salt / with hot water / and draw it through a filter and sublimate it / thus you have a white salt. Dissolve it further in warm spring water / and filter it and sublimate it / Do this five times / so it becomes white. Put it into a glass / and pour the oil onto it / and let it stand in the heat / so that the oil and salt dissolve into one oil / Then place a helm <term>Helm: the top part of a still or alembic</term> upon it / and attach a receiver / and put into it four *loth* of dissolved Scorpion <note>original: *Scorpion* — in alchemy, this often refers to a preparation of antimony or a specific volatile salt</note> / it will become white.

After that take fresh spring water / and dissolve the white Scorpion in it / so a golden water comes from it / Draw this through a filter / and put more of the white Scorpion into the golden water / and coagulate it / so a white stone comes from it / Dissolve this further in hot spring water / and draw it through a filter / and put more of the white Scorpion into it / and dissolve it / and sublimate it. Do thus with dissolving / sublimating and filtering five times : Take fresh warm spring water every time / Then it is ready to tincture <term>Tincture: a substance that can change the nature or color of other materials, usually metals</term>.

After that, melt fine gold / and cast the golden matter upon it / Thus the gold becomes completely red / like copper / and surpasses silver <note>original: ☽</note>. Cast one part of this gold <note>original: ☉</note> onto 100 parts of melted silver <note>original: *Luna*</note> / it will become gold / stable in all tests.

Also / When you have dissolved, filtered, and sublimated the Scorpion five times / then dissolve 20 *loth* of mercury <note>original: *Mercurij* / ☿</note> / and pour a spoonful of the yellow Scorpion water into it / Thus you have a tincture / And always make it well-heated beforehand / and carry it with the red gold <note>original: ☉</note> into the silver <note>original: ☽</note> / then you have true gold by all signs <note>original: *indicia*</note>.

# Red Melting Glass.

Take one *mark* <term>Mark: a unit of weight, usually around 230 grams</term> of burnt copper <note>original: "Aëris usti"</note> / wash it / dry it / and grind it small / soak it with a good vinegar / in which one *loth* of mercury sublimate <note>original: "Sublimatum"</note> has been dissolved. After that, calcine it in an open crucible for three hours / then grind it into a subtle powder / so it becomes a Saffron of Venus <note>original: "Crocus ♀," referring to a fine red copper oxide</note>. Take 1 pound of this / half a pound of burnt quartz / half a pound of crushed Venetian glass <note>Venetian glass was prized for its purity and clarity in chemical processes</note> / two and a half pounds of the residue <note>original: "Todtenkopff," literally "dead head" or Caput Mortuum, the metallic remains left after distilling acids</note> of common nitric acid <note>original: "Aquafort"</note>. Grind it small / put it into a crucible / let it flow for one hour: Treat it / as you did the black glass.

# Yellow Lead Glass.

### Calcination of Common Salt.

### Composition of the Fixing Powder.

Further / Take of black and yellow glass, equal parts <note>original: "ana"</note> of one *loth* / one *loth* of Saffron of Mars <note>original: "Croci ♂," referring to iron oxide</note> / three *loth* of the brown powder made from salt and talc / all ground small / each one individually / and mix them together / thus it is ready to fix <note>To "fix" a metal in alchemy is to render it non-volatile so it can withstand the heat of a furnace without evaporating</note> the silver <note>original: ☽ (Luna)</note>.

Also, you can graduate <note>refine to a higher purity</note> it even higher in this way. Then pour it / so it becomes beautiful / and add natural gold to it / of 24 degrees / Thus you have fixed gold.

Then take three *loth* of the prepared gold / two *loth* of fixing powder / hammer the gold into thin sheets / and make layer upon layer with the powder in a crucible / and treat it as was written before. Should it be brittle / then cement it in a Royal Cement <term>ziment Regali: a process using salts and acids to purify gold to its highest standard</term>. Or throw borax / and mercury precipitate <note>original: ☿ præcipitat</note> upon it / then it will also become malleable.

### Cement for Potable Gold.

Let it be cemented with Royal Cement <note>original: "Cemento regali," a corrosive mixture used to purify gold</note>. ### Precipitate of Gold and Mercury.

Take one *loth* <term>Loth: a traditional German unit of weight, roughly 15-16 grams</term> of gold / four *loth* of mercury / perform calcination, as you know <note>original: "vt scis"</note>, in a glass with a long neck / until it no longer rises. Then take it out / grind it / put it into a vial / let it rise again / so long / until it remains at the bottom / red. Then grind it again / etc. / and it will be prepared. It is effective against the plague, various poisons, and against the poison of mercury <note>original: "Valet contra pestem, venena diuersa, contra Mercurij venenum"</note>. ### How Gold may ascend through the Alembic: and this is the Tincture of the Sun.

Take Alsatian wine, distill it by the true and correct method, so that you have the Quintessence <term>Quintessence: The "fifth essence," a highly purified and potent extract</term> from it. But what remains behind in the first distillation, boil that down in a copper kettle to an electuary <term>Electuary: A paste or thick liquid (Latwerge) made by mixing medicine with honey or syrup</term>. Upon this pour boiling hot water <note>original: 🜄</note> (namely, that water which remained after the Quintessence was drawn off, according to the way of Raymond Lully or Theophrastus Paracelsus), and so it dissolves. Let it settle, and you will find the Tartar of Wine <term>Tartar of Wine: Potassium bitartrate, the sediment found in wine casks</term>. But if it is still black, calcine <term>Calcine: To heat a substance to high temperatures to drive off volatile matter or oxidize it</term> it until it becomes white. Thereafter, dissolve a little of the Tartar in its Essence, let it putrefy for one day, and distill it over. If the Tartar does not yet wish to rise [distill], let it putrefy for several days and distill again, for so long until it comes over. Thus, continue to dissolve the Tartar until everything passes over into the Essence.

From all flowers and herbs you can extract the true <term>Specific Property: The unique medicinal virtue or "signature" of a plant (specificam Proprietatem)</term> with this. Put this white Tartar into the Quintessence of Wine, and add the Gold <note>symbol: ☉</note> [purified by] Antimony <note>symbol: ♁</note> to it, and so it rises over. The red Spirit [passes] through the Alembic, which is its Essence or color, and it is entirely volatile. Use that as you know how.

Concerning this [Quintessence of Gold], which is made through the water of Salt, not with Wine. Count Ludwig of Oettingen <note>original: Ludouicus ab Ottinga</note> had a bailiff who for three days had neither reason nor speech, and was just about to lie down in his passing <note>original: "Hinzügen," referring to the final throes of death</note>. Of this (I say) Quintessence of Gold, he gave him three drops in rosemary water <note>original: aqua Rorisimarini</note>; and within one hour he returned to himself, and spoke, and was revived, and remained alive for a long time afterward. But his Quintessence of Gold was made with oil of Salt, which Abraham gave to his wife, who was gravely ill, and she recovered, so that she said she had not been so healthy for a long time.

He makes the oil of Salt thus: common Salt is melted three times; a fourth time it is poured into water, which he allows to stand in the cellar until it flows, and thereafter...

Take one pound / one and a half pounds of crude tartar <term>Tartarum Crudum: A salty crust found in wine barrels, used here as a flux to help metals melt</term>, whether it be red or white; let it flow <note>melt</note> together clearly, and pour a regulus <term>König: Literally 'King,' the metallic 'button' that settles at the bottom of a crucible</term>. ## The Preparation of Sulfur.

Take as much yellow cast sulfur <note>original: *Sulphuris*</note> as you wish, put it into a glazed pot, and pour the aforementioned lye into it so that it covers it slightly. Let it boil gently day and night, and skim it with an iron skimmer. As the lye boils away, pour in more fresh lye made from lime <term>Kalck: Quicklime or calcium oxide, used to create highly caustic alkaline solutions</term>, as before. When it has boiled for a day and a night, remove it from the fire and let the sulfur settle. The lye will be colored by the fattiness <note>original: Feistigkeit; referring to the oily, flammable essence or "soul" of the mineral</note> of the sulfur. Pour the yellow-colored lye into another vessel, and wash the sulfur <note>original: *Sulphur*</note> that lies at the bottom cleanly with warm water.

Continue this until the water comes away clear. Then pour fresh lye made from lime onto this washed residue <note>original: *Kalch*, here meaning the solid matter</note>, that is, sulfur <note>original: *id est, Sulphur*</note>, and boil it again day and night, skimming and refilling it. Then wash it as before. This work must be done three times in succession; in this way, the sulfur retains all its moisture <note>In alchemy, 'moisture' refers to the internal principle that gives a substance its properties</note>. Dry it over a small fire, and the sulfur will become entirely gray-colored to some extent.

Then take iron scales <term>Hammerschlag: The black flakes of iron oxide that fall from red-hot iron when it is hammered in a forge</term>, grind them fine, and wash them until they are beautifully clear. Dry them in a very gentle warmth, like sunshine. Then take two parts of the prepared sulfur and one part of the iron scales. Rub them well together, moisten them slightly with vinegar, and then let them dry in a sublimation vessel <term>Sublimatorio: An apparatus used to heat a substance until it turns to vapor and then re-solidifies in the cooler upper part of the vessel</term> with a gentle fire until the moisture evaporates. Then give it the fire as is proper for sublimation. When it has sublimated, take the sulfur and rub it again with well-washed iron scales, moisten it with vinegar, and sublimate it again as done before. Perform this sublimation three times; then the sulfur will become red, will no longer burn, and will no longer stink. Keep it until its time <note>A common phrase meaning to save the material for the next stage of a larger alchemical process</note>.
