# Concerning Revelation

<margin>7</margin> Of these herbs, take a good portion, but take as much of one as of the others; mix them together and crush them quite small and put them into the Philosophical Vessel <note>A specialized alchemical glass container, such as a retort or cucurbit, designed to withstand heat.</note>, and draw out from them the four Elements: first the Water, second the <term>Ally</term> <note>original: "Ally"; likely a derivation of the Arabic "al-qali," referring here to the volatile alkaline spirit or oily substance produced during distillation.</note>, thirdly the Fire. In this way, the Element of Earth will remain in the bottom or base of the vessel. Crush or grind this Earth to the smallest possible size, and pour its recently extracted Water back upon it, and distill or draw the Water away from it again as was done before. This distillation or Sublimation <note>The process of heating a substance until it turns to vapor and then collecting the purified result as it cools.</note> shall occur seven times, etc.

Namely, these seven times are to wake the dead or make them rise—that is, to kill them seven times through the ascent and to make them living seven times through the descent. For when Father Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure regarded as the founder of alchemy and the "father" of this Art.</note>, the inventor of this Art, was asked what the beginning and the first work of this Art might be, he answered and spoke: "You shall raise the dead seven times or exalt them or make them ascend, and let the living descend again; then you will have that which you seek and desire." For then the power of each is entirely inseparable, transformed one into the other, and a firm and lasting bond is made between the Bridegroom and the Bride—namely, between the Water and the Meal <note>original: "Mels"; likely referring to the dry, powdered substance or "flour" of the metal, though in some contexts it may signify "Mel" (Latin for honey).</note>. And in this degree, this Water of Life attains seven <term>Quintel Essentias</term> <note>original: "Quintel Essentias"; a Germanized plural of the Latin "Quinta Essentia," or the Fifth Essence—the purest, most potent celestial part of a substance.</note>; that is, a sevenfold fifth essence. For in the mentioned seven Sublimations or Distillations, it drinks in all the natures, essences, and life of the aforementioned herbs. Thereafter, you shall sublimate—that is, distill—this venerable water, which is called a Well of Life, two or three times by itself upon its Earth or dregs, and you shall cast away all impurity and foulness that it leaves behind in each sublimation. After this, you shall once again drive it very gently and slowly with a moderate fire, until the Watery Substance is pulled over entirely; keep this same substance alone and separately in a clean, well-stopped glass, for it has much magnificent power and virtue. When now the Watery Substance, as heard, is entirely out, and the Ally begins to rise, then you shall put forward another glass or receiver to receive the Ally, and strengthen the fire a little, and a little more, until nothing more of the Ally ascends. This Ally of the Philosophers you shall keep very well-sealed in a glass, for this is the Matter and our secret, to which the philosophers have given countless many names. Namely, it is called <term>Azach</term> <note>A common alchemical cover-name (Deckname) for Mercury or the universal spirit.</note>: according to the Indian language, it is or is called Gold; according to the Hungarian language, Azach is as much as to say Silver; but according to the Alexandrian and Macedonian, as much as Iron; and according to the Greek, Mercury or living silver <note>original: "Argentum viuum"</note>; according to the Hebrew, Tin; and according to the Tartar...

### The Fifth Chapter.

<margin>The Seal of Hermes</margin>
My Dear Son / much depends on the sealing or closing of the glasses / therefore you shall diligently pay attention and take heed of the following teaching / for / I will teach you here the sealing which our father **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy.</note> invented / and used / and it proceeds thus: Take first the **Philosophical** <note>original: "Philosophisch"</note> water mentioned before, which is divided with its most noble Earth / which is well mixed with its fresh Blood <note>Allegorical terms for the reagents: "Blood" often refers to the red mercury or a vitalizing agent, while "Earth" is the solid base.</note> / and put that together into a suitable one of the previously indicated glasses / but you should first diligently weigh the glass with its **Seal** <note>original: "Sigel"</note> or stopper / to / note the weight / before the matter goes into it / and weigh the matter also / and note it diligently / so that you may prepare yourself accordingly with that which follows / and then close its mouth thus: You should first have / a round glass disc or small sphere that closes upon or into the mouth of the glass / then you should have very finely crushed glass and coat the disc or sphere / and the mouth with it / just as goldsmiths are accustomed to use it for soldering / then you must likewise spread **Borax** <note>original: "Borras"; a mineral used as a flux to help glass and metals melt together at lower temperatures.</note> over it / but / the glass with the matter should first be placed in a vessel with ashes / then the mouth should be stopped with the glass [disc] / after that, lay charcoal / around and over the top / and let the coals catch fire nicely and slowly / after that, increase the fire and blow upon it gradually / until the neck and mouth become quite glowing red / then sprinkle **Borax** into the mouth / so it will / flow and melt shut and solder at the top. After this, let the fire burn out by itself / and go out / and when the glass has thus become cold of its own accord / then take the glass with the matter and place it in the furnace / as was taught before. You should also know that this sealing also happens with the tongs / namely / thus / when the neck of the glass is quite glowing red / then you should have a pair of tongs / which have been made a little hot / and press the neck shut with them / then it will also be entirely as if / it were melted shut / and then let it cool by itself with the covered coals / the form and shape of the vessel with the ashes / and it will be so.

# How the Philosophers' Furnace should be made / in which our Stone is cooked.

## The Sixth Chapter.

Son, you shall have made for yourself / a barrel or vessel of the very best potter's clay <note>original: "Haffner Erden"; a heat-resistant clay used for kilns and crucibles.</note> / which may well endure the fire / in which you shall place the stone or our water / securely enclosed. It should be so wide and spacious / that the glass standing within / has two or three fingers’ breadth of space on all sides / between the glass and the width of the vessel / and that same space should be filled with sifted ashes. Its form and shape shall be thus: / upon this same vessel a lid of potter’s clay shall also be made / so that it does not touch the glass / in which our matter is contained. However, it should be made / so that it has a handle on top / so that it may be lifted off / whenever it is necessary to inspect the matter / and this same lid must be fitted very well over the sand cupels <note>original: "Sand Capeln"; vessels used for sand baths to distribute heat evenly.</note>. When this is done / you shall coat the glass containing the matter well with good master’s lute <note>original: "Meisterleimb"; a strong, heat-resistant cement or "lute" used to seal alchemical apparatus.</note> / and place it in the ashes / in the previously described vessel / so that the glass is one part full / and remains three parts empty. After this, a furnace shall also be made of good earth / which is well-beaten and mixed with horse dung <note>original: "Pferdkot"; a traditional additive in early furnace construction that provided organic fiber to prevent the clay from cracking under high heat.</note> / and a little sand / so that it may endure the fire / and not melt. The furnace shall be round / and one ell <note>original: "Ellen"; a traditional unit of measurement, roughly the length of an arm (approx. 24–45 inches).</note> high / and nearly two ells wide. Its walls shall be 2 or 3 fingers thick / and air-holes should also be made near the ground at the foundation of the furnace in four places / for otherwise the light in the lamp <note>original: "Ampel"; a small oil lamp or burner used as a constant heat source.</note> would not burn. After this, a cross should be made of sheet iron inside the furnace / with a round hole in the middle / in which a lamp can be placed / and the iron sheet should be so wide / that there is a space or room three or four fingers wide between the walls of the furnace and the sheet. Under this sheet, however, in the middle of the furnace, a floor should be made / which shall have a round hole in the middle / large enough that one can put a fist through it. After this, the iron plate for the lamp should be prepared / and the furnace shall be raised in the front with iron / upon which the vessel with the glass / containing our matter / shall stand.

The tripod <note>original: "Dreyfuß"</note>, however, should stand one and a half hand-breadths away from or above the lamp / and this furnace should be raised so high that it reaches to the lid of the earthen vessel / which stands upon the tripod / so that when you wish to inspect the matter and its signs <note>original: "zeichen"; the specific color changes (like the Black Crow or White Swan) that indicate progress in the alchemical Work.</note> / as they appear / the height of the furnace does not hinder you in

### Regarding the Lamp used in this Furnace.
## The Seventh Chapter.

Now when the furnace is entirely finished / and the glass with the **matter** is inside it / then a lamp with oil <note>original: "Ally"; likely a derivation of the Latin "Oleum" for oil or fat used as fuel.</note> shall be lit under the vessel in which the glass with our **matter** is kept / these shall burn continuously and steadily in equal measure / and never more be extinguished / and the wicks shall be made of no more than 3 threads / and not exceeding that / therefore one should be diligent so that the oil and the wicks never fail / for in such a way / and with no other fire / will our operation of the Stone be accomplished. But take good care / that this fire does not go out nor diminish / until the completion of the work / so that your effort and labor be not in vain and lost.

## The Twelfth Chapter.

Therefore you shall know, my dear son, that the blackness in the cooking of the **Stone** appears in forty days or in forty-two days, and it also lasts until the 40th or 42nd day—at times longer or shorter, depending on whether there is much or little of the matter. Furthermore, when you have the perfect White Elixir, it does not change or transform until it comes to the perfect Red, in which the final and all-powerful strength of the **Stone** resides.

### The 18th Chapter.

## Of the Power and Effect of the Blessed Stone.

### The 19th Chapter.

This honorable, highly praised, and **blessed Philosophical Stone** restores and delivers the bodies of men from all manner of sicknesses or diseases, whatever they may be. # TREASURY OF PHILO-
# SOPHY, BY EUFERARIUS.

<margin><unclear>Ludovicus Ferrarius</unclear></margin>
<margin>The philosophers have presented the art in two ways: one true, one false.</margin>
May He be willing to reveal His bounty to us—He to whom all things belong, the Heavens, Earth, and Sea, and who could create everything out of nothing and join the unequal into harmony, and who ordained according to His goodness that the sick might be helped with medicines. Regarding this, the ancient sages—who presented this perfect understanding in their books in two ways: one true, and one false. The righteous ones <note>meaning the true alchemists</note> set down their work with veiled words, so that they might be perfectly understood by no one except their own children <note>in this context, "children" refers to their students or initiated followers</note>. They kept it hidden for this reason: so that the godless might not use this Art and become even more prepared to commit evil deeds, for which sins they would have to give an account. Therefore, take care, most beloved, that you do not reveal this Art to any unworthy person, but rather, according to philosophical custom, keep it secret; for if you prove it through the Work and find it to be righteous, the joy and love within you to preserve it will increase.

The false way, however, is described with clear words; I will now bypass the recounting of that erroneous path and its circumstances. But, most beloved, listen and pay attention to the truth, and so God will enlighten your understanding.

<margin>The true art.</margin>
<margin>Things are the 4 Elements, page 612.</margin>
Know then, that our Art is an Art of the 4 Elements, and in its essence, it is transformed within itself—a point upon which all philosophers agree. You should also know that in the aforementioned "thing" <note>referring to the primary matter of the Stone</note> under the Heavens are the 4 Elements, not according to their outward appearance, but according to their inner virtue; for this reason, the philosophers have not taught or worked this Art under the mere cover of the Art of the elements. However, when some did not understand the literal sense of this operation, they tried to attempt all of this in blood, urine, and eggs, as well as in many other similar approaches; and I likewise attempted them, and was horrified by it. And therefore, as I had fallen into complete doubt regarding this Art, I set such work aside and accomplished nothing, due to the weakness of my understanding.

Afterward, however, I came back to myself and began to reflect with **Avicenna** <note>a famous Persian polymath (c. 980–1037) whose writings on medicine and philosophy were foundational to Western alchemy</note>: if this "single thing" is indeed a single thing, how can it be? Or if it is not, how is it not? Thus, I found that the matter of all metals—

The [origin] of metals is *mercury* <note>original: "Mercurius"</note>, cooked and hardened in the body of the earth, boiled in sulfurous heat / and according to the various types of *sulfur* <note>original: "Sulphurs"</note> / and its manifold inequality / unequal metals are born in the earth. For their first *matter* <note>original: "materia," referring to the fundamental substance underlying all physical things</note> is one thing / yet it becomes distinguished / through accidental actions / and mixed within the great and small *decoction* <note>original: "Decoction," a process of heating or boiling a substance to extract its essence</note> / whether combustible or incombustible / as all *philosophers* <note>original: "Philoſophi"</note> say with one voice. For it is certain that <margin><unclear>To v.</unclear></margin> all things / are from / or of that / into which they are resolved / since [metal] is transformed into water by means of heat / thus it is evident / that it was originally water. Likewise, all metals are transformed into *mercury* <note>original: "mercurium"</note>, therefore they were originally made from *mercury* <note>original: "mercurio"</note>; however, the way to bring them back into *mercury* / will be shown below. <margin><unclear>...</unclear></margin> Through this, that which *Aristotle* <note>original: "Ariſtot."</note> speaks of in the *fourth book of Meteorology* <note>original: "quarto meteoro-rum," a foundational text for medieval science</note> is resolved; the wise masters of *alchemy* <note>original: "Alchemey"</note> should therefore know / that the *species* <note>original: "Species," meaning the essential types or categories</note> of metals cannot be changed / and that is true / unless / the same be brought / as follows / into its first *matter* <note>original: "materiam"</note>. Such restoration is easy / and possible relative to one another / for everything that grows and is born / is also multiplied / as is seen in all herbs / trees, and animals / where from one grain a thousand grains grow / and from one tree a thousand branches shoot forth / and from one human the entire human race is born / thus each is multiplied according to its kind. So, too, a metal can multiply a metal from itself / and there is no difference. Thus speaks *Aristotle* <note>original: "Ariſtotoles"</note>, whether this happens in natural or artificial *instruments* <note>original: "Inſtrumenten"</note>, etc. 

All metals, however, are born and grow in the earth / so it is also quite possible that there is manifold multiplication within them / even infinitely. But that there is diversity and multiplication in them / cannot happen otherwise / than through that / which is perfect in the metals. O dear friend, do not go astray / for what a man sows / that he shall also reap and cut; now it is sufficiently explained / what kind of stone [it is] / what its *medicine* <note>original: "Artzney"</note> is / <margin><unclear>...</unclear></margin> to which nothing foreign shall be added / only the superfluous taken from it / for such [foreign matter] does not suit it / but only / what is closest to its nature. Now I will / O most beloved / interpret for you the speech of the *philoso-*

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the "second composition" or joining, specifically focusing on the union of the solar and lunar principles to create a stable medicinal tincture.</meta>

# Treasure of Philosophy.

<margin>//</margin>The mother is moist and cold, which nourishes the newborn. Therefore, the **Sun** <note>original: "Sol"; representing Gold</note> by itself and the **Moon** <note>original: "Luna"; representing Silver</note> by itself are most impossible to cast together. But when they are united, in the manner that the hardening into **Gold** occurs, they are easily cast. Therefore Maria <note>referring to Maria Prophetissima, a foundational figure in alchemy</note> says: take the precipitated **Body** <note>original: "Corpus"</note> or clear pearls that take on no putrefaction, and rub it with *Elsapenes* <note>original: "Elsapenes"; likely a corruption of an Arabic alchemical term for a specific solvent or salt</note>, which contains within itself the **Tincture of Spirits**, and move it toward the fire; and it will soon melt completely if you project upon it his wife, the **Moon**. Therefore, if only one of these two were in our **Stone** <note>original: "Lapide"</note>, this medicine would not flow easily or provide a **Tincture**; and even if it did provide one, it would not tint any further than its own mass; the rest would pass away, just as **Mercury** <note>original: "mercurius"</note> passes away in smoke. For there would be no staying of the tincture for them; but that is our final secret: to have a medicine that flows before the disappearance of the **Mercury**. The union of these two is necessary in this our **Work**.

Hence **Geber** <note>an 8th-century alchemist known for his "sum of perfection"</note> says: in a perfect work, **Gold** is better than other metals, for it is the **Tincture of Redness** that transforms all bodies; it is the leaven <note>original: "Heffel"; literally "yeast"</note> that brings the whole dough to its proper quality. It is also the **Soul** that unites the **Spirit** with the **Body**. For just as the human body is immobile without the soul, so too the impure body—whose soul is earthly—is powerless. For the leaven of the well-prepared body transforms the entire body into its own nature. And there is no **Ferment** <note>original: "Fermentum"</note> except only the **Sun** and **Moon**, assigned to the <margin>//</margin>planets; for just as the Sun and Moon rule over other planets, so these two bodies rule over the other bodies of the metals, which are transformed into the capability of these two mentioned natures. And for this reason it is called **Ferment**, <margin>//</margin>since indeed size adds no improvement to it; as **Raymond** <note>referring to Raymond Llull</note> says: "you cannot improve this unless it is made subtle through art and operation." Therefore **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus</note> says: "Bring forth from the Sun’s radiance its shadow." Consequently, the preparation and refining of such a ferment is necessary, as in a well; for as far as the creation is concerned, it certainly washes, but not as far as the effect is concerned, unless it is first fed with a little milk, then not more, and finally with much; and thus it happens entirely with this our **Stone**.

Take therefore one quarter—that is, one part of the **Ferment**—and three parts of the **perfect Body**; let it dissolve again into the ferment, into its likeness through the **Water of Mercury**; cook it together with the gentlest fire and coagulate the **Ferment**, so that it becomes like an imperfect body, in a closed vessel: <note>original: "Geschirr"; referring to the philosopher's egg or sealed flask</note>

Some philosophers have also said: "if you do not transform the bodies into non-bodies, and the incorporeal into corporeal, you have never yet found the true light of truth," and they speak the truth. For the body first becomes **water** <note>original: "aqua"</note>, and thus the corporeal [becomes] incorporeal, which is **Spirit**; thereafter, in the joining of the spirit, the water becomes a body.

Therefore Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the mythical founder of alchemy</note> says: "reverse nature, and you will find what you seek," and that is true; for in our work, we first make a refined thing from a coarse one—that is, a water from a body—but afterward we make a dry thing from the moist—that is, an earth from water. And thus we rightly reverse the natures, for we make a spiritual thing from the corporeal, and a corporeal thing from the spiritual. And this is what the Senior <note>Senior Zadith, the Latin name for the 10th-century Arab alchemist Ibn Umail</note> says: it is a transformation of bodies from one state into the other, from one thing into the other, from an incomprehensible thing to a comprehensible thing, from a coarseness to a refinement, from body to spirituality. For thus says Aristotle: "all generation is from the aptitude in nature," and that is true, most especially in metallic generations. # Treasure of Philosophy.

> a King of Arabia has said: the water is not made hard <note>solidified or congealed</note> except by the like of its sulfur, which is within it.

Afterward, we make that which is above equal to that which is below—that is, that the body becomes a spirit, and the spirit becomes a body, just as it is at the beginning of our work, as in the sublimation <term>Sublimation: the process of heating a substance until it vaporizes and then collecting the purified deposit as it cools</term>. That which is below is equal to that which is above, and it is entirely transformed into earth.

<margin>Sublimation:</margin>
> Therefore Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founding figure of alchemy</note> says: that which is above through sublimation is below through descent; that which is below through compaction is just like that which is above through ascent, to accomplish the wonder-work of a single thing.

Water and earth have their nature; the air and fire below rise above themselves. Water and Earth <note>original: "Aqua und Terra"</note> receive and nourish Air and Fire <note>original: "Aerem und Ignis"</note>, joining and driving them together. These four elements come into agreement in our Stone <note>original: "Lapide"</note>, etc.

> Of this Senior <note>Senior Zadith, a 10th-century Arabic alchemist often cited in European texts</note> says: the fourth element in our Stone should be purified; for within it is fixed water <note>original: "aqua fixa" — a liquid that resists evaporation by heat</note>, a light air, a still earth, a fire that surrounds everything, and discord is not one with it; and these four natures are born in it, from it, and through it.

Thus it is known from the above-mentioned that our Stone is of four elements. So the Philosophers have said that our Stone has Body, Spirit, and Soul, and these three are said to be of one nature, of one thing, with one water, from one root. And they say rightly that our entire work happens with our water, and from it and out of it all things are necessary; for it dissolves the bodies <note>original: "soluiert die corpora"</note>, not according to common dissolution as the inexperienced claim—that they are turned into cloud-water <note>original: "aquam nubis"</note>—but with true philosophical dissolution, so that they are transformed into the water from which they came.

<margin><image-desc>Alchemical symbol for Vinegar followed by a cross-like mark.</image-desc></margin>
> Therefore Socrates <note>In alchemical literature, "Socrates" is often a pseudonym for an anonymous authority or refers to the "Socrates of the alchemists"</note> says: the secret in every thing and life is Water; this dissolves the body into spirit and makes the dead living; that is, the sharpest Vinegar <note>original: "Acetum"</note>, which clings to everything, surpasses everything, and scours away.

Therefore, cook our Stone <note>original: "Lapidem"</note> with the sharpest vinegar until it becomes hard, yet quite quickly, so that the vinegar does not turn into smoke and come to nothing.

<margin><image-desc>Alchemical symbol for Earth followed by the word "salt".</image-desc></margin>
Likewise, this same water calcines <term>Calcine: to reduce a substance to powder or ash through intense heat</term> the bodies and brings them back into Earth <note>original: "Terram"</note>; this very thing which blackens, whitens, and reddens the bodies, this makes them into an ash, pulverizes them and inhabits them.

> According to which King Marches <note>likely referring to King Morienus, a legendary hermit-alchemist</note> says: our Water dissolves our bodies, congeals and blackens them, washes off every body, takes away all blackness, and tinctures all blackness and makes it white; tinctures everything white and makes it red; also makes alive all the dead, leading them into eternal life.

Therefore, this Water is highly praised and highly esteemed.

Therefore, between the <term>solution</term> <note>The process of dissolving a solid into a liquid state.</note> of the <term>body</term> <note>original: "Corpus"</note> and the <term>coagulation</term> <note>The process of a liquid becoming solid or semi-solid.</note> of the <term>spirit</term> <note>original: "Spiritus"</note>, there is no difference in time, nor does anything happen within it at different intervals, etc. Thus, one is made without the other, just as during the joining of water and earth there is no unequal distribution of time. > The red likewise flows into black.

# TREATISE
## In which the entire Secret of Alchemy / of the Philosopher’s Stone is contained.

This Stone is the true **fifth essence** <note>original: "quinta essentia" — the purest, most concentrated essence of a substance</note>; for we seek no other thing in the world but this **Stone**. <margin>Calcined Saturn (Lead)</margin>
roughly two or three fingers high above it, on an iron hook made for this purpose. The jar should be properly and well-sealed so that the **spirits** <note>Volatile vapors</note> do not escape. Then, take good distilled wine vinegar again and grind the Saturn with the distilled vinegar on a stone, as fine as you possibly can. Put this into a large jug or glass called a **Cucurbit** <note>A gourd-shaped laboratory vessel used for distillation or digestion.</note>, filling it half or two-thirds full with the distilled vinegar. Stir it 3 or 4 times every day. Close it with a glass or stone lid and place it in **Mary's Bath** <note>original: "Balneum Mariæ" — a water bath used for gentle, consistent heating.</note>, or else in a warm place. Stir it three or 4 times every day with a small wood stick or spoon, and 
<margin>Warmth.</margin>
always close it up well again. The bath should not be hotter than what a hand can endure, but only lukewarm. Let it stand for fourteen days.

Mix them well together and place it back in the water bath or in a warmth as before. When it has stood for another fourteen days, pour the clear 
<margin>Dissolved Saturn.</margin>
dissolved liquid into the first batch, and pour even more distilled vinegar on it than before. Do this until the **calces of Saturn** have completely dissolved.

<margin>Brownish-yellow.</margin>

# Secret of the Philosopher’s Stone

<margin>residue <note>original: "feces"</note>.</margin>

<margin>Saturn is clear as snow. Sweet. White: sweet.</margin>

Why is it sweet as sugar candy? <note>This refers to Lead Acetate, historically called "Sugar of Lead" for its sweet taste. It has immediately become material and like nature because it is so pure and clean. Regarding the coldness that is on the outside—the spirit of taste is the most subtle thing in all the world. This is taught at length in the **Herbal** <note>original: "Kräuter-buch" — a book detailing the medicinal properties of plants.</note>: how the air permeates all herbs and flowers from the outside, for the spirit of the air resides in the innermost part of all things in the world. For God has created nothing that does not have its particular taste or "air." Taste and air are a spirit; taste comes out of the air like smoke comes from a fire. But how does it happen that a thing containing its own air tastes bitter? This comes from the residue that is rotten and stinking within the elements; this is **Choler** <note>original: "Colera" — one of the four humors, associated with heat, dryness, and bitterness.</note> or heat. For whatever is unnaturally hot always has a bitter taste. Air and taste are both one spirit, and as the spirit presses upward through the air like a hot thing, the air encloses the taste within itself and protects the subtle taste so that it is not burned by the hot Choler, as is taught at length in the *Herbal*.

<margin>taste in Saturn is sweet.</margin>
But the fact that the taste in Saturn is sweet comes from it being immediately pure and clean; it no longer has any unnatural heat within it that might burn the subtle taste. Therefore, it has the taste on the outside, and the taste has enclosed within it the spirit of the air.

Then pour over your Stone again with Paradise water <term>Paradise water: a highly purified alchemical spirit or solvent, often associated with the "mercury of the philosophers"</term> as I have taught you before in the work, and cook it in every way as previously taught, so that you may always remain in operation.

Now, my children, I shall teach you one manner of completing the Stone with the mercury <note>original: *Mercurio*</note> that is drawn out of itself, of which the philosophers speak and write: draw off its blood and sweat, and give it to him again to drink, then he will receive and keep life, and in eternity he will thirst no more. For this, thank God the Lord.

Now I will teach you the other manner, and the best way, to pour the red oil over your fixed Stone and make it fluid. You should know how much your red powder weighs; then take half as much of the red oil as the Stone weighs, and pour it onto the red powder in the glass. Place a small alembic head <note>original: *Helm*</note> upon it, and set it in fine ashes with a receiver vessel <note>original: *Recipienten*</note> before it. Give it a small fire, like the sun shines in March and no hotter, because there is still some moisture in the oil. Keep it at a steady warmth until you find no more moisture in the alembic head; then strengthen your fire a little. If more moisture is present, it will reveal itself in the head; if it does not reveal itself in six or eight days, then remove the head and place the ground glass plate back onto the mouth of the glass. Give it more fire, so hot that you can hardly endure your finger in it for as long as it takes to speak half of the Angelic Salutation <note>The *Ave Maria*; alchemists used the duration of familiar prayers to measure time before clocks were precise</note>. # Now follows the preparation of the second principle <note>original: *Principij*</note>, namely the Sulfur of the Sun <note>original: *Sulphuris Solis*</note> or of the Philosophers, which the philosophers often and frequently call the Soul <note>original: *Animam*</note>.

Pour them together into a clean flask <note>original: *Kolben*</note>, set a blind alembic head <term>Blind helm: A distillation cap without a spout, used to force vapors to condense and fall back into the vessel for "circulation"</term> upon it, seal it with the aforementioned luting <note>original: *luto supradicto*</note>, and place it in warm sand or ash—which, however, should not be too hot. Let it elevate, circulate, and putrefy for three days, and then separate it as described. Place that same Soul into a clean glass, well-sealed as first mentioned, and keep it until the Composition <note>The final joining of the three principles</note>.

However, I have taken new and earthy "inflated matter" <note>original: *materiam inflatam*</note> and placed it into a coated flask, well-sealed, and distilled it gently out of the sand. I poured it over several times and afterwards drove it over with a strong fire and separated it; thus the Soul was much more beautiful, redder, more transparent, and possessed many more colors than the other which came out of the putrefaction. I have also used a good portion of it, as can be seen in the description of the composition.

<margin>Luting</margin>
Note one more thing: when you attach the receiver or recipient vessel, you should also seal it with our luting; otherwise, you will labor in vain and will not bring the **Red Lion** into his stall, nor will you see the **Green Lion**. <note>The "Red Lion" often symbolizes the concentrated sulfur or the mercury of gold, while the "Green Lion" represents the raw mineral or the acidic solvent used at the start of the work.</note> You must also be prepared with another good luting made from egg whites, brick dust, glue, and wool, in case our luting becomes weak or tired in the great heat, so that you may come to its aid with this one. Take great care that you do not anger the **Red Lion**, lest he inflict an insurmountable harm upon you—as happened to me—and strike you poorly. All of this is to be prevented if you let our luting dry thoroughly before you light the fire. Thereafter you will know how to conduct yourself; let this be a warning to you. Thus you have also prepared the second principle, namely the Sulfur of the Philosophers.

# Regarding the Philosophical Stone.

In the same way, by varying the heat—just as you did with the others—until you have separated the Soul <note>original: *Anima*</note> from it; however, you must not drive the Spirits <note>original: *Spiritus*</note> so strongly from the Earth <note>original: *Erden*</note> as you did before in the other work, so that the Water may retain its strength and spirituality in its preparation. It would also not be harmful, since it is the preparation of Mercury <note>original: *præparatio Mercurij*</note>, if one were to distill and pour it back over repeatedly until the Soul remains entirely fixed <term>Fixed: In alchemy, a substance that is stable under heat and does not evaporate or change</term> behind, and only the Water and Air pass over together. I have not tried it myself, but I know well that it happens and becomes entirely fixed through multiple repetitions. Then the work of this third Principle <note>original: *Principij*</note> follows further, namely that of Mercury <note>original: *Mercurij*</note>: Take a well-coated flask <note>original: *Kolben*</note>, put your Earth <note>original: *Terra*</note> into it, and pour in the Water from which you separated your Soul; seal it very well with lute <term>Lute: A clay or paste used to seal laboratory vessels airtight</term>, and place it in sand. Distill it gently at first, and at the last very strongly—as strongly as you can—so that all the Spirits enter into it until no more pass over. Afterwards, let it cool and put it back into a coated flask, and distill and drive it as before; do this six or seven times, but watch carefully that the Spirit does not fly away. When this has been done, it would be necessary that you have a large amount of the prepared Earth in which the Spirit still remained, and drive that same Earth four times with its Spirit. And when this has happened, let it cool and put it back into a whole coated flask, and distill and drive it as before; do this five or six times—the more, the better—but watch carefully that the Spirit does not escape. When that has also been done, it would be necessary (according to Morienus <note>original: *secundum Morienem*; Morienus was a legendary 7th-century alchemist</note>) that the Mercury, for its Alteration <term>Alteration: A stage of transformation where the properties of the matter are changed</term>, be distilled four times with the prepared Earth in which its Spirit still remains, and the Spirit be driven into it. After all this, let it cool.

# On Philosophical Vitriol.

<margin>7 times</margin>
<margin>Water <note>The symbol ∇ represents the element of Water.</note></margin>
The more often you rectify it <note>Rectification is the process of repeated distillation to increase purity and potency.</note>, the better it is. It should be rectified seven times in this manner, or as many times as necessary until it no longer rises; this makes it much better and more virtuous for the **residues** <term>Feces: The solid matter or dregs remaining in the vessel after distillation.</term>, which will be discussed later.
Now, if you wish to use this water as medicine for the human body, place it in a small glass with a long neck, two or three hand-breadths long, upon a stove with a gentle fire. In this way, it will be perfected; and the longer it stands, the more perfect it becomes. It does not even need to be tightly sealed at the top; one only needs to ensure that no impurities fall into it.

### How the Water Should be Used.

Furthermore, take a half-beaker of wine and let one drop of the **secret water** <term>aqua secreta: A purified alchemical solvent or essence.</term> fall into it. Mix it well into the wine with a knife, for it is heavy and tends to sink to the bottom. Then taste it; if it is far too sharp, pour more wine into it; if it is too sweet, add water until it has the proper flavor that pleases you and is well-mixed, as has been said.

This substance cures the **residues** <term>Feces: In a medical context, this refers to waste products or blockages within the body.</term>, and is good in times of Plague if one washes the painful areas with it. It cures the gout <note>original: Podagram</note>, and this is the true **potable gold** <term>aurum potabile: A legendary alchemical medicine consisting of gold dissolved in a drinkable form, thought to grant eternal youth.</term>, in which the **secrets of nature** <note>original: secreta naturæ</note> are hidden. You will find this through practice; this is the true **human blood** <note>original: sanguis Humanus; likely a metaphor for its life-giving properties.</note>, the true **Celandine** <term>Chelidonia: A plant traditionally associated with the sun and used to treat eye and liver ailments.</term>. These flowers are like gold and heavy as **Mercury** <term>Mercurius: Quicksilver, often used here to describe the weight and density of the liquid.</term>. If the water is used daily, it maintains health. It should be administered in wine or Malmsey <note>A sweet, fortified Greek wine.</note>, and it is said that all the virtues of **potable gold** are within it. It is for the **falling sickness** <note>Epilepsy.</note>, making the sufferer healthy in a short time simply by washing with it. Through practice and use, you will find many virtues in it; mixed with rosewater, it becomes a confection that one may eat with meat instead of salt.

### The Oil, Very Good for Medicine.

<margin>still-head</margin>
Take the old oil and pour it over the **residues** <term>Feces</term> after the water has been drawn off by the **still-head** <term>alembicum: The cap of a distilling apparatus that collects and cools vapors.</term>. The oil that is made afterward is very good for the **falling sickness** <term>Caducum: Another term for epilepsy.</term>, fistulas, and other foul holes and sores. It has a sharp and powerful effect. However, if it were poured over the black **residues** from which the **strong water** <term>Aquafort: A corrosive acid, usually nitric acid.</term> or **secret water** was drawn, it would not be as powerful or as healing. It is still good, to be sure, but only for cases where a great effect is not required. The reason is this: the "best" residues still retain their **spirits** <term>Spiritus: Volatile essences believed to hold the medicinal power of a substance.</term> within them, which are afterward mixed with the oil, whereas the other residues have been robbed of these **spirits** and **souls** <term>Animæ: The vital or fixed essence of a substance in alchemy.</term>.

# On Philosophical Vitriol.

How one recognizes that this "heavenly water" is fixed with its salt is to be noted thus: When no spirit appears at the end of the distillation, then calcinate it in a vessel for 6 hours; then dissolve it entirely in its water that was distilled through the alembic <note>A "helm" or cap used in distillation to collect vapors.</note>, as has often been said, so that it becomes clear and pure throughout. Now, when the dissolution has occurred and it has been brought into a clear matter, then add as much rectified water by weight as there was of the <term>Vitriol</term> <note>Represented by a square symbol with an X; a sulfate mineral used as a primary alchemical material.</note>. Put it in a glass with another glass placed over it and sealed with lute <note>An airtight alchemical clay or sealant.</note> so that it does not evaporate. Set it in ashes with a gentle fire, and you will see a water shimmering like swarming ants. Let it stand, and the "Earth" <note>The solid residue or mineral base.</note> will gradually coagulate at the bottom <note>original: "in fundo"</note>; this occurs in about fifteen days. Keep it constantly in a gentle fire until the Earth resolves into a clear water in the color of the Sun <note>original: "Solis"; referring to a golden-yellow color.</note>. After this sign appears, set on the alembic and distill the water with a mild fire until the matter is quite dry, etc.

Its **Projection** <note>The process of "throwing" the alchemical powder onto a molten metal to transmute it.</note> is thus: Melt fine silver and throw some of this powder upon it, and you will have permanent gold that survives all tests. If you wish to go higher, do as you did above many times, and you shall have a perfect medicine.

### How one should multiply it.

Dissolve the medicine in water as you did above; add its rectified water to it and keep it in constant heat, as before, until the Earth is congealed. Pour [the water] off, dissolve it by itself <note>original: "per se"</note>, and it should appear in the color of the Sun. When the sign shows itself, then distill and coagulate it as has been said; thus proceed with the multiplication infinitely <note>original: "in infinitum"</note>.

Likewise, when the **secret water** <note>original: "Aqua secreta"</note> has stood for a long time in the decoction of the long-necked glass, as mentioned above, the Master believes that it dissolves into Gold <note>original: "Aurum"</note> and is very good for the human body.

My friend <note>original: "Amicus meus"</note> has seen a projection of the mentioned Stone <note>original: "Lapidis"</note> upon molten Silver <note>original: "Lunam"; the alchemical "Moon."</note>, as has been said, and saw that it turned into pure gold.

### To make Mercury out of Gold.

First, make an **aqua fortis** <term>aqua fortis</term> <note>literally "strong water"; nitric acid used for dissolving metals</note> from two parts **vitriol** <note>metallic sulfates, typically iron or copper</note> / one part **saltpeter** <note>potassium nitrate</note> / one-fourth part **cinnabar** <note>mercury sulfide</note> / one-eighth part **sal ammoniac** <note>ammonium chloride</note> / and dissolve the **gold** <note>original: "Solem"</note> / and it should be washed in all respects as the silver was before / and afterwards **putrefy** <note>to break down through rot or fermentation</note> and "kill" it with **alkaline salt** <note>original: "Sal Alkali"</note> / sal ammoniac / **salt of tartar** <note>original: "Saltamane"; likely a corruption of Sal Tartari</note> and **salt of urine** <note>original: "Sal Urinæ"</note> together with the silver / with distillation and all the labor.

### Rectified Oil of Mercury.

Mar."; a gentle water bath</note> or a **dew-bath** <note>original: "Roris"; Balneum Roris</note>, or **horse dung** <note>original: "fimum equinum"; often used as a natural source of steady fermentation heat</note> / so that it putrefies well / and becomes a thick water / from which the mercury remains at the bottom / just like an oil / that should be allowed to dry / and pour [the water] back onto it / and putrefy / and distill as before / so the mercury becomes accustomed to **solution** <note>the state of being dissolved</note> / and afterwards dissolves by itself / on a stone in the cellar or in a bath into oil / and becomes a thick **Oil of Mercury**.

**Simple Mercurial Water** <note>original: "Simplex Aqua Mercurialis"</note> is made from mercury that has not been sublimated / and in many ways / yet you have those that are prescribed above / take those before you and make them according to what they are.

# OIL OF VITRIOL
<margin>This is in Roger Bacon's treatise.</margin>

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'V' with floral and scrollwork patterns.</image-desc>
Vitriol <note>a naturally occurring sulfate mineral, often appearing as green or blue crystals</note> is a noble mineral, held in great dignity and esteem by the true philosophers—and indeed not without reason: for the Almighty and Greatest GOD has exalted it far above His other mineral creations and creatures.

And although many of the observers have noticed something from the true philosophers, they have ultimately not been able to reach the correct understanding of the philosophical cause of such secrets. It has also been the custom and habit among the ancients, as Isaac <note>likely referring to the alchemist Isaac Hollandus</note> says, that they recorded and made their secrets understood either in obscured riddles, stories, fables, or images, or else composed them in hidden philosophical sayings, sentences, and rhymes, as they have also done and said regarding Vitriol, etc.

> ->Visit the interior of the Earth; by rectifying, you will find the hidden Stone, the true medicine.<-
<note>original Latin: "Visitetis interiora Terrae, rectificando, invenietis occultum Lapidem veram medicinam." This famous sentence forms the acronym V.I.T.R.I.O.L.</note>

To understand this thus, the words themselves indeed indicate correctly, which we thus explain or interpret: Since the ancients say that one should visit the Earth by **rectifying** <term>rectification</term> <note>the process of purifying a liquid by repeated distillation</note>, "rectifying" is not to be understood as the poor, common earth of any of the mountains of vitriol.

<margin>Vitriol is green on the outside. <br/> Vitriol is red on the inside.</margin>
Furthermore, they say that the inner parts of the Earth should be visited and not the outer. Thus, vitriol is green in color on the outside, as can be seen with the eyes, but the philosophers find it red on the inside. The tongues find it or taste it from the outside as sharp and harsh, yet it is sweet and lovely on the inside. The hands touch it from the outside as hard and coarse, yet it is delicate and lovely on the inside, and is truly a subtle, noble juice, balsam, and pure oil. The noses perceive its smell as quite wild and misshapen, like sulfur, yet in its interior it is nobler and more lovely than **ambergris** <note>a rare, sweet-smelling substance used in perfumes</note> or a balsam, and is tasted as such.

Although many philosophers have perhaps dreamed, or from other indications—

However, they did not wish to understand that neither through **distillation** nor **calcination** <note>the process of heating a substance to a high temperature to reduce it to powder</note>, as they were accustomed to doing, could anything useful be brought forth—though some achieved more than others. <margin>green Oil.</margin>
as soon as it loses its green color, its oil, spirit, and the secret of all philosophers is already lost. For you should know that in all creatures—whether **vegetables** <note>original: "Vegetabilia"</note> or other minerals as they are, and also the metals—they are red in their true **essence** <term>Arcanitet</term> <note>from "Arcanum," meaning the most secret, concentrated medicinal or spiritual core of a substance</note> and in their primary state. Such **secrets** <note>original: "Arcana"</note> and praised oils should be taken from them while raw and red as blood. Therefore, there is a great error in the distillations of common apothecaries and physicians, for they have not allowed nature enough room, nor have they helped her so that she could bring her essences in the plants to such a blood-red oil.

Indeed, nature herself gives us to understand that she is capable and ready—if only she is helped—to transform herself in a short time into her own red juice and secret oil. This can be seen in the common distillation of plants, such as in **Pennyroyal** <note>original: "Pulegi"</note> and **Rue** <note>original: "Rhute"</note> and others; how from year to year they become what they are through their own **rectification** <term>rectification</term> <note>the process of refining and purifying a substance through repeated distillation or aging</note>. Thus, eventually, if they were to be preserved for several seasons, they would transform and **transmute** themselves into a blood-red oil and juice. But the reason this happens and proceeds so slowly is that the unlearned preparers, during distillation, take away the greenness too harshly and quickly, not allowing nature enough room or protecting her until the noble color transforms itself.

One sees the same thing in ripe, well-timed wines: when they age, are drawn off, and kept for a year, how they **rectify** and clarify themselves, and from day to day work and strive toward their natural colors. Nature does this in her own time and according to her own properties.

However, a **destruction, corruption, and putrefaction** <term>Putrefactio</term> <note>the alchemical stage of "blackness" where a substance breaks down or rots before it can be reborn in a higher form</note> must first occur in certain natures; and if these are successfully completed by nature, she proceeds to her rightful goal, which was given to her by GOD.

Take this as an example: if you place rain or other simple water into a beautiful glass or a well-sealed jar, set it in the air, and let it stand for a time, you will see how the elements in nature begin to **rectify** the plain, simple water. For in a few days, it will become cloudy and stinking, and will cast its **dregs** <note>original: "Feces," referring to the solid impurities or sediment</note> and coarse, earthly, and corruptible uncleanness to the

### Of Philosophical Vitriol.

But I adjure all of you by the eternal God, into whose hands this my secret shall come, that you reveal it to no one, unless you know him to be a son of philosophy, and one in whom the spirit—to obey God in heaven—flees all vice, and alone diligently pursues and devotes itself to virtue and honor. ## Beginning of the Work.

<margin>Reisig. 51. @.</margin>
First, you should know why the **putrefaction** <term>Putrefaction</term> <note>the process of alchemical "rotting" or fermentation intended to break a substance down to its base essence</note> of vitriol is undertaken, and it happens for this reason:

<margin>"</margin>
You will find no vitriol that is a true vitriol in itself, for vitriol in itself is a pure sweetness, which in its power is seldom surpassed by any sweetness in the world.

<margin>Güst.</margin>
But in this way, other types of minerals—alums and salts <note>original: "Salien"</note>—are mixed into the vitriol in the veins of the earth. From these it gains its acidity and sharpness, as is seen when it is distilled purely into its **spirit** <term>Spirit</term> <note>the volatile, airborne essence of a substance</note>, and the sharpened oil which finally reveals itself with its redness.

<margin>Spirit Oil of good flow with the drop. Gisarb:</margin>
You should not think that this is the **spirit of vitriol** <note>original: "Spiritus Vitrioli"</note>, but rather the spirit of the other mixed minerals which lie hidden beneath the colors of the vitriol. And the oil which the strength of the fire brings forth is also not the **oil of vitriol** <note>original: "Oleum Vitrioli"</note>, but a salt-spirit <note>original: "Saltzgeist"</note> from the mixed union of the salts within the vitriol.

<margin>"</margin>
For in the whole substance and nature of vitriol, no acidity nor sharpness is felt or perceived, only a very lovely, sweet, pure, and noble scent.
<margin>sweet</margin>
It is indeed true that one vitriol is always found to be purer than another, and that one contains different types <note>original: "genera"</note> of minerals than the other. Then you shall have the treasure and riches of this world; forget not the praise and blessing of God, and praise His name.

...if they are rough and impure, it brings the master-worker <note>original: "Werckmeister"; the practicing alchemist</note> great harm, for the reason that the Medicine <term>Medicine</term> <note>original: "Medicin"; another name for the Philosopher's Stone or the Tincture in its final, active state</note> remains partially stuck in the impure slag and does not touch the pure part of the metal.

Therefore, I think it right to provide a small instruction at this point, so that one does not bring the noble Medicine to nothing and uselessly pour it away with the slag. For you should know that all bodies of the imperfect metals are so impure that some hardly retain a third part, such as Antimony <term>♁</term>, some a half part, such as Copper <term>♀</term>, and some a third part, such as Lead <term>♄</term> and Tin <term>♃</term>; the rest is nothing but a foam and slag, which the Medicine casts out from the metals and separates from them.

Some have indeed claimed—though falsely and from a fictional basis—that one could tinge <term>Tinge</term> <note>original: "tingieren"; the act of changing the color and nature of a metal, usually from base to noble</note> the metals through the oils and waters of the metals, or the tinctures, so that they remain entirely whole. Some then add more and say they also remain malleable; just as I was once approached by a liar who said he had a silver Groschen <note>A common silver coin of the era</note> that was entirely transmuted into pure and malleable gold without any injury to its body. But when I told him that it could not possibly be true, as it was against Nature and her essence, he scoffed at me. However, when it came to the proof, it all amounted to nothing.

Therefore, you faithful seekers of this mystery should know that when the Medicine of the oils is spread upon an imperfect corpse <note>original: "unvollkommen Leichnam"; refers to a base metal like lead or tin</note>, the metal breaks and falls apart entirely like clay; for the Medicine penetrates all the members, and none remains unbroken. Then one must let that same earth melt together into a solid body in a crucible, and that which is under the slag will be its gold, malleable and noble.

If you wish to perform Projection upon Silver <term>☽</term>, it should first be cemented five or six times with the Rebohoth <term>Rebohoth</term> <note>An alchemical term, likely referring to a specific refining salt or a "broad place" of purification (from the Hebrew 'Rehovot')</note>, and then melted back together into a solid body. For if the Medicine were cast upon it while it is so rough, I tell you truly, you would suffer loss, and much of the noble Medicine would be kept and lost within the filthy slag.

On Tin <term>♃</term> it is better than on Iron <term>♂</term>, and on Copper <term>♀</term> even better than on Lead <term>♄</term>, as we...

...happened to us / because of the mighty great fire / so that we had to take a new vessel. Therefore, know / that the fire with which one reverberates <note>Refers to a "reverberatory" furnace where the flame is reflected or "reverberated" off the roof onto the material</note> must be tempered in a proper way / so that it must be equal to the glass-maker's fire. Since, however, this thing, according to our thought and understanding / has less annoyance and danger about it / so that no filth or other thing falls into the vessel / it is my advice / that you take a subtle linen cloth / and let that which you have distilled pass through it / and do not dry it out / thus there will remain in the cloth a perishable or destructible earth / which you should throw away / and once again through a new subtle and delicate linen cloth / let the previous liquid <term>Liquorem</term> <note>original Latin: "Liquorem"</note> run through as before / and continue this until no more filth remains in the cloth. When you now see the sign / you shall put that same liquid <term>Liquor</term> or juice back into the urinal-flask / securing it with its helm [the alembic head] and receivers <term>Recipienten</term> / so that it coagulates <term>coagulier</term> / as mentioned above / and after it has coagulated <term>coaguliert</term> / dissolve <term>soluieren</term> it again / and let it run through the cloth again / as before. Then you will see a new earth in the cloth / put it away / and this work shall be often repeated / until by God's help no more earth remains behind / or is left behind / but stays white and glittering / clean and well-polished and shining / as it was from the beginning. But you can also have another sign / which is more certain / of the purification of this matter <term>Matery</term> / or visibility / for after you have completed the distillation <term>Distillation</term> / and the entire moisture or wateriness is gone / the precious salt <term>Saltz</term> will remain in the vessel / over the fire / in the form of an oil / which / when it is taken away from the fire / is instantly coagulated <term>coaguliert</term>. You, most beloved son, do not let yourself be made weary / by the long time spent in dissolving <term>soluieren</term> / because this matter <term>Matery</term> often coagulates <term>coaguliert</term> / and every time the impurity that remains in the cloth / should be removed from it / which / if they remain behind / it will never be able to come together / with its spirit <term>Spiritu</term> <note>original Latin: "Spiritu"; the volatile essence or vaporous part of the substance</note>, which [has been drawn] out—

You shall test this with the following sign: take a little of the black body and lay it upon a glowing-hot plate; if you see that no smoke rises from it and it is not driven away by the fire, then it is finished. 

Take this same earth and place it in small glazed bowls or in glass vessels with the mouth well-sealed. Place it in the fire where it may be **reverberated** <term>reuerberiert</term> <note>subjected to intense, indirect heat where flames beat back onto the vessel</note> for 24 hours. Thereafter, remove the **calcined earth** <term>calcinierte Terra</term> <note>matter reduced to a dry powder through high heat</note> and keep it in warm ashes, well-sealed, so that it may draw no more moisture to itself. 

Furthermore, weigh the **animated water** <note>original: *Aqua animatum*</note>—that is, the soul-imbued water—and **rectify** <note>purify by redistilling</note> it seven times through the ashes. You shall then divide this rectified, animated liquid into two parts: use one part to make the earth "living" again, and the other part to **dissolve** <note>original: *soluieren*</note> gold and silver. For this purpose, take the second part of the water and see how much of the reserved earth you have by weight. Grind the earth first and place it in the urinal; then pour onto it a fourth part of the aforementioned water relative to its weight. Seal it well and place it in the **water bath** <term>Balneum</term>, but ensure the water of the bath does not touch the vessel, so that the matter is warmed by the steam alone. Let it stand thus for four consecutive days. When these have passed, remove the lid, set the alembic upon it, and distill it through the ashes. A tasteless moisture will flow out; throw this away. After this, **imbibe** <note>soak or saturate</note> it again with a fourth part of the **animal spirit** <term>Spiritu animali</term> <note>the "soul-spirit" or refined essence extracted earlier</note> as described above; digest it again as before and distill the moisture off through the ashes, as above.

Afterward, place it in the ashes, attach another receiver vessel <note>original: "Recipienten"</note> to it, and give it a stronger fire; in this way, it distills over through the "air of the fire" <note>likely referring to dry distillation or the use of hot air/vapor</note>.

But understand this: distill each one separately. When this is accomplished, pour a fresh solvent <note>original: "menstrum"</note> onto it again. Keep the "fire" that you have distilled through the air, each well-sealed in its own receiver. Close the glass vessels <note>original: "Urinal"</note> containing each "body" <note>the gold and silver</note> individually once more and set them to putrefy as described above. Strengthen the fire and drive it so long until both "bodies"—of the gold and of the silver—pass over through the distillation head <note>original: "Alembick"</note> specifically through the "revolutions of the air" <note>original: "Reuolutiones Aeris"; a term for the cycle of evaporation and condensation</note>. Even if the entire body does not pass through completely during distillation, the part remaining behind will be small, which you should save for other experiments.

Next, take the "Animated Spirit" <note>original: "Spiritum Animatum"; a potentized alchemical solvent</note> and rectify <note>purify by redistilling</note> it by itself seven times through the ash bath. By no means should you throw away any of its "earth" <note>the solid residue</note> which will always remain behind at the bottom when you reduce it; instead, always pour the rectified water back over its remaining earth. Repeat this until the seventh time. Use this same order with the "Lunar Water" <note>original: "aqua Lunari"; a preparation of silver</note> when you rectify it. After this, take these two waters and mix them together. This joining is called a "Conjunction of the Father and the Mother" <note>original: "Coniuration des Vatters und der Muter"</note>—of the Masculine with the Feminine, of the Man with the Woman. Thus you will have the "greater solvent" <note>original: "menstrum"</note>: the "animated" and the "vegetable" <note>plant-based</note> spirits joined together as one. After these three pieces have been rectified and brought into a single substance, place them in a well-sealed vessel so that no steam can escape from it...

### Experience of the 28th Experiment.

Take silver and dissolve it into water, just as we did in the previous experiment with the aforementioned water. Afterward, separate the water again from the silver by means of the water bath <note>original: "Balneum"; a vessel of hot water used for gentle, even heating</note>. Then, add to it as much of the destructive salt of human urine <note>likely ammonium chloride or "sal ammoniac," prized for its ability to dissolve metals</note> as is needed to dissolve the entire body <note>original: "Corpus"; refers to the solid metallic substance</note>. Once it is dissolved, you should set it to putrefy for 8 days. After this, distill it through the ashes <note>a sand or ash bath for higher heat than a water bath</note>, and finally strengthen the fire to sublimate <note>the process where a solid turns into vapor and hardens again at the top of the vessel</note>; thus a little will be sublimated, which you should add to that which passed through the helm <note>original: "Helm"; the top part of a still, also called an alembic</note>.

Then pour the mentioned water back onto it, which will dissolve and take on a green or sky-blue color. Distill it as described above, and you should carry this out seven times, always pouring the water back over the "earths" <note>original: "Erden"; the solid residue left at the bottom of the vessel</note> and distilling it again, strengthening the fire at the end of every distillation. After the completion of the final distillation, keep that which has passed over, and weigh the earth to see how heavy it is.

Then take the best tin and an equal amount of good cupel-silver; melt these two bodies together. Take one ounce of these mixed metals and three ounces of well-purified mercury; amalgamate them together. To this, add one ounce of the aforementioned earth, and give it its "blackness"—that is, the water that you distilled 7 times through the helm, as mentioned above. Once this is done, take care that in a single soaking <note>original: "eyntrenckung" or imbibition; the slow addition of liquid to a dry solid</note> for three parts of the mentioned amalgam, you add no more than one part of the water.

After the soaking, close the vessel with its lid and place it in the ashes for 12 hours. When the time has passed, remove the lid, place the helm upon it, and first draw off the moisture. Sublimate it over the fire, then crush again whatever was sublimated from the material remaining at the bottom and put it back into its vessel. Soak it again as before, then digest it in the ashes, and finally distill it so that the moisture drips out as before, and sublimate it also with a strong fire. You should continue this until it has "drunk up" all the water you have given it. Then you will find at the bottom of the vessel a fixed material, flowing and tingeing <note>original: "tingierend"; the power of an alchemical substance to project its quality (like color or purity) onto another metal</note>. Of this, you should take one part for every 50 parts of mercury derived from tin, and you will then have the most perfect silver.

When this putrefaction is over, take the **dissolution** and put each into its own **flask** <note>original: "Urinal," a glass vessel shaped like a uroscopy bottle</note>, and attach the **receiver** <note>original: "Recipienten," the vessel that catches the distilled liquid</note> to it, well-sealed. Distill a water down through the **water-bath** <note>original: "Balneum"</note>; then the bodies will remain behind and look like poured-out honey or oil. Over these, pour again of their own water that was distilled through the water-bath, enough so that it stands three fingers deep over it. Close both vessels with their lids and set them in putrefaction for a whole day. Afterward, open the vessels from below and distill them through the **alembic head** <note>original: "Helm"</note> in the ashes. 

Finally, strengthen the fire so that the **soul** <note>the volatile essence</note> or the **airy element** passes over into both of their distilled waters. Then, and only then, should you make the fire strongest of all, so that the **fiery element** also passes over into the **airy one**. But the composition requires neither necessity nor fire; when this dissolution has occurred, let the vessels cool and take away the receivers, which you should keep well-sealed. Put a special label or inscription on each one so that you do not make a mistake when it becomes necessary to perform this. 

Over the **earth** <note>original: "Terra," the solid residue</note>, however, pour again as above of its distilled water, purified and separated through the water-bath. When you have bound the lid on it, putrefy it as above. After this, distill it through the ashes as before, with its attached receivers in which you have kept the **souls** of these bodies. In this order, you shall proceed until the earth is examined and robbed of its original or natural moisture; then take that same earth and crush it well, put it together into a glass vessel, and keep it in warm ashes until you are ready to make something from them.

Furthermore, take the **animated spirit** <note>original: "Spiritum Animatum"</note> of the **Moon** <note>Silver</note> and **rectify** <term>rectify: To purify a liquid by distilling it repeatedly.</term> it through the ashes. Afterward, take the **animated spirit of the Sun** <note>Gold; original: "Solis"</note> and rectify it in the same way seven times through the ashes. You should keep the slime, however, which the **golden spirit** will produce in each rectification, so that the element of fire is well-guarded. When the rectifications are all completed, then take the animated spirit of the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> and also the companion spirit of the **Silver**, and put them together. Afterward, set them to **circulate** <note>a process of continuous distillation and condensation in a sealed vessel</note> in a large vessel, such as the one in which we circulated the **single-layered solvent** <note>original: "einschichtig menstrum"</note>.

[...necessary] part of the Medicine and copies of the Experiments / as well as the laws and everything else / that belongs to this Art / have been given. And this highest / and last of the Experiments I command to each of you above all other Experiments / that the Angel of the Lord may guide your hearts / to hide these secret things / and matters of Nature / you shall primarily dedicate the same to the Holy Church / to serve her with it / and to be helpful to the poor. You shall also, in this matter, take care above all things / that the Devil does not lead you aside from the right path of your promise / for he goes about us / like a roaring lion <note>A reference to 1 Peter 5:8, often used in alchemical texts to warn of the spiritual dangers of greed.</note> / and for that reason be as wise as serpents <note>A reference to Matthew 10:16, advising the alchemist to be cautious and secretive.</note> / so that this tempter does not lead you into the wrong way / for then it will come to pass / that Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, will always sustain / and protect us / in whose name this present little book shall be concluded with a blessed end / in the Year of the Lord 1330.

[...most] carefully considered / therefore I have wished to withhold or hide nothing / of what good and true things I have ever been able to find and bring about through true thoughts from the best and most proven *authors* after much suffered and vain labor in *sophistic recipes* <note>original: "Sophisticis Receptis"; refers to fraudulent or deceptive alchemical formulas that look plausible but fail in practice</note> / such as *Geber* in *his Summa* <note>original: "Geber in sua Summa"; refers to the "Summa Perfectionis Magisterii," a foundational 13th-century alchemical text attributed to Geber (Jabir ibn Hayyan)</note> / and others. [...like those who write only in] Greek / **Abohali** <note>Abohali: likely referring to Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Sina, known in the West as Avicenna</note>, **Geber** <note>Geber: the Latinized name of Jabir ibn Hayyan, the 8th-century "father of chemistry"</note>, and **Avicenna** in Arabic; **Morienes** <note>Morienes: a legendary 7th-century hermit and alchemist said to have taught the Umayyad prince Khalid ibn Yazid</note> and **Raymond** <note>original: "Raymundus"; refers to Raymond Lull (c. 1232–1316), a Majorcan philosopher and polymath to whom many alchemical works were attributed</note>, and many others like them in **Latin** / so that everyone might understand / that God has gifted all languages at once / and none need complain that one is favored over the other. That I call it such a divine and glorious thing / happens solely because / no one can come to such an Art or understand it through their own knowledge or intellect / however learned and experienced a **philosopher** <note>In alchemical texts, "Philosopher" specifically refers to a master of the Hermetic Art (alchemy)</note> he may be. As **Geber** the **philosopher** [speaks] against all those / who [try] to complete such a work from natural observation alone / in a speech where he says: The majority err in this / that they think / they must follow Nature in everything / whereas such a thing is impossible for the Art; therefore let all despisers of this my little book abstain [from it] / for I have composed it not for them / but for the **Sons of Doctrine** <note>original: "Filijs doctrinæ"; a traditional term for the chosen students or initiates of the alchemical secrets</note>, and lovers of the Art; I also wish herewith to have most friendly admonished and asked everyone / before the work / to diligently weigh and examine everything within themselves / and to see all convolutions as nothing other than pure harmony / [conveyed] with riddles / and that is the only way / to recognize the wisdom of this Art / <margin><unclear>Rhazes</unclear></margin> especially as **Rhazes** <note>original: "Raſis"; refers to Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Razi (865–925), a Persian polymath and influential alchemist</note> [says]: He who is sluggish and lazy in the reading of books / shall not be swift in the preparation of **matters** <note>original: "Materien"; the physical substances used in alchemical operations</note> / because one book explains the other / and whatever is lacking in one / will be found in another / for it would otherwise be impossible / because God has so ordained it / to find everything that properly belongs to this Art from books alone; I also wish to have especially admonished and asked everyone / who through this my little book / receives this precious treasure / not to misuse it / and to be mindful of the state of the poor / so that he is not first punished for it in the next world / [but] to give thanks to God the Almighty for such and similar gifts and presents / to Him be praise / blessing / honor / and glory / into all eternity.

# Of the Natural Philosophy of Metals.

# The first part, in which is treated by what means and way he came to the true knowledge of this Art.

**Hermes Trismegistus** <note>Hermes Trismegistus: the "Thrice-Great," a legendary Hellenistic figure regarded as the founder of alchemy</note> is rightly called the first prophet and father, indeed the first founder of this Stone; after he truly knew and experienced this Art, he left it behind in writing. He held it so high and dear that only the fear of the Last Day compelled him to describe it. This was the opinion held by all those who followed him in this regard. Hence it happens that their books, as many as there are, appear so contradictory to the readers. As King **Geber** <note>Geber: the Latinized name of Jabir ibn Hayyan, the 8th-century "father of chemistry"</note> speaks in his **Summa** <note>Summa: referring to the *Summa perfectionis magisterii*, a highly influential alchemical text</note>, [they were written] for the edification of the ignorant and the Children of Wisdom, who nonetheless initially cannot refrain from erring, so that after diligent effort and much applied labor of both mind and body, they might know all the better how to value and conceal it.

It is also mostly hidden for this reason (not to mention the labor involved here) unless great expense were involved, among those alone who hope for such things from books or through Divine inspiration. When I was about twenty years old and had been instructed at home in the basics of grammar through my father's providence, and had now been promoted to the higher arts—in which I progressed so much over about three years through the diligence of my special **tutor** <note>original: "Præceptoris"</note>—that my guardian (since both my parents had now passed away) thought it good to send me to study **jurisprudence** <note>original: "Iurisprudentiam"; the study of law</note> with the aforementioned tutor. But during these things, and before I departed from the College of Arts, I had made friends and associations with many of my schoolmates, some of whom had various **chemical books** <note>original: "Chimische Bücher"</note>, which I received from them and transcribed with the greatest diligence. Yet this was done through the means of my aforementioned tutor, who had already begun to experiment and work in this art long before, so that before I moved away, I had acquired a considerable number of these books and **recipes** <note>original: "Recepta"</note>.

As soon as I had come with my tutor to where I was to apply myself to jurisprudence, I began to read through the aforementioned recipes. Among them were several **projections** <note>term: projections; the act of casting an alchemical substance onto a base metal to transform it into gold or silver</note> that taught [transforming] one part onto ten parts, another onto 20, 30, etc. For the "red" <note>the *Rubedo*, or final stage of the alchemical work to produce gold</note>, [they taught] onto eighteen or twenty parts into the best Crown or Ducat gold, indeed as high as it is and can be possible. One was supposed to be able to be made fluid, another to withstand the test of the [touch]stone, another all tests. For the "white" <note>the *Albedo*, or the stage of the work that produces silver</note>, one should yield ten **denarii** <note>original: "Denarios"; a unit of silver weight or currency</note>, another 11; one should be stable in the fire, another withstand the mark of the stone. ...thought that nothing greater or more blissful in this whole world could happen to me. Especially because I saw that such recipes had such grand titles, one from the King of **Navarre**, another from the **Cardinal of Lorraine**, and others of that kind; so that people might be moved by such titles to have all the greater faith in them, which—along with the others—long led me by the nose <note>literal: "Narrenseil," the fool's rope; a German idiom for being deceived or led astray</note>.
