# Now follow the Fixations of Silver by itself, and also with the addition of gold and part with part, along with other beautiful, magnificent processes, including the Yellow Needle. <note>original: "Fixationes Lunae... pars cum parte... gelbe Nadel." In alchemy, "Luna" refers to silver. "Part with part" usually refers to an equal ratio of silver and gold.</note>

### And first, a Yellow Needle or Fixed Silver with the extraction of Copper and Antimony mentioned at the beginning, which passes all tests, as follows. <note>original: "♀ und ♁"; the symbols for Copper (Venus) and Antimony (Stibium).</note>

Also, take seven <term>Loth</term> <note>A German unit of weight, approximately 15 grams.</note> of raw <term>Antimony</term> and six Loth of <term>Copper</term>; with these, make a fusion in a crucible; upon it, place cast salt, one finger thick; let it heat strongly in the <term>wind furnace</term> <note>A furnace designed to create a natural draft for higher temperatures.</note> and place glowing coals upon it; let it flow strongly; pour it out to a <term>Regulus</term> <note>original: "König" (King); the metallic button that settles at the bottom of a crucible during smelting.</note>; take this, and half as much white calcined <term>Tartar</term> <note>original: "🜔"; a salt used as a flux to help metals melt and separate from impurities.</note>; rub these pieces small together; put them back into the crucible; let them flow strongly, and again place glowing coals upon it, so that the Regulus settles at the bottom; take it again, and once more take half as much calcined Tartar; rub it together; put it back into the crucible; let it flow strongly again; pour as before. Do this for a third time, so that the Regulus is well "opened up" <note>An alchemical term meaning the metal has been made receptive to further transformation.</note>; take it and weigh it; if it is 6 Loth, then add to it half a Loth of calcined Tartar; grind it together with the Regulus into a powder, and put it into a round glass that is not too tall; pour a strong <term>distilled wine</term> <note>original: "brennten Wein"; high-proof alcohol or aqua vitae.</note> that is without water upon it, so that it covers it by two fingers; <term>lute</term> it <note>Seal the vessel with a clay-like paste to make it airtight.</note>; set it in warm sand; let it rise and descend for 22 hours, not too hot; then pour fresh wine upon it; let it work thus for 21 hours; do this according to its number until the Regulus no longer smokes and flows like wax; then it is ready.

Of this, take half a Loth; let 2 Loth of purified silver (purified with <term>white sulfur</term> <note>original: "Sulphure albo."</note>) flow with it, and add it while in flux; let it sit for three-quarters of an hour, so the moisture draws the silver to itself; take that away and add a fresh portion; let it stand for half a day so it draws the moisture entirely away; save the fixed substance; take it and put distilled wine upon it, so it draws out the impurity and leaves the fixed substance behind; this can be used again; now take half a Loth of the fixed Regulus and the silver; let these 2 Loth flow strongly together in a crucible for 1 hour; in the last quarter-hour, take and add the <term>Confirmation</term> <note>A final reagent used to stabilize or "confirm" the transformation.</note> the size of a pea; pour it out, and you have the **Yellow Needle**, perfect, as mentioned above.

Nothing more is needed than confirmation <note>stabilization</note>, and this confirmation achieves the highest result; gold <note>original: "Solem", the Sun symbol.</note> appears in the <term>yellowing</term> immediately after the <term>refining</term> <note>original: "Abtrieb"; the process of cupellation, where precious metals are separated from lead in a furnace.</note>. There is no defect in this, as I have described in other places.

## A Proven Recipe for Gold Ore.

Take <term>marcasite</term>, a good <term>gold-ore</term> <note>original: "Goldkiß"; likely iron or copper pyrites containing traces of gold.</note> that passes the test wherever you wish. Do this until you have entirely drawn the fumes of the aqua fortis out of the sulfur. Then the sulfur becomes sweet and mild, and is in the form of saffron; it is also nobler and better than gold, for this sulfur is identical to the tincture that is extracted from gold, and it is called the <term>invisible sulfur</term>. Thus you have truly converted the silver into good gold, stable in all tests.

## Tincture for Weak Gold.

Take Oil of Eggs <note>original: "Oleum Ouorum"; a fatty oil traditionally extracted from hard-boiled egg yolks, used as a solvent or base</note> as much as you wish, and calcined <term>antimony</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍</note>, equal parts by weight. Mix them together until the mixture becomes hard. Put this into a flask and place it in horse manure <note>original: "fimum Equinum"; used by alchemists as a source of gentle, steady heat through natural fermentation</note>, so that it dissolves into water. Then distill it through an alembic <note>A distillation apparatus with a cooling head</note>, and whatever distills over, pour it back in. Distill it again; do this four times. Then you have a noble Red Oil <note>original: "Oleum Rubeum"</note> that tints weak gold. You should make the gold red-hot and quench it in this oil; then you will have gold of 24 degrees <note>24 carats, or pure gold</note>.

## A Tinting Stone that Permanently Tints Copper White.

Also, take mercury, sublimate it gently, and make a water from it. Distill this four times. With this water, you should mix calx of silver <note>original: "Silberkalch"; silver reduced to a fine powder or oxide</note> and sublimated <term>antimony</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍</note>. Reduce it all into a liquid, then distill and coagulate it. It will become a transparent stone, like crystal. Cast one <term>loth</term> <note>A traditional unit of weight, roughly 15 grams</note> of this upon 19 loth of purified copper; then you have a perfect white <note>meaning the copper has been transmuted into a silver-like metal</note>.

However, if you let 2 parts of the aforementioned stone flow upon 1 part of silver, the <term>silver</term> <note>original: "Luna"</note> will become brittle. Then cast one part of that brittle metal upon 30 parts of purified copper; it will turn out to your liking. Note that the antimony, the mercury water, and the silver calx should all be in equal parts.

## How to Make the Mercury Water:

Take three parts of mercury that has been sublimated seven times and one part of sal ammoniac <note>original: "Salmiar"; ammonium chloride</note> rubbed together. Put them in a glass and place it in a sand bath <note>original: "Sandcapellen"; a container of sand used to provide indirect, even heat</note> over gentle heat. It will become a hard lump. Let it rot <note>original: "putrificier"; a stage of chemical digestion or fermentation</note>, and lay it on a stone in a cellar; there it will dissolve into a water. Take three parts of this water and one part of silver calx; coagulate it in a glass and then dissolve it again. Do this three times. From this, a tincture is made: one part cast upon sixteen parts of purified mercury <note>original: "Mercurij purgati"</note> coagulates it into silver—or one part cast upon 16 parts of copper also turns it to silver.

If you wish to perform the tinting, cast one part of this upon three parts of molten silver; the silver will become brittle. Take one part of that and cast it upon 32 parts of purified copper; it will become good silver. But if you add calx of gold <note>original: "Calcem solis"; gold reduced to a powder</note> to the mercury water, and it is dissolved and coagulated three times within it, then let it flow—

### My Art Bestowed by God with Greater Profit.

Take five pounds of lead <note>original: "Saturnum"; named after the planet Saturn associated with lead</note> and let it drive the lead <note>original symbol: ♄</note> upon the cupel <term>test</term> <note>A shallow, porous vessel used in assaying to separate precious metals from base metals like lead</note> (from which it can be almost completely drawn off). Place into it one pound of copper <note>original: "Kupffer"</note> burnt with sulfur <note>original: "Sulphur"</note>. While it is driving on the cupel, one should constantly throw a little gold <note>original symbol: ☉</note> and sulfur upon it—equal parts of each, crushed together. When it has been entirely "swallowed" into the cupel—which happens in about four hours—then let the cupel cool and crush it completely. This takes about 8 hours. When it is crushed, mix in by eye twice as much common salt and a little charcoal, the size of hazelnuts. Put it into a flask <note>original: "Kolben"</note> and let it melt in a wind furnace <note>A furnace designed to create a natural or forced draft for high temperatures</note> so that the litharge <note>original: "Glette"; lead oxide</note> and copper <note>original symbol: ♀</note> become a malleable <term>regulus</term> <note>original: "König"; the metallic button found at the bottom of a crucible after smelting</note> again. This also happens in about three hours. Whatever weight is lost must afterwards be replaced on the cupel with fresh lead and copper <note>original: "Saturno und Venere"</note> according to the first preparation. It may reach its perfection in 14 days. If one sets the work on a larger scale—though the cost should not exceed 100 <term>gulden</term> <note>A gold coin used as a standard currency in the Holy Roman Empire</note>—one should give it another 14 days and thereby gain up to 1000 gulden. If, however, one wishes to put only lead and copper on the cupel, the lead gives a considerable portion of silver when it is <term>graded</term> seven times in the manner described above—namely, that it passes through seven cupels, each cupel being about a fifth or sixth part.

### Another Process, Which Proceeds Somewhat Faster Than the Other.

Also, take five pounds of silver litharge <note>original: "Silberglett"; the byproduct of refining silver</note> and one pound of copper burnt with sulfur, all crushed fine. Mix in half as much, or slightly more, common salt. Let it run on a roasting dish <note>original: "Treibscherben"</note>. After that, take sulfur, gold <note>original symbol: ☉</note>, and common salt—equal parts of each—and mix them together. For about one hour, cast this mixture upon the molten material on the dish. Thereafter, for a full hour, cast only common salt upon the material on the roasting dish. Then let it fume away completely <note>original: "abriechen"</note>, and you will find the copper is malleable. This should be burnt again with sulfur, but one should weigh it beforehand to see what weight it has lost.

### A Powder.

Also, take one *Loth* <note>A historical German unit of weight, approximately 15-16 grams</note> of fixed antimony <note>original: "Antimonij fixi"</note>, and two ounces each of sublimated lead <note>original: "Saturnum sublimatum"</note> and saffron of Mars <note>original: "Crocus Martis"; iron oxide</note>. Take one *Loth* of vitriol <note>original symbol: ⊖</note>, and equal parts of tin <note>original symbol: ♃</note> and sulfur <note>original: "Sulphur"</note>, two *Loth* each. Take brittle antimony, iron <note>original symbol: ♂</note>, and gold <note>original symbol: ☉</note>, one pound of each. Mix them; let them melt together gently in a covered flask. Then, one pound of vitriol <note>original symbol: ⊖</note> and a half-pound of sulfur should be cast upon it. Stir it with a wire and let it vent <note>original: "verpuffen"; to deflagrate or release vapors</note>; it yields a gray powder.

### Purification of Silver gives the Weight.

Take thin sheets of fine silver and cement <term>cementier</term> <note>A process of heating metal sheets packed in a powdered mixture to remove impurities</note> them with chalk for twenty-four hours. Afterward, take them out, wash them well, and cement them again with fresh chalk. Do this three times. Then cement them with prepared verdigris <note>original: "Salgrüne"; literally "salt-green," referring to copper acetate</note> also three times, and wash them clean every time. Afterward, reduce it back into a solid mass.

### Make Saffron of Venus thus, for the Specific Procedure.

Also, take copper sheets from an old kettle; coat them with sulfur and oil, and cement them for three days in a clean vessel, ensuring the sheets do not touch one another. Take care that they do not melt. Rub the lime <note>original: "Calcem"; the powdered oxide remaining after heating</note> very cleanly and well upon a marble stone. Soak it well with saltwater and alum <note>original: "Aluminis"</note>; mix in four parts of prepared tutty <note>original: "Tutiæ præparatæ"; zinc oxide recovered from the flues of smelting furnaces</note>. Calcine <term>calcinier</term> it again for three or four days, so it becomes a beautiful, lovely red. Wash the salts out <note>original: "süß ihn ab"; to "sweeten" by leaching away corrosive salts</note> with warm distilled water. You may also use common prepared salt.

### The Aqua Fortis for the Specific Procedure.

Take two parts each of vitriol <note>original symbols: ⊖ / ⊖ / ⊖</note> and one part of feathered alum <note>original: "☉ plumosum"; likely referring to *alumen plumosum*, a fibrous mineral like asbestos or halotrichite</note>. Grind each separately; mix them and distill an aqua fortis <note>Literally "strong water," a name for nitric acid</note> through the helm <note>The cooling cap of a still</note> or retort. First use a gentle fire, then strengthen the fire until the helm becomes yellow. Then keep this water separately, well-sealed. Set another receiver <note>original: "Fürlag"</note> before it and seal it well with luting <note>A clay paste used to seal alchemical joints</note> so that the spirits <note>Vapors</note> do not escape. Strengthen the fire until the helm becomes red and no more spirits come forth at all. Keep this also separately and well-closed.

# Mirror of Philosophers.

## Whoever desires to know the highest and truest
## knowledge of the Art and Wisdom / the high Wisdom /
## should examine this present little book quite diligently /
## and read it through with earnestness many times / for then
## they will become present / and partake in their
## desired goal and end.

<margin>pafy <note>Likely a cryptic shorthand or signature; such marks were common in alchemical manuscripts to denote specific sections or authorship</note></margin>
Now listen, you children of the ancient Sages / for I come here and wish to appear before you with the highest / and most long-lasting Stone <term>Stone</term> <note>The Philosopher's Stone, the legendary substance of alchemy believed to transmute base metals into gold and provide the Elixir of Life</note> / as ever possible / and primarily to reveal the state of human affairs / also the most secret treasure of the whole world / and I wish to discover the same / not in a fictitious way / nor mockingly / but in the most certain / and friendly manner. Therefore and for that reason, we wish to listen with such devotion / as diligently as I shall present the teaching of our Mastery <term>Mastery</term> <note>The *Magisterium*; the successful completion of the alchemical process or the "Great Work"</note> to you / for I will hold before you much better and more credible testimony of those things / which I myself have seen with my own eyes / and touched with my hands / against all the deceivers and land-swindlers <term>land-swindlers</term> <note>original: "Landbescheisser"; a colorful contemporary term for traveling charlatans and fraudulent alchemists who cheated patrons with false promises</note> who have ever existed / who have expended much expense / toil and labor / and ultimately achieved nothing other than a miserable outcome. For that reason, I will tell it all to you clearly and openly / so that the inexperienced / as well as the experienced / may understand something in this Mastery / and no one may be ashamed on our account. For the ancient Sages wrote the matter so incompletely and so utterly confusedly / that one might not only not understand their writing / but they also did not agree with one another / which happened primarily for those reasons / so that they might either deceive those who strive after such noble Art <term>Art</term> <note>Alchemy was traditionally referred to as the "Royal Art" or "The Art"</note> / or else deter them from their undertaking. I, for my part, however / wish to set aside all falsehood and darkness / and place the true experience entirely before your eyes / and therefore include the opinions of the Sages / which best serve such an undertaking / so that the whole matter / of which we treat / may be understood more openly and clearly.

For there is only a **single Stone**, one medicine, a single order, and this Art is the most certain of all. For our Art is not performed in many kinds of things, but in **one thing**, even if the matter is called by whatever different names and strange titles—it is always only a single thing, from a single substance. Nor is Nature improved, except within its own natural properties.

There are certain fantasizers who boast / how they can make a <term>drinkable gold</term> <note>original Latin: "aurum potabile"</note> out of common gold / or that they even believe / that the same drinkable gold / is the very best for healing / and the resistance of all illnesses / there are also some doctors / who let ducats <note>gold coins</note> boil in water / and say / how the same is the noblest and most useful for health / though it is entirely / the opposite / with their preparation / that this drinkable gold or water is no real drinkable gold / nor is this water good or useful / for making healthy / but evil and bad to drink / for neither common gold / nor other metals are good for making healthy or healing. But I may well say that such gold is good / for the purchase of medicines and confections / and what belongs to the sick / also to pay the doctor with it / it is also good that he has a basin full of ducats so that he may show the same to the sick person. For it serves him very well / that he beholds the gold <note>The author suggests a psychological benefit or "cheering up" the patient by showing them wealth, rather than the gold having a chemical effect</note> / but the true drinkable gold or *aurum potabile* of the Sages / is the prepared Elixir / and that same is the drinkable gold, not visibly / but more in its power / for it is the greatest and highest medicine / which drives out all superfluity / as much from the human body / as from whichever metals / for it transforms all imperfect metals / into the very best and truest gold / and in like manner it cleanses all imperfect metals of all leprosy <note>original: "Auſſatz"; in alchemical terms, "leprosy" refers to the corrosion, oxidation, or impurities found in base metals like lead or iron</note> and illness. Also the human body <note>original: "Leichnam"; here meaning the living body or physical frame</note> / and this is thus most certain / and not at all doubtful / and mark you / that this is the meaning of all Sages. But those fools who regard common gold as drinkable gold / those same are blind and more than blind / also deceivers / for if common gold gave away something of its perfection to another / then that same gold would remain imperfect in itself.

### Arnoldus.
<note>Likely Arnold of Villanova, a medieval physician and alchemist.</note>

Join our servant to his fragrant sister, so they will give birth to the Art together; for when the white, shining woman is led to the red man, they immediately help one another. And in their embrace, they are coupled together; by their own power they are dissolved, and by their own power they are killed, so that out of the two, one single body <note>original: "Leichnam" (corpse). In alchemy, "killing" the matter refers to breaking it down so it can be reborn in a purified state.</note> may remain.

### The Mirror.

You have asked how many types of true colors there are; I will gladly tell you rightly. You should know that there are three perfect colors from which all others take their beginning: the first color is **Black**, the second **White**, and the third **Red**. <note>These represent the three main stages of the alchemical "Great Work": *nigredo* (blackening/putrefaction), *albedo* (whitening/purification), and *rubedo* (reddening/perfection).</note> There are also many other intermediate colors which one should not be concerned with, for many other colors appear before the white color is achieved.

### Hortulanus the Philosopher.
<note>Hortulanus, or "The Gardener," was a 14th-century commentator on the Emerald Tablet of Hermes.</note>

At that point occurs the joining of the two bodies; this same union is necessary for our mastery. If out of these two bodies alone only a single body were in our Stone, it would never yield any tincture <note>The "tincture" is the transformative essence of the Philosopher's Stone that can change base metals into gold.</note>. Therefore, it is necessary that one joins these same two bodies. When the two are now joined, and in the joining of the Stone have accepted one another, then the Stone is pregnant in the belly of the wind. This is what the wise man said: "The wind has carried him in its belly." <note>This is a direct quote from the *Emerald Tablet*, one of the most famous foundational texts of alchemy.</note> It is clear that the wind is the Air, and that the Air is the Life, and the Life is the Soul—that is, Oil and Water.

### Hermes the Philosopher.
<note>Referring to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure to whom many alchemical works are attributed.</note>

I, who am elevated above all circles of the world, have seen four faces which had a single Father. One face is in the mountains, the second in the air, the third in the stones, and the fourth in the hollows.

### Mirror.

Here the bodies are placed into putrefaction <note>The process of decay or breaking down of the starting materials, known as the *Nigredo* stage.</note> and become a black earth. When you see the matter turn black, rejoice, for this is the beginning of your Work.

### Arnoldus.

<margin>bell metal</margin>
Burn our bell metal <term>bell metal: a specific alloy of copper and tin, used here as a code for the starting material of the work</term> in a gentle fire until it becomes a single body and the tincture <note>The concentrated essence or "spirit" of the material that has the power to transform other substances.</note> has been drawn out. You should not, however, mix such a tincture entirely or raise it up all at once; rather, it should come out little by little every day until a long time has passed.

### Hermes the Philosopher.

I am the black of the white, and the red of the white, and the yellow color of the red. Truly I am, truthfully I speak, and I am no liar. You should know that the head of this art is the Raven, which flies without wings in the blackness of the night and in the clarity of the day. From the bitterness that is in its throat, the substance is taken; from its body, the redness <note>The stage of *Rubedo*, or the final perfection of the Work.</note> is taken; and from its hands is taken the clear water.

### Hermes the Philosopher.

Therefore, you should understand and receive this gift of God, and keep it hidden from all the unwise. For it is hidden within the halls of the metals; its stone is earthly, and it lies in a visible color, in high mountains, a wide open sea. See, I have explained all the figures to you.

### Arnoldus.

<margin>bell metal</margin>
But when it first becomes black, we say that this same blackness is a key to the Work. For the work cannot proceed without blackness; the blackness is the tincture or color that we seek herein, with which we tinge every body. This tincture is hidden within its bell metal, just as the soul is hidden in the human body.

## Mirror.

Therefore, you, most beloved son, when you are engaged in the Work, be diligent that you first obtain the black color. Then you will be certain that you are rotting <note>failing or decomposing the material to release its essence</note> the substances you have put in, and that you understand the right path.

<margin>☞</margin>
What resides above the matter <term>matter: the physical substance being transformed in the alchemical vessel</term> are dark mists; they are spirits or smoke. This earth, which sits above the water, will descend in the other vessel down to the bottom of the container, and from it, worms will grow <note>The "growth of worms" or "snakes" is a common alchemical metaphor for the first signs of life or reorganization emerging from the decaying, "dead" matter.</note>.

Furthermore, the Sages <note>original: "Weisen." Refers to the historical alchemical authorities like Hermes or Geber.</note> see that the matter thickens and is turned into earth, and that this thickening initially floated upon the water. As they allowed it to slowly thicken, they saw the earth sink into the water until it rested on the bottom beneath the liquid. Because this earth was yellow-colored, black, and stinking, they declared that this was the true destruction <note>original: "Zerstörung." In this context, it refers to the necessary decomposition or "death" of the old form so a new one can emerge.</note>.

### Geber.
<note>Geber refers to Jabir ibn Hayyan (c. 721–813), a legendary figure in Islamic alchemy whose writings were foundational to European alchemical thought.</note>

For this entire mastery <term>mastery: the skilled practice of the Great Work.</term> rests solely upon a single thing. This we wish to show you through the sayings of the Sages <note>original: "Weiſen"</note> and according to the measure we ourselves have seen and prepared with great labor and diligence. We have recognized that this same single thing is perfect in itself for the White and the Red <note>The "White" and "Red" represent the final stages of the alchemical work: the White Stone (albedo) for making silver, and the Red Stone (rubedo) for making gold.</note>. # The Black Crow's Head.
<note>original: "Der schwartze Rabenkopff." In alchemical symbolism, the Crow’s Head represents the *Nigredo* or "blackening" stage, where the matter is decomposed and purified through "death."</note>

### Black earth in which worms are born.
<note>original Latin: "Terra nigra in qua nascuntur vermes."</note>

This is the black and stinking earth of the Sages <term>Sages: The legendary alchemists and philosophers whose secret writings formed the basis of the "Great Art."</term>, in which worms grow, where one swallows the other; for the destruction of one thing is the birth of another. For this earth lies at the bottom of the vessel and dissolves <note>original: "solviert sich"</note> entirely into the water as before.

Here it is asked: in what time is the Stone turned into the black color, and what is the sign of its proper dissolution? I answer: when the black color appears, this same blackness is a certain sign of the proper putrefaction <term>putrefaction: a stage of chemical breakdown often compared to organic decay, seen as necessary for the "rebirth" of the matter.</term> and dissolution of the Stone. But when the blackness has entirely disappeared, it is a sign that the Stone has completely putrefied and dissolved itself.

Mirror of Philosophy. 812

<margin>white brass</margin>
Whiteness comes to redness through cooking, if the fire is constantly regulated; when our white brass <note>In alchemy, "brass" (laton) refers to the metallic matter during its middle stages of purification. "White brass" is the matter that has reached the silver stage but is not yet gold.</note> is diligently cooked, it will become the very best red. Therefore come these following words: Before the whiteness, there shall be no redness, but it shall give off its clear light; it shall not boil, but rest in constant warmth, so long until it has its shine, until it takes away the greenness, and the red color comes out of the white.

<margin>dry & <unclear>until</unclear> <unclear>red</unclear></margin>
Therefore it should be boiled down in a dry fire and dry calcination <term>calcination|the process of heating a substance to high temperatures to achieve decomposition or a change in state, often reducing it to a powder</term>, so long until it becomes red like cinnabar <term>cinnabar|a bright red mineral (mercury sulfide) that was the primary source of mercury and a symbol for the "Red" stage</term>; after this, you should add no water nor any other thing to it, until it has been boiled down to its perfect redness.

->Nillius.<-

If it happens that it has become red through further cooking, it will give off a color of eternal gold; it is an herb called Adrop <note>original: "Adrop"; a code name used by alchemists, often referring to lead or the raw material of the Stone</note>, Dunachy, Alot; from this the medicine is made. And it is found on a high mountain in the field at N. <note>The letter "N" is likely used here as a placeholder for a secret location</note>. For in the number of seven days the whole work is contained; thus in the seventh number everything is formed and made stable. 
Start this work very often again, and distill it often through seven whitenesses, so that the order of the days remains.

### Note the property of this our Stone.

<margin>Medicine.</margin>
Thus it also has a powerful virtue to heal all kinds of sickness, above all other medicines of the physicians; for it gladdens the soul, strengthens the power, preserves virtue, and puts away old age; it does not let the blood rot nor allow it to take the upper hand, nor the choler <term>choler|yellow bile, one of the four "humors" or bodily fluids; it was believed to cause irritability and heat</term> to burn, nor the melancholy <term>melancholy|black bile, the humor associated with sadness and coldness</term> to take hold; instead, it increases the blood beyond measure and purifies it. What is in the spiritual members, that it cleanses; and all bodily members it restores powerfully again, and protects them from harm. Thus it heals in the very best way all hot and cold diseases, above all other medicines; for if the sickness had lasted a whole year, it heals it in 12 days; but if it were an old sickness that had lasted many years, it will heal it in a month. And to speak briefly, it drives out all evil moisture and puts good moisture in its place. It gives favor and honor; whoever carries this Stone with him, it gives him safety, boldness, and victory in battle. And in this is accomplished the highest secret, above the preciousness of the whole world, a most noble treasure to which no thing can be compared. To him who has it, God preserves his mind, so that he does not reveal it to the ignorant, or that it be made public.

Mirror of Philosophy. 813

## This Book is Called God’s Gift.

And thus is completed the noble gift of God, which is a secret and an incomparable treasure; for as Plato says, whoever possesses this gift of God holds the empire or the command of the whole world, for he has reached the end of all riches and has broken the bond of nature. This is not only because he is able to transmute all imperfect bodies into the purest gold and silver, but most of all because he can protect and preserve humans and every other animal from all diseases.

<margin>24</margin>
<margin>Crystal-like sheet. white: Elixir</margin>
The crystalline plate <note>original: "Christallen Blech"; likely referring to the brittle, shimmering surface of the purified "White Stone" before it is ground into powder</note>, which is the white elixir: if one gives a piece the size of a mustard seed to a person with a fever, it heals them. Also, if a leper is purified with this same plate through the four seasons of the year, he becomes healthy and is delivered from his leprosy. And if anyone had the evil leprous disease called Elephantiasis <note>original: "Eleuantiasis"; a term used in the Middle Ages to describe a severe form of leprosy that thickens the skin</note>, if they were purified twice a year—namely in March and in the autumn month—with the red powder from which the saffron-colored medicine is made, they would be healed. Both powders, red and white, bring health; that which is falling into the danger of death, it also heals paralysis. And if the powder is held before the nostrils of a woman in labor, she shall be delivered. This is what Hermes says.

Geber <note>Jabir ibn Hayyan (c. 721–815), a foundational figure in alchemy whose Latinized works were central to European science</note>, however, says that the red elixir heals all long-lasting diseases of which the physicians have despaired, and makes a person living again, so that he renews himself like an eagle and lives for five hundred years and even longer, as some Sages have done; for they used such an elixir three times a week, in a portion as large as a mustard seed.

There is an herb called Saturn <note>In alchemy, Saturn is the name for lead; here it refers to the "plant" or "root" of the metallic work</note>, from the cinnamon <note>original: "Canel"; can refer to cinnamon or a tube/pipe, but here likely describes the reddish-brown color of the matter</note>, from which such a medicine is made; for every like thing strengthens its like, every form rejoices in its own form, and every species rejoices in its own species. Therefore, note that all diseases that arise from the crown of the head to the soles of the feet—if the disease were a month old, it shall be healed in one day; but if it were a year old, it shall be healed in a month. Because it heals all imperfect metals of all disease <note>In alchemical philosophy, "rust" or "corrosion" in metals was seen as a disease that the Stone "cured" by turning the metal into gold</note>, so too does it heal all human bodies. Therefore, our established Stone is not unjustly called the Great Theriac <term>theriac|originally a medicinal concoction used as an antidote for poison, but in alchemy, it refers to a universal panacea or "cure-all"</term>, as much for the bodies of humans as for those of metals, of which Hermes, a King of the Greeks and a Father of the Sages, says: If you were to take our elixir every day for seven days, in a weight of three mustard seeds, your gray hair will fall from your head and black hair will grow in its place; and thus, from an old man, you shall create a young one.

->Hermes.<-

<meta>This page continues the theoretical and authoritative grounding of the alchemical treatise, transitioning from the practical medicinal results described on page 813 to the formal definitions and philosophical justifications of the art provided by legendary figures like Hermes Trismegistus and Thomas Aquinas.</meta>

Mirror of Philosophy. 814

->Hermes.<-

This book, however, is called the *Book of the Composition of Alchemy*, and what alchemy is, and what its composition is. The Latin language has not known this name and composition of alchemy until now; in the present discourse, it sets forth this unknown and wonderful name under the explanation of clarity. Hermes, however, and other sages after him, interpret this name thus, and say in the *Book of Essential Transformation* that alchemy is a corporeal essence <note>original: "leibliche Weſenheit"; a physical substance or being</note>, composed of one and one <note>likely referring to the alchemical marriage of opposites, such as Sulphur and Mercury</note>, which joins the most noble things together through art and action, and transforms them into a better species through natural mixing.

->Thomas Aquinas.<-

The transmutation of metals is such that the essence of one thing is changed into the essence of another thing. Although Aristotle and Avicenna <note>Ibn Sina (c. 980–1037), a Persian polymath whose works on chemistry and medicine were central to medieval European science</note> say that practitioners of alchemy should know that the form of metals can never be changed, it is written later that this is only possible if that same form is brought back into its First Matter <term>First Matter: also called Prima Materia, the formless, primal base substance from which all matter was thought to originate</term>. This same matter is nearest and most similar to all metals, especially to living Mercury <note>original: "Mercurio"; referring here to "philosophical mercury" or quicksilver</note>, but at first, this same matter is a Water. Yet such water is very much devoted and related to nature—indeed, as if it were natural—although nature is aided by art.

And through these difficult things, many have become fools who have spent their youth on this art and lost their wealth. There are so many kinds of labor described by these ignorant people that are quite harmful, so that even if you spent all your wealth on this work, you would afterward despair of the art and never obtain the desired piece. I consider all things, just as kings have had subtle workers who afterward hardly or not at all reached the perfect end. I once believed the art was not true or just, but I went into myself and considered the *Books of Secrets* of Aristotle and Avicenna, and I found them to be in the truth, even though they explained it in a confused and inverted way. I also weighed the books of their opponents and found similar deceptions. I also weighed the natural principles <note>original: "Anſenge"; beginnings or foundations</note> and found that one could perform the art through them; for I have seen that living quicksilver penetrated through metals, and that other metals grew from it. Therefore, I admonish that no one should venture to begin the work—for the sake of the things yet to be told—unless he be quite well-experienced in natural principles, and well-practiced and knowledgeable in the guidance of the
<meta>catchword: Distillations</meta>

<summary>This page defines alchemy through the authorities of Hermes and Thomas Aquinas, arguing that transmutation is possible if metals are returned to their "First Matter." Aquinas shares his personal journey from skepticism to belief in the art, warning against the "foolish" methods of ignorant practitioners.</summary>

Distillation / Coagulation / Solution / and most of all in the regulation of the fire / so that he is not a man who wishes to hurry / but one who is slow / and who wishes to act with time, cleanly and cautiously / it is a stone that is animal, spiritual, growing, and earthly <note>These four categories refer to the belief that the "Philosopher's Stone" contains the essences of the four kingdoms: animal, vegetable, mineral, and the spiritual realm.</note> / from which is extracted the virtue of the white color / or the clear redness / so that they add nothing to it / and it is extracted through the separation of the four elements / their purification and joining together in the name of the Lord. Take one pound of it / rub it small / and strongly upon a marble stone <note>A flat marble slab used for grinding materials into fine powder.</note> / and soak it with one and a half pounds of common oil / so it becomes like a dough / if you throw a little of this same dough upon many parts of the metals / it will transform them into right good silver or gold / therein the four elements are hardened and purified / some with one spirit and body / and although I have not tested this work / I nevertheless perceive it to be natural and true / and believe also that it is well known to everyone. # Mirror.

But so that you may understand the right meaning all the more clearly / we wish to show you in which hour / and on which day / and also in which month one shall begin our Masterpiece / and we say / whoever shall work otherwise / he will certainly err and fail / and whoever will work according to our command / he will certainly see the true, righteous Art / and the right Mastery. Therefore we command / that one should take the Stone of the Wise <term>Stone of the Wise: The Philosopher's Stone, the legendary substance capable of turning base metals into gold.</term> with all its essence / and that one should take out from that same stone its very purest and most subtle essence / and that one should set that in the Vessel of the Wise / and that one seal the mouth of the vessel / according to the custom of the Sages / and that one place it in the Furnace of the Wise / when the sun goes down. All this, however, must happen on a Monday / and this work shall happen and be started in the middle of the "Christ-month" (which is called December) / until the middle of the month of January under the sign of Capricorn / then one shall light the Fire of the Wise / throughout the entire sign / and govern the work / according to the custom of the Sages / and be diligent / so that in the aforementioned sign of Capricorn the entire volatile matter is made permanent and stable. <note>In alchemy, "fixing" a substance means turning a volatile or evaporating material into a solid, stable form that can withstand heat.</note>

<meta>This page continues the practical instructions for the alchemical "Great Work," transitioning from the philosophical definitions of the previous page to the specific manual operations of regulating furnace heat and observing the color changes of the substance.</meta>

Mirror of Philosophy. 816

# Mirror.

So great should be the heat that you can keep your hands unharmed between the walls of the furnace; in such heat let it stand until you see the matter <note>original: "Matery", referring to the alchemical substance undergoing transformation</note> begin to turn black. And if it takes too long and does not wish to turn black, then strengthen the fire a little; then you will see that the matter will blacken. When this happens, rejoice, for this is the beginning of the digestion <note>original: "Derwung", an archaic term for digestion or decoction</note>; then keep the fire in a steady state until all colors have passed away. And when you now see the matter become white in some measure, then increase the fire for it gently and more and more, until it comes to a perfect, stable white color; then it has enough, and the White [Work] <note>The "Albedo" phase, signifying the purification of the substance.</note> for the white is accomplished. But one should govern the fire very slowly according to the signs shown by the matter, until it rises into the white color.

# Geber in his book, called *The Sum*, in the 16th Chapter, on the Beginnings of Natural Things.

<margin>sealed</margin>
<margin>luted</margin>
<note>To "lute" is to seal a vessel with a specialized clay or cement to make it airtight and heat-resistant.</note>
It is to be noted that after our Stone has been purified and perfectly cleansed of all corruptible things, and thereafter is joined, then you have no need to further loosen the vessel, nor to open it, but only that God might protect it so that it does not break. And therefore the Sages have said that the entire mastery <note>The completion of the Great Work or "Magisterium."</note> shall be accomplished in one single vessel; and it is to be known that it shall be completed in 40 days and as many nights. No fixed time can be set for the Work toward the white color after the proper purification, except for how well the artist <term>Artist: the alchemist performing the work</term> labors; and in 60 or 90 days it is accomplished toward the Redness <note>The "Rubedo" or final stage of the alchemical process, resulting in the Philosopher's Stone.</note>, or even in 91 days at the very most; and these are the correct goals and times for the entire completion of the Work; and when you have come to this, then praise the Lord Jesus Christ.
->Amen.<-
